A dark green, textured cloth book cover featuring two gold-stamped emblems.

In the upper left corner is the seal of the Theosophical Society. This circular emblem consists of an Ouroboros <note>original: "Ouroboros"; a serpent swallowing its own tail</note>—which symbolizes eternity and the cycle of rebirth. Inside the Ouroboros are two interlaced triangles forming a hexagram, representing the union of spirit and matter. In the center of the hexagram is an Egyptian Ankh, the symbol of life. At the top of the hexagram, within the circle of the serpent, is a smaller circle containing a swastika <note>In this context, a traditional Eastern symbol of evolution and the motion of the universe, predating its 20th-century political misuse</note>.

In the lower right corner is a stylized monogram of the Theosophical Society. It depicts a large Tau cross (forming the letter 'T') with a serpent coiled around it in the shape of the letter 'S', signifying the initials "TS" for the Society.

<header>PREFACE</header>

# PREFACE

---

The *Theosophical Glossary* suffers from the disadvantage of being an almost entirely posthumous work <note>published after the death of the author</note>, of which the author only saw the first thirty-two pages in proof. This is all the more regrettable because H.P.B. <note>Helena Petrovna Blavatsky, 1831–1891, co-founder of the Theosophical Society</note>, as was her habit, was adding considerably to her original manuscript. She would no doubt have increased the volume far beyond its present limits, and so would have shed light on many obscure terms that are not included in the present Glossary. More importantly, she would have provided us with a sketch of the lives and teachings of the most famous Adepts <note>highly advanced practitioners or masters of esoteric wisdom</note> of the East and West.

The *Theosophical Glossary* intends to provide information on the principal Sanskrit, Pahlavi, Tibetan, Pali, Chaldean, Persian, Scandinavian, Hebrew, Greek, Latin, Kabbalistic, and Gnostic words, as well as Occult terms generally used in Theosophical literature. These are primarily found in *Isis Unveiled*, *Esoteric Buddhism*, *The Secret Doctrine*, *The Key to Theosophy*, and so on; as well as in the monthly magazines *The Theosophist*, *Lucifer*, and *The Path*, and other publications of the Theosophical Society. The articles marked [w.w.w.], which explain words found in the *Kabbalah* or which illustrate Rosicrucian or Hermetic doctrines, were contributed at the special request of H.P.B. by Brother W. W. Westcott, M.B., P.M., and P.Z., who is the Secretary General of the Rosicrucian Society and the Instructor <note>original: "Præmonstrator"</note> of the Kabbalah to the Hermetic Order of the G.D. <note>The Golden Dawn, a secret society devoted to the study and practice of the occult, metaphysics, and paranormal activities</note>.

H.P.B. also desired to express her special gratitude—regarding the organization of facts—to the *Sanskrit-Chinese Dictionary* by Eitel, *The Hindu Classical Dictionary* by Dowson, *The Vishnu Purana* by Wilson, and the *Royal Masonic Cyclopedia* by Kenneth Mackenzie.

As the undersigned can make no claim to the elaborate and extraordinary scholarship required for editing the diverse and multilingual contents of H.P.B.’s last contribution to Theosophical literature, there will necessarily be mistakes in transliteration and other details which specialists in scholarship will immediately notice. Meanwhile, however, as nearly every Orientalist has his own system, varying transliterations may be excused in the present work and should not be blamed entirely on the "Karma" <note>the spiritual principle of cause and effect</note> of the editor.

->G. R. S. MEAD.<-

London, *January*, 1892.

<summary>This preface by G.R.S. Mead introduces H.P. Blavatsky's posthumous glossary, noting its wide linguistic scope and the contributions of W.W. Westcott. Mead acknowledges the challenges of editing such a complex, multilingual work after the author's death.</summary>

<keywords>Theosophy, H.P. Blavatsky, G.R.S. Mead, W.W. Westcott, occultism, linguistics, posthumous works, esoteric literature, Kabbalah, Rosicrucianism</keywords>

# THEOSOPHICAL GLOSSARY

## A.

**A.**—The first letter in all the world-alphabets except for a few, such as the Mongolian, Japanese, Tibetan, and Ethiopian, among others. It is a letter of great mystic power and “magic virtue” to those who have adopted it, and for whom its numerical value is *one*. It is the *Aleph* of the Hebrews, symbolized by the Ox or Bull; the *Alpha* of the Greeks, the one and the first; and the *Az* of the Slavonians, signifying the pronoun “I” (referring to the divine concept “I am that I am”). Even in Astrology, Taurus (the Ox, Bull, or *Aleph*) is the first of the Zodiacal signs <note>In some ancient systems, the zodiac began with Taurus rather than Aries</note>, its color being white and yellow. The sacred *Aleph* acquires an even more marked sanctity with the Christian Kabbalists <note>Mystics who applied Jewish Kabbalistic principles to Christian theology</note> when they learn that this letter typifies the Trinity in Unity, as it is composed of two *Yods* <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>, one upright and the other reversed, joined by a slanting bar or connection, depicted as—א. Kenneth R. H. Mackenzie states that “the St. Andrew’s cross is occultly connected to it.” The divine name, the first in the series corresponding with *Aleph*, is *AêHêIêH* or *Ahih* when written without vowels, and this is a Sanskrit root.

**Aahla** (*Egyptian*). One of the divisions of the *Kerneter* <note>The dwelling place of the gods or the underworld</note> or infernal regions, also known as *Amenti*; the word means the “Field of Peace.”

**Aanroo** (*Egyptian*). The second division of *Amenti*. The celestial field of Aanroo is encircled by an iron wall. The field is covered with wheat, and the “Defunct” <note>The deceased soul</note> are represented gleaning it for the “Master of Eternity.” Some stalks are three, others five, and the highest are seven cubits high. Those who reached the last two numbers entered the state of bliss (which is called in Theosophy *Devachan* <note>A peaceful, heavenly state between incarnations</note>); the disembodied spirits whose harvest was only three cubits high went into lower regions (*Kâmaloka* <note>A semi-material plane where desires and passions are purged; similar to purgatory</note>). To the Egyptians, wheat was the symbol of the *Law of Retribution* or *Karma*. The cubits referred to the seven, five, and three human “principles” <note>The different layers of the human constitution, such as body, soul, and spirit</note>.

**Aaron** (*Hebrew*). The elder brother of Moses and the first Initiate of

the Hebrew Lawgiver. The name means the *Illuminated*, or the *Enlightened*. Aaron thus heads the line, or Hierarchy, of the initiated *Nabim* <note>original: Nabim; Hebrew for "Prophets"</note>, or Seers.

**Ab** (*Hebrew*). The eleventh month of the Hebrew civil year; the fifth of the sacred year beginning in July.

**Abaddon** (*Hebrew*). An angel of hell, corresponding to the Greek Apollyon <note>meaning "The Destroyer"</note>.

**Abatur** (*Gnostic*). In the Nazarene system, the "Ancient of Days"—the *High Ancient* <note>original Latin: Antiquus Altus</note> and the Father of the *Demiurge* <note>term for the artisan or creator of the physical world</note> of the Universe—is called the *Third Life* or "Abatur." He corresponds to the Third "Logos" <note>the "Word" or manifested deity</note> in the *Secret Doctrine*. (See *Codex Nazaraeus* <note>The sacred scripture of the Mandaeans</note>).

**Abba Amona** (*Hebrew*). Literally, "Father-Mother"; the occult names of the two higher *Sephiroth* <note>emanations of God in the Kabbalah</note>, *Chokmah* <note>Wisdom</note> and *Binah* <note>Understanding</note>, of the upper triad, the apex of which is *Sephira* or *Kether* <note>The Crown</note>. From this triad issues the lower seven levels of the Sephirothal Tree.

**Abhamsi** (*Sanskrit*). A mystic name of the "four orders of beings," which are: Gods, Demons, *Pitris* <note>ancestral spirits</note>, and Men. Orientalists somehow connect the name with "waters," but esoteric philosophy connects its symbolism with *Akasa*—the ethereal "waters of space." This is because the "four orders of (lower) beings" and the three higher Orders of Spiritual Beings are born upon the bosom and the seven planes of "space." (See *Secret Doctrine* Vol. I, p. 458, and "Ambhamsi.")

**Abhasvaras** (*Sanskrit*). The *Devas* <note>shining beings or deities</note> or "Gods" of Light and Sound; the highest of the upper three celestial regions (planes) of the second *Dhyana* <note>state of profound meditation</note>. They are a class of gods sixty-four in number, representing a certain cycle and an occult number.

**Abhava** (*Sanskrit*). Negation, or the non-being of individual objects; the *noumenal* <note>the thing-in-itself, as opposed to how it appears to the senses</note> substance, or abstract objectivity.

**Abhaya** (*Sanskrit*). "Fearlessness"—a son of *Dharma* <note>Duty or Law</note>; and also a religious life of duty. As an adjective meaning "Fearless," Abhaya is a title given to every Buddha.

**Abhayagiri** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, "Mount Fearless" in Ceylon <note>modern-day Sri Lanka</note>. It has an ancient *Vihara* or Monastery in which the well-known Chinese traveler Fa-hien found 5,000 Buddhist priests and ascetics in the year 400 of our era. It also housed a School called *Abhayagiri Vasinah*, the "School of the Secret Forest." This philosophical school was regarded as heretical because the ascetics studied the doctrines of both the "greater" and the "smaller" vehicles—the *Mahayana* and the *Hinayana* systems—as well as *Triyana*, or the three successive degrees of Yoga. This is much like how a certain Brotherhood functions now beyond the Himalayas. This proves that the "disciples of Katyayana" were and are as non-sectarian as their humble admirers, the Theosophists, are today. (See the "*Sthavirah*" School.) This was the most mystical of all the schools and was renowned for the number of *Arhats* <note>enlightened saints</note> it produced. The Brotherhood of *Abhayagiri* called themselves the disciples of Katyayana, the favorite *Chela* <note>disciple</note> of Gautama Buddha. Tradition says that owing to...

**Abhidharma** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). The metaphysical (third) part of the *Tripitaka*, a very philosophical Buddhist work by Kâtyâyana.

**Abhijnâ** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). Six phenomenal (or "supernatural") gifts which Sâkyamuni Buddha acquired during the night on which he reached Buddhahood. (This is the "fourth" degree of Dhyâna—the seventh in esoteric teachings—which must be attained by every true Arhat. In China, the initiated Buddhist ascetics count six such powers, but in Ceylon they count only five. The first Abhijnâ is *Divyachakchus*, the instantaneous view of anything one wills to see; the second is *Divyasrotra*, the power of comprehending any sound whatever, etc.)

**Abhimânim** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). The name of Agni (fire), the "eldest son of Brahmâ"; in other words, the first element or Force produced in the universe at its evolution (the fire of creative desire). By his wife Swâhâ, Abhimânim had three sons (the fires) Pâvaka, Pavamâna, and Suchi, and these had "forty-five sons who, with the original son of Brahmâ and his three descendants, constitute the forty-nine fires" of Occultism.

**Abhimanyu** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). A son of Arjuna. He killed Lakshmana on the second day of the great battle of the Mahâbhârata, but was himself killed on the thirteenth day.

**Abhûtârajasas** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). A class of gods or *Devas* during the period of the fifth Manvantara <note>original: Manyantara; a period of cosmic manifestation</note>.

**Abib** (<note>Hebrew</note>). The first Jewish sacred month, which begins in March; it is also called Nîsan.

**Abiegnus Mons** (<note>Latin</note>). A mystic name from which, as if from a certain mountain, Rosicrucian documents are often said to be issued—"Monte Abiegno." There is a connection with Mount Meru and other sacred hills. [w.w.w.]

**Ab-i-hayat** (<note>Persian</note>). Water of immortality. It is supposed to give eternal youth and everlasting life to whoever drinks of it.

**Abiri** (<note>Greek</note>). See Kabiri, also written Kabeiri: the Mighty Ones, celestials, and sons of Zedec the just one. They are a group of deities worshipped in Phoenicia; they seem to be identical with the Titans, Corybantes, Curetes, Telchines, and the *Dii Magni* <note>Great Gods</note> of Virgil. [w.w.w.]

**Ablanathanbalba** (<note>Gnostic</note>). A term similar to "Abracadabra." It is said by C. W. King to have meant "thou art a father to us"; it reads the same from either end and was used as a charm in Egypt. (See "Abracadabra.")

**Abracadabra** (<note>Gnostic</note>). This symbolic word first occurs in a medical treatise in verse by Samonicus, who flourished during the reign of the Emperor Septimius Severus. Godfrey Higgins says it comes from *Abra* or *Abar*, meaning "God" in Celtic, and *cad*, meaning "holy"; it was used as a charm and engraved on *Kameas* <note>magical squares or talismans</note> as an amulet. [w.w.w.]

# THEOSOPHICAL

Godfrey Higgins was nearly right, as the word “Abracadabra” is a later corruption of the sacred Gnostic term “<term>Abrasax</term>.” The latter itself was a still earlier corruption of a sacred and ancient Coptic or Egyptian word: a magic formula which meant in its symbolism “Hurt me not” and addressed the deity in his hieroglyphics as “Father.” It was generally attached to an amulet or charm and worn as a *Tat* (see that entry) on the breast under the garments.

**<term>Abraxas</term>** or **<term>Abrasax</term>** (<note>Gnostic</note>). Mystic words which have been traced as far back as Basilides, the Pythagorean of Alexandria, in 90 <gloss>A.D.</gloss> He uses <term>Abraxas</term> as a title for Divinity—the supreme of the Seven—and as having 365 virtues. In Greek numeration: *a* = 1, *b* = 2, *r* = 100, *a* = 1, *x* = 60, *a* = 1, *s* = 200, totaling 365 days of the year, the solar year, or a cycle of divine action. C. W. King, author of *The Gnostics*, considers the word similar to the Hebrew *Shemhamphorash*, a holy word and the extended name of God. An <term>Abraxas</term> gem usually shows a man’s body with the head of a cock, one arm with a shield, and the other with a whip. [w.w.w.]

**<term>Abraxas</term>** is the counterpart of the Hindu <term>Abhîmânim</term> (see that entry) and Brahmâ combined. It is these compound and mystic qualities which caused Oliver, the great Masonic authority, to connect the name of <term>Abraxas</term> with that of Abraham. This was unwarranted; the virtues and attributes of <term>Abraxas</term>, which are 365 in number, should have shown him that the deity was connected with the Sun and the solar division of the year—indeed, that <term>Abraxas</term> is the original form (antitype), and the Sun is the symbolic representation (type).

**<term>Absoluteness</term>**. When predicated of the UNIVERSAL PRINCIPLE, it denotes an abstract noun, which is more correct and logical than to apply the adjective “absolute” to that which has neither attributes nor limitations, nor can it have any.

**<term>Ab-Soo</term>** (<note>Chaldean</note>). The mystic name for Space, meaning the dwelling of *Ab* the “Father,” or the head of the source of the Waters of Knowledge. The lore of the latter is concealed in the invisible space or <term>âkâsic</term> regions.

**<term>Acacia</term>** (<note>Greek</note>). Innocence; and also a plant used in Freemasonry as a symbol of initiation, immortality, and purity; the tree furnished the sacred Shittim wood of the Hebrews. [w.w.w.]

**<term>Achamôth</term>** (<note>Gnostic</note>). The name of the second, the inferior Sophia. Esoterically and among the Gnostics, the elder Sophia was the Holy Spirit (the female Holy Ghost) or the *Sakti* of the Unknown and the *Divine Spirit*; while Sophia <term>Achamôth</term> is only the personification of the female aspect of the creative male Force in nature; she is also the Astral Light.

**<term>Achar</term>** (<note>Hebrew</note>). The Gods over whom (according to the Jews) Jehovah is the God.

**<term>Âchâra</term>** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). Personal and social (religious) obligations.

**<term>Âchârya</term>** (<note>Sanskrit</note>). A spiritual teacher or Guru, such as Sankar-âchârya; literally, a “teacher of ethics.” This is a name generally given to Initiates and others, meaning “Master.”

<summary>This page defines various Gnostic, Chaldean, and Sanskrit terms, focusing heavily on the solar and divine symbolism of Abraxas and the Gnostic personification of Sophia Achamôth. It also touches on Masonic symbols like the Acacia and definitions of spiritual teachers and absolute principles.</summary>
<keywords>Abraxas, Abrasax, Gnosticism, Basilides, C.W. King, Shemhamphorash, Ab-Soo, Acacia, Sophia Achamôth, Astral Light, Âchârya, Guru</keywords>

### GLOSSARY

**Achath** (*Hebrew*). The one, the first, feminine; *achad* being masculine. A <term>Talmudic</term> word applied to <term>Jehovah</term>. It is noteworthy that the <term>Sanskrit</term> term *ak* means "one," *ekata* means "unity," and <term>Brahmâ</term> is called *âk* or *eka*, "the first," from which the <term>Hebrew</term> word and its application are derived.
**Acher** (*Hebrew*). The <term>Talmudic</term> name for the <term>Apostle Paul</term>. The <term>Talmud</term> narrates the story of the four <term>Tanaim</term> who entered the <term>Garden of Delight</term> (that is, came to be initiated): <term>Ben Asai</term>, who looked and lost his sight; <term>Ben Zoma</term>, who looked and lost his reason; <term>Acher</term>, who caused damage in the garden and failed; and <term>Rabbi Akiba</term>, who alone succeeded. The <term>Kabbalists</term> say that <term>Acher</term> is <term>Paul</term>.
**Acheron** (*Greek*). One of the rivers of Hell in <term>Greek mythology</term>.
**Achit** (*Sanskrit*). Absolute non-intelligence; as *Chit* is—in contrast—absolute intelligence.
**Achyuta** (*Sanskrit*). That which is not subject to change or fall; the opposite of *Chyuta*, "fallen." A title of <term>Vishnu</term>.
**Acosmism** (*Greek*). The precreative period, when there was no <term>Kosmos</term> but <term>Chaos</term> alone.
**Ad** (*Assyrian*). *Ad*, "the Father." In <term>Aramean</term>, *ad* means "one," and *ad-ad* means "the only one."
**Adah** (*Assyrian*). Borrowed by the <term>Hebrews</term> for the name of their <term>Adah</term>, father of <term>Jubal</term>, etc. However, <term>Adah</term> meaning "the first" or "the one" is universal property. There are reasons to think that *Ak-ad* means the first-born or Son of <term>Ad</term>. *Adon* was the first "Lord" of <term>Syria</term>. (See *Isis Unveiled* II., pp. 452, 453).
**Adam** (*Hebrew*). In the <term>Kabbalah</term>, <term>Adam</term> is the "only-begotten" and also means "red earth." (See "Adam-Adami" in the *Secret Doctrine* II., p. 452). It is almost identical with <term>Athamas</term> or <term>Thomas</term>, and is rendered into <term>Greek</term> by *Didumos*, the "twin"—<term>Adam</term>, "the first," in chapter 1 of <term>Genesis</term>, being shown as "male-female" <note>androgynous</note>.
**Adam Kadmon** (*Hebrew*). <term>Archetypal Man</term>; <term>Humanity</term>. The "Heavenly Man" not fallen into sin; <term>Kabbalists</term> refer it to the <term>Ten Sephiroth</term> on the plane of human perception. [w.w.w.]
In the <term>Kabbalah</term>, <term>Adam Kadmon</term> is the manifested <term>Logos</term> corresponding to our <term>Third Logos</term>; the <term>Unmanifested</term> being the first paradigmatic ideal Man, symbolizing the Universe in *abscondito* <note>in concealment</note>, or in its "privation" in the <term>Aristotelian</term> sense. The <term>First Logos</term> is the "Light of the World," the <term>Second</term> and the <term>Third</term> being its gradually deepening shadows.
**Adamic Earth** (*Alchemy*). Called the "true oil of gold," or the "primal element" in <term>Alchemy</term>. It is but one remove from the pure homogeneous element.
**Adbhuta Brâhmaṇa** (*Sanskrit*). The <term>Brâhmaṇa</term> of miracles; it treats of marvels, auguries, and various phenomena.
**Adbhuta Dharma** (*Sanskrit*). The "law" of things never heard before. A class of <term>Buddhist</term> works on miraculous or phenomenal events.

<term>Adept</term> (*Latin*). *Adeptus*, "He who has obtained." In Occultism, one who has reached the stage of Initiation and become a Master in the science of Esoteric philosophy.

<term>Adhi</term> (*Sanskrit*). Supreme, paramount.

<term>Adhishtânam</term> (*Sanskrit*). Basis; a principle in which some other principle inheres.
<term>Adhyâtmika duhkha</term> (*Sanskrit*). The first of the three kinds of pain; literally, "Evil proceeding from Self"—an evil induced or generated by the Self, or by man himself.

<term>Adi-bhûta</term> (*Sanskrit*). The first Being; also the primordial element. *Adbhuta* is a title of <term>Vishnu</term>, the "first Element" containing all elements, "the unfathomable deity."
<term>Adi-Buddha</term> (*Sanskrit*). The First and Supreme Buddha—not recognized in the Southern Church <note>Theravada Buddhism</note>. The Eternal Light.
<term>Adi-budhi</term> (*Sanskrit*). Primeval Intelligence or Wisdom; the eternal Budhi or Universal Mind. Used for *Divine Ideation*, with "Mahâbuddhi" being synonymous with <term>MAHÂT</term>.
<term>Adikrit</term> (*Sanskrit*). Literally, the "first produced" or made. The creative Force, which is eternal and uncreated, but manifests periodically. <term>Adi-nâtha</term> (*Sanskrit*). The "first Lord"—*Âdi* means "first" (masculine), and *nâtha* means "Lord."
<term>Adi-nidâna</term> (*Sanskrit*). First and Supreme Causality; from *Âdi* (the first) and *Nidâna* (the principal cause, or the chain of cause and effect).
<term>Adi-Sakti</term> (*Sanskrit*). Primeval, divine Force; the female creative power and aspect within and of every male god. The *Sakti* in the Hindu Pantheon is always the spouse of a god.
<term>Adi-Sanat</term> (*Sanskrit*). Literally, "First Ancient." The term corresponds to the Kabbalistic "Ancient of Days," since it is a title of <term>Brahmâ</term>—called in the *Zohar* the *Atteekah d'Atteekeen*, or "the Ancient of the Ancients," etc.
<term>Aditi</term> (*Sanskrit*). The Vedic name for the <term>Mûlaprakriti</term> of the Vedan-

THEOSOPHICAL

supreme Deity, Zeus, or Jupiter. With the moderns, Ether—for the meaning of which in physics and chemistry see *Webster’s Dictionary* or any other. In esotericism, <term>Æther</term> is the third principle of the Cosmic Septenary; the Earth being the lowest, then the Astral light, Ether, and <term>Akâsha</term> (phonetically *Akâsha*) the highest.

**Æthrobacy** (*Gr.*). Literally, walking on, or being lifted into the air with no visible agent at work; “levitation”. It may be conscious or unconscious; in the one case it is magic, in the other it is either disease or a power which requires a few words of elucidation. We know that the Earth is a magnetic body; in fact, as some scientists have found, and as Paracelsus affirmed some 300 years ago, it is one vast magnet. It is charged with one form of electricity—let us call it positive—which it evolves continuously by spontaneous action in its interior or center of motion. Human bodies, in common with all other forms of matter, are charged with the opposite form of electricity, the negative. That is to say, organic or inorganic bodies, if left to themselves, will constantly and involuntarily charge themselves with and evolve the form of electricity opposite to that of the earth itself. Now, what is weight? Simply the attraction of the earth. “Without the attraction of the earth you would have no weight”, says Professor Stewart; “and if you had an earth twice as heavy as this, you would have double the attraction”. How then, can we get rid of this attraction? According to the electrical law stated above, there is an attraction between our planet and the organisms upon it, which keeps them upon the surface of the globe. But the law of gravitation has been counteracted in many instances by the levitation of persons and inanimate objects. How do we account for this? The condition of our physical systems, say theurgic philosophers, is largely dependent upon the action of our will. If well-regulated, it can produce “miracles”; among others, a change of this electrical polarity from negative to positive; the man’s relations with the earth-magnet would then become repellent, and “gravity” for him would cease to exist. It would then be as natural for him to rush into the air until the repellent force had exhausted itself as it had been, before, for him to remain upon the ground. The altitude of his levitation would be measured by his ability, greater or less, to charge his body with positive electricity. Once this control over the physical forces is obtained, the alteration of his levity or gravity would be as easy as breathing. (See *Isis Unveiled*, Vol. I., page xxiii.)

**Afrits** (*Arab.*). A name for native spirits regarded as devils by Muslims. Elementals much dreaded in Egypt.

**Agapæ** (*Gr.*). Love Feasts; the early Christians kept such festivals as a token of sympathy, love, and mutual benevolence. It became necessary to abolish them as an institution because of great abuse; Paul, in his First Epistle to the Corinthians, complains of misconduct at the feasts of the Christians. <note>Initialed by W.W.W., referring to William Wynn Westcott</note>

# GLOSSARY

**Agastya (Sk.).** The name of a great <term>Rishi</term>, who is greatly revered in Southern India; he is the reputed author of hymns in the *Rig Veda* and a great hero in the *Râmâyana*. In Tamil literature, he is credited with being the first instructor of the Dravidians in science, religion, and philosophy. It is also the name of the star "Canopus."

**Agathodæmon (Gr.).** The beneficent, good Spirit, as contrasted with the bad one, <term>Kakodæmon</term>. The "Brazen Serpent" of the Bible is the former; the flying serpents of fire are an aspect of Kakodæmon. The <term>Ophites</term> called Agathodæmon the Logos and Divine Wisdom, which in the Bacchanalian Mysteries was represented by a serpent standing erect on a pole.

**Agathon (Gr.).** Plato’s Supreme Deity. Literally, "The Good," our <term>ALAYA</term>, or "Universal Soul."

**Aged (Kab.).** One of the <term>Kabbalistic</term> names for <term>Sephira</term>, also called the Crown, or *Kether*.

**Agla (Heb.).** This Kabbalistic word is a <term>talisman</term> composed of the initials of the four words "<term>Ateh Gibor Leolam Adonai</term>," meaning "You are mighty forever, O Lord." MacGregor Mathers explains it this way: "A, the first; A, the last; G, the trinity in unity; L, the completion of the great work." <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Agneyastra (Sk.).** The fiery missiles or weapons used by the gods in the exoteric *Purânas* and the *Mahâbhârata*; these are the magic weapons said to have been wielded by the fourth race (the Atlanteans). This "weapon of fire" was given by <term>Bharadwâja</term> to <term>Agnivesa</term>, the son of Agni, and by him to <term>Drona</term>, although the *Vishnu Purâna* contradicts this, stating that it was given by the sage <term>Aurva</term> to <term>King Sagara</term>, his <term>chela</term>. They are frequently mentioned in the *Mahâbhârata* and the *Râmâyana*.

**Agni (Sk.).** The God of Fire in the *Veda*; the oldest and most revered of gods in India. He is one of the three great deities—Agni, *Vâyu*, and *Sûrya*—and also all three, as he is the triple aspect of fire: in heaven as the Sun; in the atmosphere or air (*Vâyu*) as Lightning; and on earth as ordinary Fire. Agni belonged to the earlier Vedic *Trimûrti* before Brahmâ and Siva were introduced.

**Agni Bâhu (Sk.).** An ascetic son of <term>Manu Swâyambhuva</term>, the "Self-born."

**Agni Bhuvah (Sk.).** Literally, "born of fire"; the term is applied to the four races of <term>Kshatriyas</term> (the second or warrior caste) whose ancestors are said to have originated from fire. Agni Bhuvah is the son of Agni, the God of Fire; Agni Bhuvah is the same as <term>Karttîkeya</term>, the God of War. (See *Sec. Doct.*, Vol. II., p. 550.)

**Agni Dhâtu Samâdhi (Sk.).** A kind of contemplation in <term>Yoga</term> practice where *Kundalini* is raised to the extreme and infinity appears as a single sheet of fire. This is an ecstatic condition.

**Agni Hotri (Sk.).** The priests who served the Fire-God in Aryan antiquity. The term Agni Hotri denotes an oblation.

**Agni-ratha** (*Sk.*). A "Fiery Vehicle" literally. A kind of flying machine. Mentioned in ancient works of magic in India and in the epic poems.

**Agnishwâttas** (*Sk.*). A class of <term>Pitris</term>, the creators of the first ethereal race of men. They are our solar ancestors, as contrasted with the <term>Barhishads</term>, the "lunar" <term>Pitris</term> or ancestors, though they are explained differently in the <term>Purânas</term>.

**Agnoia** (*Gr.*). "Divested of reason," literally "irrationality," when speaking of the animal Soul. According to Plutarch, Pythagoras and Plato divided the human soul into two parts (the higher and lower <term>manas</term>)—the rational or <term>noëtic</term> and the irrational, or <term>agnoia</term>, sometimes written "annoia."

**Agnostic** (*Gr.*). A word claimed by Mr. Huxley to have been coined by him to indicate one who believes nothing that cannot be demonstrated by the senses. The later schools of Agnosticism provide more philosophical definitions of the term.

**Agra-Sandhânî** (*Sk.*). The "Assessors" or <term>Recorders</term> who, at the judgment of a disembodied Soul, read the record of its life in the heart of that "Soul." These are almost the same as the <term>Lipikas</term> of the *Secret Doctrine*. (See *Sec. Doct.*, Vol. I., p. 105.)

**Agruerus** A very ancient Phoenician god. The same as Saturn.

**Aham** (*Sk.*). "I"—the basis of <term>Ahankâra</term>, Self-hood.

**Ahan** (*Sk.*). "Day," the Body of Brahmâ, in the <term>Purânas</term>.

**Ahankâra** (*Sk.*). The conception of "I," Self-consciousness or Self-identity; the "I," the egotistical and <term>mâyâvic</term> principle in man, caused by our ignorance, which separates our "I" from the Universal ONE-SELF. Personality, Egoism.

**Aheie** (*Heb.*). Existence. He who exists; corresponds to <term>Kether</term> and <term>Macroprosopus</term>.

**Ah-hi** (Sensar), **Ahi** (*Sk.*), or Serpents. <term>Dhyân Chohans</term>. "Wise Serpents" or Dragons of Wisdom.

**Ahi** (*Sk.*). A serpent. A name of <term>Vritra</term>, the Vedic demon of drought.

**Ahti** (*Scand.*). The "Dragon" in the <term>Eddas</term>.

**Ahu** (*Scand.*). "One" and the first.

**Ahum** (*Zend*). The first three principles of septenary man in the <term>Avesta</term>; the gross living man and his vital and astral principles.

**Ahura** (*Zend*). The same as <term>Asura</term>, the holy, the Breath-like. Ahura Mazda, the <term>Ormuzd</term> of the Zoroastrians or Parsis, is the Lord who bestows light and intelligence, whose symbol is the Sun (See "Ahura Mazda"), and of whom Ahriman—a European form of "Angra Mainyu" (*q.v.*)—is the dark aspect.

Buddha as a supreme god (Isvara), instead of seeing the name as representing a principle or an abstract philosophical symbol.

**Aitareya** (*Sk*.). The name of an Aranyaka (Brahmana) and an Upanishad of the *Rig Veda*. Some of its portions are purely Vedantic.

**Aith-ur** (*Chald*.). Solar fire, divine Ether.

**Aja** (*Sk*.). “Unborn,” uncreated; an epithet belonging to many of the primordial gods, but especially to the first *Logos*—a radiation of the Absolute on the plane of illusion.

**Ajitas** (*Sk*.). One of the occult names of the twelve great gods incarnating in each Manvantara. Occultists identify them with the Kumaras. They are called Jnana (or Gnana) Devas. Also, a form of Vishnu in the second Manvantara. They are also called Jayas.

**Ajnana** (*Sk*.) or **Agyana** (*Bengali*). Non-knowledge; an absence of knowledge rather than “ignorance” as it is generally translated. An Ajnani means a “profane person.”

**Akar** (*Eg*.). The proper name of that division of the Ker-neter infernal regions which may be called Hell. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Akasa** (*Sk*.). The subtle, supersensory spiritual essence which pervades all space; the primordial substance erroneously identified with Ether. But it is to Ether what Spirit is to Matter, or *Atma* to *Kama rupa*. It is, in fact, the Universal Space in which the eternal Ideation of the Universe lies inherent in its ever-changing aspects on the planes of matter and objectivity, and from which radiates the *First Logos*, or expressed thought. This is why it is stated in the *Puranas* that Akasa has but one attribute—namely, sound—for sound is but the translated symbol of *Logos*—“Speech” in its mystic sense. In the same sacrifice (the *Jyotishtoma Agnishtoma*), it is called the “God Akasa.” In these sacrificial mysteries, Akasa is the all-directing and omnipotent Deva who plays the part of Sadasya, the superintendent over the magical effects of the religious performance, and it had its own appointed *Hotri* (priest) in ancient times who took its name. Akasa is the indispensable agent of every *Kritya* (magical performance), whether religious or profane. The expression “to stir up the Brahma” means to stir up the power which lies latent at the bottom of every magical operation, Vedic sacrifices being, in fact, nothing if not ceremonial magic. This power is Akasa—in another aspect, *Kundalini*—occult electricity, the alkahest of the alchemists in one sense, or the universal solvent, the same *anima mundi* on the higher plane as the astral light is on the lower. “At the moment of the sacrifice the priest becomes imbued with the spirit of Brahma and is, for the time being, Brahma himself.” (*Isis Unveiled*).

**Akbar**. The great Mughal Emperor of India, the famous patron of religions, arts, and sciences, and the most liberal of all the Muslim sovereigns. There has never been a more tolerant or enlightened ruler than the Emperor Akbar, either in India or in any other Muslim country.

**Akiba (Heb.).** The only one of the four *Tanaim* (initiated prophets) who, entering the *Garden of Delight* (of the occult sciences), succeeded in becoming initiated while all the others failed. (See the *Kabbalistic Rabbis*).

**Akshara (Sk.).** Supreme Deity; literally, “indestructible,” ever perfect.

**Akta (Sk.).** Anointed: a title of *Twashtri* or *Visvakarman*, the highest “Creator” and *Logos* in the *Rig-Veda*. He is called the “Father of the Gods” and “Father of the sacred Fire.” (See note page 101, Vol. II, *Sec. Doct.*)

**Akûpâra (Sk.).** The Tortoise, the symbolic turtle on which the earth is said to rest.

**Al** or **El (Heb.).** This deity-name is commonly translated as “God,” meaning mighty or supreme. The plural is *Elohim*, which is also translated in the Bible by the word “God” in the singular. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Al-ait (Phœn.).** The God of Fire, an ancient and very mystical name in Koptic Occultism.

**Alaparus (Chald.).** The second *divine* king of Babylonia who reigned for “three *Sari*.” According to *Berosus*, the first king of the *divine* Dynasty was *Alorus*. He was “the appointed Shepherd of the people” and reigned for ten *Sari* (or 36,000 years, a *Saros* being 3,600 years).

**Alaya (Sk.).** The Universal Soul (See *Secret Doctrine* Vol. I, pp. 47 et seq.). The name belongs to the Tibetan system of the contemplative *Mahâyâna School*. It is identical with *Akâsa* in its mystical sense, and with *Mûlaprakriti* in its essence, as it is the basis or root of all things.

**Alba Petra (Lat.).** The white stone of initiation. The “white carnelian” mentioned in St. John’s *Revelation*.

**Al-Chazari (Arab.).** A Prince-Philosopher and Occultist. (See *Book Al-Chazari*).

**Alchemists.** From *Al* and *Chemi* (fire), or the god and patriarch *Kham*; also the name of Egypt. The Rosicrucians of the Middle Ages, such as *Robertus de Fluctibus* (Robert Fludd), *Paracelsus*, *Thomas Vaughan* (Eugenius Philalethes), *Van Helmont*, and others, were all alchemists who sought for the *hidden spirit* in all inorganic matter. Some people—indeed, the great majority—have accused alchemists of charlatanry and false pretenses. Surely such men as *Roger Bacon*, *Agrippa*, *Henry Khunrath*, and the Arabian *Geber* (the first to introduce some of the secrets of chemistry into Europe) can hardly be treated as impostors—and certainly not as fools. Scientists who are reforming the science of physics based on the atomic theory of *Democritus*, as restated by *John Dalton*, conveniently forget that *Democritus* of Abdera was an alchemist. They also forget that a mind capable of penetrating so far into the secret operations of nature in one direction must have had good reasons to study and become a Hermetic philosopher. *Olaus Borrichius* says

**Alchemy**, in Arabic *Ul-Khemi*, is, as the name suggests, the chemistry of nature. *Ul-Khemi* or *Al-Kîmiâ*, however, is only an Arabianized word, taken from the Greek *χημεία* (*chemeia*) from *χυμός*—“juice”, sap extracted from a plant. Dr. Wynn Wescott says: "The earliest use of the actual term ‘alchemy’ is found in the works of Julius Firmicus Maternus, who lived in the days of Constantine the Great. The Imperial Library in Paris contains the oldest extant alchemic treatise known in Europe; it was written by Zosimus the Panopolite about 400 A.D. in the Greek language; the next oldest is by Æneas Gazeus, 480 A.D.” It deals with the finer forces of nature and the various conditions in which they are found to operate. Seeking under the veil of language, more or less artificial, to convey to the uninitiated as much of the *mysterium magnum* <note>great mystery</note> as is safe in the hands of a selfish world, the alchemist postulates as his first principle the existence of a certain Universal Solvent by which all composite bodies are resolved into the homogeneous substance from which they are evolved, which substance he calls pure gold, or *summa materia* <note>ultimate matter</note>. This solvent, also called *menstruum universale*, possesses the power of removing all the seeds of disease from the human body, of renewing youth and prolonging life. Such is the *lapis philosophorum* (philosopher’s stone). Alchemy first penetrated into Europe through Geber, the great Arabian sage and philosopher, in the eighth century of our era; but it was known and practiced long ages ago in China and in Egypt, numerous papyri on alchemy and other proofs of its being the favorite study of kings and priests having been exhumed and preserved under the generic name of Hermetic treatises. (See “Tabula Smaragdina”). Alchemy is studied under three distinct aspects, which admit of many different interpretations, namely: the Cosmic, Human, and Terrestrial. These three methods were typified under the three alchemical properties—sulphur, mercury, and salt. Different writers have stated that there are three, seven, ten, and twelve processes respectively; but they are all agreed that there is but one object in alchemy, which is to transmute gross metals into pure gold. What that gold, however, really is, very few people understand correctly. No doubt there is such a thing in nature as transmutation of the baser metals into the nobler, or gold. But this is only one aspect of alchemy, the terrestrial or purely material, for we sense logically the same process taking place in the bowels of the earth. Yet, besides and beyond this interpretation, there is in alchemy a symbolical meaning, purely psychic and spiritual. While the Kabbalist-Alchemist seeks for the realization of the former, the Occultist-Alchemist, spurning the gold of the mines, gives all his attention and directs his efforts only towards the transmutation of the baser *quaternary* <note>the four lower principles of man</note> into the divine upper *trinity* of man, which when finally blended are one. The spiritual, mental, psychic, and physical planes of human existence are in alchemy compared to the

Little or nothing is known by the world concerning the origin of this archaic branch of philosophy; but it is certain that it predates the construction of any known Zodiac and, as it deals with the personified forces of nature, probably also predates any of the world's mythologies. Nor is there any doubt that the true secret of transmutation (on the physical plane) was known in ancient times and lost before the dawn of the so-called historical period. Modern chemistry owes its best fundamental discoveries to alchemy, but regardless of the undeniable truism of the latter—that there is but one element in the universe—chemistry has classified metals as elements and is only now beginning to discover its gross mistake. **Alcyone** (*Gr.* <note>Greek</note>), or Halcyone, daughter of Aeolus and wife of Ceyx, who drowned while traveling to consult the oracle, upon which she threw herself into the sea. Consequently, both were changed, through the mercy of the gods, into kingfishers. The female is said to lay her eggs *on the sea and keep it calm* during the seven days before and seven days after the winter solstice. This has a very occult significance in ornithomancy <note>divination by the flight or songs of birds</note>.

**Alectromancy** (*Gr.* <note>Greek</note>). Divination by means of a rooster or other bird; a circle was drawn and divided into spaces, each assigned to a letter; corn was spread over these places, and a record was made of the successive lettered divisions from which the bird took grains of corn. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Alethæ** (*Phœn.* <note>Phoenician</note>). "Fire Worshippers" from *Al-ait*, the God of Fire. These are the same as the Kabiri or divine Titans. As the seven emanations of Agruerus (Saturn), they are connected with all the fire, solar, and "storm" gods (*Maruts*).

**Aletheia** (*Gr.* <note>Greek</note>). Truth; also Alethia, one of Apollo's nurses.

**Alexandrian School** (of Philosophers). This famous school arose in Alexandria (Egypt), which was for several centuries the great seat of learning and philosophy. It was famous for its library, which bears the name "Alexandrian," founded by Ptolemy Soter, who died in 283

The most celebrated schools of Gnostics had their origin in Alexandria. Philo Judaeus, Josephus, Iamblichus, Porphyry, Clement of Alexandria, Eratosthenes the astronomer, Hypatia the virgin philosopher, and countless other stars of the second magnitude, all belonged at various times to these great schools and helped to make Alexandria one of the most justly renowned seats of learning that the world has ever produced.

**Alhim** (*Hebrew* <note>Heb.</note>). See "Elohim".

**Alkahest** (*Arabic* <note>Arab.</note>). The universal solvent in Alchemy (see "**Alchemy**"); but in mysticism, the Higher Self, the union with which turns matter (lead) into gold and restores all compound things, such as the human body and its attributes, to the primeval essence.

**Almadel, the Book.** A treatise on Theurgy <note>Theurgia</note> or White Magic by an unknown medieval European author; it is frequently found in volumes of manuscripts <note>MSS.</note> called Keys of Solomon. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Almeh** (*Arabic* <note>Arab.</note>). Dancing girls; the same as the Indian *nautches*, the temple and public dancers.

**Alpha Polaris** (*Latin* <note>Lat.</note>). The same as *Dhruva*, the pole-star of 31,105 years ago.

**Alswider** (*Scandinavian* <note>Scand.</note>). "All-swift", the name of the horse of the moon, in the *Eddas*.

**Altruism** (*Latin* <note>Lat.</note>). From *alter* = other. A quality opposed to egoism. Actions tending to do good to others, regardless of self.

**Alze, Liber, de Lapide Philosophico.** An alchemical treatise by an unknown German author; dated 1677. It is to be found reprinted in the Hermetic Museum; in it is the well-known design of a man with legs extended and his body hidden by a seven-pointed star. Eliphaz Lévi has copied it. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Ama** (*Hebrew* <note>Heb.</note>), **Amia** (*Chaldean* <note>Chald.</note>). Mother. A title of Sephira Binah, whose "divine name is Jehovah" and who is called "Supernal Mother".

**Amânasa** (*Sanskrit* <note>Sk.</note>). The "Mindless", the early races of this planet; also certain Hindu gods.

**Amara-Kosha** (*Sanskrit* <note>Sk.</note>). The "immortal vocabulary". The oldest dictionary known in the world and the most perfect vocabulary of classical Sanskrit; by Amara Sinha, a sage of the second century.

**Ambâ (Sanskrit <note>Sk.</note>).** The name of the eldest of the seven *Pleiades*, the heavenly sisters who were each married to a *Rishi* belonging to the *Saptariksha*, or the seven *Rishis* of the constellation known as the *Great Bear*.

**Ambhâmsi (Sanskrit <note>Sk.</note>).** A name for the chief of the *Kumâras*, *Sanat-Sujâta*, signifying the "waters." This epithet will become more comprehensive when we remember that the later version of *Sanat-Sujâta* was *Michael*, the *Archangel*, who is called in the *Talmud* the "*Prince of Waters*," and in the *Roman Catholic Church* is regarded as the patron of gulfs and promontories. *Sanat-Sujâta* is the immaculate son of the immaculate mother (*Ambâ* or *Aditi*, chaos and space) or the "waters" of limitless space. (See *Secret Doctrine*, Vol. I., p. 460.)

**Amdo (Tibetan <note>Tib.</note>).** A sacred locality and the birthplace of *Tson-kha-pa*, the great *Tibetan* reformer and the founder of the *Gelukpa* (yellow caps), who is regarded as an *Avatar* of *Amita-buddha*.

**Amên.** In *Hebrew*, this is formed of the letters A M N = 1, 40, 50 = 91, and is thus a symbol for "*Jehovah Adonai*" = 10, 5, 6, 5 and 1, 4, 50, 10 = 91 together; it is one form of the *Hebrew* word for "truth." In common parlance, *Amen* is said to mean "so be it." <note>w.w.w.</note>
But, in esoteric terms, *Amen* means "the concealed." *Manetho Sebennites* says the word signifies that which is hidden, and we know through *Hecatæus* and others that the *Egyptians* used the word to call upon their great *God of Mystery*, *Ammon* (or "*Ammas*, the hidden god") to make himself visible and manifest to them. *Bonomi*, the famous *hieroglyphist*, quite appropriately calls his worshippers the "*Amen-oph*," and Mr. *Bonwick* quotes a writer who says: "*Ammon*, the hidden god, will remain hidden forever until revealed in human form; gods who are far away are useless." *Amen* is styled the "*Lord of the new-moon festival*." *Jehovah-Adonai* is a new form of the ram-headed god *Amoun* or *Ammon* <note>see entry</note> who was invoked by the *Egyptian* priests under the name of *Amen*.

**Amenti (Egyptian <note>Eg.</note>).** Esoterically and literally, the dwelling of the *God Amen*, or *Amoun*, or the "hidden," secret god. Exoterically, it is the kingdom of *Osiris* divided into fourteen parts, each of which was set aside for some purpose connected with the state of the deceased after death. Among other things, in one of these was the *Hall of Judgment*. It was the "*Land of the West*," the "*Secret Dwelling*," the *dark land*, and the "*doorless house*." But it was also *Ker-neter*, the "*abode of the gods*," and the "*land of ghosts*" like the "*Hades*" of the *Greeks* <note>see entry</note>. It was also the "*Good Father’s House*" (in which there are "many mansions"). The fourteen divisions comprised, among many others, *Aanroo* <note>see entry</note>, the hall of the *Two Truths*, the *Land of Bliss*, *Neter-xer* "the funeral (or burial) place," *Otamer-xer*, the "*Silence-loving Fields*," and also many other mystical halls and dwellings—one like the *Sheol* of the *Hebrews*, another like the *Devachan* of the *Occultists*, etc. Out of the fifteen gates of the abode of *Osiris*, there were two chief ones: the "gate of entrance" or *Rustu*, and the "gate of exit" (reincarnation), *Amh*.

But there was no room in Amenti to represent the orthodox Christian Hell. The worst place of all was the Hall of Eternal Sleep and Darkness. As Lepsius puts it, the deceased “sleep [therein] in incorruptible forms; they do not wake to see their brethren, they no longer recognize father and mother, and their hearts feel nothing toward their wife and children. This is the dwelling of the god *All-Dead*. . . . Each person trembles to pray to him, for he does not hear. Nobody can praise him, for he does not notice those who adore him. Neither does he notice any offering brought to him.” This god is the Karmic Decree; the land of Silence—the abode of those who die as absolute disbelievers, those dead from accidents before their allotted time, and finally the dead on the threshold of Avitchi. Avitchi is never in *Amenti* or any other subjective state, except in one case, but is located on this land of forced rebirth. These individuals did not stay very long even in their state of heavy sleep, oblivion, and darkness, but were carried more or less speedily toward Amh, the “exit gate.”

**Amesha Spentas** (*Zend*). Amshaspends. The six angels or divine Forces personified as gods who attend to Ahura Mazda, of whom he is the synthesis and the seventh. They are one of the prototypes of the Roman Catholic “Seven Spirits” or Angels with Michael as their chief, or the “Celestial Host”; the “Seven Angels of the Presence.” They are the Builders, the *Cosmocratores* of the Gnostics, and are identical to the Seven Prajâpatis, the Sephiroth, etc. (*see these terms*).

**Amitâbha.** The Chinese adaptation of the Sanskrit *Amrita Buddha*, or the “Immortal Enlightened One,” a name for Gautama Buddha. The name has variations such as Amita, Abida, Amitâya, etc., and is explained as meaning both “Boundless Age” and “Boundless Light.” The original conception of the ideal of an impersonal divine light has been personified over time.

**Ammon** (*Eg.*). One of the great gods of Egypt. Ammon or Amoun is much older than Amoun-Ra and is identified with Baal-Hammon, the Lord of Heaven. Amoun-Ra was Ra the Spiritual Sun, the “Sun of Righteousness,” etc., for—“the Lord God is a Sun.” He is the God of Mystery, and the hieroglyphics of his name are often reversed. Esoterically, he is Pan, All-Nature, and therefore the universe and the “Lord of Eternity.” As declared by an old inscription, Ra was “begotten by Neith but not engendered.” He is called the “self-begotten” Ra, and he created goodness from a glance of his fiery eye, just as Set-Typhon created evil from his own. As Ammon (also Amoun and Amen)-Ra, he is “Lord of the worlds enthroned on the Sun’s disk and appears in the abyss of heaven.” A very ancient hymn spells the name “*Amen-ra*” and hails him as the “Lord of the thrones of the earth. . . . Lord of Truth, father of the gods, maker of man, creator of the beasts, Lord of Existence, Enlightener of the Earth, sailing in heaven in tranquility. . . . All hearts are softened at beholding thee, sovereign of life, health, and strength! We worship thy spirit who alone made us,” etc., etc. (See Bonwick’s *Egyptian Belief*). **Ammonius Saccas**. A great and good philosopher who lived in Alexandria between the second and third centuries of our era, and who was the founder of the Neo-Platonic School of Philaletheians or “lovers of truth.” He was of humble birth and born to Christian parents, but gifted with such remarkable, almost divine goodness that he was called *Theodidaktos*, the “god-taught.” He honored what was good in Christianity, but broke with it and the churches very early, as he was unable to find in it any superiority over the older religions.

**Amrita** (*Sk.*). The ambrosial drink or food of the gods; the food that gives immortality. The elixir of life churned out of the ocean of milk in the Purânic allegory. An old Vedic term applied to the sacred Soma juice in the Temple Mysteries.

**Amûlam Mûlam** (*Sk.*). Literally, the “rootless root”; Mûlaprakriti of the Vedântins, the spiritual “root of nature.”

**Amun** (*Copt.*). The Egyptian god of wisdom, who had only Initiates or Hierophants serving him as priests.

**Anâ** (*Chald.*). The “invisible heaven” or Astral Light; the heavenly mother of the terrestrial sea, *Mar*, which is likely the origin of Anna, the mother of Mary.

**Anacalypsis** (*Gr.*), or an “Attempt to withdraw the veil of the Saitic Isis,” by Godfrey Higgins. This is a very valuable work, now obtainable only at extravagant prices; it treats the origin of all myths, religions, and mysteries, and displays an immense wealth of classical learning. <note>w.w.</note>

**Anagâmin** (*Sk.*). *Anagam*. One who is no longer to be reborn into the world of desire. This is the stage before becoming an Arhat and ready for Nirvana. It is the third of the four grades of holiness on the path to final Initiation.

**Anâhata Chakram** (*Sk.*). The seat or “wheel” of life; the heart, according to some commentators.

**Anâhata Shabda** (*Sk.*). The mystic voices and sounds heard by the Yogi at the beginning stage of his meditation. It is the third of the four states of sound, otherwise called Madhyamâ—the fourth state being when it is perceptible by the physical sense of hearing. The sound in its previous stages is not heard except by those who have developed their internal, highest spiritual senses. The four stages are called respectively, Parâ, Pashyantî, Madhyamâ, and Vaikharî.

**Anitia** (*Chald.*). A derivation from Anâ (see entry), a goddess identical to the Hindu Annapurna, one of the names of Kali—the female aspect of Siva—in her most favorable form.

**Analogeticists.** The disciples of Ammonius Saccas (*q.v.*), so-called because of their practice of interpreting all sacred legends, myths, and mysteries by a principle of analogy and correspondence. This principle is now found in the Kabbalistic system and is especially prominent in the Schools of Esoteric Philosophy in the East. (See "The Twelve Signs of the Zodiac" by T. Subba Row in *Five Years of Theosophy*.)

**Ânanda** (*Sk.*). Bliss, joy, intense happiness, or felicity. The name of the favorite disciple of Gautama, the Lord Buddha.

**Ânanda-Lahari** (*Sk.*). "The wave of joy"; a beautiful poem written by Sankarâchârya, which is a hymn to Pârvatî that is highly mystical and occult.

**Ânandamaya-Kosha** (*Sk.*). "The illusive Sheath of Bliss," meaning the mâyâvic or illusory form, the appearance of that which is formless. "Bliss," or the higher soul. The Vedantic name for one of the five Koshas or "principles" in man; it is identical with our Âtmâ-Buddhi or the Spiritual Soul.

**Ananga** (*Sk.*). The "Bodiless." A title for Kâma, the god of love.

**Ananta-Sesha** (*Sk.*). The Serpent of Eternity—the couch of Vishnu during Pralaya (*lit.*, "endless remainder").

**Anastasis** (*Gr.*). The continued existence of the soul.

**Anatu** (*Chald.*). The female aspect of Anu (*q.v.*). She represents the Earth and Depth, while her consort represents the Heaven and Height. She is the mother of the god Hea and produces heaven and earth. Astronomically, she is Ishtar, Venus, and the Ashtoreth of the Jews.

**Anaxagoras** (*Gr.*). A famous Ionian philosopher who lived around 500 B.C., studied philosophy under Anaximenes of Miletus, and settled in Athens during the time of Pericles. Socrates, Euripides, Archelaus, and other distinguished men and philosophers were among his disciples and pupils. He was a highly learned astronomer and was one of the first to explain publicly what Pythagoras had taught secretly—namely, the movements of the planets, the eclipses of the sun and moon, etc. It was he who taught the theory of Chaos, based on the principle that "nothing comes from nothing," and the theory of atoms as the underlying essence and substance of all bodies, being "of the same nature as the bodies they formed." He taught that these atoms were initially set in motion by *Nous* (Universal Intelligence, the Mahat of the Hindus), which *Nous* is an immaterial, eternal, spiritual entity. Through this combination, the world was formed: the dense material bodies sank down, while the ethereal atoms (or fiery ether) rose and spread into the upper celestial regions. Preceding modern science by over 2,000 years, he taught that the stars were made of the same material as our earth and that the sun was a glowing mass; that the moon was a dark, uninhabitable body receiving its light from the sun; and that comets were wandering stars or bodies. Beyond this science, he admitted that he was thoroughly convinced that the real existence of things perceived by our senses could not be demonstrably proved. He died in exile at Lampsacus at the age of seventy-two.

**Ancients, The.** A name given by Occultists to the seven creative Rays, born of Chaos, or the “Deep.”

**Anda-Katâha** (*Sk.*). The outer covering, or the “shell” of Brahmâ’s egg; the area within which our manifested universe is encompassed.

**Androgyne Goat** (of Mendes). See “Baphomet.”

**Androgyne Ray** (*Esot.*). The first differentiated ray; the Second Logos; Adam Kadmon in the *Kabbalah*; the “male and female created he them” of the first chapter of *Genesis*.

**Audumla** (*Scand.*). The symbol of nature in Norse mythology; the cow who licks the salt rock, from which the divine Buri is born, before man’s creation.

**Angâraka** (*Sk.*). Fire Star; the planet Mars; in Tibetan, *Mig-mar*.

**Augiras.** One of the Prajâpatis. A son of Daksha; a lawyer, etc.

**Angirasas** (*Sk.*). The generic name of several Purânic individuals and things; a class of Pitris, the ancestors of man; a river in Plaksha, one of the Sapta Dwîpas (*q.v.*).

**Angra Mainyus** (*Zend*). The Zoroastrian name for Ahriman; the evil spirit of destruction and opposition who (in the *Vendîdâd*, Fargard I) is said by Ahura Mazda to “counter-create by his witchcraft” every beautiful thing the God creates; for “Angra Mainyu is all death.”

**Anima Mundi** (*Lat.*). The “Soul of the World,” the same as the *Alaya* of the Northern Buddhists; the divine essence which permeates, animates, and informs all, from the smallest atom of matter to man and god. It is, in a sense, the “seven-skinned mother” of the stanzas in the *Secret Doctrine*, the essence of seven planes of sentience, consciousness, and differentiation, both moral and physical. In its highest aspect, it is *Nirvâna*; in its lowest, the Astral Light. It was considered feminine by the Gnostics, the early Christians, and the Nazarenes; it was bisexual with other sects, who considered it only in its four lower planes. It is of an igneous, ethereal nature in the objective world of form (and then called ether), and divine and spiritual in its three higher planes. When it is said that every human soul was born by detaching itself from the *Anima Mundi*, it means, esoterically, that our higher Egos are of an essence identical with It, which is a radiation of the ever-unknown Universal Absolute.

**Anjala** (*Sk.*). One of the personified powers which spring from Brahmâ’s body—the Prajâpatis.

**Anjana** (*Sk.*). A serpent, a son of Kasyapa Rishi.

**Annamaya Kosha** (*Sk.*). A Vedantic term. The same as *Sthûla Sharîra* or the physical body. It is the first “sheath” of the five sheaths accepted by the Vedantins, a sheath being the same as what is called a “principle” in Theosophy.

**Annapura** (*Sk.*). See “Anâ.”

There rose out of the Erythræan Sea on several occasions a semi-demon named Oannes or Annedotus who, although part animal, taught the Chaldeans useful arts and everything that could humanize them. (See Lenormant *Chaldean Magic*, p. 203, and also "Oannes.") [w.w.w.]

**Anoia** (*Gr.*). "Lack of understanding" or "folly." Anoia is the name given by Plato and others to the lower Manas when it is too closely allied with Kâma, which is irrational (*agnoia*). The Greek word *agnoia* is evidently a derivation from and cognate to the Sanskrit word *ajnâna* (phonetically, *agnyana*), meaning ignorance, irrationality, or absence of knowledge. (See "Agnoia" and "Agnostic.")

**Anouki** (*Ek.*). <note>Probably referring to the Egyptian goddess Anuket.</note> A form of Isis; the goddess of life, from which name comes the Hebrew *Ank*, life. (See "Anuki").

**Ansumat** (*Sk.*). A Puranic personage, the "nephew of 60,000 uncles" (King Sagara's sons), who were reduced to ashes by a single glance from Kapila Rishi's "Eye."

**Antahkarana** (*Sk.*), or Antaskarana. The term has various meanings, which differ with every school of philosophy and sect. Thus, Sankarâchârya renders the word as "understanding"; others as "the internal instrument, the Soul, formed by the thinking principle and egoism"; whereas the Occultists explain it as the path or bridge between the Higher and the Lower Manas—the divine *Ego* and the personal Soul of man. It serves as a medium of communication between the two and conveys from the Lower to the Higher Ego all those personal impressions and thoughts of men which can, by their nature, be assimilated and stored by the undying Entity, and thus be made immortal with it. These are the only elements of the evanescent *Personality* that survive death and time. It therefore stands to reason that only that which is noble, spiritual, and divine in man can testify in Eternity to his having lived.

**Anthesteria** (*Gr.*). The feast of Flowers (*Floralia*): during this festival the rite of Baptism or purification was performed in the Eleusinian Mysteries in the temple lakes, the Limnae, when the candidates (*Mystæ*) were made to pass through the "narrow gate" of Dionysus to emerge as full Initiates.

**Anthropology.** The Science of man; it embraces, among other things:—*Physiology*, or that branch of natural science which discloses the mysteries of the organs and their functions in men, animals, and plants; and also—and especially—*Psychology*, or the great (and in our days, too much neglected) science of the soul, both as an entity distinct from the spirit and in its relation to the spirit and body. In modern science, psychology deals only or principally with conditions of the nervous system and almost absolutely ignores the psychical essence and nature. Physicians call the science of insanity psychology and name the chair of lunacy in medical colleges by that designation. (*Isis Unveiled.*)

**Anu** *(Sk.).* An "atom," a title of Brahma, who is said to be an atom just as the infinite universe is. This is a hint at the pantheistic nature of the god.
**Anu** *(Chald.).* One of the highest Babylonian deities, "King of Angels and Spirits, Lord of the city of Erech." He is the Ruler and God of Heaven and Earth. His symbol is a star and a kind of Maltese cross—emblems of divinity and sovereignty. He is an abstract divinity supposed to animate the whole expanse of ethereal space or heaven, while his "wife" animates the more material planes. Both are the types of the Ouranos and Gaia of Hesiod. They sprang from the original Chaos. All his titles and attributes are descriptive and indicate health, physical and moral purity, antiquity, and holiness. Anu was the earliest god of the city of Erech. One of his sons was *Bil* or *Vil-Kan*, the god of fire, various metals, and weapons. George Smith very appropriately sees in this deity a close connection with a kind of crossbreed between "the biblical Tubal Cain and the classical Vulcan" . . . who is also considered to be "the most potent deity in relation to witchcraft and spells generally."
**Anubis** *(Gr.).* The dog-headed god, identical in a certain aspect with Horus. He is preeminently the god who deals with the disembodied or the resurrected in post-mortem life. *Anepou* is his Egyptian name. He is a psychopompic deity, "the Lord of the Silent Land of the West, the land of the dead, the preparer of the way to the other world," to whom the dead were entrusted to be led by him to Osiris, the Judge. In short, he is the "embalmer" and the "guardian of the dead." He is one of the oldest deities in Egypt, Mariette Bey having found the image of this deity in tombs of the Third Dynasty.
**Anugîtâ** *(Sk.).* One of the *Upanishads*. A very occult treatise. (See *The Sacred Books of the East*).
**Anugraha** *(Sk.).* The eighth creation in the *Vishnu Purana*.
**Anuki** *(Eg.).* See "*Anouki*" above. "The word *Ank* in Hebrew means 'my life,' my being, which is the personal pronoun *Anochi*, from the name of the Egyptian goddess *Anouki*," says the author of the *Hebrew Mystery*, or the *Source of Measures*.
**Anumati** *(Sk.).* The moon at the full; when from a god—Soma—she becomes a goddess.
**Anumitis** *(Sk.).* Inference or deduction in philosophy.
**Anunnaki** *(Chald.).* Angels or Spirits of the Earth; also terrestrial Elementals.
**Anunit** *(Chald.).* The goddess of Akkad; *Lucifer*, the morning star. Venus as the evening star was Ishtar of Erech.

"parentless", "self-existing", born without any parents or progenitors. A term applied to certain self-created gods and the Dhyâni Buddhas.
**Anuttara** (*Sk.*). Unrivaled, peerless. Thus *Anuttara Bodhi* means "unexcelled or unrivaled intelligence"; *Anuttara Dharma*, unrivaled law or religion, etc.
**Anyâmsam Aniyâsâm** (*Sk.*). *Ano-ranîyânsam* (in the *Bhagavad-gîtâ*). Literally, "the most atomic of the atomic; the smallest of the small." Applied to the universal deity, whose essence is everywhere.
**Aour** (*Chald.*). The synthesis of the two aspects of astro-etheric light: the *od*—the life-giving—and the *ob*—the death-giving light.
**Apâm Napât** (*Zend*). A mysterious being, corresponding to the *Fohat* of the occultists. It is both a Vedic and an Avestan name. Literally, the name means the "Son of the Waters" (of space, i.e., Ether), for in the *Avesta*, *Apâm Napât* stands between the *fire-yazatas* and the *water-yazatas* (See *Secret Doctrine*, Vol. II, p. 400, note).
**Apâna** (*Sk.*). "Inhalation breath"; a practice in *Yoga*. *Prâna* and *apâna* are the "exhalation" and the "inhalation" breaths. It is called the "vital wind" in the *Anugîtâ*.
**Apap** (*Eg.*), in Greek *Apophis*. The symbolic Serpent of Evil. The *Solar Boat* and the *Sun* are the great slayers of *Apap* in the *Book of the Dead*. It is Typhon, who, having killed Osiris, incarnates in *Apap* to seek to kill Horus. Like *Taoër* (or *Ta-ap-oer*), the female aspect of Typhon, *Apap* is called "the devourer of souls." This is true, since *Apap* symbolizes the animal body as matter left soulless and to itself. As Osiris is, like all other solar gods, a type of the Higher Ego (*Christos*), Horus (his son) is the lower *Manas* or the personal Ego. On many monuments, one can see Horus killing *Apap*, helped by a number of dog-headed gods armed with crosses and spears. An Orientalist says: "The God Horus, standing as conqueror upon the Serpent of Evil, may be considered the earliest form of our well-known group of Saint George (who is Michael) and the Dragon, or holiness trampling down sin." Draconianism did not die with the ancient religions but has passed entirely into the latest form of Christian worship.
**Aparinâmin** (*Sk.*). The Immutable and Unchangeable; the opposite of *Parinâmin*, which is subject to modification, differentiation, or decay.
**Aparoksha** (*Sk.*). Direct perception.
**Apâva** (*Sk.*). Literally, "He who sports in the Water." Another aspect of *Nârâyana* or *Vishnu* and of *Brahmâ* combined; for *Âpava*, like the latter, divides himself into two parts, male and female, and creates *Virâj*, who creates *Manu*. The name is explained and interpreted in various ways in Brahmanical literature.
**Apavarga** (*Sk.*). Emancipation from repeated births.

incarnate in the sacred white Bull. Apis was the bull-god that—on reaching the age of twenty-eight, the age when Osiris was killed by Typhon—was put to death with great ceremony. It was not the Bull that was worshipped but the Osiridian symbol; just as Christians now kneel before the Lamb, the symbol of Jesus Christ, in their churches.

**Apocrypha** (*Gr.*). Very erroneously explained and accepted as doubtful or spurious. The word simply means secret, esoteric, or hidden.

**Apollo Belvidere.** Of all the ancient statues of Apollo—the son of Jupiter and Latona, called Phoebus, Helios, the radiant one, and the Sun—the best and most perfect is the one known by this name, which is in the Belvidere gallery of the Vatican at Rome. It is called the *Pythian Apollo*, as the god is represented at the moment of his victory over the serpent Python. The statue was found in the ruins of Antium in 1503.

**Apollonius of Tyana** (*Gr.*). A wonderful philosopher born in Cappadocia about the beginning of the first century; an ardent Pythagorean who studied the Phoenician sciences under Euthydemus, and Pythagorean philosophy and other studies under Euxenus of Heraclea. According to the tenets of this school, he remained a vegetarian for the whole of his long life, fed only on fruit and herbs, drank no wine, wore garments made only of plant fibers, walked barefooted, and let his hair grow to its full length, as did all the Initiates before and after him. He was initiated by the priests of the temple of Aesculapius (Asclepios) at Aegae and learned many of the "miracles" for healing the sick performed by the god of medicine. Having prepared himself for a higher initiation by a silence of five years and by travel—visiting Antioch, Ephesus, Pamphylia, and other parts—he journeyed via Babylon to India, after all his close disciples had abandoned him, as they feared to go to the "land of enchantments." A casual disciple named Damis, however, whom he met on his way, accompanied him in his travels. At Babylon, he was initiated by the Chaldeans and Magi, according to Damis, whose narrative was copied by someone named Philostratus a hundred years later. After his return from India, he showed himself to be a true Initiate, in that the plagues and earthquakes, deaths of kings, and other events which he prophesied occurred as predicted. At Lesbos, the priests of Orpheus, being jealous of him, refused to initiate him into their particular mysteries, though they did so several years later. He preached the purest and noblest ethics to the people of Athens and other cities, and the phenomena he produced were as wonderful as they were numerous and well-attested. "How is it," inquires Justin Martyr in dismay—"how is it that the talismans (*telesmata*) of Apollonius have power? For they prevent, as we see, the fury of the waves, the violence of the winds, and the attacks of wild beasts; and while our Lord's miracles are preserved by tradition alone, those of Apollonius are most numerous and actually demonstrated by present facts?" . . . . (*Quest, XXIV*). But an answer is easily found to this in the fact that after crossing the Hindu Kush, Apollonius had

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

He had been directed by a king to the abode of the *Sages*, where they may still reside to this day, and by whom he was taught unsurpassed knowledge. His dialogues with the Corinthian Menippus indeed give us the esoteric catechism and disclose (when understood) many an important mystery of nature. Apollonius was the friend, correspondent, and guest of kings and queens, and no marvelous or “magic” powers are better attested than his. At the end of his long and wonderful life, he opened an esoteric school at Ephesus and died at the age of almost one hundred years.

**Aporrheta** (*Gr.*). Secret instructions upon esoteric subjects given during the Egyptian and Grecian Mysteries.

**Apsaras** (*Sk.*). An Undine or Water-Nymph from the Paradise or Heaven of Indra. In popular belief, the Apsarases are the “wives of the gods” and called *Surangânâs*, and by a less honorable term *Sumad-âtmajâs* or the “daughters of pleasure”; for it is told in fables about them that when they appeared at the churning of the Ocean, neither the Gods (Suras) nor the Demons (Asuras) would take them as legitimate wives. Urvasi and several others of them are mentioned in the *Vedas*. In Occultism, they are certain “sleep-producing” aquatic plants and inferior forces of nature.

**Ar-Abu Nasr-al-Farabi**, called in Latin Alpharabius, a Persian and the greatest Aristotelian philosopher of the age. He was born in 950 A.D. and is reported to have been murdered in 1047. He was an Hermetic philosopher and possessed the power of hypnotizing through music, making those who heard him play the lute laugh, weep, dance, and do whatever he liked. Some of his works on Hermetic philosophy may be found in the Library of Leyden.

**Arahat** (*Sk.*). Also pronounced and written Arhat, Arhan, Rahat, etc., “the worthy one”; literally, “deserving divine honors.” This was the name first given to the Jain and subsequently to the Buddhist holy men initiated into the esoteric mysteries. The Arhat is one who has entered the best and highest path and is thus emancipated from rebirth.

**Arani** (*Sk.*). The “female Arani” is a name of the Vedic Aditi (esoterically, the womb of the world). *Arani* is a *Swastika*, a disc-like wooden vehicle in which the Brahmins generated fire by friction with *pramantha*, a stick, which is the symbol of the male generator. This is a mystic ceremony with a world of secret meaning in it and is very sacred, though it has been perverted into phallic significance by the materialism of the age.

**Aranyaka** (*Sk.*). Holy hermits or sages who dwelt in the forests of ancient India. Also a portion of the *Vedas* containing Upanishads, etc.

**Araritha** (*Heb.*). A very famous seven-lettered Kabbalistic wonder-word; its numeration is 813; its letters are collected by Notaricon from the sentence “one principle of his unity, one beginning of his individuality, his change is unity.” <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Arasa Maram** (*Sk.*). The Hindu sacred tree of knowledge. In occult philosophy, it is a mystic word.

**Arba-il** (*Chaldean*). The Four Great Gods. *Arba* is Aramaic for four, and *il* is the same as Al or El. Three male deities and a female who is virginal yet reproductive form a very common ideal of the Godhead. [w.w.w]

**Archangel** (*Greek*). Highest supreme angel. From the Greek *arch*, “chief” or “primordial,” and *angelos*, “messenger.”

**Archæus** (*Greek*). “The Ancient.” Used for the oldest manifested deity; a term employed in the Kabbalah; “archaic,” old, ancient.

**Archobiosis** (*Greek*). Primeval beginning of life.

**Archetypal Universe** (*Kabbalistic*). The ideal universe upon which the objective world was built. [w.w.w]

**Archons** (*Greek*). In secular and biblical language, “rulers” and princes; in Occultism, primordial planetary spirits.

**Archontes** (*Greek*). The archangels after becoming *Ferouers* (see entry) or their own shadows, having a mission on earth; a mystic ubiquity, implying a double life; a kind of hypostatic action—one of purity in a higher region, the other of terrestrial activity exercised on our plane. (See *Iamblichus, De Mysteriis* II, Chapter 3.)

**Ardath** (*Hebrew*). This word occurs in the Second Book of Esdras, 9:26. The name has been given to one of the recent “occult novels” where much interest is excited by the visit of the hero to a field in the Holy Land so named; magical properties are attributed to it. In the Book of Esdras, the prophet is sent to this field called Ardath “where no house is built” and bidden to “eat there *only* the flowers of the field, taste no flesh, drink no wine, and pray to the highest continually, and then will I come and talk with you.” [w.w.w]

**Ardha-Nâri** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, “half-woman.” Siva represented as androgynous, as half male and half female—a type of combined male and female energies. (See the occult diagram in *Isis Unveiled*, Vol. II.)

**Ardhanârîswara** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, “the bisexual lord.” Esoterically, the unpolarized states of cosmic energy symbolized by the Kabbalistic Sephira, Adam Kadmon, etc.

**Ares.** The Greek name for Mars, god of war; also a term used by Paracelsus for the differentiated Force in the Cosmos.

**Argha** (*Chaldean*). The ark, the womb of Nature; the crescent moon and a life-saving ship; also a cup for offerings, a vessel used for religious ceremonies.

**Arghyanâth** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, “lord of libations.”

**Arian.** A follower of Arius, a presbyter of the Church in Alexandria in the fourth century. One who holds that Christ is a created and human being, inferior to God the Father, though a grand and noble man, a true adept versed in all the divine mysteries.

**Aristobulus** (*Greek*). An Alexandrian writer, and an obscure phi-
