**Arithmomancy** (*Greek*). The science of correspondences between gods, men, and numbers, as taught by Pythagoras. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Arjuna** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, the “white.” The third of the five Pandu brothers, or the reputed sons of Indra (esoterically the same as Orpheus). A disciple of Krishna, who visited him and married Subhadrâ, Krishna’s sister, besides many other wives, according to the allegory. During the fratricidal war between the *Kauravas* and the *Pandavas*, Krishna instructed him in the highest philosophy while serving as his charioteer. (See *Bhagavad Gita*.)

**Ark of Isis.** At the great Egyptian annual ceremony, which took place in the month of Athyr, the boat of Isis was carried in procession by the priests, and *Collyrian* cakes or buns, marked with the sign of the cross (*Tat*), were eaten. This was in commemoration of the weeping of Isis for the loss of Osiris, the Athyr festival being very impressive. “Plato refers to the melodies on the occasion as being very ancient,” writes Mr. Bonwick (*Egyptian Belief and Modern Thought*). “The *Miserere* in Rome has been said to be similar to its melancholy cadence and to be derived from it. Weeping, veiled virgins followed the ark. The *Norns*, or veiled virgins, wept also for the loss of our Saxon forefathers’ god, the ill-fated but good *Baldur*.”

**Ark of the Covenant.** Every ark-shrine, whether with the Egyptians, Hindus, Chaldeans, or Mexicans, was a phallic shrine, the symbol of the *yoni* or womb of nature. The *seket* of the Egyptians—the ark, or sacred chest—stood on the *ara*, its pedestal. The ark of Osiris, with the sacred relics of the god, was “of the same size as the Jewish ark,” says S. Sharpe, the Egyptologist; it was carried by priests with staves passed through its rings in sacred procession, just like the ark around which David, the King of Israel, danced. Mexican gods also had their arks. Diana, Ceres, and other goddesses as well as gods had theirs. The ark was a boat—“a vehicle” in every case. “Thebes had a sacred ark 300 cubits long,” and “the word *Thebes* is said to mean ark in Hebrew,” which is but a natural recognition of the place to which the chosen people are indebted for their ark. Moreover, as Bauer writes, “the Cherub was not first used by Moses.” The winged Isis was the cherub or *Arieh* in Egypt, centuries before the arrival there of even Abram or Sarai. “The external likeness of some of the Egyptian arks, surmounted by their two winged human figures, to the ark of the covenant, has often been noticed.” (*Bible Educator.*) And not only the “external” but the internal “likeness” and sameness are now known to all. The arks, whether of the covenant or of honest, straightforward, Pagan symbolism, had originally and now have one and the same meaning. The chosen people appropriated the idea and forgot to acknowledge its source. It is the same as in the case of the “Urim” and “Thummim”

**Arka** (*Sanskrit*). The Sun.

**Arkites.** The ancient priests who were assigned to the Ark, whether of Isis or the Hindu *Argua*, and who were seven in number, like the priests of the Egyptian *Tat* or any other cruciform symbol of the *three* and the *four*, the combination of which gives a male-female number. The *Argha* (or ark) was the fourfold female principle, and the flame burning over it the triple *lingam*.

**Aroueris** (*Greek*). The god Harsiesi, who was the elder Horus. He had a temple at Ambos. If we bear in mind the definition of the chief Egyptian gods by Plutarch, these myths will become more comprehensible; as he well says: "Osiris represents the beginning and principle; Isis, that which receives; and Horus, the compound of both. Horus, engendered between them, is not eternal nor incorruptible, but, being always in generation, he endeavors through the vicissitudes of imitations and by periodic passion (yearly re-awakening to life) to continue always young, as if he should never die." Thus, since Horus is the personified physical world, Aroueris, or the "elder Horus," is the ideal Universe; and this accounts for the saying that "he was begotten by Osiris and Isis when these were still in the bosom of their mother"—Space. There is indeed a good deal of mystery about this god, but the meaning of the symbol becomes clear once one has the key to it.

**Artephius.** A great Hermetic philosopher, whose true name was never known and whose works are without dates, though it is known that he wrote his *Secret Book* in the 12th century. Legend has it that he was one thousand years old at that time. There is a book on dreams by him in the possession of an Alchemist, now in Baghdad, in which he reveals the secret of seeing the past, the present, and the future in sleep, and of remembering the things seen. There are only two copies of this manuscript in existence. The book on *Dreams* by the Jew Solomon Almulus, published in Hebrew at Amsterdam in 1642, has a few reminiscences from the earlier work of Artephius.

**Artes** (*Egyptian*). The Earth; the Egyptian god Mars.

**Artufas.** A generic name in South America and the islands for temples of *nagalism* or serpent worship.

**Arundhatî** (*Sanskrit*). The "Morning Star"; Lucifer-Venus.

**Arûpa** (*Sanskrit*). "Bodiless," formless, as opposed to *rupa*, "body," or form.

**Arvâksrotas** (*Sk.*). The seventh creation, that of man, in the *Vishnu Purâna*.

**Arwaker** (*Scand.*). Literally, “early waker.” The horse of the Sun's chariot driven by the maiden Sol, in the *Eddas*.

**Ârya** (*Sk.*). Literally, “the holy”; originally the title of Rishis—those who had mastered the “*Âryasatyâni*” (which see) and entered the *Âryamârga* path to Nirvâna or Moksha, the great “fourfold” path. However, the name has now become an epithet for a race, and our Orientalists, depriving the Hindu Brahmans of their birthright, have labeled all Europeans as Aryans. In esotericism, because the four paths or stages can only be entered through great spiritual development and “growth in holiness,” they are called the “four fruits.” The degrees of Arhatship—called respectively Srotâpatti, Sakridâgâmin, Anâgâmin, and Arhat, or the four classes of Âryas—correspond to these four paths and truths.

**Ârya Bhata** (*Sk.*). The earliest Hindu algebraist and astronomer, with the exception of Asura Maya (which see); the author of a work called *Ârya Siddhânta*, a system of Astronomy.

**Ârya-Dâsa** (*Sk.*). Literally, “Holy Teacher.” A great sage and Arhat of the Mahâsamghika school.

**Aryahata** (*Sk.*). The “Path of Arhatship,” or of holiness.

**Âryasangha** (*Sk.*). The Founder of the first Yogâchârya School. This Arhat, a direct disciple of Gautama the Buddha, is most inexplicably confused and mixed up with a person of the same name who is said to have lived in Ayôdhya (Oude) about the fifth or sixth century of our era and who taught Tântrika worship in addition to the Yogâchârya system. Those who sought to make it popular claimed that he was the same Âryasangha who had been a follower of Sâkyamuni, and that he was 1,000 years old. Internal evidence alone is sufficient to show that the works written by him and translated about the year 600 of our era—works full of Tantra worship, ritualism, and tenets followed today extensively by the “red-cap” sects in Sikhim, Bhûtan, and Little Tibet—cannot be the same as the lofty system of the early Yogâchârya school of pure Buddhism, which is neither northern nor southern, but absolutely esoteric. Although none of the genuine Yogâchârya books (the *Narjol chodpa*) have ever been made public or available for sale, one still finds much from the older system in the *Yogâchârya Bhûmi Shâstra* of the *pseudo*-Âryasangha, into whose tenets he may have been initiated. It is, however, so mixed with Shaivism and Tântrika magic and superstitions that the work defeats its own purpose, despite its remarkable dialectical subtlety. How unreliable the conclusions are that our Orientalists reach, and how contradictory the dates assigned by them, can be seen in the present case. While Csoma de Körös (who, incidentally, never became acquainted with the Gelukpa (yellow-caps), but obtained all his information from “red-cap” lamas of the borderland) places the *pseudo*-Âryasangha in the seventh century of our era; Was-

**Aryasatyâni** (*Sk.*). The Four Truths or the four dogmas, which are (1) *Dukha*, or the fact that misery and pain are the unavoidable concomitants of sentient (esoterically physical) existence; (2) *Samudaya*, the truth that suffering is intensified by human passions; (3) *Nirôdha*, the fact that the crushing out and extinction of all such feelings is possible for a man "on the path"; (4) *Mârga*, the narrow way, or the path which leads to such a blessed result.

**Aryavarta** (*Sk.*). The "land of the Aryas," or India. The ancient name for Northern India, where the Brahmanical invaders ("from the Oxus," say the Orientalists) first settled. It is incorrect to apply this name to the whole of India, since Manu gives the name "the land of the Aryas" only to "the region between the Himalaya and the Vindhya ranges, from the eastern to the western sea."

**Asakrit Samâdhi** (*Sk.*). A certain degree of ecstatic contemplation. A stage in *Samâdhi*.

**Âsana** (*Sk.*). The third stage of *Hatha Yoga*, one of the prescribed postures of meditation.

**Asat** (*Sk.*). A philosophical term meaning "non-be-ness," or rather *non-being*. The "incomprehensible nothingness." *Sat*, the immutable, eternal, ever-present, and the one real "Be-ness" (not Being), is spoken of as being "born of *Asat*, and *Asat* begotten by *Sat*." The unreal, or <term>Prakriti</term>: objective nature regarded as an illusion. Nature, or the illusory shadow of its one true essence.

**Asathor** (*Scand.*). The same as <term>Thor</term>. The god of storms and thunder, a hero who receives *Miölnir*, the "storm-hammer," from its makers, the dwarfs. With it, he conquers *Alvis* in a "battle of words"; shatters the head of the giant *Hrungir*; punishes *Loki* for his magic; destroys the whole race of giants in *Thrymheim*; and, as a good and benevolent god, sets up landmarks with it, sanctifies marriage bonds, blesses law and order, and performs every good and awe-inspiring feat with its help. A god in the *Eddas* who is almost as great as <term>Odin</term>. (See "Miölnir" and "Thor's Hammer.")

**Asava Samkhaya** (*Pali*). The “end of the stream,” one of the six “*Abhijnâs*” (*q.v.*). A phenomenal knowledge of the end of the stream of life and the series of rebirths.

**Asburj**. One of the legendary peaks in the Tenerife range. A great mountain in the traditions of Iran that corresponds in its allegorical meaning to the *World-mountain*, *Meru*. Asburj is the mountain “at the foot of which the sun sets.”

**Asch Metzareph** (*Heb*.). The Cleansing Fire, a *Kabbalistic* treatise dealing with *alchemy* and the relationship between metals and planets. [w.w.w.]

**Ases** (*Scand*.). The creators of the *dwarfs* and *elves*, the *elementals* below men, in the *Norse* poems. They are the offspring of *Odin*; the same as the *Æsir*.

**Asgard** (*Scand*.). The kingdom and the habitat of the *Norse gods*, the *Scandinavian Olympus*; situated “higher than the Home of the *Light-Elves*,” but on the same plane as *Jotunheim*, the home of the *Jotuns*, the wicked giants skilled in magic with whom the gods are at eternal war. It is evident that the gods of *Asgard* are the same as the *Indian Suras* (gods) and the *Jotuns* are the *Asuras*, both representing the conflicting powers of nature—beneficial and harmful. They are also the prototypes of the *Greek gods* and the *Titans*.

**Ash** (*Heb*.). Fire, whether physical or symbolic; also written in *English* as *As*, *Aish*, and *Esch*.

**Ashen and Langhan** (*Kolarian*). Certain ceremonies for casting out evil spirits, similar to the practice of exorcism among *Christians*, used by the *Kolarian tribes* in *India*.

**Asherah** (*Heb*.). A word that occurs in the *Old Testament* and is commonly translated as “*groves*,” referring to idolatrous worship, but it likely referred to ceremonies of sexual depravity; it is a feminine noun. [w.w.w.]

**Ashmog** (*Zend*). The *Dragon* or *Serpent*, a monster with a camel’s neck in the *Avesta*; a kind of allegorical *Satan* who, after the *Fall*, “lost its nature and its name.” Called in the old *Hebrew* (*Kabbalistic*) texts the “*flying camel*”; evidently a recollection or tradition in both cases of prehistoric or *antediluvian monsters*, half-bird, half-reptile.

**Ashtadisa** (*Sk*.). The eight-faced space. An imaginary division of space represented as an *octagon* and at other times as a *dodecahedron*.

**Ashta Siddhis** (*Sk*.). The eight accomplishments in the practice of *Hatha Yoga*.

**Ashtar Vidyâ** (*Sk*.). The most ancient of the *Hindu* works on *Magic*. Although there is a claim that the entire work is in the hands of some *occultists*, *Orientalists* consider it lost. A very few fragments of it still exist, and even these are heavily distorted.

**Asiras** (*Sk.*). Elementals without heads; *literally*, “headless”; used also to refer to the first two human races.

**Asita** (*Sk.*). A proper name; a son of Bharata; a Rishi and a Sage.

**Aski-kataski-haix-tetrax-damnameneus-aision.** These mystic words, which Athanasius Kircher tells us meant “Darkness, Light, Earth, Sun, and Truth,” were, says Hesychius, engraved upon the zone or belt of the Diana of Ephesus. **Asmoneans.** Priest-kings of Israel whose dynasty reigned over the Jews for 126 years. They issued the Canon of the Mosaic Testament in contrast to the “Apocrypha” (*q.v.*) or Secret Books of the Alexandrian Jews and the Kabbalists, and they maintained the literal meaning of the former. Until the time of John Hyrcanus, they were Hasideans (*Chasidim*) and Pharisees; but later they became Sadducees or Zadokites, who were assertors of priestly rule as distinguished from Rabbinical rule.

**Asoka** (*Sk.*). A celebrated Indian king of the Maurya dynasty which reigned at Magadha. There were in reality two Asokas, according to the chronicles of Northern Buddhism, though the first Asoka—the grandfather of the second, named by Prof. Max Müller the “Constantine of India”—was better known by his name Chandragupta. It is the former who was called Piadasi (Pali) “the beautiful,” and *Devânam-piya* “the beloved of the gods,” and also *Kâlâsoka*; while the name of his grandson was *Dharmâsôkâ*—the Asoka of the good law—on account of his devotion to Buddhism. Moreover, according to the same source, the second Asoka had never followed the Brahmanical faith, but was a Buddhist by birth. It was his grandfather who had been first converted to the new faith, after which he had a number of edicts inscribed on pillars and rocks, a custom also followed by his grandson. Asoka was the most zealous supporter of Buddhism; he maintained sixty to seventy thousand monks and priests in his palace, erected 84,000 topes and stupas throughout India, reigned thirty-six years, and sent missions to Ceylon and throughout the world. The inscriptions of various edicts published by him display the most noble ethical sentiments, especially the edict at Allahabad, on the so-called "Asoka’s column" in the Fort. The sentiments are lofty and poetic, breathing tenderness for animals as well as men, and a lofty view of a king’s mission regarding his people—a view that might be followed with great success in the present age of cruel wars and barbarous vivisection.

**Asomatous** (*Gr.*). *Lit.*, without a material body, incorporeal; used for celestial Beings and Angels.

**Asrama** (*Sk.*). A sacred building, a monastery or hermitage for ascetic purposes. Every sect in India has its *Ashrams*.

**Assassins.** A masonic and mystic order founded by Hassan Sabah in Persia in the eleventh century. The word is a European corruption of "Hassan," which forms the chief part of the name. They were simply *Sufis* and, according to tradition, were known to use *hashish* to bring about celestial visions. As shown by our late brother Kenneth Mackenzie, "they were teachers of the secret doctrines of Islamism; they encouraged mathematics and philosophy, and produced many valuable works. The chief of the Order was called Sheik-el-Jebel, translated as the '*Old Man of the Mountains*,' and, as their Grand Master, he possessed the power of life and death."

**Assorus** (*Chald.*). The third group of progeny (Kissan and Assorus) from the Babylonian Duad, Tauthe and Apason, according to the theogonies of Damascius. From this last group emanated three others, the last of which, Aus, begot Belus—"the fabricator of the World, the Demiurgus."

**Assur** (*Chald.*). A city in Assyria; the ancient location of a library from which George Smith excavated the earliest known tablets, which he dates to about 1500 B.C., called *Assur Kileh Shergat*.

**Assurbanipal** (*Chald.*). The Sardanapalus of the Greeks, "the greatest of the Assyrian sovereigns, far more memorable for his magnificent patronage of learning than for the greatness of his empire," writes the late G. Smith, and adds: "*Assurbanipal added more to the Assyrian royal library than all the kings who had gone before him*." As the distinguished Assyriologist tells us in another part of his "Babylonian and Assyrian Literature" (*Chald. Account of Genesis*) that "the majority of the texts preserved belong to the earlier period previous to 1600 B.C.," and yet asserts that "it is to tablets written in his (Assurbanipal’s) reign (673 B.C.) that we owe almost all our knowledge of early Babylonian history," one is well justified in asking, "How do you know?"

**Assyrian Holy Scriptures.** Orientalists identify seven such books: the Books of Mamit, of Worship, of Interpretations, and of Going to Hades; two Prayer Books (*Kanmagarri* and *Kanmikri*: Talbot), and the Kantolite, the lost Assyrian Psalter.

**Assyrian Tree of Life.** “Asherah” (see also *q.v.*). It is translated in the Bible as “grove” and appears 30 times. It is called an ‘idol’; and Maachah, the grandmother of Asa, King of Jerusalem, is accused of having made for herself such an idol, which was a *lingam*. For centuries, this was a religious rite in Judea. But the original Asherah was a pillar with seven branches on each side, topped by a globular flower with three projecting rays; it was not a *phallic* stone, as the Jews made of it, but a metaphysical symbol. “Merciful One, who raises the dead to life!” was the prayer uttered before the Asherah on the banks of the Euphrates. The “Merciful One” was neither the personal god of the Jews (who brought the “grove” from their captivity) nor any extra-cosmic god, but rather the higher triad in man, symbolized by the globular flower with its three rays.

**Asta-dasha** (*Sk.*). Perfect, Supreme Wisdom; a title of Deity.

**Aster't** (*Heb.*). Astarte, the Syrian goddess and consort of Adon, or Adonai.

**Astræa** (*Gr.*). The ancient goddess of justice whom the wickedness of men drove away from earth to heaven, where she now dwells as the constellation *Virgo*.

**Astral Body**, or Astral “Double.” The ethereal counterpart or shadow of a human or animal. The *Linga Sharira*, the “Doppelgänger.” The reader must not confuse it with the ASTRAL SOUL, which is another name for the lower Manas, or the so-called Kama-Manas, the reflection of the HIGHER Ego.

**Astral Light** (*Occult*). The invisible region that surrounds our globe, just as it surrounds every other. It corresponds to the *Linga Sharira* or the Astral Double in man as the second Principle of Kosmos (the third being Life, for which it is the vehicle). It is a subtle essence visible only to a clairvoyant eye, and is the second-lowest (the lowest being the earth) of the seven Akashic or Cosmic Principles. Eliphas Lévi calls it the great Serpent and the Dragon, from which every evil influence radiates upon humanity. This is true; but why not add that the Astral Light gives out nothing but what it has received? It is the great terrestrial crucible in which the vile moral and physical emanations of the earth, upon which the Astral Light is fed, are all converted into their subtlest essence and radiated back with intensity, thus becoming moral, psychic, and physical epidemics. Finally, the Astral Light is the same as the *Sidereal Light* of Paracelsus and other Hermetic philosophers. Physically, it is the ether of modern science. Metaphysically, and in its spiritual or occult sense, ether is much more than is often imagined. In occult physics and alchemy, it is well demonstrated to enclose within its shoreless waves

Alchemists and Hermetists believe that their astral, or sidereal ether—besides the previously mentioned properties of sulfur, and white and red *magnesia*, or *magnes*—is the *anima mundi*, the workshop of Nature and of all the Cosmos, spiritually as well as physically. The ‘grand *magisterium*’ asserts itself in the phenomenon of mesmerism and in the ‘levitation’ of human and inert objects; it may be called the ether from its spiritual aspect. The designation *astral* is ancient and was used by some of the Neoplatonists, although some claim that the word was coined by the Martinists. Porphyry describes the celestial body which is always joined with the soul as ‘immortal, luminous, and star-like.’ The root of this word may be found, perhaps, in the Scythian *Aist-aer*—which means star—or the Assyrian *Istar*, which, according to Burnouf, has the same sense.” (*Isis Unveiled*.)

**Astrolatry** (*Gr*.). Worship of the Stars.

**Astrology** (*Gr*.). The science which defines the action of celestial bodies upon mundane affairs and claims to foretell future events from the position of the stars. Its antiquity is such that it is placed among the very earliest records of human learning. It remained for long ages a secret science in the East, and its final expression remains so to this day; its exoteric application has been brought to any degree of perfection in the West only during the period since Varaha Mihira wrote his book on Astrology some 1,400 years ago. Claudius Ptolemy, the famous geographer and mathematician, wrote his treatise *Tetrabiblos* about 135 A.D., which is still the basis of modern astrology. The science of horoscopy is studied now chiefly under four heads: *viz*., (1) *Mundane*, in its application to meteorology, seismology, agriculture, etc. (2) *State* or *civic*, in regard to the fate of nations, kings, and rulers. (3) *Horary*, in reference to the solving of doubts arising in the mind upon any subject. (4) *Genethliacal*, in its application to the fate of individuals from the moment of their birth to their death. The Egyptians and the Chaldeans were among the most ancient devotees of astrology, though their modes of reading the stars and modern practices differ considerably. The former claimed that Belus—the Bel or Elu of the Chaldeans, a descendant of the *divine Dynasty*, or the Dynasty of the king-gods—had belonged to the land of Chemi (Egypt) and had left it to found a colony from Egypt on the banks of the Euphrates. There, a temple ministered by priests in the service of the “lords of the stars” was built, and those priests adopted the name of *Chaldeans*. Two things are known: (a) that Thebes (in Egypt) claimed the honor of inventing astrology; and (b) that it was the Chaldeans who taught that science to other nations. Now, Thebes significantly predated not only “Ur of the Chaldees” but also Nippur, where Bel was first worshipped—Sin, his son (the moon), being the presiding deity of Ur, the birthplace of Terah, the Sabian and star-worshipper, and of Abram, his son, the great...

If the title of Astrologer later fell into disrepute in Rome and elsewhere, it was due to the fraud of those who wanted to profit from what was an essential part of the sacred Science of the Mysteries. Being ignorant of the latter, they developed a system based entirely on mathematics instead of transcendental metaphysics, using the physical celestial bodies merely as its *upadhi* or material basis. **Astronomos** (*Gr.*). The title given to the Initiate in the Seventh Degree of the reception of the Mysteries. In ancient times, Astronomy was synonymous with Astrology; and the great Astrological Initiation took place in Thebes, Egypt, where the priests perfected—if they did not entirely invent—the science. Having passed through the degrees of *Pastophoros*, *Neocoros*, *Melanophoros*, *Kistophoros*, and *Balahala* (the degree of the Chemistry of the Stars), the neophyte was taught the mystic signs of the Zodiac in a circle dance representing the movement of the planets (similar to the dance of Krishna and the Gopis, which is celebrated to this day in Rajputana). Afterward, he received a cross, the Tau (or Tat), becoming an *Astronomos* and a Healer. (See *Isis Unveiled*, Vol. II, p. 365). Astronomy and Chemistry were inseparable in these studies. “Hippocrates had such a strong faith in the influence of the stars on living beings and their diseases that he expressly recommended not to trust physicians who are ignorant of astronomy.” (Arago.) Unfortunately, the key to the final door of Astrology or Astronomy has been lost by the modern astrologer; and without it, how can he ever be able to answer the pertinent remark made by the author of *Mazzaroth*, who writes: “people are said to be born under one sign while in reality they are born under another, because the sun is now seen among different stars at the equinox”? Nevertheless, even the few truths he does know have brought to his science such eminent and scientific believers as Sir Isaac Newton, Bishops Jeremy Taylor and Joseph Hall, Archbishop Ussher, Dryden, Flamsteed, Ashmole, John Milton, Steele, and a host of noted Rosicrucians.

**Asura Mazda** (*Sk.*). In the Zend language, *Ahura Mazda*. The same as Ormuzd or Mazdeò; the god of Zoroaster and the Parsis.

**Asuramaya** (*Sk.*). Also known as Mayâsura. An Atlantean astronomer, considered a great magician and sorcerer, who is well known in Sanskrit works.

**Asuras** (*Sk.*). Exoterically, they are elementals and evil gods—considered malevolent; demons, and *no gods*. But esoterically—the reverse is true. For in the most ancient portions of the *Rig Veda*, the term is used for the Supreme Spirit, and therefore the Asuras are spiritual and divine. It is only in the last book of the *Rig Veda*, its latest part, and in the *Atharva Veda* and the *Brahmanas*, that the epithet—which had been given to Agni (the greatest Vedic Deity), to Indra, and to Varuna—has come to signify the opposite of gods. *Asu* means breath, and it is with his breath that Prajâ-pati (Brahmâ) creates the Asuras. When ritualism and dogma triumphed over the Wisdom religion, the initial letter *a* was adopted as a negative prefix, and the term ended by signifying “not a god,” with *Sura* meaning only a deity. But in the Vedas, the Suras have always been connected with Surya, the sun, and regarded as inferior deities or devas.

**Aswamedha** (*Sk.*). The Horse-sacrifice; an ancient Brahmanical ceremony.

**Aswattha** (*Sk.*). The Bo-tree, the tree of knowledge, *ficus religiosa*.

**Aswins** (*Sk.*), or *Aswinau* (dual); or again, *Aswinî-Kumârau*, are the most mysterious and occult deities of all, who have “puzzled the oldest commentators.” Literally, they are the “Horsemen” or the “divine charioteers,” as they ride in a golden chariot drawn by horses, birds, or animals, and “*are possessed of many forms*.” They are two Vedic deities, the twin sons of the sun and the sky, the latter of which becomes the nymph Aswinî. In mythological symbolism, they are “the bright harbingers of Ushas, the dawn,” who are “ever young and handsome, bright, agile, and swift as falcons,” and who “prepare the way for the brilliant dawn for those who have patiently waited through the night.” They are also called the “physicians of Swarga” (or Devachan), because they heal every pain and suffering and cure all diseases. Astronomically, they are asterisms. They were enthusiastically worshipped, as their epithets show. They are the “Ocean-born” (*i.e., space-born*) or *Abdhijau*, “crowned with lotuses” or *Pushkara-srajam*, etc. Yâska, the commentator in the *Nirukta*, thinks that “the Aswins represent the transition from darkness to light”—cosmically, and we may add, metaphysically as well. But Muir and Goldstücker are inclined to see in them ancient “horsemen of great renown,” simply because of the legend “that the gods refused the Aswins admittance to a sacrifice on the ground that they had been on too familiar terms with men.” This is exactly the case because, as explained by the same Yâska, “they are identified with heaven and earth,” only for a completely different reason. Truly they are like the *Ribhus*, “originally renowned mortals (but also non-renowned occasionally) who in the course of time are translated into the companionship of gods”; and they show a negative character, “the result of the alliance of light with darkness,” simply because these twins are, in the esoteric philosophy, the *Kumâra-Egos*, the reincarnating “Principles” in this Manvantara.

**<term>Atalanta Fugiens</term>** (*Lat*.). A famous treatise by the eminent Rosicrucian Michael Maier; it contains many beautiful engravings of Alchemical symbolism. **<term>Atarpi</term>** (*Chald*.), or *Atarpi-nisi*, “the man.” A person who was “pious toward the gods” and who prayed to the god Hea to remove the evil of drought and other afflictions before the Deluge was sent. The story is found on one of the most ancient Babylonian tablets and relates to the sin of the world. In the words of G. **<term>Atash Behram</term>** (*Zend*). The sacred fire of the Parsis, kept burning perpetually in their fire-temples.

**<term>Athanor</term>** (*Occult*.). The “astral” fluid of the Alchemists, their Archimedean lever; exoterically, the furnace of the Alchemist.

**<term>Atharva Veda</term>** (*Sk*.). The fourth <term>Veda</term>; literally, a magic incantation containing aphorisms, spells, and magic formulas. It is one of the most ancient and revered books of the Brahmans.

**<term>Athenagoras</term>** (*Gr*.). A Platonic philosopher of Athens who wrote a Greek Apology for the Christians in 177 A.D. It was addressed to the Emperor Marcus Aurelius to prove that the accusations brought against them—namely, that they were incestuous and ate murdered children—were untrue.

**<term>Athor</term>** (*Eg*.). “Mother Night.” Primeval Chaos in Egyptian cosmogony; the goddess of night.

**<term>Atîvahikâs</term>** (*Sk*.). Among the *Visishtadwaitees*, these are the <term>Pitris</term> or <term>Devas</term> who help the disembodied soul, or <term>Jiva</term>, in its transit from its dead body to <term>Paramapadha</term>.

**<term>Atlantidae</term>** (*Gr.*). The ancestors of the Pharaohs and the forefathers of the Egyptians, according to some, and as Esoteric Science teaches. **<term>Augoeides</term>** (*Gr.*). Bulwer Lytton calls it the “Luminous Self,” or our Higher Ego. But Occultism makes it something distinct from this. It is a mystery. The *Augoeides* is the luminous divine radiation of the Ego which, when incarnated, is but its shadow—pure as it is yet. This is explained in the *Amshaspends* and their *Ferouers*.

**<term>Aum</term>** (*Sk.*). The sacred syllable; the triple-lettered unit; hence the trinity in one.

**<term>Aura</term>** (*Gr. and Lat.*). A subtle invisible essence or fluid that emanates from human and animal bodies and even things. It is a psychic effluvium, partaking of both the mind and the body, as it is the electro-vital, and at the same time an electro-mental aura; called in Theosophy the *âkâsic* or magnetic aura.

**<term>Aurnavâbha</term>** (*Sk.*). An ancient Sanskrit commentator.

The mystic formula “Om mani padme hum” is specially used to invoke their joint help. While popular fancy claims many incarnations on earth for Avalokiteswara and sees in him, not incorrectly, the spiritual guide of every believer, the esoteric interpretation sees in him the Logos, both celestial and human. Therefore, when the Yogâchârya School has declared Avalokiteswara as Padmapâni “to be the Dhyâni Bodhisattva of Amitâbha Buddha,” it is indeed because the former is the spiritual reflex in the world of forms of the latter, both being one—one in heaven, the other on earth.

**<term>Avarasâila Sanghârama</term>** (*Sk.*). *Literally*, the School of the Dwellers on the western mountain. A celebrated *Vihâra* (monastery) in Dhanakstchâka according to Eitel, “built 600 B.C., and deserted A.D. 600.”

**<term>Avastan</term>** (*Sk.*). An ancient name for Arabia.

**<term>Avasthas</term>** (*Sk.*). States, conditions, positions.

**<term>Avatâra</term>** (*Sk.*). Divine incarnation. The descent of a god or some exalted Being, who has progressed beyond the necessity of rebirths, into the body of a simple mortal. Krishna was an avatar of Vishnu.

All the Spirits of the Elements were subject to him, so says the legend, and it further tells us that owing to his knowledge of the Elixir of Life, he still lives as an adept who will reveal himself to the profane at the end of a certain cycle.

**<term>Avidyâ</term>** (*Sk.*). Opposed to *Vidyâ*, Knowledge. Ignorance which proceeds from, and is produced by, the illusion of the Senses or *Viparyaya*.

**<term>Avikâra</term>** (*Sk.*). Free from degeneration; changeless—used in reference to deity.

**<term>Avîtchi</term>** (*Sk.*). A state: not necessarily only after death or between two births, for it can take place on earth as well. *Literally*, “uninterrupted hell.” The last of the eight hells, we are told, “where the *culprits die and are reborn without interruption*—yet not without hope of final redemption.” This is because Avîtchi is another name for Myalba (our earth) and also a state to which some soulless men are condemned on this physical plane.

**<term>Avyakta</term>** (*Sk.*). The unrevealed cause; indiscrete or undifferentiated; the opposite of *Vyakta*, the differentiated. The former is used for the unmanifested, and the latter for the manifested Deity, or for Brahma and Brahmâ.

**<term>Axieros</term>** (*Gr.*). One of the Kabiri.
**<term>Axiocersa</term>** (*Gr.*). One of the Kabiri.
**<term>Axiocersus</term>** (*Gr.*). One of the Kabiri.

**<term>Ayana</term>** (*Sk.*). A period of time; two Ayanas complete a year, one being the period of the Sun’s progress northward, and the other southward in the ecliptic.

**<term>Ayin</term>** (*Heb.*). Literally, “Nothing,” from which comes the name of Ain-Soph. (See “*Ain*”).

**<term>Aymar, Jacques</term>**. A famous Frenchman who had great success in the

He who comprehends the mystery of Azazel, says <term>Aben-Ezra</term>, “will learn the mystery of God’s name,” and truly. See “<term>Typhon</term>” and the scapegoat made sacred to him in <term>ancient Egypt</term>.

**Azhi-Dahaka** (*Zend*). One of the <term>Serpents</term> or <term>Dragons</term> in the legends of <term>Iran</term> and the <term>Avesta Scriptures</term>; the allegorical destroying <term>Serpent</term> or <term>Satan</term>.

**Aziluth** (*Heb.*). The name for the world of the <term>Sephiroth</term>, called the world of <term>Emanations Olam Aziluth</term>. The globes A and Z of our terrestrial chain are in <term>Aziluth</term>. (See *Secret Doctrine*).

## B.
**B.**—The second letter in almost all alphabets, also the second in the Hebrew. Its symbol is a house, the form of Beth, the letter itself indicating a dwelling, a shed, or a shelter. “As a compound of a root, it is constantly used to show that it had to do with stone—for instance, when stones are set up at Bethel. The Hebrew value as a numeral is two. Joined with its predecessor, it forms the word *Ab*, the root of ‘father’, Master, or one in authority; it has the Kabbalistic distinction of being the first letter in the Sacred Volume of the Law. The divine name connected with this letter is *Bakhour*.” (R. M. Cyclop.)

**Baal** (*Chald.*). Baal or Adon (Adonai) was a phallic god. “Who shall ascend the hill (the high place) of the Lord? Who shall stand in the place of his *Kadushu* (which see)?” (*Psalms 24:3*.) The “circle-dance” performed by King David around the ark was the dance prescribed by the Amazons in the Mysteries, the dance of the daughters of Shiloh (*Judges 21, etc.*), and the same as the leaping of the prophets of Baal (*1 Kings 18*). He was named Baal-Tzephon, or god of the crypt (Exodus), and *Seth*, or the pillar (phallus), because he was the same as Ammon (or Baal-Hammon) of Egypt, called “the hidden god.” Typhon, called Set, who was a great god in Egypt during the early dynasties, is an aspect of Baal and Ammon, as well as of Siva, Jehovah, and other gods. Baal is the all-devouring Sun; in one sense, the fiery Moloch.

**Babil Mound** (*Chald. Heb.*). The site of the Temple of Bel at Babylon.

**Bacchus** (*Gr.*). Exoterically and superficially the god of wine and the vintage, and of licentiousness and joy; but the esoteric meaning of this personification is more abstruse and philosophical. He is the Osiris of Egypt, and his life and significance belong to the same group as the other solar deities, all of whom are “sin-bearing,” killed, and resurrected—for example, as Dionysos or Atys of Phrygia (Adonis, or the Syrian Tammuz), as Ausonius, Baldur (which see), etc. All these were put to death, mourned for, and restored to life. The rejoicings for Atys took place at the *Hilaria* on the “pagan” Easter, March 15th. Ausonius, a form of Bacchus, was slain “at the vernal equinox, March 21st, and rose in three days.” Tammuz, the double of Adonis and Atys, was mourned by the women at the “grove” of his name “over Bethlehem, where the infant Jesus cried,” says St. Jerome. Bacchus is murdered, and his mother collects the fragments of his lacerated body just as Isis does those of Osiris, and so on.

Dionysus Iacchus, torn to shreds by the Titans, Osiris, and Krishna, all descended into Hades and returned again. **Bacon, Roger.** A Franciscan monk, famous as an expert in Alchemy and Magic Arts. He lived in the thirteenth century in England. He believed in the philosopher’s stone in the same way all the experts of Occultism *believe in it*; and also in philosophical astrology. He is accused of having made a bronze head which, having an acoustic apparatus hidden in it, seemed to utter oracles that were actually words spoken by Bacon himself in another room. He was a wonderful physicist and chemist, and is credited with having invented gunpowder, though he said he had the secret from “Asian (Chinese) wise men.”

**Baddha** (*Sk.*). Bound, conditioned; as is every mortal who has not made himself free through Nirvana.

**Bagavadam** (*Sk.*). A Tamil Scripture on Astronomy and other matters.

**Bagh-bog** (*Slavonic*). “God”; a Slavonic name for the Greek Bacchus, whose name became the prototype for the name God, or *Bagh* and *bog* or *bogh*; the Russian word for God.

**Bahak-Zivo** (*Gn.*). The “father of the Genii” in the *Codex Nazaraeus*. The Nazarenes were an early semi-Christian sect.

**Bal** (*Heb.*). Commonly translated as “Lord,” but also refers to Bel, the Chaldean god, and Baal, an “idol.”

**Bala** (*Sk.*), or *Panchabalani*. The “five powers” to be acquired in Yoga practice: full trust or faith, energy, memory, meditation, and wisdom.

**Baldur** (*Scand.*). The “Giver of all Good.” The bright God who is “the best, and all mankind are loud in his praise; so fair and dazzling is he in form and features that rays of light seem to issue from him” (*Edda*). Such was the birth-song chanted to Baldur, who resurrects as Wali, the spring Sun. Baldur is called the “well-beloved,” the “Holy one,” “who alone is without sin.” He is the “God of Goodness,” who “shall be born again when a new and purer world has arisen from the ashes of the old, sin-laden world (Asgard).” He is killed by the crafty Loki because Frigga, the mother of the gods, “while entreating all creatures and all lifeless things to swear that they will not injure the well-beloved,” forgets to mention “the weak mistletoe bough,” just as the mother of Achilles forgot her son’s heel. A dart is made from it by Loki, and he places it in the hands of blind Hodur, who kills the sunny-hearted god of light with it. The Christmas mistletoe is probably a memory of the mistletoe that killed the Northern God of Goodness.

**Bal-ilu** (*Chald.*). One of the many titles of the Sun.

**Bamboo Books.** Most ancient and certainly prehistoric Chinese works containing the antediluvian records of the *Annals of China*. They were found in the tomb of King Seang of Wai, who died in 295 B.C., and claim to go back many centuries.

**Bandha** (*Sk.*). Bondage; life on this earth; from the same root as *Baddha*.

**Baphomet** (*Gr.*). The androgynous goat of Mendes. (See *Secret Doctrine*, I. 253). According to Western—and especially French—Kabalists, the Templars were accused of worshipping Baphomet, and Jacques de Molay, the Grand Master of the Templars, along with all his brother Masons, died as a consequence. But esoterically and philologically, the word never meant “goat,” nor even anything as objective as an idol. According to Von Hammer, the term means “baptism” or *initiation into Wisdom*, from the Greek words βαφὴ and νητισμα, and from the relation of Baphometus to Pan. Von Hammer must be right. It was a Hermetic-Kabalistic symbol, but the entire story invented by the clergy was false. (See “Pan”).

**Baptism** (*Gr.*). The rite of purification performed during the initiation ceremony in the sacred tanks of India, and also the later identical rite established by John “the Baptist” and practiced by his disciples and followers, who were not Christians. This rite was ancient when it was adopted by the Chrestians of the earliest centuries. Baptism belonged to the earliest Chaldean-Akkadian theurgy; it was religiously practiced in the nocturnal ceremonies in the Pyramids where we see to this day the font in the shape of a sarcophagus; it was known to take place during the Eleusinian mysteries in the sacred temple lakes; and it is practiced even now by the descendants of the ancient Sabians. The Mandaeans (the *El Mogtasilas* of the Arabs) are, despite their deceptive name of “St. John Christians,” less Christian than the orthodox Muslim Arabs around them. They are pure Sabians; and this is very naturally explained when one remembers that the great Semitic scholar Renan has shown in his *Vie de Jésus* that the Aramaic verb *seba*, the origin of the name Sabian, is a synonym of the Greek βαπτίζω. The modern Sabians, the Mandaeans—whose vigils and religious rites, performed face to face with the silent stars, have been described by several travelers—have still preserved the theurgic, baptismal rites of their distant and nearly forgotten ancestors, the Chaldean Initiates. Their religion is one of multiple baptisms, of seven purifications in the name of the seven planetary rulers, the “seven Angels of the Presence” of the Roman Catholic Church. The Protestant Baptists are but the pale imitators of the *El Mogtasilas* or Nazarenes who practice their Gnostic rites in the deserts of Asia Minor. (See “Boodhasp”).

**Bardesanes** or *Bardaisan*. A Syrian Gnostic, erroneously regarded as a Christian theologian, born at Edessa (*Essene Chronicle*) around 155 of our era (*Essemani Bibl. Orient.* i. 389). He was a great astrologer following the Eastern Occult System. According to Porphyry

The fact is that most of his teachings, however much they may have been altered by his numerous Gnostic followers, can be traced to Indian philosophy, and even more to the occult teachings of the Secret System. Thus, in his *Hymns*, he speaks of the creative Deity as “Father-Mother,” and elsewhere of “Astral Destiny” (*Karma*), of “Minds of Fire” (the *Agni Devas*), etc. He connected the Soul (the personal *Maenas*) with the Seven Stars, deriving its origin from the *Higher Beings* (the divine Ego); and therefore, he “admitted spiritual resurrection but denied the resurrection of the body,” as charged by the Church Fathers. Ephraim shows him preaching the signs of the Zodiac and the importance of birth hours, and “proclaiming the seven.” Calling the Sun the “Father of Life” and the Moon the “Mother of Life,” he shows the latter “laying aside her garment of light (principles) for the renewal of the Earth.” Photius cannot understand how, while accepting “the Soul as free from the power of *genesis* (destiny of birth)” and possessing free will, he still placed the body under the rule of birth (*genesis*). For “they (the Bardesanists) say that wealth and poverty, sickness and health, death, and all things not within our control are works of destiny” (*Bibl. Cod.* 223, p. 221—f). This is most evidently <term>Karma</term>, which does not at all preclude free will. Hippolytus makes him a representative of the Eastern School. Speaking of Baptism, Bardesanes is quoted as saying (*loc. cit.* pp. 985—ff.), “It is not, however, the Bath alone which makes us free, but the knowledge of who we are, what we have become, where we were before, where we are hastening, from where we are redeemed, what is generation (birth), and what is re-generation (re-birth).” This points plainly to the doctrine of reincarnation. His conversation (*Dialogue*) with Awida and Barjamina on Destiny and Free Will shows it: “What is called Destiny is an order of outflow given to the Rulers (Gods) and the Elements, according to which order the Intelligences (Spirit-Egos) are changed by their descent into the Soul, and the Soul by its descent into the body.” (See the Treatise, found in its Syriac original and published with an English translation in 1855 by Dr. Cureton, *Spicileg. Syriac.* in the British Museum.)

## **Bardesanian** (**System**).
The “<term>Codex of the Nazarenes</term>,” a system worked out by a certain Bardesanes. It is called by some a <term>Kabala</term> within the <term>Kabala</term>; a religion or sect whose esotericism is presented in names and allegories that are entirely *sui-generis*. A very old <term>Gnostic</term> system. This <term>codex</term> has been translated into Latin. Whether it is right to call the <term>Sabeanism</term> of the <term>Mendaites</term> (wrongly called <term>St. John’s Christians</term>), contained in the <term>Nazarene Codex</term>, “the <term>Bardesanian system</term>,” as some do, is doubtful; for the doctrines of the <term>Codex</term> and the names of the Good and Evil Powers within it are older than <term>Bardaisan</term>. Yet the names are identical in both systems.

**<term>Baresma</term>** (*Zend*). A plant used by Mobeds (Parsi priests) in the fire-temples, where consecrated bundles of it are kept.

**<term>Barhishad</term>** (*Sk.*). A class of the "lunar" Pitris or "Ancestors," Fathers who are believed in popular superstition to have maintained the sacred household flame and made fire-offerings in their past incarnations. Esoterically, they are the Pitris who evolved their shadows or *chhayas* to create the first man with them. (See *Secret Doctrine*, Vol. II.)

**<term>Basileus</term>** (*Gr.*). The Archon or Chief who had the outer supervision during the Eleusinian Mysteries. While the latter was an initiated layman and magistrate at Athens, the *Basileus* of the inner Temple was part of the staff of the great Hierophant, and as such was one of the chief *Mystæ* and belonged to the inner mysteries.

**<term>Basilidean</term>** (*System*). Named after Basilides, the founder of one of the most philosophical Gnostic sects. Clement of Alexandria speaks of Basilides the Gnostic as "a *philosopher devoted to the contemplation of divine things*." While he claimed that he had all his doctrines from the Apostle Matthew and from Peter through Glaucus, Irenæus reviled him, Tertullian stormed at him, and the Church Fathers did not have enough words of disgrace against the "heretic." And yet, on the authority of St. Jerome himself—who describes with indignation what he had found in the only *genuine Hebrew copy of the Gospel of Matthew* (See *Isis Unveiled*, Vol. II. 181) which he obtained from the Nazarenes—the statement of Basilides becomes more than credible, and if accepted would solve a great and perplexing problem. His 24 volumes of *Interpretation of the Gospels* were, as Eusebius tells us, burned. It is unnecessary to say that these gospels were not our present Gospels. Thus, truth was ever crushed.

**<term>Bassantin</term>, James**. A Scottish astrologer. He lived in the 16th century and is said to have predicted to Sir Robert Melville in 1562 the death of Mary, the unfortunate Queen of Scots, and all the events connected with it.

**<term>Bath</term>** (*Heb.*). Daughter.

**<term>Bath Kol</term>** (*Heb.*). Daughter of the Voice: the Divine *afflatus*, or inspiration, by which the prophets of Israel were inspired as if by a voice from Heaven and the Mercy-Seat. In Latin, *Filiâ Vocis*. An analogous ideal is found in Hindu exoteric theology named Vâch: the voice, the female essence, an aspect of Aditi, the mother of the gods and primeval Light; a mystery. [w.w.w.]

**<term>Batoo</term>** (*Eg.*). The first man in Egyptian folklore. Noun, the heavenly artist, creates a beautiful girl—the original of the Greek Pandora—and sends her to Batoo, after which the happiness of the first man is destroyed.

**<term>Batria</term>** (*Eg.*). According to tradition, the wife of the Pharaoh and the teacher of Moses.

### Beel-Zebub (Heb.).
The disfigured *Baal* of the Temples, and more correctly Beel-Zebul. Beel-Zebub literally means "god of flies"; a mocking epithet used by the Jews, and an incorrect and confused rendering of the "god of the sacred scarabs," the divinities watching over mummies and acting as symbols of transformation, regeneration, and immortality. Beel-Zebul properly means the "God of the Dwelling," and is spoken of in this sense in *Matthew* x. 25. As Apollo—originally not a Greek but a Phoenician god—was the healing god, *Paean*, or physician, as well as the god of oracles, he gradually became transformed into the "Lord of the Dwelling," a household deity, and thus was called Beel-Zebul. He was also, in a sense, a psychopomp god, caring for souls as did Anubis. Beel-Zebub was always the oracle god, and was only confused and identified with Apollo later on.

### Bel (Chald.).
The oldest and mightiest god of Babylonia, one of the earliest trinities: Anu (*q.v.*); Bel, "Lord of the World," father of the gods, Creator, and "Lord of the City of Nippur"; and Hea, maker of fate, Lord of the Deep, God of Wisdom and esoteric knowledge, and "Lord of the city of Eridu." The wife of Bel, or his female aspect (*Shakti*), was Belat, or Beltis, "the mother of the great gods," and the "Lady of the city of Nippur." The original Bel was also called Enu, Elu, and Kaptu (see *Chaldean Account of Genesis*, by G. Smith). His eldest son was the Moon God Sin (whose names were also Ur, Agu, and Itu), who was the presiding deity of the city of Ur, named in his honor by one of his names. Now Ur was the birthplace of Abram (see "Astrology"). In the early Babylonian religion, the Moon was—like Soma in India—a male deity, and the Sun was a female deity. This led almost every nation into great civil wars between lunar and solar worshippers—for example, the contests between the Lunar and Solar Dynasties, the Chandra and Suryavansa in ancient Aryavarta. We find the same thing on a smaller scale between the Semitic tribes. Abram and his father Terah are shown migrating from Ur and carrying their lunar god (or its descendant) with them; for Jehovah Elohim or El—another form of Elu—has always been connected with the moon. It is the Jewish lunar chronology which has led "civilized" European nations into the greatest blunders and mistakes. Merodach, the son of Hea, became the later Bel and was worshipped at Babylon. His other title, Belas, has a number of symbolic meanings.

### Bela-Shemesh (Chald. Heb.).
"The Lord of the Sun," the name of the moon during that period when the Jews became in turn solar and lunar worshippers, and when the Moon was a male and the Sun was a female deity. This period embraced the time between the allegorical expulsion of Adam and Eve from Eden down to the equally allegorical Noachian flood. (See *Secret Doctrine*, I. 397.)

A bronze tablet inlaid with mosaic designs (now in the Museum at Turin) which once belonged to the famous Cardinal Bembo. Its origin and date are unknown. It

**Ben** (*Heb.*). A son; a common prefix in proper names to denote the son of so-and-so, *e.g.*, Ben Solomon, Ben Ishmael, *etc.*

**Be-ness.** A term coined by Theosophists to translate more accurately the essential meaning of the untranslatable word *Sat*. The latter word does not mean "Being," for it presupposes a sentient feeling or some consciousness of existence. But, as the term *Sat* is applied solely to the absolute Principle—the universal, unknown, and ever-unknowable Presence that philosophical Pantheism postulates in the Cosmos, calling it the basic root of the Cosmos and the Cosmos itself—"Being" was no fit word to express it. Indeed, the latter is not even, as translated by some Orientalists, "the incomprehensible Entity"; for it is no more an Entity than a non-entity, but both. It is, as stated, absolute *Be-ness*, not *Being*—the one without a second, undivided, and indivisible All—the root of all Nature, visible and invisible, objective and subjective, to be sensed by the highest spiritual intuition but never to be fully comprehended.

**Ben Shamesh** (*Heb.*). The children or the "Sons of the Sun." The term belongs to the period when the Jews were divided into sun and moon worshipers—Elites and Belites. (See "Bela-Shemesh.")

**Benoo** (*Eg.*). A word applied to two symbols, both taken to mean "Phoenix." One was the *Shen-shen* (the heron), and the other a nondescript bird called the *Rech* (the red one), and both were sacred to Osiris. It was the latter that was the regular Phoenix of the great Mysteries, the typical symbol of self-creation and resurrection through death—a type of the Solar Osiris and of the divine Ego in man. Yet both the Heron and the *Rech* were symbols of cycles; the former of the solar year of 365 days, the latter of the tropical year or a period covering almost 26,000 years. In both cases, the cycles were the types of the return of light from darkness—the yearly and great cyclic return of the sun-god to his birthplace, or his Resurrection. The *Rech-Benoo* is described by Macrobius as living 660 years and then dying, while others stretched its life as long as 1,460 years. Pliny the Naturalist describes the *Rech* as a large bird with gold and purple wings and a long blue tail. As every reader is aware, according to tradition, the Phoenix, on feeling its end approaching, builds for itself a funeral pyre on top of the sacrificial altar and then proceeds to consume itself there as a burnt offering. Then a worm appears in the ashes, which grows and develops rapidly into a new Phoenix, resurrected from the ashes of its predecessor.

**Berasit** (*Heb.*). The first word of the book of Genesis. The Eng-

The established version translates this as “In the beginning,” but this rendering is disputed by many scholars. Tertullian approved of “In power”; Grotius used “When first”; but the authors of the *Targum of Jerusalem*, who surely should have known Hebrew if anyone did, translated it as “In Wisdom.” Godfrey Higgins, in his *Anacalypsis*, insists on *Berasit* being the sign of the ablative case, meaning “in,” and *ras*, *rasit*, being an ancient word for *Chokmah*, or “wisdom.” <note>w.w.w.</note>
Berashit or Berasheth is a mystic word among the Kabbalists of Asia Minor.

**Bergelmir** (*Scand.*). The one giant who escaped in a boat from the general slaughter of his brothers—the children of the giant Ymir—who were drowned in the blood of their raging Father. He is the Scandinavian Noah, as he also becomes the father of giants after the Deluge. The lays of the Norsemen show the grandsons of the divine Buri—Odin, Wili, and We—conquering and killing the terrible giant Ymir and creating the world out of his body.

**Berosus** (*Chald.*). A priest of the Temple of Belus who wrote the history of the Cosmogony for Alexander the Great, as taught in the Temples, based on the astronomical and chronological records preserved there. The fragments we have in the so-called translations of Eusebius are certainly as untrustworthy as the biographer of the Emperor Constantine—whom he made into a saint (!!)—could make them. The only guide to this Cosmogony may now be found in the fragments of the Assyrian tablets, which were evidently copied almost entirely from the earlier Babylonian records. Whatever Orientalists may say, these are undeniably the originals of the Mosaic Genesis, the Flood, the Tower of Babel, the story of the infant Moses set afloat on the waters, and other events. While the fragments from the Cosmogony of Berosus—so carefully re-edited and probably mutilated and expanded by Eusebius—are not great proof of the antiquity of these Babylonian records (given that the priest of Belus lived three hundred years after the Jews were carried captive to Babylon, suggesting they might have been borrowed by the Assyrians from them), later discoveries have made such a comforting hypothesis impossible. It is now fully established by Oriental scholars that not only did “Assyria borrow its civilization and written characters from Babylonia,” but the Assyrians copied their *literature* from Babylonian sources. Moreover, in his first Hibbert lecture, Professor Sayce shows that the culture of both Babylonia itself and the city of Eridu was of foreign importation; according to this scholar, the city of Eridu already stood “6,000 years ago on the shores of the Persian Gulf,” which is roughly the same time that *Genesis* describes the Elohim creating the world, sun, and stars out of nothing.

**Bes** (*Eg.*). A phallic god, the god of desire and pleasure. He is represented standing on a lotus, ready to devour his own offspring (Abydos). He is a relatively modern deity of foreign origin.

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

**Bestla** (*Scand.*). The daughter of the “Frost giants,” the sons of Ymir; married to Buri, and the mother of Odin and his brothers (*Edda*).
**Beth** (*Heb.*). House, dwelling.
**Beth Elohim** (*Heb.*). A Kabbalistic treatise dealing with angels, the souls of men, and demons. The name means “House of the Gods.”
**Betyles** (*Phœn.*). Magical stones. Ancient writers call them “animated stones”; oracular stones, believed in and used by both Gentiles and Christians. (See *Secret Doctrine* II, p. 342).
**Bhadra Vihara** (*Sk.*). Literally, “the Monastery of the Sages or Bodhisattvas.” A certain *Vihara* or *Matham* in Kanyâkubdja.
**Bhadrakalpa** (*Sk.*). Literally, “The Kalpa of the Sages.” Our present period is a Bhadra Kalpa, and exoteric teaching claims it lasts 236 million years. It is “so called because 1,000 Buddhas or sages appear in the course of it” (*Sanskrit-Chinese Dictionary*). “Four Buddhas have already appeared,” it adds; but as over 151 million years have already passed out of the 236 million, it seems like a rather uneven distribution of Buddhas. This is the way exoteric or popular religions confuse everything. Esoteric philosophy teaches us that every Root-race has its chief Buddha or Reformer, who also appears in the seven sub-races as a Bodhisattva (see entry). Gautama Sakyamuni was the fourth and also the fifth Buddha: the fifth, because we are in the fifth root-race; the fourth, as the chief Buddha in this fourth Round. The Bhadra Kalpa, or the “period of stability,” is the name of our present Round, esoterically—its duration applying, of course, only to our globe (D); the “1,000” Buddhas are thus in reality limited to only forty-nine in total.
**Bhadrasena** (*Sk.*). A Buddhist king of Magadha.
**Bhagats** (*Sk.*). Also called *Sokha* and *Sivnath* by the Hindus; one who exorcises evil spirits.
**Bhagavad-gîta** (*Sk.*). Literally, “the Lord’s Song.” A portion of the *Mahabharata*, the great epic poem of India. It contains a dialogue in which Krishna—the “Charioteer”—and Arjuna, his *Chela*, have a discussion about the highest spiritual philosophy. The work is preeminently occult or esoteric.
**Bhagavat** (*Sk.*). A title of the Buddha and of Krishna. “The Lord,” literally.
**Bhao** (*Sk.*). A ceremony of divination among the Kolarian tribes of Central India.
**Bhârata Varsha** (*Sk.*). The land of Bharata, an ancient name of India.
**Bhargavas** (*Sk.*). An ancient race in India; from the name of Bhrigu, the Rishi.
**Bhâshya** (*Sk.*). A commentary.
**Bhâskara** (*Sk.*). One of the titles of *Sûrya*, the Sun; meaning “life-giver” and “light-maker.”

<header>GLOSSARY 53</header>

**Bhava** (*Sk.*). Being, or state of being; the world, a birth, and also a name of Shiva.

**Bhikshu** (*Sk.*). In Pali *Bikkhu*. The name given to the first followers of Sakyamuni Buddha. *Literally*, "mendicant scholar." The Sanskrit Chinese Dictionary explains the term correctly by dividing Bhikshus into two classes of *Sramanas* (Buddhist monks and priests), *namely*, "esoteric mendicants who control their nature by the (religious) law, and exoteric mendicants who control their nature by *diet*;" and it adds, less correctly: "every true Bhikshu is supposed to work miracles."

**Bhons** (*Tib.*). The followers of the old religion of the Indigenous people of Tibet; of pre-Buddhist temples and ritualism; the same as Dugpas, "red caps," though the latter name usually applies only to sorcerers.

**Bhrantidarsanatah** (*Sk.*). *Literally*, "false comprehension or apprehension"; something conceived of based on false appearances as a *mayavic*, illusory form.

**Bhrigu** (*Sk.*). One of the great Vedic Rishis. He is called "Son" by Manu, who entrusts to him his *Institutes*. He is one of the Seven Prajapatis, or progenitors of mankind, which is equivalent to identifying him with one of the creative gods, placed by the Puranas in Krita Yuga, or the first age—that of purity. Dr. Wynn Wescott reminds us of the fact that the late and very scholarly Dr. Kenealy (who spelled the name Brighoo), made this Muni (Saint) the fourth out of his twelve "divine messengers" to the world, adding that he appeared in Tibet in A.N. 4800 and that his religion spread to Britain, where his followers raised the megalithic temple of Stonehenge. This, of course, is a hypothesis, based merely on Dr. Kenealy's personal speculations.

**Bhûmi** (*Sk.*). The earth, also called *Prithivi*.

**Bhur-Bhuva** (*Sk.*). A mystic invocation, as *Om*, *Bhur*, *Bhuva*, *Swar*, meaning "Om, earth, sky, heaven." This is the exoteric explanation.

**Bhuranyu** (*Sk.*). "The rapid" or the swift. Used of a missile—an equivalent also of the Greek *Phoroneus*.

**Bhur-loka** (*Sk.*). One of the 14 lokas or worlds in Hindu Pantheism; our Earth.

**Bhutadi** (*Sk.*). Elementary substances, the origin and the germinal essence of the elements.

**Bhutan.** A country of heretical Buddhists and Lamaists beyond Sikkim, ruled by the Dharma Raja, a nominal vassal of the Dalai Lama.

**Bhûhta-vidyâ** (*Sk.*). The art of exorcising, or of treating and curing demonic possession. Literally, "Demon" or "Ghost-knowledge."

**Bhûta-sarga** (*Sk.*). Elemental or beginning Creation, *that is*, when matter was several degrees less material than it is now.

<term>Bhûtesa</term> (*Sk*.). Or *Bhûteswara*; literally, “Lord of beings or of existing lives.” A name applied to Vishnu, to Brahma, and to Krishna.

<term>Bhûts</term> (*Sk*.). *Bhûta*: Ghosts, phantoms. To call them “demons,” as the Orientalists do, is incorrect. For, while on the one hand a Bhûta is “a malignant spirit which haunts cemeteries, lurks in trees, animates dead bodies, and deludes and devours human beings” in popular fancy; in India, Tibet, and China, by Bhûtas are also meant “heretics” who smear their bodies with ashes, or Shaiva ascetics (Siva being regarded in India as the King of Bhûtas).

<term>Bhuva-loka</term> (*Sk*.). One of the 14 worlds.

<term>Bhuvana</term> (*Sk*.). A name of Rudra or Siva, one of the Indian Trimurti (Trinity).

<term>Bifrôst</term> (*Scand*.). A bridge built by the gods to protect Asgard. On it “the third Sword-god, known as Heimdal or Riger,” stands night and day girded with his sword, for he is the watchman selected to protect Asgard, the abode of gods. Heimdal is the Scandinavian Cherubim with the flaming sword, “which turned every way to keep the way of the tree of life.”

<term>Bihar Gyalpo</term> (*Tib*.). A king deified by the Dugpas. A patron over all their religious buildings.

<term>Bînah</term> (*Heb*.). Understanding. The third of the 10 Sephiroth, the third of the Supernal Triad; a female potency, corresponding to the letter *hé* of the Tetragrammaton IHVH. Bînah is called AIMA, the Supernal Mother, and “the great Sea.” [w.w.w.]

<term>Birs Nimrud</term> (*Chald*.). Believed by the Orientalists to be the site of the Tower of Babel. The great pile of Birs Nimrud is near Babylon. Sir H. Rawlinson and several Assyriologists examined the excavated ruins and found that the tower consisted of seven stages of brickwork, each stage of a different color, which shows that the temple was devoted to the seven planets. Even with its three higher stages or floors in ruins, it still rises 154 feet above the level of the plain. (See “Borsippa”).

<term>Black Dwarfs</term>. The name of the Elves of Darkness, who creep about in the dark caverns of the earth and fabricate weapons and utensils for their divine fathers, the Æsir or Ases. Also called “Black Elves.”

<term>Black Fire</term> (*Zohar*). A Kabbalistic term for Absolute Light and Wisdom; called “black” because it is incomprehensible to our finite intellects.

<term>Black Magic</term> (*Occult*.). Sorcery; necromancy, or the raising of the dead, and other selfish abuses of abnormal powers. This abuse may be unintentional; yet it is still “black magic” whenever anything is produced phenomenally simply for one’s own gratification.

<term>B’ne Alhim</term> or *Benî Elohim* (*Heb*.). “Sons of God,” literally or more correctly “Sons of the gods,” as Elohim is the plural of Eloah. A group of angelic powers related by analogy to the Sephira *Hôd*. [w.w.w.]

## Boat of the Sun.
This sacred solar boat was called *Sekti*, and it was steered by the dead. Among the Egyptians, the highest exaltation of the Sun was in *Aries* and the depression in *Libra*. (See “Pharaoh,” the “Son of the Sun”). A blue light—which is the “Sun’s Son”—is seen streaming from the bark <note>A small ship or sailing vessel</note>. The ancient Egyptians taught that the real color of the Sun was blue, and Macrobius also states that its color is a pure blue before it reaches the horizon and after it disappears below. It is curious to note in this regard the fact that it was only in 1881 that physicists and astronomers discovered that “our Sun is really blue.” Professor Langley devoted many years to confirming this fact. Assisted by the magnificent scientific apparatus of physical science, he finally succeeded in proving that the apparent yellow-orange color of the Sun is due only to the effect of absorption exerted by its atmosphere of vapors, which are chiefly metallic. In sober truth and reality, it is not “a white Sun but a blue one”—something which the Egyptian priests had discovered without any known scientific instruments many thousands of years ago!

## Boaz (*Heb.*).
The great-grandfather of David. The word comes from *B*, meaning “in,” and *oz*, meaning “strength,” a symbolic name of one of the pillars at the porch of King Solomon’s temple. [w.w.w.]

## Bodha-Bodhi (*Sk.*).
Wisdom-knowledge.

## Bodhi or Sambodhi (*Sk.*).
Receptive intelligence, as opposed to *Buddhi*, which is the potentiality of intelligence.

## Bodhi Druma (*Sk.*).
The *Bo* or *Bodhi* tree; the tree of “knowledge,” the *Pippala* or *ficus religiosa* in botany. It is the tree under which Sâkyamuni meditated for seven years and then reached Buddhaship. It is claimed that it was originally 400 feet high; but when Hiouen-Tsang <note>The 7th-century Chinese Buddhist monk Xuanzang</note> saw it, around the year 640 of our era, it was only 50 feet high. Cuttings from it have been carried all over the Buddhist world and are planted in front of almost every Vihâra or famous temple in China, Siam, Ceylon, and Tibet.

## Bodhidharma (*Sk.*).
Wisdom-religion; or the wisdom contained in *Dharma* (ethics). Also the name of a great Arhat *Kshatriya* (one of the warrior caste), the son of a king. It was Panyatara, his guru, who “gave him the name Bodhidharma to mark his understanding (bodhi) of the Law (dharma) of Buddha.” (Chin. San. Dict.). Bodhidharma, who flourished in the sixth century, traveled to China, to which he brought a precious relic: the almsbowl of the Lord Buddha.

## Bodhisattva (*Sk.*).
Literally, “he whose essence (*sattva*) has become intelligence (*bodhi*)”; those who need only one more incarnation to become perfect Buddhas, that is, to be entitled to Nirvâna. This applies to *Manushi* (terrestrial) Buddhas. In the metaphysical sense, *Bodhisattva* is a title given to the sons of the celestial *Dhyâni* Buddhas.

## Bodhyanga (*Sk.*).
Literally, the seven branches of knowledge or understanding. One of the 37 categories of the *Bodhi pakchika dharma*.

**Bono, Peter.** A Lombard; a great adept in the Hermetic Science, who traveled to Persia to study Alchemy. Returning from his voyage, he settled in Istria in 1330 and became famous as a Rosicrucian. A Calabrian monk named Lacinius is credited with having published in 1702 a condensed version of Bono’s works on the transmutation of metals. There is, however, more of Lacinius than of Bono in the work. Bono was a genuine adept and an Initiate; and such people do not leave their secrets behind them in MSS <note>manuscripts</note>.

**Boodhasp (*Chald.*).** An alleged Chaldean; but in esoteric teaching, he is a Buddhist (a Bodhisattva) from the East, who was the founder of the esoteric school of Neo-Sabeism, and whose secret rite of baptism passed entirely into the Christian rite of the same name. For almost three centuries before our era, Buddhist monks overran the whole country of Syria, made their way into the Mesopotamian valley, and even visited Ireland. The names *Ferho* and *Faho* of the *Codex Nazaræus* are but a corruption of Fho, Fo, and Pho—the names which the Chinese, Tibetans, and even Nepalese often give to Buddha.

**Book of the Dead.** An ancient Egyptian ritualistic and occult work attributed to Thoth-Hermes. It is found in the coffins of ancient mummies.

**Book of the Keys.** An ancient Kabbalistic work.

**Borj (*Pers.*).** The World Mountain, a volcano or fire-mountain; the same as the Indian Meru.

**Borri, Joseph Francis.** A great Hermetic philosopher, born at Milan in the 17th century. He was an adept, an alchemist, and a devoted occultist. He knew too much and was, therefore, condemned to death for heresy in January 1661, after the death of Pope Innocent X. He escaped and lived for many years afterward, until he was finally recognized by a monk in a Turkish village, denounced, claimed by the Papal Nuncio, taken back to Rome, and imprisoned on August 10th, 1675. But facts show that he escaped from his prison in a way no one could account for.

**Borsippa (*Chald.*).** The planet-tower, wherein Bel was worshipped in the days when star-worshippers <note>astrolaters</note> were the greatest astronomers. It was dedicated to Nebo, the god of Wisdom. (See "Birs Nimrud".)

**Both-al (*Irish*).** The Both-al of the Irish is the descendant and copy of the Greek Batylos and the Beth-el of Canaan, the "house of God" (*q.v.* <note>Latin "quod vide," meaning "which see"</note>).

**Bragadini, Marco Antonio.** A Venetian Rosicrucian of great achievements, an Occultist and Kabbalist who was beheaded in 1595 in Bavaria for making gold.

**Bragi (*Scand.*).** The god of New Life, of the reincarnation of nature and man. He is called "the divine singer" without spot or blemish. He is represented as gliding in the ship of the Dwarfs of Death during

the death of nature (*pralaya*), lying asleep on the deck with his golden-stringed harp near him and dreaming the dream of life. When the vessel crosses the threshold of Nain, the Dwarf of Death, Bragi awakes and, sweeping the strings of his harp, sings a song that echoes over all the worlds. This song describes the rapture of existence and awakens silent, sleeping nature out of her long death-like sleep.

**Brahma** (*Sk.*). The student must distinguish between Brahma the neuter and Brahmâ the male creator of the Indian Pantheon. The former, Brahma or Brahman, is the impersonal, supreme, and unknowable Principle of the Universe, from whose essence everything emanates and into which everything returns. It is incorporeal, immaterial, unborn, eternal, without beginning, and without end. It is all-pervading, animating the highest god as well as the smallest mineral atom. Brahmâ, on the other hand—the male and the alleged Creator—exists periodically in his manifestation only, and then returns to *pralaya*; that is, he disappears and is annihilated.

**Brahmâ's Day.** A period of 2,160,000,000 years during which Brahmâ—having emerged from his golden egg (*Hiranyagarbha*)—creates and fashions the material world (acting simply as the fertilizing and creative force in Nature). After this period, the worlds being destroyed in turn by fire and water, he vanishes along with objective nature, and then follows Brahmâ's Night.

**Brahmâ's Night.** A period of equal duration, during which Brahmâ is said to be asleep. Upon awakening, he begins the process again, and this continues for an AGE of Brahmâ, composed of alternating "Days" and "Nights" and lasting 100 years (each year consisting of 360 "Days" and "Nights" of 2,160,000,000 years each). It takes fifteen digits to express the duration of such an age; after it expires, the *Mahapralaya*, or the Great Dissolution, begins and lasts in its turn for the same duration of fifteen digits.

**Brahmâ Prajâpati** (*Sk.*). "Brahmâ, the Progenitor," literally the "Lord of Creatures." In this aspect, Brahmâ is the synthesis of the Prajâpati or creative forces.

**Brahmâ Vâch** (*Sk.*). Male and female Brahmâ. Vâch is also sometimes called the female Logos; for Vâch literally means "Speech." (See *Manu*, Book I, and *Vishnu Purâna*).

**Brahma Vidyâ** (*Sk.*). The knowledge or esoteric science regarding the two Brahmas and their true nature.

**Brahmâ Virâj** (*Sk.*). The same: Brahmâ, separating his body into two halves—male and female—creates Vâch and Virâj within them. In simpler and esoteric terms, Brahmâ (the Universe), through differentiation, produced material nature (Virâj) and spiritual, intelligent Nature (Vâch)—which is the Logos of Deity or the manifested expression of eternal divine Ideation.

**Brahmâcharî** (*Sk.*). A Brahmin ascetic; one vowed to celibacy—essentially a monk or a religious student.

# GLOSSARY

**Brahmâjnâni** *(Sk.).* One possessed of complete Knowledge; an *Illuminatus* in esoteric language.

**Brâhman** *(Sk.).* The highest of the four castes in India; one who is supposed—or rather, who imagines himself—to be as high among men as Brahman, the ABSOLUTE of the Vedas, is high among or above the gods.

**Brâhmana period** *(Sk.).* One of the four periods into which Vedic literature has been divided by scholars of the Orient.

**Brâhmanas** *(Sk.).* Hindu Sacred Books. Works composed by and for Brahmans. These are commentaries on those portions of the Vedas that were intended for the ritualistic use and guidance of the "twice-born" (Dwija) or Brahmans.

**Brahmanaspati** *(Sk.).* The planet Jupiter; a deity in the *Rig-Veda*, known in exoteric works as Brihaspati, whose wife Târâ was carried away by Soma (the Moon). This led to a war between the gods and the Asuras.

**Brahmâpuri** *(Sk.).* Literally, "the City of Brahmâ."

**Brahmâputras** *(Sk.).* The Sons of Brahmâ.

**Brahmarandhra** *(Sk.).* A spot on the crown of the head connected to the heart by the *Sushumna*, a cord in the spinal column. A mystic term that has significance only in mysticism.

**Brahmârshîs** *(Sk.).* The Brahminical Rishis.

**Bread and Wine.** Baptism and the Eucharist have their direct origin in pagan Egypt. There, the "waters of purification" were used (the Mithraic font for baptism being borrowed by the Persians from the Egyptians), as were bread and wine. "Wine in the Dionysian cult, as in the Christian religion, represents that blood which, in different senses, is the life of the world" (Brown, in *The Dionysiak Myth*). Justin Martyr says, "In imitation of which the devil did the same in the Mysteries of Mithras, for you either know or may know *that they also take bread and a cup of water in the sacrifices of those who are initiated and pronounce certain words over it*." (See "Holy Water".)

**Briareus** *(Gr.).* A famous giant in the *Theogony* of Hesiod. The son of Coelus and Terra, he was a monster with 50 heads and 100 arms. He is prominent in the wars and battles between the gods.

**Briatic World** or *Briah* *(Heb.).* This world is the second of the Four worlds of the Kabbalists and refers to the highest created "Arch-angels," or to Pure Spirits. [w.w.w.]

**Bride.** The tenth Sephira, Malkuth, is called by the Kabbalists the Bride of Microprosopus; she is the final Hé of the Tetragrammaton; in a similar manner, the Christian Church is called the Bride of Christ. [w.w.w.]

**Brihadâranyaka** *(Sk.).* The name of an *Upanishad*. One of the sacred and *secret* books of the Brahmins; an *Aranyaka* is a treatise appended to the Vedas and considered a subject of special study by those
