**Brihaspati** (*Sk*.). The name of a deity, and also of a *Rishi*. It is likewise the name of the planet Jupiter. He is the personified *Guru* and priest of the gods in India; he is also the symbol of exoteric ritualism as opposed to esoteric mysticism. Hence, he is the opponent of King Soma—the moon, but also the sacred juice drunk at initiation—the parent of Budha, Secret Wisdom.

**Briseus** (*Gr*.). A name given to the god Bacchus after his nurse, *Brisô*. He also had a temple at Brisa, a promontory on the island of Lesbos.

**Brothers of the Shadow**. A name given by Occultists to sorcerers, and especially to the Tibetan *Dugpas*, many of whom are found in the Bhon sect of the Red Caps (*Dugpa*). The term is applied to all practitioners of black or *left-hand magic*.

**Bubasté** (*Eg*.). A city in Egypt that was sacred to cats, and where their principal shrine was located. Many hundreds of thousands of cats were embalmed and buried in the caves of Beni-Hassan-el-Amar. Since the cat was a symbol of the moon, it was sacred to Isis, its goddess. It sees in the dark, and its eyes have a phosphorescent luster that frightens night birds of evil omen. The cat was also sacred to Bast, and was therefore called “the destroyer of the Sun’s (Osiris’) enemies.”

**Buddha** (*Sk*.). *Literally*, “The Enlightened.” The highest degree of knowledge. To become a Buddha, one must break through the bondage of sense and personality; one must acquire a complete perception of the REAL SELF and learn not to separate it from all other selves. One must learn by experience, above all, the utter unreality of all phenomena in the visible Kosmos; one must reach a complete detachment from all that is evanescent and finite, and live while still on Earth in the immortal and the everlasting alone, in a supreme state of holiness.

**Buddha Siddhârta** (*Sk*.). The name given to Gautama, the Prince of Kapilavastu, at his birth. It is an abbreviation of *Sarvârthasiddha* and means the “realization of all desires.” *Gautama*, which means “the most victorious (*tama*) on earth (*gau*),” was the priestly name of the Sâkya family, the royal patronymic of the dynasty to which Gautama’s father, King Suddhodhana of Kapilavastu, belonged. Kapilavastu was an ancient city and the birthplace of the Great Reformer; it was destroyed during his lifetime. In the title *Sâkyamuni*, the last part, *muni*, is translated as meaning one who is “mighty in charity, isolation, and silence,” and the first part, *Sâkya*, is the family name. Every Orientalist or Pundit knows the story of Gautama Buddha by heart—the most perfect of mortal men the world has ever seen—but none of them seem to suspect the esoteric meaning underlying his prenatal biography, that is, the significance of the popular story. The *Lalitavistâra* tells the tale but abstains from hinting at the truth. The 5,000 *Jâtakas*, or the accounts of former births (reincarnations), are taken literally

Yet the detailed account of these, and the statement that during them he worked his way up through every stage of transmigration—from the lowest animate and inanimate atom and insect up to the highest, or *man*—contains simply the well-known occult aphorism: “a stone becomes a plant, a plant an animal, and an animal a man.” Every human being who has ever existed has passed through the same evolution. But the hidden symbolism in the sequence of these rebirths (*jâtaka*) contains a perfect history of evolution on this earth, both *pre-* and *post-*human, and is a scientific exposition of natural facts. One truth that is not veiled but bare and open is found in their nomenclature—namely, that as soon as Gautama had reached the human form, he began exhibiting the utmost unselfishness, self-sacrifice, and charity in every personality.

Buddha Gautama, the fourth of the Sapta (Seven) Buddhas and Sapta Tathâgatas, was born according to Chinese chronology in 1024 B.C.; but according to the Sinhalese chronicles, on the 8th day of the second (or fourth) moon in the year 621 before our era. He fled from his father’s palace to become an ascetic on the night of the 8th day of the second moon, 597 B.C. Having passed six years in ascetic meditation at Gaya and perceiving that physical self-torture was useless for bringing enlightenment, he decided to strike out on a new path until he reached the state of Bodhi. He became a full Buddha on the night of the 8th day of the twelfth moon in the year 592, and finally entered Nirvâna in the year 543, according to Southern Buddhism. Orientalists, however, have decided upon several other dates.

All the rest is allegorical. He attained the state of Bodhisattva on earth when in the personality called Prabhâpala. Tushita stands for a place on this globe, not for a paradise in the invisible regions. The selection of the Sâkya family and his mother Mâyâ as “the purest on earth” is in accordance with the model of the nativity of every Savior, God, or deified Reformer. The tale about his entering his mother’s womb in the shape of a white elephant is an allusion to his innate wisdom, as an elephant of that color is a symbol of every Bodhisattva. The statements that at Gautama’s birth the newborn babe walked seven steps in four directions, that an Udumbara flower bloomed in all its rare beauty, and that the Nâga kings immediately proceeded “to baptize him,” are all allegories in the terminology of the Initiates and are well understood by every Eastern Occultist. The entire events of his noble life are given in occult numbers, and every so-called miraculous event—so lamented by Orientalists as confusing the narrative and making it impossible to separate truth from fiction—is simply the allegorical veiling of the truth. It is as comprehensible to an Occultist learned in symbolism as it is difficult to understand for a European scholar ignorant of Occultism. For instance, after reminding his disciples of the immortality of the *Dharmakâya*, Buddha is said to have passed into *Samâdhi* and lost himself in Nirvana—*from which no one can return*. Yet, despite this, the Buddha is shown bursting open the coffin's lid and stepping out of it, saluting with folded hands his mother Mâyâ. She had suddenly appeared in the air, even though she had died seven days after his birth, and so on. Since Buddha was a *Chakravartti* (one who turns the wheel of the Law), his body could not be consumed by ordinary fire during its cremation. What happens? Suddenly, a jet of flame burst out of the *Svastica on his chest* and reduced his body to ashes. Limited space prevents giving more examples. Regarding his status as one of the true and undeniable SAVIOURS of the world, it is enough to say that even the most fanatical orthodox missionary—unless he is hopelessly insane or has no regard for historical truth—cannot find a single accusation against the life and personal character of Gautama, the "Buddha." Without claiming divinity, and allowing his followers to lean toward atheism rather than the degrading superstition of *deva* or idol worship, his path in life was holy and divine from beginning to end. During the 45 years of his mission, he was as blameless and pure as a god—or as a god ought to be. He is a perfect example of a divine, godly man. He reached Buddhahood—that is, complete enlightenment—entirely through his own merit and individual efforts, as no god is supposed to have any personal merit in the practice of goodness and holiness. Esoteric teachings claim that he renounced Nirvana and gave up the *Dharmakâya* garment to remain a "Buddha of compassion" within reach of the miseries of this world. The religious philosophy he left behind has produced generations of good and unselfish men for over 2,000 years. His is the only absolutely bloodless religion among all existing religions: it is tolerant and liberal, teaching universal compassion and charity, love and self-sacrifice, poverty, and contentment with one’s lot, whatever it may be. No persecutions or enforcement of faith by fire and sword have ever disgraced it. No god who vomits thunder and lightning has interfered with its pure commandments; and if the simple, humane, and philosophical code of daily life left to us by the greatest human reformer ever known were ever to be adopted by mankind at large, then indeed an era of bliss and peace would dawn for humanity.

**Buddhachhâyâ** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, "the shadow of Buddha." It is said to become visible during certain great events and imposing ceremonies performed at temples in commemoration of glorious acts of Buddha’s life. Hiouen-tseng, the Chinese traveler, names a certain cave where it occasionally appears on the wall, but adds that only he "whose mind is perfectly pure" can see it.

**Buddhaphala** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, "the fruit of Buddha," the fruition of *Arahattvaphala*, or Arhatship.

**Buddhism.** <term>Buddhism</term> is now split into two distinct Churches: the Southern and the Northern Church. The former is said to be the purer form, as it has more religiously preserved the original teachings of the Lord <term>Buddha</term>. It is the religion of <term>Ceylon</term>, <term>Siam</term>, <term>Burmah</term>, and other places, while Northern <term>Buddhism</term> is confined to <term>Tibet</term>, <term>China</term>, and <term>Nepaul</term>. Such a distinction, however, is incorrect. If the <term>Southern Church</term> is closer—in that it has not departed, except perhaps in some trifling dogmas due to the many councils held after the death of the <term>MASTER</term>, from the public or *exoteric* teachings of <term>Sâkyamuni</term>—the <term>Northern Church</term> is the result of <term>Siddhârta Buddha</term>’s *esoteric* teachings, which he confined to his elect <term>Bhikshus</term> and <term>Arhats</term>. In fact, <term>Buddhism</term> in the present age cannot be justly judged by either one or the other of its *exoteric* popular forms. Real <term>Buddhism</term> can be appreciated only by blending the philosophy of the <term>Southern Church</term> and the metaphysics of the <term>Northern Schools</term>. If one seems too iconoclastic and stern, and the other too metaphysical and transcendental—even to the point of being overgrown with the weeds of Indian *exotericism*, many of the gods of its <term>Pantheon</term> having been transplanted under new names to <term>Tibetan</term> soil—it is entirely due to the popular expression of <term>Buddhism</term> in both Churches. In their correspondence to each other, they stand as <term>Protestantism</term> does to <term>Roman Catholicism</term>. Both err through an excess of zeal and erroneous interpretations, though neither the <term>Southern</term> nor the <term>Northern Buddhist clergy</term> has ever consciously departed from the truth, and even less have they acted under the dictates of *priestocracy*, ambition, or with an eye to personal gain and power, as the two Christian Churches have.

**Buddhochinga** (*Sk*.). The name of a great Indian <term>Arhat</term> who went to <term>China</term> in the 4th century to spread <term>Buddhism</term> and converted masses of people by means of miracles and most wonderful magical feats.

**Budha** (*Sk*.). “The Wise and Intelligent,” the Son of <term>Soma</term> (the <term>Moon</term>), and of <term>Rokini</term> or <term>Taraka</term>, wife of <term>Brihaspati</term> who was carried away by King <term>Soma</term>; this led to the great war between the <term>Asuras</term>, who sided with the <term>Moon</term>, and the <term>Gods</term> who defended <term>Brihaspati</term> (Jupiter), who was their *Purohita* (family priest). This war is known as the *Tarakamaya*. It is the original version of the war in <term>Olympus</term> between the <term>Gods</term> and the <term>Titans</term> and also of the war (in *Revelation*) between <term>Michael</term> (<term>Indra</term>) and the <term>Dragon</term> (personifying the <term>Asuras</term>).

**Bull-Worship** (See “<term>Apis</term>”). The ram-headed gods all belong to the latter aspect, while the bull belongs to the former. <term>Osiris</term>, to whom the bull was sacred, was never regarded as a <term>phallic deity</term>; neither was <term>Siva</term> with his <term>Bull Nandi</term>, despite the *lingham*. Those who view the solar gods and the bulls as having a phallic character, or who connect the Sun with such symbolism, are mistaken. It is only the lunar gods, the rams, and the lambs that are priapic. It is hardly appropriate for a religion—which, however unconsciously, has adopted a pre-eminently lunar god for its worship and emphasized its choice by selecting the lamb (whose sire is the ram—a symbol just as pre-eminently phallic) as its most sacred symbol—to disparage older religions for using the same symbolism. **Butler.** An English name assumed by an <term>adept</term>, a disciple of some Eastern Sages, about whom many fanciful stories circulate. It is said, for instance, that Butler was captured during his travels in 1629 and sold into captivity. He became the slave of an Arabian philosopher, a great <term>alchemist</term>, and finally escaped, robbing his master of a large quantity of <term>red powder</term>. According to more reliable records, only the last portion of this story is true. Adepts who could be robbed without their knowledge would be unworthy of the name. Butler, or rather the person who assumed this name, robbed his "master" (whose free disciple he was) of the *secret of transmutation* and misused his knowledge—that is, he sought to turn it to his personal profit, but was quickly punished for it. After performing many wonderful cures by means of his "stone" (meaning the <term>occult knowledge</term> of an initiated adept) and producing extraordinary phenomena—to some of which Val Helmont <note>Likely referring to Jan Baptista van Helmont (1580–1644), the Flemish chemist and physician.</note>, the famous <term>Occultist</term> and <term>Rosicrucian</term>, was a witness—not for the benefit of humanity but for his own vainglory, Butler was imprisoned in the Castle of Viloord in Flanders and passed almost the whole of his life in confinement. He lost his powers and died miserable and unknown. Such is the fate of every Occultist who misuses his power or desecrates the sacred science.

**Bythos** (*Gr.*). A <term>Gnostic</term> term meaning "Depth" or the "great Deep." <term>Chaos</term>. It is equivalent to space, before anything had formed itself within it from the primordial atoms that exist eternally in its spatial depths, according to the teachings of <term>Occultism</term>.

## C.

**C.**—The third letter of the English alphabet, which has no equivalent in Hebrew except *Caph* (see under **K**).

<term>Cabar Zio</term> (*Gnostic*). “The mighty Lord of Splendor” (*Codex Nazarœus*); those who procreate seven beneficent lives, “who shine in their own form and light” to counteract the influence of the seven “badly-disposed” stars or principles. These are the offspring of Kar-abtanos, the personification of lust and matter. The latter are the seven physical planets; the former are their genii or Rulers.

<term>Cabeiri or Kabiri</term> (*Phœnician*). Deities held in the highest veneration at Thebes, Lemnos, Phrygia, Macedonia, and especially at Samothrace. They were mystery gods, and no uninitiated person had the right to name or speak of them. Herodotus identifies them as fire-gods and points to Vulcan as their father. The Kabiri presided over the Mysteries, and their true number has never been revealed, as their occult meaning is very sacred.

<term>Cabletow</term> (*Masonic*). A Masonic term for a specific object used in the Lodges. Its origin lies in the thread of the Brahman ascetics—a thread which is also used for magical purposes in Tibet.

<term>Cadmus</term> (*Greek*). The reputed inventor of the letters of the alphabet. He may have been their originator and teacher in Europe and Asia Minor; however, in India, letters were known and used by the Initiates ages before his time.

<term>Caduceus</term> (*Greek*). The Greek poets and mythologists took the idea of the Caduceus of Mercury from the Egyptians. The Caduceus is found as two serpents entwined around a rod on Egyptian monuments built before the time of Osiris. The Greeks altered this. We find it again in the hands of Aesculapius, taking a different form than the wand of Mercurius or Hermes. It is a cosmic, sidereal (astral), or astronomical symbol, as well as a spiritual and even physiological one; its significance changes depending on its application. Metaphysically, the Caduceus represents the descent of primeval and primordial matter into dense terrestrial matter—the one Reality becoming Illusion. (See <note>The Secret Doctrine, Volume I, page 550.</note> *Sect. Doct. I. 550.*) Astronomically, the head and tail represent the points of the ecliptic where the planets, and even the sun and moon, meet in close embrace. Physiologically, it is the symbol of the restoration of the equilibrium lost between Life, as a unit, and the currents of life performing various functions in the human body.

<term>Cæsar</term>. A famous astrologer and “professor of magic” (that is, an Occultist) during the reign of Henry IV of France. “He was reputed to have been strangled by the devil in 1611,” as Brother Kenneth Mackenzie tells us.

# GLOSSARY

**Cagliostro.** A famous Adept, whose real name is claimed (by his enemies) to have been Joseph Balsamo. He was a native of Palermo and studied under a mysterious foreigner of whom little has been discovered. His accepted history is too well known to need repetition, and his real history has never been told. His fate was that of every human being who proves that he knows more than his fellow creatures; he was "stoned to death" by persecutions, lies, and infamous accusations, and yet he was the friend and adviser of the highest and mightiest of every land he visited. He was finally tried and sentenced in Rome as a heretic and was said to have died during his confinement in a state prison. (See "*Mesmer*.") Yet his end was not entirely undeserved, as he had been untrue to his vows in some respects, had fallen from his state of chastity, and yielded to ambition and selfishness.

**Cain** or *Kayn (Hebrew)*. In esoteric symbology, he is said to be identical with Jehovah or the "Lord God" of the fourth chapter of *Genesis*. It is held, moreover, that Abel is not his brother, but his female aspect. (See *Secret Doctrine*, under the entry.)

**Calvary Cross.** This form of cross does not date from Christianity. It was known and used for mystical purposes thousands of years before our era. It formed an integral part of various rituals in Egypt and Greece, in Babylon and India, as well as in China, Mexico, and Peru. It is a cosmic as well as a physiological (or phallic) symbol. That it existed among all the "heathen" nations is testified to by Tertullian. "How does the Athenian Minerva differ from the body of a cross?" he asks. "The origin of your gods is derived from figures molded on a cross. All those rows of images on your standards are the appendages of crosses; those hangings on your banners are the robes of crosses." And the fiery champion was right. The *tau* or **T** is the most ancient of all forms, and the cross or the *tat* (see entry) is just as ancient. The *crux ansata*, the cross with a handle, is in the hands of almost every god, including Baal and the Phoenician Astarte. The *croix cramponnée* is the Indian *Swastika*. It has been exhumed from the lowest foundations of the ancient site of Troy, and it appears on Etruscan and Chaldean relics of antiquity. As Mrs. Jamieson shows: "The *ankh* of Egypt was the crutch of St. Anthony and the cross of St. Philip. The *Labarum* of Constantine . . . . was an emblem long before in Etruria. Osiris had the *Labarum* for his sign; Horus appears sometimes with the long Latin cross. The Greek pectoral cross is Egyptian. It was called by the Church Fathers 'the devil's invention before Christ.' The *crux ansata* is upon the old coins of Tarsus, just as the Maltese cross is upon the breast of an Assyrian king. . . . The cross of Calvary, so common in Europe, occurs on the breasts of mummies. . . . It was suspended around the necks of sacred serpents in Egypt. . . . Strange Asiatic tribes bringing tribute to Egypt are noticed with garments studded with crosses, and Sir Gardner Wilkinson dates this picture to <term>1500 B.C.</term>" Finally, "*Typhon*, the Evil One, is chained by a cross!" (*Egyptian Belief and Modern Thought*).

### **Campanella**, *Tomaso*. A Calabrian, born in 1568, who from his childhood displayed strange powers and dedicated his entire life to the Occult Arts. The story claiming he was initiated into the secrets of alchemy during his boyhood and thoroughly instructed in the secret science by a Rabbi-Kabbalist in a fortnight by means of *notaricon* is a ridiculous invention. Occult knowledge, even when inherited from a previous birth, does not return to a new personality within fifteen days. He became an opponent of the Aristotelian materialistic philosophy while in Naples and was forced to flee for his life. Later, the Inquisition attempted to try and condemn him for the practice of magic arts, but its efforts were defeated. During his lifetime, he wrote a vast number of magical, astrological, and alchemical works, most of which are no longer in existence. He is reported to have died in the Jacobin convent in Paris on May 21, 1639.

### **Canarese.** The language of the Karnataka region, originally called Kanara, one of the divisions of South India.

### **Capricornus** (*Lat.*). The 10th sign of the Zodiac (*Makâra* in Sanskrit), considered—on account of its hidden meaning—the most important among the constellations of the mysterious Zodiac. It is fully described in the *Secret Doctrine* and therefore requires only a few more words. Whether, according to exoteric statements, Capricornus was related in any way to the wet-nurse Amalthea who fed Jupiter with her milk, or whether it was the god Pan who transformed himself into a goat and left his mark upon the celestial records, matters little. Each of these fables has its significance. Everything in Nature is intimately connected to the rest; therefore, students of ancient lore will not be overly surprised to be told that even the seven steps taken in the direction of each of the four points of the compass—totaling 28 steps—taken by the newborn infant Buddha are closely related to the 28 stars of the constellation of Capricornus.

### **Cardan**, *Jérôme*. An astrologer, alchemist, kabbalist, and mystic well-known in literature. He was born at Pavia in 1501 and died at Rome in 1576.

### **Carnac.** A very ancient site in Brittany (France) containing a temple of massive stone structure sacred to the Sun and the Dragon; it is of the same type as Karnak in ancient Egypt and Stonehenge in England. (See "The Origin of the Satanic Myth" in *Archaic Symbolism*.) It was built by the prehistoric high priests of the Solar Dragon, or symbolized Wisdom (the Solar *Kumâras* who incarnated being the highest). Each of the stones was personally placed there by the successive adept-priests in power and commemorated in symbolic language the degree of power, status, and knowledge of each. (See further *Secret Doctrine* II. 381, and following, and also "Karnak".)

### **Caste.** Originally the system of the four hereditary classes into which the Indian population was divided: Brahman, Kshatriya, Vaisya,

**Causal Body.** This "body," which is not actually a body in either an objective or subjective sense, but is *Buddhi*, the Spiritual Soul, is named such because it is the direct cause of the *Sushupti* (deep sleep) condition, leading to the *Turya* state, the highest state of *Samâdhi*. It is called *Kâranopâdhi*, "the basis of the Cause," by the *Raja Yoga* practitioners; and in the Vedanta system, it corresponds to both the *Vignânamaya* and *Anandamaya Kosha*. The latter comes next to *Atma* and is therefore the vehicle of the universal Spirit. *Buddhi* alone could not be called a "Causal Body," but it becomes so in conjunction with *Manas*, the incarnating Entity or Ego.

**Cazotte, *Jacques*.** The remarkable seer who predicted the beheading of several royal personages and his own decapitation at a lively supper some time before the first French Revolution. He was born at Dijon in 1720 and studied mystic philosophy in the school of Martinez Pasqualis at Lyons. On September 11, 1791, he was arrested and condemned to death by the president of the revolutionary government—a man who, shameful to state, had been his fellow student and a member of the Mystic Lodge of Pasqualis at Lyons. Cazotte was executed on September 25 on the Place du Carrousel.

**Cecco d'Ascoli.** Surnamed "Francesco Stabili." He lived in the thirteenth century and was considered the most famous astrologer of his day. A work of his published at Basle in 1485, called *Commentarii in Sphæram Joannis de Sacrobosco*, is still in existence. He was burnt alive by the Inquisition in 1327.

**Cerberus** (*Gr., Lat.*). Cerberus, the three-headed canine monster who was supposed to watch at the threshold of Hades, came to the Greeks and Romans from Egypt. It was the monster—half-dog and half-hippopotamus—that guarded the gates of Amenti. The mother of Cerberus was *Echidna*, a being half-woman and half-serpent, who was much honored in Etruria. Both the Egyptian and Greek Cerberus are symbols of Kâmaloka and its uncouth monsters, the discarded shells of mortals.

**Ceres** (*Lat.*). In Greek, *Demeter*. As the female aspect of Pater Aether <note>The original text reads "Peter Æther," likely a typo for Pater (Father) Ether</note> or Jupiter, she is esoterically the productive principle in the all-pervading Spirit that quickens every germ in the material universe.

**Chabrat Zereh Aur Bokher** (*Heb.*). An order of Rosicrucian origin whose members study the Kabbalah and Hermetic sciences; it admits both sexes and has many grades of instruction. The members meet in private, and the very existence of the Order is generally unknown. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**Chadâyatana** (*Sk.*). Literally, the six dwellings or *gates* in man for the reception of sensations. Thus, on the physical plane, these are the eyes, nose, ears, tongue, body (or touch), and mind as a product of the physical brain; and on the mental plane (esoterically), they are spiritual sight, smell, hear—

**Chaitanya (Sk.).** The founder of a mystical sect in India. A relatively modern sage, believed to be an *avatar* of Krishna.

**Chakna-padma-karpo (Tib.).** "He who holds the lotus," used for *Chenresi*, the Bodhisattva. It is not a purely Tibetan word, but half Sanskrit.

**Chakshub (Sk.).** The "eye." *Loka-chakshub*, or "the eye of the world," is a title for the Sun.

**Chaldean Book of Numbers.** A work that contains everything found in the *Zohar* of Simeon Ben-Jochai, and much more. It must be older by many centuries, and in one sense its original, as it contains all the fundamental principles taught in the Jewish Kabbalistic works but none of their blinds <note>intentional veils or symbolic diversions used to hide secrets from the uninitiated</note>. **Chaldeans,** or *Kasdim.* At first a tribe, then a caste of learned Kabbalists. They were the scholars, the magicians of Babylonia, astrologers, and diviners. The famous Hillel, the precursor to Jesus in philosophy and ethics, was a Chaldean. Franck, in his *Kabbala*, points to the close resemblance between the "secret doctrine" found in the *Avesta* and the religious metaphysics of the Chaldeans.

**Chandra (Sk.).** The Moon; also a deity. The terms *Chandra* and *Soma* are synonyms.

**Chandragupta (Sk.).** The first Buddhist King in India and the grandfather of Asoka; he is the *Sandracottus* mentioned by the clumsy Greek writers who traveled to India in Alexander’s time. (See "*Asoka*".)

**Chandra-kanta (Sk.).** "The moon-stone," a gem claimed to be formed and developed under moonbeams, which give it occult and magical properties. It has a very cooling effect on fever if applied to both temples.

**Chandramanam (Sk.).** The method of calculating time by the Moon.

**Chandrayana (Sk.).** The lunar year chronology.

**Chandra-vansa (Sk.).** The "Lunar Race," in contrast to *Suryavansa*, the "Solar Race." However, this reveals the deep occult meaning of the *Avatar*, a meaning that only esoteric philosophy can explain. She is the vulture-headed Goddess found in the oldest period of Abydos, who belongs—according to Mariette Bey—to the first Dynasty. This would make her about 7,000 years old, even by the admission of those Orientalists who tend to downplay historical timelines. As Mr. Bonwick tells us in his excellent work on Egyptian belief: "Neïth, Nut, Nepte, Nuk (her names as variously read!) is a philosophical conception worthy of the nineteenth century after the Christian era, rather than the thirty-ninth before it or earlier than that." And he adds: "Neïth or Nout is neither more nor less than the Great Mother, and yet the Immaculate Virgin, or female God from whom all things proceeded." Neïth is the "Father-Mother" of the *Stanzas of the Secret Doctrine*, the Swabhâvat of the Northern Buddhists—the truly immaculate Mother and the prototype of the latest "Virgin" of all; for, as Sharpe says, "the Feast of Candlemas—in honor of...

**Charnock, Thomas.** A great alchemist of the sixteenth century; a surgeon who lived and practiced near Salisbury, studying the art in some neighboring cloisters with a priest. It is said that he was initiated into the final secret of transmutation by the famous mystic William Bird, who "had been a prior of Bath and paid the expense of repairing the Abbey Church from the gold which he made by the red and white elixirs" (*Royal Mas. Cycl.*). Charnock wrote his *Breviary of Philosophy* in the year 1557 and the *Enigma of Alchemy* in 1574.

**Charon** (*Gr.*). The Egyptian *Khu-en-ua*, the hawk-headed Steersman of the boat conveying the Souls across the black waters that separate life from death. Charon, the Son of Erebus and Nox, is a variant of Khu-en-ua. The dead were obliged to pay an *obolus*, a small piece of money, to this grim ferryman of the Styx and Acheron; therefore the ancients always placed a coin under the tongue of the deceased. This custom has been preserved in our own times, for most of the lower classes in Russia place coppers in the coffin under the head of the dead for *post-mortem* expenses.

**Chârvâka** (*Sk.*). There were two famous beings of this name. One a <term>Rakshasa</term> (demon) who disguised himself as a <term>Brahman</term> and entered <term>Hastinâ-pura</term>; whereupon the <term>Brahmans</term> discovered the imposture and reduced <term>Chârvâka</term> to ashes with the fire of their eyes—that is, magnetically by means of what is called in Occultism the "black glance" or evil eye. The second was a terrible materialist and denier of all but matter, who, if he could come back to life, would put to shame all the "freethinkers" and "agnostics" of the day. He lived before the <term>Ramayanic</term> period, but his teachings and school have survived to this day, and he has even now followers, who are mostly to be found in Bengal.

**Chastanier, Benedict.** A French mason who established in London in 1767 a Lodge called "The Illuminated Theosophists".

**Chatur mukha** (*Sk.*). The "four-faced one", a title of <term>Brahmâ</term>.

**Chatur varna** (*Sk.*). The four castes (*literally*, colors).

**Châturdasa Bhuvanam** (*Sk.*). The fourteen lokas or planes of existence. Esoterically, the dual seven states.

**Chaturyonî** (*Sk.*). Written also *tchatur-yoni*. The same as <term>Karmaya</term> or "the four modes of birth"—four ways of entering on the path of birth as decided by Karma: (a) birth from the womb, as humans and mammals; (b) birth from an egg, as birds and reptiles; (c) from moisture and air-germs, as insects; and (d) by sudden self-transformation, as <term>Bodhisattvas</term> and Gods (<term>Anupadaka</term>).

**Chava** (*Heb.*). The same as Eve: "the Mother of all that lives"; "Life".

**Chelâ** (*Sk.*). A disciple, the pupil of a Guru or Sage, the follower of some adept of a school of philosophy (literally, "child").

**Chemi** (*Eg.*). The ancient name of Egypt.

**Cheru** (*Scand.*). Or Heru. A magic sword, a weapon of the "sword god" Heru. In the *Edda*, the *Saga* describes it as destroying its possessor should he be unworthy of wielding it. It brings victory and fame only in the hand of a virtuous hero.

**Cherubim** (*Heb.*). According to the Kabbalists, a group of angels which they specially associated with the Sephira Jesod. In Christian teaching, an order of angels who are "watchers." *Genesis* places Cherubim to guard the lost Eden, and the Old Testament frequently refers to them as guardians of the divine glory. Two winged representations in gold were placed over the Ark of the Covenant; colossal figures of the same were also placed in the Sanctum Sanctorum of the Temple of Solomon. Ezekiel describes them in poetic language. Each Cherub appears to have been a composite figure with four faces—of a man, eagle, lion, and ox—and was certainly winged. Parkhurst, in his entry for *Cherub*, suggests that the derivation of the word is from *K*, a particle of similarity, and *RB* or *RUB*, meaning greatness, master, or majesty, and thus an image of godhead. Many other nations have displayed similar figures as symbols of deity; for example, the Egyptians in their figures of Serapis, as Macrobius describes in his *Saturnalia*; the Greeks had their triple-headed Hecate, and the Latins had three-faced images of Diana, as Ovid tells us, *ecce procul ternis Hecate variata figuris* <note>"behold from afar Hecate in her three-fold form"</note>. Virgil also describes her in the fourth Book of the *Aeneid*. Porphyry and Eusebius write the same of Proserpine. The Vandals had a many-headed deity they called Triglaf. The ancient German races had an idol, Rodigast, with a human body and the heads of an ox, eagle, and man. The Persians have some figures of Mithras with a man's body, a lion's head, and four wings. Add to these the Chimera, the Sphinx of Egypt, Moloch, Astarte of the Syrians, and some figures of Isis with bull's horns and feathers of a bird on the head. [w.w.w.]

**Chesed** (*Heb.*). "Mercy," also named Gedulah, the fourth of the ten Sephiroth; a masculine or active potency. [w.w.w.]

**Chhâyâ** (*Sk.*). "Shade" or "Shadow." The name of a creature produced by Sanjna, the wife of Surya, from herself (astral body). Unable to endure the intensity of her husband, Sanjna left Chhaya in her place as a wife, going away herself to perform spiritual austerities. Chhaya is the astral image of a person in esoteric philosophy.

**Chhandoga** (*Sk.*). A *Samhita* collection of the *Sama Veda*; also a priest or a chanter of the *Sama Veda*.

**Chhanmûka** (*Sk.*). A great Bodhisattva among Northern Buddhists, famous for his profound love for humanity; he is regarded in esoteric schools as a *Nirmanakâya*.

**Chhannagarikah** (*Tib.*). Literally, "the school of six cities." A famous philosophical school where *Chelas* are prepared before entering the Path.

**Chhassidi** or Chassidim. In the Septuagint, *Assidai*, and in English, *Assideans*. They are also mentioned in *1 Maccabees* 7:13 as being put to death along with many others. They were the followers of Mattathias, the father of the Maccabeans, and were all initiated mystics or Jewish adepts. The word means "skilled" or "learned in all wisdom, both human and divine." Mackenzie (*R.M.C.*) regards them as the guardians of the Temple dedicated to preserving its purity; however, as Solomon and his Temple are both allegorical and had no historical existence, the "Temple" in this case refers to the "body of Israel" and its morality. Scaliger connects this Society of the Assideans with that of the Essenes, considering it to be the predecessor of the latter.

**Chhaya loka** (*Sk.*). The world of Shades; similar to Hades, the world of the *Eidola* and *Umbræ* (ghosts and shadows). We call it *Kâmaloka*.

**Chiah** (*Heb.*). Life; *Vita*, *Revivificatio*. In the Kabbalah, it is the second highest essence of the human soul, corresponding to *Chokmah* (Wisdom).

**Chichhakti** (*Sk.*). *Chih-Sakti*; the power that generates thought.

**Chidagnikundum** (*Sk.*). Literally, "the fire-hearth in the heart"; the seat of the force that extinguishes all individual desires.

**Chidâkâsam** (*Sk.*). The field or basis of consciousness.

**Chifflet, Jean**. A Canon-Kabbalist of the 18th century, reputed to have acquired a key to Gnostic works from Coptic Initiates; he wrote a two-part work on Abraxas, the esoteric portion of which was burned by the Church.

**Chiim** (*Heb.*). [w.w.w.]

**China**. The Kabbalah of. One of the oldest known Chinese books is the *Yih King*, or *Book of Changes*. It is reported to have been written in 2850 B.C. in the dialect of the Accadian black races of Mesopotamia. It is a highly complex system of Mental and Moral Philosophy, containing a scheme of universal relation and divination. Abstract ideas are represented by lines, half-lines, circles, and points. Thus, a circle represents YIH, the Great Supreme; a solid line is attributed to YIN, the Masculine Active Power; two half-lines are YANG, the Feminine Passive Power. KWEI is the animal soul, SHAN is the intellect, KHIEN is heaven or the Father,

**Chit** (*Sk.*). Abstract Consciousness.

**Chnoumis** (*Gr.*). The same as Chnouphis and Kneph. A symbol of creative force; according to Plutarch, Chnoumis or Kneph is “the unmade and eternal deity.” He is represented as blue (ether), and with his ram’s head and an asp between the horns, he might be mistaken for Ammon or Chnouphis (see entry). In fact, all these gods are solar and represent, under various aspects, the phases of generation and fertilization. Their ram’s heads indicate this meaning: a ram always symbolizes generative energy in the abstract, while the bull was the symbol of strength and the creative function. All were facets of one god, whose attributes were individualized and personified. According to Sir G. Wilkinson, Kneph or Chnoumis was “the idea of the Spirit of God”; and Bonwick explains that, as *Av* (“matter” or “flesh”), he was criocephalic (ram-headed), wearing a solar disk on his head, standing on the serpent Mehen, with a viper in his left hand and a cross in his right, intent upon the work of creation in the underworld (which, esoterically, refers to the earth). The Kabbalists identify him with Binah, the third <term>Sephirah</term> of the Sephirothal Tree, or “Binah represented by the Divine name of Jehovah.” If, as Chnoumis-Kneph, he represents the Indian Narâyana (the Spirit of God moving on the waters of space), then as Eichton or Ether, he holds in his mouth an Egg—the symbol of evolution; and as *Av*, he is Shiva, the Destroyer and the Regenerator. As Deveria explains: “His journey to the lower hemisphere appears to symbolize the evolution of substances, which are born to die and then be reborn.” Esoterically, however, and as taught by the Initiates of the inner temple, Chnoumis-Kneph was pre-eminently the god of reincarnation. **Chnouphis** (*Gr.*). Nouf in Egyptian. Another aspect of Ammon, and the personification of his generative power *in action*, as Kneph is of the same *in potential*. He is also ram-headed. If in his aspect as Kneph he is the Holy Spirit with the creative ideation brooding within him, as Chnouphis, he is the angel who “enters into” the virgin soil and flesh. A prayer on a papyrus, translated by the French Egyptologist Chabas, says: “O Sepui, Cause of being, who has formed your own body! O only Lord, proceeding from Noum! O divine substance, created from itself! O God, who has made the substance which is in him! O God, who has made his own father and impregnated his own mother.” This shows the origin of the Christian doctrines of the Trinity and immaculate conception. He is seen on a monument seated near a potter’s wheel, forming men out of clay. The fig-leaf is sacred to him, which alone is sufficient to prove him a phallic god—an idea which is carried out by the inscription: “he who made that which is, the creator of beings, the first existing, he who made all that exists to exist.” Some see in him the incarnation of Ammon-Ra, but he is the latter himself in his phallic aspect; for, like Ammon, he is “his mother’s husband,” i.e., the male or impregnating side of Nature. His names vary, as Cnouphis, Noum, Khem, and Khnum or Chnoumis. As he represents the Demiurgos (or Logos) from the material, lower aspect of the soul of the World, he is the Agathodæmon symbolized sometimes by a Serpent; and his wife Athōr or Maut (Môt mother), or Sate, “the daughter of the Sun,” carrying an arrow on a sunbeam (the ray of conception), stretches as “mistress over the lower portions of the atmosphere,” below the constellations, as Neïth expands over the starry heavens. (See “Chaos.”)

**Chohan** (*Tib.*). “Lord” or “Master”; a chief; thus *Dhyan-Chohan* would correspond to “Chief of the Dhyanis” or Celestial Lights—which in English would be translated as Archangels.

**Chokmah** (*Heb.*). Wisdom; the second of the ten Sephiroth, and the second of the supernal Triad. A masculine potency corresponding to the Yod (1) of the Tetragrammaton IHVH, and to *Ab*, the Father. <note>w.w.w. refers to William Wynn Westcott.</note>

**Chréstos** (*Gr.*). The early Gnostic form of Christ. It was used in the fifth century B.C. by Æschylus, Herodotus, and others. The *Manteumata pythochresta*, or the “oracles delivered by a Pythian god” through a pythoness, are mentioned by the former (Choeph. 901). *Chrésterion* is not only “the seat of an oracle,” but an offering to, or for, the oracle. *Chréstés* is one who explains oracles, “a prophet and soothsayer,” and *Chrésterios* is one who serves an oracle or a god. The earliest Christian writer, Justin Martyr, in his first *Apology*, calls his co-religionists *Chréstians*. “It is only through ignorance that men call themselves Christians instead of *Chréstians*,” says Lactantius (book iv., chapter vii.). borrowed from the Temple vocabulary of the Pagans. *Chréstos* meant in that vocabulary a disciple on probation, a candidate for hierophantship. When he had attained to this through initiation, long trials, and suffering, and had been "anointed" (i.e., "rubbed with oil," as were initiates and even idols of the gods, as the final touch of ritual observance), his name was changed to *Christos*, the "purified," in esoteric or mystery language. In mystic symbology, indeed, *Chréstés* or *Christos* meant that the "Way," the *Path*, was already trodden and the goal reached; when the fruits of the arduous labor uniting the personality of fleeting clay with the indestructible INDIVIDUALITY transformed it into the immortal EGO. "At the end of the *Way* stands the *Chréstés*," the Purifier, and once the union was accomplished, the Chrestos, the "man of sorrow," became Christos himself. Paul, the Initiate, knew this and meant exactly this when he is made to say, in a poor translation: "I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you" (Galatians 4:19), the true rendering of which is . . . . "until you form the Christos within yourselves." But the uninitiated, who knew only that *Chréstés* was somehow connected with priest and prophet and knew nothing about the hidden meaning of Christos, insisted—as did Lactantius and Justin Martyr—on being called *Chréstians* instead of Christians. Every good individual, therefore, may find Christ in his "inner man," as Paul expresses it (Ephesians 3:16, 17), whether he is a Jew, Muslim, Hindu, or Christian. Kenneth Mackenzie seemed to think that the word *Chréstos* was a synonym of Soter, "an appellation assigned to deities, great kings and heroes," indicating "Savior"—and he was right. For, as he adds: "It has been applied redundantly to Jesus Christ, whose name Jesus or Joshua carries the same interpretation. The name Jesus, in fact, is more a title of honor than a name—the true name of the Savior of Christianity being Emmanuel, or God with us (Matthew 1:23). . . . Great divinities among all nations, who are represented as expiatory or self-sacrificing, have been designated by the same title." (*R. M. Cyclopedia*) The Asklepios (or Aesculapius) of the Greeks had the title of *Soter*.

**Christian Scientist.** A newly coined term for denoting the practitioners of an art of healing by will. The name is a misnomer, since a Buddhist or Jew, Hindu or Materialist, can practice this new form of Western Yoga with equal success, if he can only guide and control his will with sufficient firmness. The "Mental Scientists" are another rival school. These work by a universal denial of every imaginable disease and evil, and claim through logic that since the Universal Spirit cannot be subject to the ailments of the flesh, and since every atom is Spirit and exists within Spirit, and since finally they—the healers and the healed—are all absorbed in this Spirit or Deity, there is not, nor can there be, such a thing as disease. This in no way prevents both Christian and Mental Scientists from succumbing to disease and harboring chronic illnesses in their own bodies just like ordinary mortals.

**Chthonia** (Greek). Chaotic earth in the Hellenic cosmogony.
**Chuang**. A great Chinese philosopher.
**Chubilgan** (Mongolian). Or Khubilkhan. The same as Chutuktu.
**Chutuktu** (Tibetan). An incarnation of Buddha or of some Bodhisattva, as believed in Tibet, where there are generally five manifest and two secret Chutuktus among the high Lamas.
**Chyuta** (Sanskrit). Means "the fallen" into generation, as a Kabbalist would say; the opposite of *achyuta*, something that is not subject to change or differentiation; said of deity.
**Circle**. There are several "Circles" with mystic adjectives attached to them. Thus we have: (1) the "Decussated or Perfect Circle" of Plato, who shows it decussated (crossed) in the form of the letter **X**; (2) the "Circle-dance" of the Amazons, around a Priapic image, the same as the dance of the *Gopis* around the Sun (Krishna), the shepherdesses representing the signs of the Zodiac; (3) the "Circle of Necessity" of 3,000 years of the Egyptians and of the Occultists, the duration of the cycle between rebirths or reincarnations being from 1,000 to 3,000 years on average. This will be treated under the term "Rebirth" or "Reincarnation."
**Clairaudience**. The faculty, whether innate or acquired through occult training, of hearing all that is said at any distance.
**Clairvoyance**. The faculty of seeing with the inner eye or spiritual sight. As it is used now, it is a loose and flippant term, encompassing a lucky guess due to natural shrewdness or intuition, and also that faculty which was so remarkably exercised by Jacob Boehme and Swedenborg. Real clairvoyance means the faculty of seeing through the densest matter (the matter disappearing at the will and before the spiritual eye of the Seer), and regardless of time (past, present, and future) or distance.
**Clemens Alexandrinus**. A Church Father and a prolific writer, who had been a Neoplatonist and a disciple of Ammonius Saccas. He lived between the second and third centuries of our era, in Alexandria.
**Cock**. A highly occult bird, much regarded in ancient augury and symbolism. According to the *Zohar*, the cock crows three times before a person's death; and in Russia and all Slavic countries, whenever a person is ill on the premises where a cock is kept, its crowing is held to be a sign of inevitable death, unless the bird crows at the hour of midnight, or immediately afterward, when its crowing is considered natural. As the cock was sacred to Aesculapius, and as the latter was called the *Soter* (Savior) who raised the dead to life, the Socratic exclamation "We owe a cock to Aesculapius," just before the Sage's death, is very suggestive. **Codex Nazaraeus (Lat.).** The “Book of Adam”—the latter name meaning *anthropos*, Man or Humanity. The Nazarene faith is sometimes called the Bardesanian system, though Bardesanes (155 to 228 B.C.) does not seem to have had any connection with it. True, he was born at Edessa in Syria and was a famous astrologer and Sabian before his alleged conversion. But he was a well-educated man of noble family and would not have used the almost incomprehensible Chaldeo-Syriac dialect mixed with the mystery language of the Gnostics in which the *Codex* is written. The sect of the Nazarenes was pre-Christian. Pliny and Josephus speak of the Nazarites as being settled on the banks of the Jordan 150 years B.C. (*Antiquities of the Jews* xiii. p. 9); and Munk says that the “Nasiareate was an institution established before the laws of Musah” or Moses (Munk, p. 169). Their modern name is *El Mogtasila* in Arabic; in European languages, they are the Mandaeans or “Christians of St. John.” (See “Baptism.”) But if the term Baptists may well be applied to them, it is not with the Christian meaning: for while they were and still are Sabians, or pure astrologers, the Mandaeans of Syria, called the Galileans, are pure polytheists, as every traveler in Syria and on the Euphrates can ascertain once he acquaints himself with their mysterious rites and ceremonies. (See *Isis Unveiled* ii. 290, *et seq*.) So secretly did they preserve their beliefs from the very beginning that Epiphanius, who wrote against the Heresies in the 4th century, confesses himself unable to say what they believed in (1. 122); he simply states that they never mention the name of Jesus, nor do they call themselves Christians (loc. cit. 190). Yet it is undeniable that some of the alleged philosophical views and doctrines of Bardesanes are found in the codex of the Nazarenes. (See Norberg’s *Codex Nazaraeus*, or the “Book of Adam,” and also “Mandaeans.”)

**Coeur, Jacques.** A famous Treasurer of France, born in 1408, who allegedly obtained his office through black magic. He was reputed to be a great alchemist, and his wealth became fabulous; but he was soon banished from the country, and retiring to the Island of Cyprus, he died there in 1460, leaving behind enormous wealth, endless legends, and a bad reputation.

**Coffin-Rite, or *Pastos*.** This was the final rite of Initiation in the Mysteries in Egypt, Greece, and elsewhere. **Collanges**, Gabriel de. Born in 1524. The best astrologer in the 16th century and an even better Kabbalist. He spent a fortune in the unraveling of its mysteries. It was rumored that he died from poison administered to him by a Jewish Rabbin-Kabbalish.

**College of Rabbis**. A college at Babylon; most famous during the early centuries of Christianity. Its glory, however, was greatly darkened by the appearance in Alexandria of Hellenic teachers, such as Philo Judæus, Josephus, Aristobulus, and others. The former took revenge on their successful rivals by speaking of the Alexandrians as theurgists and unclean prophets. But the Alexandrian believers in thaumaturgy were not regarded as sinners or impostors when *orthodox* Jews were at the head of such schools of "*hazim*." These were colleges for teaching prophecy and occult sciences. Samuel was the chief of such a college at Ramah; Elisha at Jericho. Hillel had a regular academy for prophets and seers; and it is Hillel, a pupil of the Babylonian College, who was the founder of the Sect of the Pharisees and the great orthodox Rabbis.

**Collemann**, Jean. An Alsatian, born at Orleans, according to K. Mackenzie; other accounts say he was a Jew, who found favor, due to his astrological studies, with both Charles VII and Louis XI, and that he had a bad influence on the latter.

**Collyridians**. A sect of Gnostics who, in the early centuries of Christianity, transferred their worship and reverence from Astoreth to Mary, as Queen of Heaven and Virgin. Regarding the two as identical, they offered to the latter, as they had done to the former, buns and cakes on certain days, with sexual symbols represented on them.

**Continents**. In the Buddhist cosmogony according to Gautama Buddha's exoteric doctrine, there are numberless systems of worlds (or *Sakwala*) all of which are born, mature, decay, and are destroyed periodically. Orientalists translate the teaching about "the four great continents which do not communicate with each other," as meaning that "upon the earth there are four great continents" (see Hardy's *Eastern Monachism*, p. 4), while the doctrine simply means that around or above the earth there are four worlds on either side—that is, the earth appearing as the fourth on each side of the arc.

**Corybantes**. *Mysteries* of the. These were held in Phrygia in honor of Atys, the youth beloved by Cybele. The rites were very elaborate within the temple and very noisy and tragic in public. They began with a public mourning of the *death of Atys* and ended in tremendous rejoicing at his *resurrection*. The statue or image of the victim of Jupiter's jealousy was placed during the ceremony in a <term>pastos</term> (coffin), and the priests sang of his sufferings. Atys, like Visvakarma in India, was a representative of Initiation and Adeptship. He is shown as being born im-

**Cosmocratores** (Gr.). “Builders of the Universe,” the “world architects,” or the Creative Forces personified.

**Cow-Worship.** The idea of any such “worship” is as mistaken as it is unfair. No Egyptian worshipped *the cow*, nor does any Hindu worship this animal now, though it is true that the cow and bull were sacred then as they are today, but only as the natural physical symbol of a metaphysical ideal. This is much like how a church made of bricks and mortar is sacred to the civilized Christian because of its associations and not because of its walls. The cow was sacred to Isis, the Universal Mother or Nature, and to Hathor, the female principle in nature. These two goddesses are allied to both the sun and moon, as the disk and the cow’s horns (crescent) prove. (See “Hathor” and “Isis”.) In the *Vedas*, the Dawn of Creation is represented by a cow. This dawn is Hathor, and the day which follows—or Nature already formed—is Isis, for both are one except in the matter of time. Hathor the elder is “the mistress of the seven mystical cows” and Isis, “the Divine Mother,” is the “cow-horned,” the *cow of plenty* (or Nature and Earth). As the mother of Horus (the physical world), she is the “mother of all that lives.” The *ouat* was the symbolic eye of Horus, the right being the sun and the left being the moon. The right “eye” of Horus was called “the cow of Hathor” and served as a powerful amulet, just as the dove in a nest of rays or glory, with or without the cross, is a talisman for Latin and Greek Christians. The *Bull* and the *Lion*, which we often find accompanying Luke and Mark in the frontispiece of their respective *Gospels* in the Greek and Latin texts, are explained as symbols—which is indeed the fact. Why not admit the same in the case of the Egyptian sacred Bulls, Cows, Rams, and Birds?

**Cremer, John.** An eminent scholar who for over thirty years studied Hermetic philosophy in pursuit of its practical secrets while he was simultaneously the Abbot of Westminster. While on a voyage to Italy, he met the famous Raymond Lully, whom he persuaded to return with him to England. Lully revealed to Cremer the secrets of the stone, for which service the monastery offered daily prayers for him. According to the *Royal Masonic Cyclopedia*, Cremer, “having obtained a profound knowledge of the secrets of Alchemy, became a most celebrated adept in occult philosophy . . . lived to a good old age, and died in the reign of King Edward III.”

**Crescent.** Sin was the Assyrian name for the moon, and *Sin-ai* the Mount, the birthplace of Osiris, of Dionysos, Bacchus, and several other gods. According to Rawlinson, the moon was held in higher esteem than the sun at Babylon because *darkness preceded light*. The crescent was, therefore, a sacred symbol with almost every nation before it became the standard of the Turks. The author of *Egyptian Belief* says, "The crescent... is not essentially a Muslim ensign. On the contrary, it was a Christian one, derived through Asia from the Babylonian Astarte, Queen of Heaven, or from the Egyptian Isis... whose emblem was the crescent. The Greek Christian Empire of Constantinople held it as their protection <note>palladium: a safeguard or source of protection</note>. Upon the conquest by the Turks, the Muslim Sultan adopted it as the symbol of his power. Since that time, the crescent has been made to oppose the idea of the cross."

**Criocéphale** (*Gr.*). Ram-headed; a term applied to several deities and emblematic figures, notably those of ancient Egypt, which were designed about the period when the Sun passed, at the Vernal Equinox, from the sign Taurus to the sign Aries. Prior to this period, bull-headed and horned deities prevailed. Apis was the type of the Bull deity, while Ammon was the ram-headed type. Isis, too, had a cow's head allotted to her. Porphyry writes that the Greeks united the Ram to Jupiter and the Bull to Bacchus. [w.w.w.]

**Crocodile.** "The great reptile of Typhon." The seat of its "worship" was Crocodilopolis, and it was sacred to Set and Sebak—its alleged creators. The primitive Rishis in India, the *Manus* and Sons of Brahmâ, are each the progenitors of some animal species of which they are the alleged "father"; in Egypt, each god was credited with the formation or creation of certain animals which were sacred to him. Crocodiles must have been numerous in Egypt during the early dynasties, if one is to judge by the almost incalculable number of their mummies. Thousands upon thousands have been excavated from the grottoes of Moabdeh, and many a vast *necropolis* of that Typhonic animal is still left untouched. But the crocodile was only worshiped where its god and "father" received honors. Typhon (see "Typhon") had once received such honors and, as Bunsen shows, had been considered a great god. His words are, "Down to the time of Ramses, 1300 B.C., Typhon was one of the most venerated and powerful gods, a god who pours blessings and life on the rulers of Egypt." As explained elsewhere, Typhon is the material aspect of Osiris. When Typhon, the Quaternary, kills Osiris—the triad or divine Light—and metaphorically cuts him into 14 pieces, and separates himself from the "god," he incurs the abhorrence of the masses; he becomes the evil god, the storm and hurricane god, the burning sand of the desert, the constant enemy of the Nile, and the "slayer of the evening beneficent dew," because Osiris is the ideal Universe, Siva the great Regenerative Force, and Typhon the material portion of it—the evil side of the god, or the Destroying Siva. This is why the crocodile is also partly venerated and partly abhorred. The appearance of the crocodile in the

The desert, far from the water, foretold the happy event of the coming flood—this is why it was worshipped at Thebes and Ombos. But it destroyed thousands of humans and animals every year—this is also why the Crocodile was hated and persecuted at Elephantine and Tentyra.

**Cross.** Mariette Bey has shown its antiquity in Egypt by proving that in all the primitive tombs, “*the plan of the chamber has the form of a cross*.” It is the symbol of the brotherhood of races and people. It was laid on the chests of corpses in Egypt, just as it is now placed on the bodies of deceased Christians—and, in its *Swastika* form (*croix cramponnée*), on the hearts of Buddhist adepts and Buddhas. (See “Calvary Cross.”)

**Crux Ansata** (*Lat.*). The handled cross, ☥; whereas the *tau* is T, in this form, and the oldest Egyptian cross or the *tat* is like this: +. The *crux ansata* was the symbol of immortality, but the *tat*-cross was that of spirit-matter and had the significance of a sexual emblem. The *crux ansata* was the primary symbol in the Egyptian Masonry established by Count Cagliostro. Masons must have truly forgotten the original meaning of their highest symbols if some of their authorities still insist that the *crux ansata* is only a combination of the *cteis* (or *yoni*) and *phallus* (or *lingham*). This is far from the truth. The handle or *ansa* had a double meaning, but never a phallic one. As an attribute of Isis, it was the mundane circle; as a symbol of law on the chest of a mummy, it represented immortality—an endless and beginningless eternity that descends upon and grows out of the plane of material nature. This is the horizontal feminine line surmounting the vertical male line—the fertilizing male principle in nature or spirit. Without the handle, the *crux ansata* became the *tau* (T), which on its own is an androgynous symbol, and becomes purely phallic or sexual only when it takes the shape of a plus sign (+).

**Crypt** (*Gr.*). A secret subterranean vault; some were for the purpose of initiation, others for burial. There were crypts under every temple in antiquity. There was one on the Mount of Olives, lined with red stucco, and built before the arrival of the Jews.

**Curetes.** The priest-initiates of ancient Crete in the service of Cybele. Initiation in their temples was very severe; it lasted twenty-seven days, during which time the candidate was left alone in a crypt to undergo terrible trials. Pythagoras was initiated into these rites and emerged victorious.

**Cutha.** An ancient city in Babylonia after which a tablet giving an account of “creation” is named. The “Cutha tablet” speaks of a “temple of Sittam” in the sanctuary of Nergal, the “giant king of war and lord of the city of Cutha.” This text is purely esoteric and must be read symbolically, if it is read at all.

**Cycle.** From the Greek *kuklos*. The ancients divided time into endless cycles—wheels within wheels. All such periods were of various durations, and each marked the beginning or the end of an event, either

**Cynocephalus** (*Gr.*). The Egyptian *Hapi*. There was a notable difference between the ape-headed gods and the "Cynocephalus" (*Simia hamadryas*), a dog-headed baboon from Upper Egypt. The latter, whose sacred city was Hermopolis, was sacred to the lunar deities and Thoth-Hermes, and was therefore an emblem of secret wisdom—as was Hanuman, the monkey-god of India, and later, the elephant-headed Ganesha. The mission of the Cynocephalus was to show the way for the dead to the Seat of Judgment and Osiris, whereas the ape-gods were all phallic. They are almost invariably found in a crouching posture, holding in one hand the *outa* (the eye of Horus), and in the other the sexual cross. Isis is sometimes seen riding on an ape to designate the fall of divine nature into generation.

## D.
—Both in the English and Hebrew alphabets, this is the fourth letter, whose numerical value is four. The symbolic significance in the *Kabbalah* of the *Daleth* is “*door*.” It is the Greek Δ, through which the world (whose symbol is the *tetrad* or number four) issued, producing the divine seven. The name of the *Tetrad* was *Harmony* to the Pythagoreans, “because it is a *diatessaron* in *sesquitertia*.” With the Kabbalists, the divine name associated with *Daleth* was *Daghoul*.

**Daath** (*Heb.*). *Knowledge*; “the conjunction of *Chokmah* and *Binah*, *Wisdom* and *Understanding*: sometimes, in error, called a *Sephira*.” [w.w.w.]

**Dabar** (*Heb.*). D (a) B (a) R (im), meaning the “*Word*,” and the “*Words*” in the Chaldean *Kabbalah*, *Dabar* and *Logoi*. (See *Sec. Doct., I. p.* 350, and “*Logos*,” or “*Word*”).

**Dabistan** (*Pers.*). The land of *Iran*; ancient *Persia*.

**Dache-Dachus** (*Chald.*). The dual emanation of *Moymis*, the progeny of the dual or androgynous World-Principle, the male *Apason* and female *Tauthe*. Like all theocratic nations possessing Temple mysteries, the Babylonians never mentioned the “*One*” *Principle of the Universe*, nor did they give it a name. This led *Damascius* (*Theogonies*) to remark that, like the rest of the “*barbarians*,” the Babylonians passed it over in silence. *Tauthe* was the mother of the gods, while *Apason* was her self-generating male power; *Moymis*, the ideal universe, was her only-begotten son, who in turn emanated *Dache-Dachus*, and finally *Belus*, the *Demiurge* of the objective Universe.

**Dactyli** (*Gr.*). From *daktulos*, “*a finger*.” The name given to the Phrygian *Hierophants of Kybele*, who were regarded as the greatest magicians and exorcists. They were five or ten in number because of the *five* fingers on one hand that blessed, and the *ten* on both hands which evoke the gods. They also healed by manipulation or mesmerism.

**Dadouchos** (*Gr.*). The torch-bearer, one of the four celebrants in the *Eleusinian mysteries*. There were several attached to the temples, but they appeared in public only at the *Panathenaean Games* at Athens to preside over the so-called “*torch-race*.” (See *Mackenzie’s R. M. Cyclopaedia*.)

**Daemon** (*Gr.*). In the original *Hermetic works* and ancient classics, this has a meaning identical with that of “*god*,” “*angel*,” or “*genius*.” The *Daemon* of *Socrates* is the incorruptible part of the man, or rather the real inner man whom we call *Nous* or the rational divine *Ego*. **Daenam** (*Pahlavi*). *Literally*, "Knowledge," the principle of understanding in man, the rational Soul, or <term>Manas</term>, according to the <term>Avesta</term>.

**Dag, Dagon** (*Hebrew*). "Fish" and also "Messiah." Dagon was the Chaldean man-fish <term>Oannes</term>, the mysterious being who arose daily out of the depths of the sea to teach people every useful science. He was also called <term>Annedotus</term>.

**Dâgoba** (*Sanskrit*), or **Stûpa**. *Literally:* a sacred mound or tower for Buddhist holy relics. These are pyramid-shaped mounds scattered all over India and Buddhist countries, such as Ceylon, Burmah, Central Asia, etc. They are of various sizes and generally contain some small relics of Saints or those claimed to have belonged to <term>Gautama</term>, the <term>Buddha</term>. As the human body is supposed to consist of 84,000 <term>dhâtus</term> (organic cells with definite vital functions in them), <term>Asoka</term> is said for this reason to have built 84,000 <term>dhâtu-gopas</term> or <term>Dâgobas</term> in honor of every cell of the Buddha's body, each of which has now become a <term>dhârmadhâtu</term> or holy relic. There is in Ceylon a <term>Dhâtu-gopa</term> at <term>Anurâdhapura</term>, said to date from 160 <small>B.C.</small> They are now built pyramid-like, but the primitive Dâgobas were all shaped like towers with a cupola and several <term>tchhatra</term> (umbrellas) over them. Eitel states that the Chinese Dâgobas all have from 7 to 14 <term>tchhatras</term> over them, a number which is symbolic of the human body.

**Daitya Gura** (*Sanskrit*). The instructor of the giants, called <term>Daityas</term> (*q.v.*). Allegorically, it is the title given to the planet <term>Venus-Lucifer</term>, or rather to its indwelling Ruler, <term>Sukra</term>, a male deity (See *Sec. Doct.*, ii. p. 30).

**Daityas** (*Sanskrit*). Giants, Titans, and exoterically demons, but in truth identical with certain <term>Asuras</term>, the intellectual gods, the opponents of the useless gods of ritualism and the enemies of <term>puja</term>, sacrifices.

**Daivi-prakriti** (*Sanskrit*). Primordial, homogeneous light, called by some Indian Occultists "the Light of the <term>Logos</term>" (see *Notes on the Bhagavat Gita*, by T. Subba Row, B.A., L.L.B.); when differentiated, this light becomes <term>FOHAT</term>.

**Dâkinî** (*Sanskrit*). Female demons, vampires, and blood-drinkers (*asrapas*). In the <term>Purânas</term>, they attend upon the goddess <term>Kâli</term> and feed on human flesh. A species of evil "Elementals" (*q.v.*).

**Daksha** (*Sanskrit*). A form of <term>Brahmâ</term>, and his son in the <term>Purânas</term>. But the <term>Rig Veda</term> states that "<term>Daksha</term> sprang from <term>Aditi</term>, and <term>Aditi</term> from <term>Daksha</term>," which proves him to be a personified correlating Creative

The Orientalists seem very perplexed about what to make of him; but Roth is closer to the truth than anyone when saying that Daksha is the spiritual power and, at the same time, the male energy that generates the gods in eternity, which is represented by Aditi. The Purânas, as a matter of course, anthropomorphize the idea and show Daksha instituting "sexual intercourse on this earth" after trying every other means of procreation. The generative Force, spiritual at the beginning, naturally becomes at the most material end of its evolution a procreative Force on the physical plane; and so far the Purânic allegory is correct, as the Secret Science teaches that our present mode of procreation began toward the end of the third Root-Race.

**Daladâ** (*Sk.*). A very precious relic of Gautama Buddha; namely, his supposed left canine tooth preserved at the great temple at Kandy, Ceylon. Unfortunately, the relic shown is not genuine. The real relic has been securely hidden for several hundred years, ever since the shameful and bigoted attempt by the Portuguese (the ruling power in Ceylon at the time) to steal and dispose of the actual relic. What is shown in place of the real thing is the monstrous tooth of some animal.

**Dama** (*Sk.*). Restraint of the senses.

**Dambulla** (*Sk.*). The name of a huge rock in Ceylon. It is about 400 feet above sea level. Its upper portion is excavated, and several large cave-temples, or *Vihâras*, are cut out of the solid rock, all of these dating from before the Christian era. They are considered the best-preserved antiquities on the island. The north side of the rock is vertical and quite inaccessible, but on the south side, about 150 feet from its summit, its huge overhanging granite mass has been fashioned into a platform with a row of large cave-temples excavated in the surrounding walls—evidently at an enormous sacrifice of labor and money. Two *Vihâras* may be mentioned out of the many: the *Maha Raja Vihâra*, 172 feet in length and 75 in breadth, in which there are more than fifty figures of Buddha, most of them larger than life and all formed from the solid rock. A well has been dug out at the foot of the central *Dâgoba*, and from a fissure in the rock, beautiful clear water constantly drips into it, which is kept for sacred purposes. In the other, the *Maha Dewiyo Vihâra*, a gigantic figure of the dead Gautama Buddha can be seen, 47 feet long, reclining on a couch and pillow cut out of solid rock like the rest. "This long, narrow, and dark temple, the position and placid appearance of Buddha, together with the stillness of the place, tend to impress the viewer with the idea that he is in the chamber of death. The priest asserts... that such was Buddha, and such were those (an attendant stands at his feet) who witnessed the last moments of his mortality" (Hardy’s *Eastern Monachism*). The view from Dambulla is magnificent. On the large rock platform, which now seems to be visited more by very intelligent tame white monkeys than by monks, there stands a huge Bo-Tree, one of the numerous offshoots from the original Bo-Tree under which the Lord Siddhârtha reached Nirvana.

# GLOSSARY

“About 50 feet from the summit there is a pond which, as the priests assert, is never without water.” (*The Ceylon Almanac, 1834.*)

**Dammâpadan** (*Pali*). A Buddhist work containing moral precepts.

**Dâna** (*Sk.*). Almsgiving to mendicants, literally, “charity,” the first of the six Paramitas in Buddhism.

**Dânâvas** (*Sk.*). Almost the same as *Daityas*; giants and demons, the opponents of the ritualistic gods.

**Dangma** (*Sk.*). In Esotericism, a purified Soul. A Seer and an Initiate; one who has attained full wisdom.

**Daos** (*Chald.*). The seventh King (shepherd) of the divine Dynasty, who reigned over the Babylonians for the space of ten *sari*, or 36,000 years, a *saros* being of 3,600 years’ duration. In his time four Annedoti, or Men-fishes (Dagons), made their appearance.

**Darâsta** (*Sk.*). Ceremonial magic practiced by the central Indian tribes, especially among the Kolarians.

**Dardanus** (*Gr.*). The Son of Jupiter and Electra, who received the Kabeiri gods as a dowry and took them to Samothrace, where they were worshiped long before the hero laid the foundations of Troy, and before Tyre and Sidon were ever heard of, though Tyre was built 2760 B.C. (See for fuller details “Kabiri.”)

**Darha** (*Sk.*). The ancestral spirits of the Kolarians.

**Darsanas** (*Sk.*). The Schools of Indian philosophy, of which there are six; Shad-darsanas or six demonstrations.

**Dasa-sil** (*Pali*). The ten obligations or commandments taken by and binding upon the priests of Buddha; the five obligations or *Pansil* are taken by laymen.

**Dava** (*Tib.*). The moon, in Tibetan astrology.

**Davkina** (*Chald.*). The wife of Hea, “the goddess of the lower regions, the consort of the Deep,” the mother of Merodach, the Bel of later times, and mother to many river-gods; Hea being the god of the lower regions, the “lord of the Sea or abyss,” and also the lord of **Wisdom**.

**Dayanisi** (*Aram.*). The god worshiped by the Jews along with other Semites as the “Ruler of men”; Dionysos—the Sun; whence Jehovah-Nissi, or Iao-Nisi, the same as Dionysos or Jove of Nyssa. (See *Isis Unveiled*, II. 526).

**Day of Brahmâ.** See “Brahmâ’s Day,” etc.

**Dayus** or **Dyaus** (*Sk.*). A Vedic term. The unrevealed Deity, or that which reveals Itself only as light and the bright day—metaphorically.

**Death, Kiss of.** According to the Kabbalah, the earnest follower does not die by the power of the Evil Spirit, Yetzer ha Rah, but by a kiss from the mouth of Jehovah Tetragrammaton, meeting him in the Haikal Ahabah or Palace of Love. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Dei termini** (*Lat*.). The name for pillars with human heads representing Hermes, placed at crossroads by the ancient Greeks and Romans. Also the general name for deities presiding over boundaries and frontiers.

**Deist**. One who admits the existence of a god or gods but claims to know nothing of them and denies revelation. A Freethinker of olden times.

**Demerit**. In Occult and Buddhist terminology, a constituent of Karma. It is through *avidya*, or ignorance of *vidya* (divine illumination), that merit and demerit are produced. Once an Arhat obtains full illumination and perfect control over his personality and lower nature, he ceases to create “merit and demerit.”

**Demeter**. The Hellenic name for the Latin Ceres, the goddess of grain and agriculture. The astronomical sign, *Virgo*. The Eleusinian Mysteries were celebrated in her honor.

**Demiurgic Mind**. The same as “Universal Mind.” *Mahat*, the first “product” of Brahma, or Brahma himself.

**Demiurgos** (*Gr*.). The Demiurge or Artificer; the Supernal Power which built the universe. Freemasons derive their phrase of “Supreme Architect” from this word. For the Occultists, it is the third manifested Logos, or Plato’s “second god”; the second *logos* is represented by Plato as the “Father,” the only Deity that he dared mention as an Initiate into the Mysteries.

**Demon est Deus Inversus** (*Lat*.). A Kabbalistic axiom; literally, “the devil is God reversed”; which means that there is neither evil nor good, but that the forces which create the one create the other, according to the nature of the materials they find to work upon.

**Demonologia** (*Gr*.). Treatises or Discourses upon Demons, or Gods in their dark aspects.

**Demons**. According to the Kabbalah, the demons dwell in the world of Assiah, the world of matter and of the “shells” of the dead. They are the Klippoth. There are Seven Hells, whose demon dwellers represent personified vices. Their prince is Samaël, and his female companion is Isheth Zenunim—the woman of prostitution; united in aspect, they are named “The Beast,” Chiva. [w.w.w.]

**Demrusch** (*Pers*.). A Giant in the mythology of ancient Iran.

**Denis, Angoras**. “A physician of Paris, astrologer, and alchemist in the 14th century” (R.M.C.).

**Deona Mati**. In the Kolarian dialect, one who exercises <note>This likely means "exorcises."</note> evil spirits.

**Dervish**. A Muslim—Turkish or Persian—ascetic. A nomadic and wandering monk. Dervishes, however, sometimes live in communities. They are often called the “whirling charmers.” Apart from his austerities of life, prayer, and contemplation, the Turkish, Egyptian, or Arabic devotee presents very little similarity with the Hindu fakir, who is

The dervish may also be a strong mesmerist, but he will never voluntarily submit to the abominable and almost incredible self-punishment which the fakir invents for himself with an ever-increasing avidity, until nature gives way and he dies in slow and excruciating torture. **Desatir.** A very ancient Persian work called the *Book of Shet*. It speaks of the thirteen Zoroasters and is very mystical.

**Deva** (*Sk.*). A god, a “resplendent” deity. Deva-Deus, from the root *div*, “to shine”. A Deva is a celestial being—whether good, bad, or indifferent. Devas inhabit “the three worlds”, which are the three planes above us. There are 33 groups or 330 million of them.

**Deva Sarga** (*Sk.*). Creation: the origin of the principles, said to be Intelligence born from the qualities or the attributes of nature.

**Devachan** (*Sk.*). The “dwelling of the gods”. A state intermediate between two earth-lives, which the Ego (Atma-Buddhi-Manas, or the Trinity made One) enters after its separation from Kama Rupa and the disintegration of the lower principles on earth.

**Devajnânas** (*Sk.*). or *Daivajna*. The higher classes of celestial beings; those who possess divine knowledge.

**Devaki** (*Sk.*). The mother of Krishna. She was imprisoned in a dungeon by her brother, King Kansa, for fear of the fulfillment of a prophecy which stated that a son of his sister would dethrone and kill him. Despite the strict watch kept, Devaki was overshadowed by Vishnu, the Holy Spirit, and thus gave birth to that god’s avatar, Krishna. (See “Kansa”).

**Deva-laya** (*Sk.*). “The shrine of a Deva”. The name given to all Brahmanical temples.

**Deva-lôkas** (*Sk.*). The abodes of the Gods or Devas in superior spheres. The seven celestial worlds above Meru.

**Devamâtri** (*Sk.*). Literally, “the mother of the gods”. A title of Aditi, or Mystic Space.

**Dêvanâgarî** (*Sk.*). Literally, “the language or letters of the devas” or gods. The characters of the Sanskrit language. The alphabet and the art of writing were kept secret for ages, as only the *Dwijas* (Twice-born) and the *Dikshitas* (Initiates) were permitted to use this art. It was a crime for a Shudra to recite a verse of the *Vedas*, and for any of the two lower castes (Vaishya and Shudra) to know the letters was an offense punishable by death.
