**Devapi** (*Sk.*). A Sanskrit Sage of the race of Kuru, who, together with another Sage (Moru), is supposed to live throughout the four ages and until the coming of *Maitreya Buddha*, or *Kalki* (the last Avatar of Vishnu); who, like all the *Saviors of the World* in their last appearance, like Sosiosh of the Zoroastrians and the *Rider of St. John's Revelation*, will appear seated on a *White Horse*. The two, Devapi and Moru, are supposed to live in a Himalayan retreat called *Kalapa* or *Katapa*. This is a Purânic allegory.

**Devarshis**, or *Deva-rishi* (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, "god rishis"; the divine or god-like saints, those sages who attain a fully divine nature on earth.

**Devasarman** (*Sk.*). A very ancient author who died about a century after Gautama Buddha. He wrote two famous works, in which he denied the existence of both *Ego* and *non-Ego*, the one as successfully as the other.

**Dhârana** (*Sk.*). That state in *Yoga* practice when the mind has to be fixed unflinchingly on some object of meditation.

**Dhâranî** (*Sk.*). In Buddhism—both Southern and Northern—and also in Hinduism, it means simply a mantra or mantras—sacred verses from the *Rig Veda*. In ancient times these mantras or Dhâranî were all considered mystical and practically effective in their use. At present, however, it is the *Yogachârya* school alone which proves the claim in practice. When chanted according to given instructions, a Dhâranî produces wonderful effects. Its occult power, however, does not reside in the *words* but in the inflection or accent given and the resulting sound created by it. (See "Mantra" and "Akasa").

**Dharma** (*Sk.*). The sacred Law; the Buddhist Canon.

**Dharmachakra** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, The turning of the "wheel of the Law". The emblem of Buddhism as a system of cycles and rebirths or reincarnations.

**Dharmakâya** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, "the glorified spiritual body" called the "Vesture of Bliss". The third, or highest of the *Trikâya* (Three Bodies), the attribute developed by every "Buddha", *that is*, every initiate who has crossed or reached the end of what is called the "fourth Path" (in esotericism the sixth "portal" prior to his entry on the seventh). The highest of the *Trikâya*, it is the fourth of the *Buddhakchêtra*, or Buddhic planes of consciousness, represented figuratively in Buddhist asceticism as a robe or vesture of luminous Spirituality. In popular Northern Buddhism these vestures or robes are: (1) Nirmanakâya, (2) Sambhogakâya, (3) and Dharmakâya, the last being the highest and most refined of all, as it places the ascetic on the threshold of Nir-

**Dharmaprabhâsa** (*Sk.*). The name of the Buddha who will appear during the seventh Root-race. (See “Ratnâvabhâsa Kalpa,” when sexes will no longer exist.)

**Dharmasmriti Upasthâna** (*Sk.*). A very long compound word containing a very mystical warning: “Remember, the constituents (of human nature) originate according to the *Nidânas*, and are not originally the Self,” which refers to what the Esoteric Schools teach, rather than the ecclesiastical interpretation.

**Dharmâsôka** (*Sk.*). The name given to the first Asoka after his conversion to Buddhism—King Chandragupta, who served “Dharma,” or the law of Buddha, throughout his long life. King Asoka (the second) was not converted but was born a Buddhist.

**Dhâtu** (*Pali*). Relics of Buddha’s body collected after his cremation.

**Dhruva** (*Sk.*). An Aryan Sage, now the Pole Star. A *Kshatriya* (one of the warrior caste) who became a *Rishi* through religious austerities and was, for this reason, raised by Vishnu to his high position in the skies. Also called *Grah-Adhâr* or “the pivot of the planets.”

**Dhyan Chohans** (*Sk.*). Literally, “The Lords of Light.” The highest gods, corresponding to the Roman Catholic Archangels. They are the divine Intelligences charged with the supervision of the Cosmos.

**Dhyâna** (*Sk.*). In Buddhism, one of the six Paramîtas of perfection; a state of abstraction that carries the ascetic practicing it far above this plane of sensory perception and out of the world of matter. Literally, “contemplation.” The six stages of Dhyan differ only in the degree of abstraction of the personal Ego from sensory life.

**Dhyâni Bodhisattvas** (*Sk.*). In Buddhism, the five sons of the Dhyâni Buddhas. They have a mystical meaning in Esoteric Philosophy.

**Dhyâni Buddhas** (*Sk.*). Those “of the Merciful Heart”; worshipped especially in Nepal. These also have a secret meaning.

**Dhyâni Pasa** (*Sk.*). “The rope of the Dhyanis” or Spirits; the “Ring Pass Not” (See *The Secret Doctrine*, Stanza V, Volume I, page 129).

<term>Dioscuri</term> (Greek). The name of Castor and Pollux, the sons of Jupiter and Leda. Their festival, the *Dioscuria*, was celebrated with much rejoicing by the Lacedaemonians.

<term>Dipamkara</term> (Sanskrit). Literally, “the Buddha of fixed light”; a predecessor of Gautama, the Buddha.

<term>Diploteratology</term> (Greek). The production of mixed monsters; abbreviated as teratology.

<term>Dis</term> (Greek). In the Theogony of Damascius, the same as *Protogonos*, the “first-born light,” called by that author “the disposer of all things.”

<term>Dises</term> (Scandinavian). The later name for the divine women called Valkyries, Norns, etc., in the *Edda*.

<term>Disk-worship</term>. This was very common in Egypt but not until later times, as it began with Amenoph III, a Dravidian, who brought it from Southern India and Ceylon. It was *Sun-worship* under another form, the *Aten-Nephru*; Aten-Ra is identical with the Adonai of the Jews, the “Lord of Heaven” or the Sun. The winged disk was the emblem of the Soul. The Sun was at one time the symbol of Universal Deity shining on the whole world and all creatures; the Sabaeans regarded the Sun as the Demiurge and a Universal Deity, as did also the Hindus, and as do the Zoroastrians to this day. The Sun is undeniably the one creator of physical nature. Lenormant was obliged, despite his orthodox Christianity, to denounce the resemblance between disk-worship and Jewish worship. “Aten represents the Adonai or Lord, the Assyrian Tammuz, and the Syrian Adonis. . . .” (*The Great Dionysian Myth*)

<term>Divyachakchus</term> (Sanskrit). Literally, “celestial Eye” or divine seeing and perception. It is the first of the six “Abhijnas” (see entry), the faculty developed by Yoga practice to perceive any object in the Universe, at whatever distance.

<term>Divyasrotra</term> (Sanskrit). Literally, “celestial Ear” or divine hearing. The second of the “Abhijnas,” or the faculty of understanding the language or sound produced by any living being on Earth.

<term>Djati</term> (Sanskrit). One of the twelve “Nidanas” (see entry); the cause and the effect in the mode of birth taking place according to the “Chatur Yoni” (see entry), when in each case a being, whether man or animal, is placed in one of the six (esoterically seven) *Gati* or paths of sentient existence. These, counting downward, are: (1) the highest Dhyani (*Anupadaka*); (2) Devas; (3) Men; (4) Elementals or Nature Spirits; (5) Animals; (6) lower Elementals; (7) organic Germs. In the popular or exoteric nomenclature, there are Devas, Men, Asuras, Beings in Hells, Pretas (hungry demons), and Animals.

<term>Djin</term> (Arabic). Elementals; Nature Spirits; Genii. The *Djins* or *Jins* are much dreaded in Egypt, Persia, and elsewhere.

<term>Donar</term> (Scandinavian), or *Thunar*, *Thor*. In the North, the God of Thunder. He was the *Jupiter Tonans* (Thundering Jupiter) of Scandinavia. Just as the oak was dedicated to Jupiter, it was also sacred to Thor, and his altars were overshadowed with oak trees. Thor, or Donar, was the offspring of Odin, "the omnipotent God of Heaven," and of Mother Earth.

<term>Dondam-pai-den-pa</term> (Tibetan). The same as the Sanskrit term *Paramarthasatya* or "absolute truth," the highest spiritual self-consciousness and perception, divine self-consciousness; a very mystical term.

<term>Doppelgänger</term> (German). A synonym for the "Double" and for the "Astral body" in occult parlance.

<term>Dorjesempa</term> (Tibetan). The "Diamond Soul," a name of the celestial Buddha.

<term>Dorjeshang</term> (Tibetan). A title of Buddha in his highest aspect; a name of the supreme Buddha; also called *Dorje*.

<term>Double</term>. The same as the "Astral body" or "Doppelgänger."

<term>Double Image</term>. The name among the Jewish Kabbalists for the *Dual Ego*, called respectively: the Higher, *Metatron*, and the Lower, *Samael*. They are represented allegorically as the two inseparable companions of man through life, one being his Guardian Angel and the other his Evil Demon.

<term>Dracontia</term> (Greek). Temples dedicated to the Dragon, the emblem of the Sun and the symbol of Deity, Life, and Wisdom. The Egyptian Karnak, the Carnac in Brittany, and Stonehenge are well-known examples of Dracontia.

In Babylonian antiquities, it is referred to as the "scaly one" and is connected on many gems with Tiamat, the sea. "The Dragon of the Sea" is repeatedly mentioned. with the Dragon. Bel and the Dragon, Apollo and Python, Osiris and Typhon, Sigur and Fafnir, and finally St. George and the Dragon, are the same. They were all solar gods, and wherever we find the Sun, there also is the Dragon, the symbol of Wisdom—Thoth-Hermes. The Hierophants of Egypt and of Babylon called themselves “Sons of the Serpent-God” and the “Sons of the Dragon.” “I am the Serpent, I am a Druid,” said the Druid of the Celto-Britannic regions, for the Serpent and the Dragon were both symbols of Wisdom, Immortality, and Rebirth. As the serpent casts its old skin only to reappear in a new one, so does the immortal Ego cast off one personality only to assume another.

<term>Draupnir</term> (*Scandinavian*). The golden armlet of Wodan or Odin, the companion of the spear Gungnir which he holds in his right hand; both are endowed with wonderful magic properties.

<term>Dravidians</term>. A group of tribes inhabiting Southern India; the original inhabitants.

<term>Dravya</term> (*Sanskrit*). Substance (metaphysically).

<term>Drishti</term> (*Sanskrit*). Skepticism; unbelief.

<term>Druids</term>. A priestly caste which flourished in Britain and Gaul. They were initiates who admitted females into their sacred order and initiated them into the mysteries of their religion. They never entrusted their sacred verses and scriptures to writing, but, like the Brahmans of old, committed them to memory; a feat which, according to the statement of Caesar, took twenty years to accomplish. Like the Parsis, they had no images or statues of their gods. The Celtic religion considered it blasphemy to represent any god, even of a minor character, in a human figure. It would have been well if the Greek and Roman Christians had learned this lesson from the “pagan” Druids. The three chief commandments of their religion were:—“Obedience to divine laws; concern for the welfare of mankind; bearing all the evils of life with fortitude.”

<term>Druzes</term>. A large sect numbering about 100,000 adherents, living on Mount Lebanon in Syria. Their rites are very mysterious, and no traveler who has written anything about them knows the whole truth for a certainty. They are the *Sufis* of Syria. They resent being called Druzes as an insult, but call themselves the “disciples of Hamsa,” their Messiah, who came to them in the ninth century from the “Land of the Word of God,” which land and word they kept religiously secret. The Messiah to come will be the same Hamsa, but called *Hakem*—the “All-Healer.” (See *Isis Unveiled*, II., 308, and following.)

<term>Dudaim</term> (*Hebrew*). Mandrakes. The *Atropa Mandragora* plant is mentioned in *Genesis*, xxx., 14, and in the *Song of Solomon*: the name is related in Hebrew to words meaning “breasts” and “love.” The plant was notorious as a love charm and has been used in many forms of black magic.

**Dugpas** (*Tibetan*). *Literally*, "Red Caps," a sect in Tibet. Before the arrival of Tsongkhapa in the fourteenth century, the Tibetans—whose Buddhism had deteriorated and been dreadfully corrupted with the tenets of the old *Bhon* religion—were all Dugpas. From that century, however, and after the rigid laws imposed upon the *Gelukpas* (yellow caps) and the general reform and purification of Buddhism (or Lamaism), the Dugpas have devoted themselves more than ever to sorcery, immorality, and drunkenness. Since then, the word *Dugpa* has become a synonym for "sorcerer," "adept of black magic," and everything vile. There are few, if any, Dugpas in Eastern Tibet, but they congregate in Bhutan, Sikkim, and the borderlands generally. Because Europeans are not permitted to penetrate further than those borders, and because Orientalists have never studied Buddho-Lamaism in Tibet proper—instead judging it by hearsay and from what Cosmo di Köros, Schlagintweit, and a few others have learned of it from Dugpas—they confuse both religions and group them under one heading. They thus present pure *Dugpaism* to the public instead of Buddho-Lamaism. In short, Northern Buddhism in its purified, metaphysical form is almost entirely unknown.

**Dukkha** (*Sanskrit*). Sorrow, pain.

**Dumah** (*Hebrew*). The Angel of Silence (Death) in the Kabbalah.

**Durga** (*Sanskrit*). *Literally*, "inaccessible." The female potency of a god; the name of Kali, the wife of Shiva, the *Maheshvara*, or "the great god."

**Dustcharitra** (*Sanskrit*). The "ten evil acts"; namely, three acts of the body, *namely*, taking life, theft, and adultery; four evil acts of the mouth, *namely*, lying, exaggeration in accusations, slandering, and foolish talk; and three evil acts of the mind (Lower Manas), *namely*, envy, malice or revenge, and unbelief.

**Dwapara Yuga** (*Sanskrit*). The third of the "Four Ages" in Hindu Philosophy; or the second age counted from the bottom.

**Dwarf of Death**. In the *Edda* of the Norsemen, Ivaldi, the Dwarf of Death, hides Life in the depths of the great ocean and then sends her up into the world at the right time. This Life is Iduna, the beautiful maiden and daughter of the "Dwarf." She is the Eve of the Scandinavian Lays, for she gives the apples of ever-renewed youth to the gods of Asgard to eat; but these gods, instead of being cursed for doing so and doomed to die, thereby provide renewed youth yearly to the earth and to men after every short and sweet sleep in the arms of the Dwarf. Iduna is raised from the ocean when Bragi (*which see*), the Dreamer of Life, who is without spot or blemish, crosses the silent waste of waters while asleep. Bragi is the divine ideation of Life, and Iduna is living Nature—Prakriti, Eve.

**Dwesa** (*Sanskrit*). Anger. One of the three principal states of mind (of which 63 are listed), which are *Râga*—pride or evil desire, *Dwesa*—anger, of which hatred is a part, and *Moha*—the ignorance of truth. These three are to be steadily avoided.

**Dwijâ** (*Sanskrit*). "Twice-born." In ancient times, this term was used only for the initiated Brahmans; but now it is applied to every man belonging to the first of the four castes who has undergone a certain ceremony.

**Dwija Brahman** (*Sanskrit*). The investiture with the sacred thread that now constitutes the "second birth." Even a Sudra <note>The lowest of the four traditional Hindu castes.</note> who chooses to pay for the honor becomes a *dwijâ* after the ceremony of passing through a silver or golden cow.

**Dwipa** (*Sanskrit*). An island or a continent. The Hindus have seven (*Sapta dwipa*); the Buddhists only four. This is due to a misunderstood reference by the Lord Buddha who, using the term metaphorically, applied the word *dwipa* to the races of men. The four Root-races which preceded our fifth were compared by Siddhartha to four continents or islands which dotted the ocean of birth and death—*Samsâra*.

**Dynasties.** In India there are two, the Lunar and the Solar, or the *Somavansa* and the *Suryavansa*. In Chaldea and Egypt there were also two distinct kinds of dynasties, the *divine* and the *human*. In both countries people were ruled in the beginning of time by dynasties of gods. In Chaldea they reigned one hundred and twenty Sari, or 432,000 years in all; which amounts to the same figures as a Hindu *Mahayuga*, 4,320,000 years. The chronology prefacing the *Book of Genesis* (English translation) is given as "Before Christ, 4004." But the figures are a rendering by solar years. In the original Hebrew, which preserved a lunar calculation, the figures are 4,320 years. This "coincidence" is well explained in Occultism.

**Dyookna** (*Kabbalah*). The shadow of eternal Light. The "Angels of the Presence" or archangels. The same as the *Ferouer* in the *Vendidad* and Zoroastrian works.

**Dzyn or Dzyan** (*Tibetan*). Written also *Dzen*. A corruption of the Sanskrit *Dhyan* and *Jnâna* (or *gnyâna* phonetically)—Wisdom, divine knowledge. In Tibetan, learning is called *dzin*.

### E.—
The fifth letter in the English alphabet. The <term>he</term> (soft) of the Hebrew alphabet becomes in the Ehevi system of reading that language an E. Its numerical value is five, and its symbolism is a <term>window</term>; the womb, in the Kabbala. In the order of the divine names it stands for the fifth, which is <term>Hadoor</term> or the “majestic” and the “splendid.”

**Ea** (<term>Chaldean</term>). also *Hea*. The second god of the original Babylonian trinity composed of Anu, Hea, and Bel. Hea was the “Maker of Fate,” “Lord of the Deep,” “God of Wisdom and Knowledge,” and “Lord of the City of Eridu.”

**Eagle**. This symbol is one of the most ancient. With the Greeks and Persians, it was sacred to the Sun; with the Egyptians, under the name of <term>Ah</term>, to Horus, and the Copts worshipped the eagle under the name of <term>Ahom</term>. It was regarded as the sacred emblem of Zeus by the Greeks, and as that of the highest god by the Druids. The symbol has passed down to our day; when following the example of the pagan Marius, who, in the second century B.C., used the double-headed eagle as the ensign of Rome, the Christian crowned heads of Europe made the double-headed sovereign of the air sacred to themselves and their descendants. Jupiter was satisfied with a one-headed eagle and so was the Sun. The Imperial houses of Russia, Poland, Austria, Germany, and the late Empire of the Napoleons, have adopted a two-headed eagle as their device.

**Easter**. The word evidently comes from Ostara, the Scandinavian goddess of spring. She was the symbol of the resurrection of all nature and was worshipped in early spring. It was a custom with the pagan Norsemen at that time to exchange colored <term>eggs</term> called the eggs of Ostara. These have now become <term>Easter-Eggs</term>. As expressed in <term>Asgard</term> and the <term>Gods</term>: “Christianity put another meaning on the old custom, by connecting it with the feast of the Resurrection of the Savior, who like the hidden life in the egg, slept in the grave for three days before he awakened to new life.” This was the more natural since Christ was identified with that same Spring Sun which awakens in all his glory, after the dreary and long death of winter. (See “<term>Eggs</term>.”)

**Ebionites** (<term>Hebrew</term>). <term>Literally</term>, “the poor”; the earliest sect of Jewish Christians, the other being Nazarenes. They existed when the term “Christian” was not yet heard of. Many of the relations of <term>Iassou</term> (Jesus), the adept ascetic around whom the legend of Christ was formed, were among the Ebionites. As the existence of these mendicant ascetics can be traced at least a century earlier than chronological Christianity.

### Edom (<term>Hebrew</term>).
Edomite Kings. A deeply concealed mystery is found in the allegory of the seven Kings of Edom, who “reigned in the land of Edom before any King reigned over the children of Israel.” (Gen. 36:31.) The Kabbalah teaches that this Kingdom was one of “unbalanced forces” and necessarily of an unstable character. The world of Israel is a type of the condition of the worlds which came into existence after the later period when equilibrium had been established. <note>w.w.w. likely refers to William Wynn Westcott, a prominent occultist and contemporary of the author.</note>

On the other hand, the Eastern Esoteric philosophy teaches that the seven Kings of Edom are not the type of perished worlds or unbalanced forces, but the symbol of the seven human Root-races, four of which have passed away, the fifth is passing, and two are still to come. Though in the language of esoteric *blinds*, the hint in *St. John’s Revelation* is clear enough when it states in chapter 17, verse 10: “And there are seven Kings; five are fallen, and one (the fifth, still) is, and the other (the sixth Root-race) has not yet come. . . .” Had all the *seven Kings of Edom* perished as worlds of “unbalanced forces,” how could the fifth still be, and the others “not yet come”? In *The Kabbalah Unveiled*, we read on page 48, “The seven Kings had died and their possessions had been broken up,” and a footnote emphasizes the statement by saying, “these seven Kings are the Edomite Kings.”

### Edris (<term>Arabic</term>).
or *Idris*. Meaning “the learned One,” an epithet applied by the Arabs to Enoch.

### Eggs (**Easter**).
Eggs were symbolized from an early time. There was with the Hindus the “Mundane Egg,” in which Brahma gestated, also called the *Hiranya-Gharba*, and the Mundane Egg of the Egyptians, which proceeds from the mouth of the “unmade and eternal deity,” Kneph, and which is the emblem of generative power. Then there is the “Egg of Babylon,” which hatched Ishtar, and was said to have fallen from heaven into the Euphrates. Therefore, colored eggs were used yearly during spring in almost every country; in Egypt, they were exchanged as sacred symbols in the spring-time, which was, is, and ever will be the emblem of birth or rebirth—cosmic and human, celestial and terrestrial. They were hung up in Egyptian temples and are so suspended to this day in Mahometan <note>Modernly referred to as Muslim or Islamic.</note> mosques.

In his system, he shows the uppermost regions from the zenith of the Universe to the moon belonging to the gods, or planetary Spirits, according to their hierarchies and classes. **Ego** (*Lat.*). "Self"; the consciousness in man "I am I"—or the feeling of "I-am-ship." Esoteric philosophy teaches the existence of two *Egos* in man: the mortal or *personal*, and the Higher, the Divine and the Impersonal; it calls the former "personality" and the latter "Individuality."

**Egoity**. From the word "Ego." Egoity means "individuality," never "personality," and is the opposite of egoism or "selfishness," which is the characteristic *par excellence* of the latter.

**Egregores**. Eliphas Lévi calls them the "chiefs of the souls who are the spirits of energy and action," whatever that may or may not mean. The Oriental Occultists describe the Egregores as Beings whose bodies and essence are a tissue of the so-called astral light. They are the shadows of the higher Planetary Spirits whose bodies are made of the essence of the higher divine light.

**Eheyeh** (*Heb.*). "I am," according to Ibn Gebirol, but not in the sense of "I am that I am."

**Eidolon** (*Gr.*). The same as that which we term the human phantom, the astral form.

**Eka** (*Sk.*). "One"; also a synonym of <term>Mahat</term>, the *Universal Mind*, as the principle of Intelligence.

**Ekana-rupa** (*Sk.*). The One (and the Many) bodies or forms; a term applied by the <term>Puranas</term> <note>The OCR reads "Parānas," likely a typo for the Puranas, a body of Indian sacred literature.</note> to Deity.

**El-Elion** (*Heb.*). A name of the Deity borrowed by the Jews from the Phoenician *Elon*, a name of the Sun.

**Elementals**. Spirits of the Elements. The creatures evolved in the four Kingdoms or Elements—earth, air, fire, and water. At the present stage of learning, it has been thought best to apply the term to the spooks or phantoms of disembodied persons, in general—to those whose temporary residence is the *Kâma Loka*. Eliphas Lévi and some other Kabbalists make little distinction between elementary spirits who have been human and those beings that inhabit the elements and are the blind forces of nature. Once separated from their higher triads and their bodies, these souls remain in their *Kâma-rupic* envelopes and are irresistibly drawn to the earth among elements compatible with their coarse natures. Their stay in the *Kâma Loka* varies in its duration, but it ends invariably in disintegration, dissolving like a column of mist, atom by atom, into the surrounding elements.

**Elephanta.** An island near Bombay, India, on which are the well-preserved ruins of the cave-temple of that name. It is one of the most ancient in the country and is certainly a Cyclopean work, though the late J. Fergusson denied it a great antiquity.

**Eleusinia** (*Gr.*). The Eleusinian Mysteries were the most famous and the most ancient of all the Greek Mysteries (except for the Samothracian), and were celebrated near the hamlet of Eleusis, not far from Athens. Epiphanius traces them back to the days of Inachos (1800 B.C.), though another version has it that they were founded by Eumolpus, a King of Thrace and a Hierophant. They were celebrated in honor of Demeter, the Greek Ceres and the Egyptian Isis; and the last act of the performance referred to a sacrificial victim of atonement and a resurrection, when the Initiate was admitted to the highest degree of “Epopt” (*q.v.*). The festival of the Mysteries began in the month of Boëdromion (September), the time of the grape harvest, and lasted from the 15th to the 22nd—seven days. The Hebrew feast of Tabernacles, the feast of *Ingathering*, in the month of Ethanim (the seventh), also began on the 15th and ended on the 22nd of that month. According to some, the name of the month (Ethanim) is derived from Adonim, Adonia, Attenim, or Ethanim, and was in honor of Adonaï or Adonis (Thammuz), whose death was lamented by the Hebrews in the groves of Bethlehem. The sacrifice of both “Bread and Wine” was performed before the Mysteries of initiation, and during the ceremony, the mysteries were divulged to the candidates from the *petromata*, a kind of book made of two stone tablets (*petrai*) joined at one side and made to open like a volume. (See *Isis Unveiled* II., pp. 44 and 91, *et seq*., for further explanations.)

**Elivagar** (*Scand.*). The waters of Chaos, called in the cosmogony of the Norsemen “the stream of Elivagar.”

**Elohîm** (*Heb.*). Also *Alhim*, the word being variously spelled. Godfrey Higgins, who has written much upon its meaning, always spells it *Aleim*. The Hebrew letters are *aleph, lamed, hé, yod, mem*, and are numerically 1, 30, 5, 10, 40=86. **Eloï** (*Gn.*). The Genius or ruler of Jupiter; its Planetary Spirit. (See Origen, *Contra Celsum*).

**Elu** (*Sing.*). An ancient dialect used in Ceylon.

**Emanation**, *the Doctrine of.* In its metaphysical meaning, it is opposed to Evolution, yet one with it. Science teaches that evolution is physiologically a mode of generation in which the germ that develops the fetus already pre-exists in the parent, the development and final form and characteristics of that germ being accomplished in nature; and that in cosmology, the process takes place blindly through the correlation of the elements and their various compounds. Occultism answers that this is only the apparent mode, the real process being Emanation, guided by intelligent Forces under an immutable Law. Therefore, while Occultists and Theosophists believe thoroughly in the doctrine of Evolution as given by Kapila and Manu, they are Emanationists rather than Evolutionists. The doctrine of Emanation was at one time universal. It was taught by the Alexandrian as well as by the Indian philosophers, by the Egyptian, the Chaldean, and Hellenic Hierophants, and also by the Hebrews (in their Kabbalah, and even in *Genesis*). For it is only due to deliberate mistranslation that the Hebrew word <term>asdt</term> has been translated as "angels" in the Septuagint, when it means *Emanations* or *Aeons*, precisely as with the Gnostics. Indeed, in Deuteronomy (33:2), the word <term>asdt</term> or <term>ashdt</term> is translated as "fiery law," while the correct rendering of the passage should be "from his right hand went [not a fiery law, but] a fire according to law"; that is, the fire of one flame is imparted to and caught up by another, like a trail of inflammable substance. This is precisely emanation. As shown in *Isis Unveiled*: "In Evolution, as it is now beginning to be understood, there is supposed to be in all matter an impulse to take on a higher form—a supposition clearly expressed by Manu and other Hindu philosophers of the highest antiquity. The philosopher's tree illustrates it in the case of the zinc solution. The controversy between the followers of this school and the Emanationists may be briefly stated thus: The Evolutionist stops all inquiry at the borders of 'the Unknowable'; the Emanationist believes that nothing can be evolved—or, as the word means, unwombed or born—unless it has first been involved, thus indicating that life is from a spiritual potency above the whole."

**Empusa** (*Gr.*). A ghoul, a vampire, an evil demon taking various forms.

**En** (or **Ain**) **Soph** (*Heb.*). The endless, limitless, and boundless. The absolute deific Principle, impersonal and unknowable. It means literally "no-thing"—that is, nothing that could be classed with anything

Exoterically, mythology makes Eros the god of lustful, animal desire, which is the origin of the term *erotic*; esoterically, it is different. (See "Kama").

### <term>F.</term>
—The sixth letter of the <term>English</term> alphabet, for which there is no equivalent in <term>Hebrew</term>. It is the double <term>F</term> of the <term>Aeolians</term> which became the <term>Digamma</term> for some mysterious reasons. It corresponds to the <term>Greek phi</term>. As a <term>Latin</term> numeral, it denotes 40; with a dash over the letter (<term>F</term>), it denotes 400,000.

### <term>Faces</term> (<term>Kabbalistic</term>),
or, as in <term>Hebrew</term>, <term>Partzupham</term>. The word usually refers to <term>Areek Anpeen</term> or Long Face, and <term>Zeir-Anpen</term>, or Short Face, and <term>Resha Hivrah</term>, the “White Head” or Face. The <term>Kabbala</term> states that from the moment of their appearance (the hour of differentiation of matter), all the material for future forms was contained in the three Heads, which are one and called <term>Atteekah Kadosha</term> (Holy Ancients and the Faces). It is when the Faces look toward each other that the “Holy Ancients” in three Heads, or <term>Atteekah Kadosha</term>, are called <term>Areek Appayem</term>, i.e., “Long Faces.” (See <term>Zohar</term> iii., 292a.) This refers to the three Higher Principles, cosmic and human.

### <term>Fafnir</term> (<term>Scand</term>.).
The <term>Dragon of Wisdom</term>.

### <term>Fahian</term> (<term>Chin</term>.).
A <term>Chinese</term> traveler and writer in the early centuries of <term>Christianity</term> who wrote on <term>Buddhism</term>.

### <term>Fa-Hwa-King</term> (<term>Chin</term>.).
A <term>Chinese</term> work on <term>Cosmogony</term>.

### <term>Faizi</term> (<term>Arab</term>.).
Literally the “heart.” A writer on <term>occult</term> and <term>mystic</term> subjects.

### <term>Fakir</term> (<term>Arab</term>.).
A <term>Muslim ascetic</term> in <term>India</term>, a <term>Mohammedan</term> “<term>Yogi</term>.” The name is often applied, though erroneously, to <term>Hindu ascetics</term>; for strictly speaking, only <term>Muslim ascetics</term> are entitled to it. This loose way of calling things by general names was adopted in *<term>Isis Unveiled</term>*, but is now corrected.

### <term>Falk</term>, <term>Cain Chenul</term>.
A <term>Kabbalistic Jew</term> reputed to have worked “miracles.” <term>Kenneth Mackenzie</term> quotes in regard to him from the <term>German</term> annalist <term>Archenoilz’</term> work on <term>England</term> (1788): “There exists in <term>London</term> an extraordinary man who for thirty years has been celebrated in <term>Kabbalistic</term> records. He is named <term>Cain Chenul Falk</term>. A certain <term>Count de Rantzow</term>, who recently died in the service of <term>France</term> with the rank of <term>Field-Marshal</term>, certifies that he has seen this <term>Falk</term> in <term>Brunswick</term>, and that evocations of spirits took place in the presence of credible witnesses.” These “spirits” were <term>Elementals</term>, whom <term>Falk</term> brought into view by the conjurations used by every <term>Kabbalist</term>. His son, <term>Johann Frederich Falk</term>, likewise a <term>Jew</term>, was also a <term>Kabbalist</term> of repute and was once the head of a <term>Kabbalist college</term> in <term>London</term>. His occupation was that of a <term>jeweler</term> and <term>appraiser of diamonds</term>, and he was a wealthy man.

### <term>Farbauti</term> (*Scand.*). 
A giant in the *Edda*; literally, “the oarsman”; the father of <term>Loki</term>, whose mother was the giantess <term>Laufey</term> (leafy isle). This is a genealogy which makes W. S. W. Anson remark in *Asgard and the Gods* that probably the oarsman or <term>Farbauti</term> “was . . . . . the giant who saved himself from the flood in a boat, and the latter (<term>Laufey</term>) was the island to which he rowed”—which is an additional variation of the <term>Deluge</term>.

### <term>Fargard</term> (*Zend*). 
A section or chapter of verses in the *Vendidad* of the <term>Parsis</term>.

### <term>Farvarshi</term> (*Mazdaean*). 
The same as *Ferouer*, or the opposite (as contrasted) double. The spiritual counterpart of the still more spiritual original. Thus, <term>Ahriman</term> is the *Ferouer* or the <term>Farvarshi</term> of <term>Ormuzd</term>—“*demon est deus inversus*” <note>the devil is God inverted</note>—the Satan of God. <term>Michael</term> the Archangel, “he who is like god”, is a *Ferouer* of that god. A <term>Farvarshi</term> is the shadowy or dark side of a Deity—or its darker lining.

### <term>Ferho</term> (*Gnostic*). 
The highest and greatest creative power according to the <term>Nazarene Gnostics</term>. (*Codex Nazaræus*).

### <term>Fetahil</term> (*Gr.*). 
The lower creator, in the same *Codex*.

### <term>First Point</term>. 
Metaphysically, the first point of manifestation, the germ of primeval differentiation, or the point in the infinite Circle “whose center is everywhere, and circumference nowhere”. The Point is the <term>Logos</term>.

### <term>Fire (Living)</term>. 
A figure of speech to denote deity, the “One” life. A theurgic term, used later by the <term>Rosicrucians</term>. The symbol of the living fire is the sun, certain of whose rays develop the fire of life in a diseased body, impart the knowledge of the future to the sluggish mind, and stimulate to active function a certain psychic and generally dormant faculty in man. The meaning is very occult.

### <term>Fire-Philosophers</term>. 
The name given to the <term>Hermetists</term> and <term>Alchemists</term> of the Middle Ages, and also to the <term>Rosicrucians</term>. The latter, the successors of the <term>Theurgists</term>, regarded fire as the symbol of Deity. It was the source, not only of material atoms, but the container of the spiritual and psychic Forces energizing them. Broadly analyzed, fire is a triple principle; esoterically, it is a septenary, as are all the rest of the Elements. As man is composed of Spirit, Soul, and Body, plus a fourfold aspect, so is Fire. As in the works of <term>Robert Fludd</term> (<term>de Fluctibus</term>), one of the famous <term>Rosicrucians</term>, Fire contains (1) a visible flame (Body); (2) an invisible, astral fire (Soul); and (3) Spirit. The four aspects are heat (life), light (mind), electricity (<term>Kâmic</term>, or molecular powers), and the Synthetic Essence, *beyond Spirit*, or the radical cause of its existence and manifestation. **Fifty Gates of Wisdom** (*Kab.*). The number is a *blind* <note>a term used in occultism to hide a true meaning from the uninitiated</note>, and there are really 49 gates. This is because Moses—than whom the Jewish world has no higher adept—reached and passed only the 49th, according to the Kabbalah. These "gates" typify the different planes of Being or *Ens*. They are thus the "gates" of Life and the "gates" of understanding or degrees of occult knowledge. These 49 (or 50) gates correspond to the seven gates in the seven caves of Initiation into the Mysteries of Mithra (see Celsus and Kircher). The division of the 50 gates into five chief gates—each including *ten*—is again a blind. It is in the fourth gate of these five (beginning from the fourth and ending at the tenth, which comprises the world of Planets, thus making seven and corresponding to the seven lower Sephiroth) that the key to their meaning lies hidden. They are also called the "gates of Binah" or understanding.

**Flagæ** (*Herm.*). A name given by Paracelsus to a particular kind of guardian angel or genii.

**Flame** (*Holy*). The "Holy Flame" is the name given by the Eastern Asiatic Kabbalists (Semites) to the *Anima Mundi*, the "world-soul." The Initiates were called the "Sons of the Holy Flame."

**Fludd** (*Robert*), generally known as *Robertus de Fluctibus*, the chief of the "Philosophers by Fire." He was a celebrated English Hermetist of the sixteenth century and a voluminous writer. He wrote on the essence of gold and other mystic and occult subjects.

**Fluvii Transitus** (*Lat.*). Or the "crossing of the River" (Chebar). Cornelius Agrippa provides this alphabet. In the *Ars Quatuor Coronatorum*, Vol. III, part 2, 1890—which is the report of the proceedings of the Quatuor Coronati Lodge of Freemasons, No. 2076—one will find copies of this alphabet, as well as the curious old letters called Melachim and the Celestial alphabet, provided by W. Wynn Westcott, P.M. <note>Past Master</note>. This lodge seems to be the only one in England that truly studies "the hidden mysteries of Nature and Science" in earnest.

**Fohat** (*Tib.*). A term used to represent the active (male) potency of the Sakti (female reproductive power) in nature. It is the essence of cosmic electricity. An occult Tibetan term for *Daiviprakriti*, or primordial light; in the universe of manifestation, it is the ever-present electrical energy and ceaseless destructive and formative power. Esoterically it is the same: Fohat is the universal propelling *Vital Force*, serving as both the propeller and the result.

**Foh-tchou** (*Chin.*). *Literally*, "Buddha’s Lord," though it simply means the teacher of the doctrines of Buddha. Foh refers to a Guru who generally lives in a temple of a Shakyamuni Buddha—the Foh-Maeyu.

**Fountain of Life** (*De Materia Universali* and *Fons Vitæ*). Western <term>Kabbalists</term> have proclaimed it a truly <term>Kabbalistic</term> work. Several <term>manuscripts</term>, in Latin and Hebrew, of this wonderful production have been discovered by scholars in public libraries; among others, one was found by <term>Munk</term> in 1802. The Latin name of <term>Ibn Gebirol</term> was <term>Avicebron</term>, a name well known to all Oriental scholars.

**<term>Four Animals</term>**. The symbolic animals of the vision of <term>Ezekiel</term> (the <term>Mercabah</term>). "Among the first Christians, the celebration of the <term>Mysteries of the Faith</term> was accompanied by the burning of seven lights, along with incense, the <term>Trishagion</term>, and the reading of the book of the gospels, upon which was depicted—both on the covers and the pages—the winged man, lion, bull, and eagle" (*Qabbalah*, by <term>Isaac Myer</term>, LL.B.). To this day, these animals are represented along with the four <term>Evangelists</term> and placed before their respective gospels in the editions of the <term>Greek Church</term>. Each represents one of the four lower classes of worlds or planes, into the likeness of which each *personality* is cast. Thus, the Eagle (associated with <term>St. John</term>) represents cosmic <term>Spirit</term> or <term>Ether</term>, the all-piercing <term>Eye of the Seer</term>; the Bull of <term>St. Luke</term> represents the waters of Life, the all-generating element and cosmic strength; the Lion of <term>St. Mark</term> represents fierce energy, undaunted courage, and cosmic fire; while the human Head or the Angel, which stands near <term>St. Matthew</term>, is the synthesis of all three combined in the higher <term>Intellect of man</term> and in cosmic <term>spirituality</term>. All these symbols are Egyptian, Chaldean, and Indian. Eagle, Bull, and Lion-headed gods are plentiful, and all represented the same idea, whether in the Egyptian, Chaldean, Indian, or Jewish religions; but beginning with the <term>Astral body</term>, they went no higher than the cosmic Spirit or the <term>Higher Manas</term>—since <term>Atma-Buddhi</term> (or <term>Absolute Spirit and Spiritual Soul</term>, its vehicle) is incapable of being symbolized by concrete images.

**<term>Fravasham</term>** (*Zend*). Absolute spirit.

**<term>Freya</term>** or *Frigga* (*Scandinavian*). In the *Edda*, <term>Frigga</term> is the mother of the gods, similar to <term>Aditi</term> in the *Vedas*. She is identical with the Northern <term>Frea</term> of the Germans, and in her lowest aspect, she was worshiped as the all-nourishing Mother Earth. She was seated on her golden throne, formed of webs of golden light, with three divine virgins as her handmaidens and messengers, and she was occupied with spinning golden threads with which to reward good men. She is <term>Isis</term> and <term>Diana</term> at the same time, for she is also <term>Holda</term>, the mighty huntress, and she is <term>Ceres-Demeter</term>, who protects agriculture—the moon and nature.

**<term>Frost Giants</term>** or *Hrimthurses* (*Scandinavian*). They are the great builders, the <term>Cyclopes</term> and <term>Titans</term> of the Norsemen, and they play a prominent part in the *Edda*. It is they who build the strong wall around <term>Asgard</term> (the Scandinavian Olympus) to protect it from the <term>Jotuns</term>, the wicked giants.

**<term>Flyfot</term>** (*Scandinavian*). A weapon of <term>Thor</term>, like the <term>Swastika</term> or the <term>Jaina</term>, the four-footed cross; it is generally called "Thor's Hammer".

## G.

**G.**—The seventh letter in the English alphabet. "In Greek, <term>Chaldean</term>, <term>Syriac</term>, Hebrew, <term>Assyrian</term>, <term>Samaritan</term>, <term>Etrurian</term>, <term>Coptic</term>, in the modern <term>Romaic</term> and <term>Gothic</term>, it occupies the third place in the alphabet, while in <term>Cyrillic</term>, <term>Glagolitic</term>, <term>Croatian</term>, Russian, <term>Serbian</term>, and <term>Wallachian</term>, it stands fourth." As the name of "God" begins with this letter (in <term>Syriac</term>, *gad*; Swedish, *gud*; German, *gott*; English, *god*; Persian, *gada*, etc.), there is an occult reason for this which only the students of esoteric philosophy and of the *<term>Secret Doctrine</term>*, explained esoterically, will thoroughly understand; it refers to the three <term>logoi</term>—the last, the <term>Elohim</term>, and the emanation of the latter, the androgynous <term>Adam Kadmon</term>. All these peoples have derived the name of "God" from their respective traditions, which are more or less clear echoes of the esoteric tradition. Spoken and "Silent Speech" (writing) are a "gift of the gods," say all the national traditions, from the old Aryan <term>Sanskrit</term>-speaking people who claim that their alphabet, the <term>Devanâgari</term> (literally, the language of the <term>devas</term> or gods) was given to them from heaven, down to the Jews, who speak of an alphabet—the parent of the one which has survived—as having been a celestial and mystical symbolism given by the angels to the patriarchs. Hence, every letter had its manifold meaning. A symbol itself of celestial beings and objects, it was, in its turn, represented on earth by similar corresponding objects whose form symbolized the shape of the letter. The present letter, called in Hebrew <term>gimel</term> and symbolized by a long camel's neck, or rather a serpent standing erect, is associated with the third sacred divine name, <term>Ghadol</term> or <term>Magnus</term> (great). Its numeral is four, representing the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> and the sacred <term>Tetraktys</term>; hence its sacredness. With other people it stood for 400, and with a dash over it, for 400,000.

**Gabriel.** According to the <term>Gnostics</term>, the "Spirit" or <term>Christos</term>, the "messenger of life," and <term>Gabriel</term> are one. The former "is sometimes called the Angel <term>Gabriel</term>—in Hebrew 'the mighty one of God'—" and among the <term>Gnostics</term> took the place of the <term>Logos</term>, while the Holy Spirit was considered one with the <term>Æon</term> *Life* (see *Irenæus* I., xii.). Therefore we find <term>Theodoret</term> saying (in *Hæret. Fab.*, II., vii.): "The heretics agree with us (Christians) concerning the beginning of all things . . . but they say there is not one <term>Christ</term> (God), but *one* above and the *other below*. And this latter formerly dwelt in many; but the Jesus, they at one time say is *from* God, and at another they call him a Spirit." The key to this is given in the esoteric philosophy. The "spirit" with the <term>Gnostics</term> was a female potency exoterically; it was

**Gæa** (*Gr.*). Primordial Matter in the Cosmogony of Hesiod; Earth, as some believe; the wife of Ouranos, the sky or heavens. The female personage of the primeval Trinity, composed of Ouranos, Gæa, and Eros.

**Gaffarillus**. An Alchemist and philosopher who lived in the middle of the seventeenth century. He is the first philosopher known to maintain that every natural object (for example, plants, living creatures, etc.), when burned, retained its form in its ashes and that it could be raised again from them. This claim was justified by the eminent chemist Du Chesne, and after him Kircher, Digby, and Vallemont have assured themselves of the fact by demonstrating that the astral forms of burned plants could be raised from their ashes. A recipe for raising such astral phantoms of flowers is given in a work of Oetinger, *Thoughts on the Birth and the Generation of Things*.

**Gaganeswara** (*Sk.*). “Lord of the Sky,” a name of Garuda.

**Gai-hinnom** (*Heb.*). The name of Hell in the Talmud.

**Gambatrin** (*Scand.*). The name of Hermodur’s “magic staff” in the Edda.

**Ganadevas** (*Sk.*). A certain class of celestial Beings who are said to inhabit Maharloka. They are the rulers of our Kalpa (Cycle) and therefore termed Kalpâdhikârin, or Lord of the Kalpas. They last only “One Day” of Brahmâ.

**Grandapada** (*Sk.*). <note>Likely a misspelling of Gaudapada.</note> A celebrated Brahman teacher, the author of the Commentaries on the *Sankhya Karika*, *Mandukya Upanishad*, and other works.

**Gândhâra** (*Sk.*). A musical note of great occult power in the Hindu gamut—the third of the diatonic scale.

**Gandharva** (*Sk.*). The celestial choristers and musicians of India. In the *Vedas* these deities reveal the secrets of heaven and earth and esoteric science to mortals. They had charge of the sacred Soma plant and its juice, the ambrosia drunk in the temple which gives “omniscience.”

**Gan-Eden** (*Heb.*). Also *Ganduniyas*. (See “Eden”).

**Ganesa** (*Sk.*). The elephant-headed God of Wisdom, the son of Siva. He is the same as the Egyptian Thoth-Hermes, and Anubis or Hermanubis (*q.v.*). The legend shows him as having lost his human head, which was replaced by that of an elephant.

**Gangâ** (*Sk.*). The Ganges, the principal sacred river in India.

There are two versions of its myth: one relates that Gangâ (the goddess), having transformed herself into a river, flows from the big toe of Vishnu; the other says that the Gangâ drops from the ear of Siva into the Anavatapta lake, then passes out through the mouth of the silver cow (*gômukhi*), crosses all of Eastern India, and falls into the Southern Ocean. "An 'heretical superstition'", remarks Mr. Eitel in his *Sanskrit-Chinese Dictionary*, "ascribes sin-cleansing power to the waters of the Ganges." One would say this is no more a "superstition" than the belief that the waters of Baptism and the Jordan have "sin-cleansing power."

**Gangâdwâra** (*Sk.*). Literally, "The gate or door of the Ganges"; the name of a town now called Hardwar, at the foot of the Himalayas.

**Gangi** (*Sk.*). A renowned Sorcerer in the time of Kâsyapa Buddha (a predecessor of Gautama). Gangi was regarded as an incarnation of Apalâla, the Nâga (Serpent), the guardian Spirit of the Sources of Subhavastu, a river in Udyâna. Apalâla is said to have been converted to the good Law by Gautama Buddha and to have become an Arhat. The allegory of the name is understandable: all the Adepts and Initiates were called *nâgas*, "Serpents of Wisdom."

**Ganinnânse.** A Sinhalese priest who has not yet been ordained—from *gana*, an assemblage or brotherhood. The higher ordained priests "are called *terunnânse* from the Pali *thêro*, an elder" (Hardy).

**Garm** (*Scand.*). The Cerberus of the *Edda*. This monstrous dog lived in the Gnypa cavern in front of the dwelling of Hel, the goddess of the underworld.

**Garuda** (*Sk.*). A gigantic bird in the *Râmâyana*, the steed of Vishnu. Esoterically—the symbol of the great Cycle.

**Gâthâ** (*Sk.*). Metrical chants or hymns consisting of moral aphorisms. A gâthâ of thirty-two words is called Âryâgiti.

**Gâti** (*Sk.*). The six (esoterically *seven*) conditions of sentient existence. These are divided into two groups: the three higher and the three lower paths. To the former belong the devas, the asuras, and (*immortal*) men; to the latter (in exoteric teachings) belong creatures in hell, *pretas* or hungry demons, and animals. Explained esoterically, however, the last three are the personalities in Kâmaloka, elementals, and animals. The seventh mode of existence is that of the Nirmanakâya (q.v.).

**Gâtra** (*Sk.*). *Literally*, the limbs (of Brahmâ) from which the "mind-born" sons, the seven Kumâras, were born.

**Gautama** (*Sk.*). The Prince of Kapilavastu, son of Suddhodana, the Sakya king of a small realm on the borders of Nepal; born in the seventh century B.C., he is now called the "Saviour of the World." Gautama or Gotama was the sacerdotal name of the Sakya family, and Siddhartha was Buddha's name before he became a Buddha. Sakya Muni means the Saint of the Sakya family. Born a simple mortal, he rose to Buddhaship through his own personal and unaided merit. A man—truly greater than any god!

**Gayâ** (*Sk.*). An ancient city of Magadha, a little northwest of modern Gaya. It was at the former that Sakyamuni reached his Buddhahood under the famous Bodhi tree, *Bodhidruma*.

**Gayâtri** (*Sk.*), also *Sâvitri*. A most sacred verse addressed to the Sun in the Rig-Veda, which the Brahmans must repeat mentally every morning and evening during their devotions.

**Geber** (*Heb.*), or *Gibborim*. "Mighty men"; the same as the *Kabirim*. In heaven, they are regarded as powerful angels; on earth, they are the giants mentioned in chapter 6 of *Genesis*.

**Gebirol, Salomon Ben Jehudah**. Called in literature *Avicebron*. An Israelite by birth, a philosopher, poet, and Kabbalist; a voluminous writer and a mystic. He was born in the eleventh century at Malaga (1021), educated at Saragossa, and died at Valencia in 1070, murdered by a Muslim. His fellow religionists called him Solomon the Sephardi, or the Spaniard, and the Arabs called him Abu Ayyub Suleiman ben Yahya Ibn Gabirol, while the scholastics named him Avicebron (see Myer’s *Qabbalah*). Ibn Gabirol was certainly one of the greatest philosophers and scholars of his age. He wrote much in Arabic, and most of his manuscripts have been preserved. His greatest work appears to be the *Megôr Hayyîm*, that is, the *Fountain of Life*, "one of the earliest exposures of the secrets of the Speculative Kabbalah," as his biographer informs us (see "Fons Vitæ").

**Geburah** (*Heb.*). A Kabbalistic term; the fifth Sephira, a female and passive potency, meaning severity and power; from it, the Pillar of Severity is named. [w.w.w.]

**Gedulah** (*Heb.*). Another name for the Sephira *Chesed*.

**Gehenna**, in Hebrew *Hinnom*. Not a hell at all, but a valley near Jerusalem where Israelites sacrificed their children to Moloch. In that valley, a place named *Tophet* was situated, where a fire was perpetually maintained for sanitary purposes. The prophet Jeremiah informs us that his countrymen, the Jews, used to sacrifice their children at that spot.

**Gehs** (*Zend*). Parsi prayers.

**Gelukpa** (*Tib.*). Literally "Yellow Caps"; the highest and most orthodox Buddhist sect in Tibet, the antithesis of the *Dugpa* ("Red Caps"), the old "devil worshippers."

**Gemara** (*Heb.*). The latter portion of the Jewish Talmud, begun by Rabbi Ashi and completed by Rabbis Mar and Meremar around 300 A.D. [w.w.w.] Literally "to finish," it is a commentary on the Mishna.

**Gematria** (*Heb.*). A division of the practical Kabbalah. It shows the numerical value of Hebrew words by summing up the values of the letters composing them; furthermore, it shows by this means analogies between words and phrases. [w.w.w.] One of the arithmetical methods for extracting the hidden meaning from letters, words, and sentences.

**Gems.** Three precious. In Southern Buddhism, these are the sacred books, the Buddhas, and the priesthood. In Northern Buddhism and its secret schools, they are the Buddha, his sacred teachings, and the Narjols (Buddhas of Compassion).

**Genesis.** The whole of the Book of Genesis, down to the death of Joseph, is found to be a barely altered version of the Cosmogony of the Chaldeans, as is now repeatedly proven from the Assyrian tablets. The first three chapters are transcribed from the allegorical narratives of the beginnings common to all nations. Chapters four and five are a new allegorical adaptation of the same narration in the secret *Book of Numbers*; chapter six is an astronomical narrative of the solar year and the seven *cosmocratores* from the Egyptian original of the *Pymander* and the symbolic visions of a series of *Enochioi* (Seers)—from whom also came the Book of Enoch. The beginning of Exodus and the story of Moses is that of the Babylonian Sargon, who, having flourished (as even that unwilling authority Dr. Sayce tells us) 3750 B.C., preceded the Jewish lawgiver by almost 2300 years. (See *Secret Doctrine*, vol. II., pp. 691 *et seq.*). Nevertheless, *Genesis* is an undeniably esoteric work. It has not borrowed from, nor has it disfigured the universal symbols and teachings upon the lines of which it was written, but simply adapted the eternal truths to its own national spirit and clothed them in cunning allegories comprehensible only to its Kabbalists and Initiates. The Gnostics have done the same, each sect in its own way, as thousands of years before, India, Egypt, Chaldea, and Greece had also dressed the same incommunicable truths each in its own national garb. The key and solution to all such narratives can be found only in the esoteric teachings.

**Genii** (*Lat.*). A name for Aeons, or angels, among the Gnostics. The names of their hierarchies and classes are simply legion.

**Geonic Period.** The era of the Geonim may be found mentioned in works treating of the Kabbalah; the ninth century A.D. is implied. [w.w.w.]

**Gharma** (*Sk.*). A title of Karttikeya, the Indian god of war and the Kumara born of Shiva’s drop of sweat that fell into the Ganges.

**Ghôcha** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, “the miraculous Voice.” The name of a great Arhat, the author of *Abhidharmamrita Shastra*, who restored sight to a blind man by anointing his eyes with the tears of the audience, who were moved by his (Ghocha’s) supernatural eloquence.

**Gilgoolem** (*Heb.*). The cycle of rebirths among the Hebrew Kabbalists; with the orthodox Kabbalists, it is the “whirling of the soul” after death, which finds no rest until it reaches Palestine, the “promised land,” and its body is buried there.

**Gimil** (*Scand.*). “The Cave of Gimil” or Wingolf. A kind of Heaven or Paradise, or perhaps a New Jerusalem, built by the “Strong

**Ginnungagap** (*Scand*.). Literally the “cup of illusion”; the abyss of the great deep, or the shoreless, beginningless, and endless yawning gulf; which in esoteric language we call the “World’s Matrix”, the primordial living space. The cup that contains the universe, hence the “cup of illusion”.

**Giöl** (*Scand*.). The Styx, the river Giöl which had to be crossed before the netherworld was reached, or the cold Kingdom of Hel. It was spanned by a gold-covered bridge, which led to the gigantic iron fence that encircles the palace of the Goddess of the Underworld or Hel.

**Gna** (*Scand*.). One of the three handmaidens of the goddess Freya. She is a female Mercury who bears her mistress’ messages into all parts of the world.

**Gnâna** (*Sk*.). Knowledge as applied to the esoteric sciences.

**Gnân Devas** (*Sk*.). Lit., “the gods of knowledge”. The higher classes of gods or *devas*; the “mind-born” sons of Brahmâ, and others including the *Mânasa-putras* (the Sons of Intellect). Esoterically, our reincarnating Egos.

**Gnânasakti** (*Sk*.). The power of true knowledge, one of the seven great forces in Nature (*six*, exoterically).

**Gnâtha** (*Sk*.). The Kosmic Ego; the conscious, intelligent Soul of Kosmos.

**Gnomes** (*Alch*.). The Rosicrucian name for the mineral and earth elementals.

**Gnôsis** (*Gr*.). Lit., “knowledge”. The technical term used by the schools of religious philosophy, both before and during the first centuries of so-called Christianity, to denote the object of their inquiry. This Spiritual and Sacred Knowledge, the *Gupta Vidyâ* of the Hindus, could only be obtained by Initiation into Spiritual Mysteries of which the ceremonial “Mysteries” were a type.

**Gnostics** (*Gr*.). The philosophers who formulated and taught the Gnôsis or Knowledge (*q.v*.). They flourished in the first three centuries of the Christian era: the following were eminent, Valentinus, Basilides, Marcion, Simon Magus, etc. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Gnyрa** (*Scand*.). The cavern watched by the dog Garm (*q.v*.).

**Gogard** (*Zend*). The Tree of Life in the *Avesta*.

**Golden Age.** The ancients divided the life cycle into the Golden, Silver, Bronze, and Iron Ages. The Golden was an age of primeval purity, simplicity, and general happiness.

**Gonpa** (*Tib*). A temple or monastery; a *Lamasery*.

**Gopîs** (*Sk*.). Shepherdesses—the playmates and companions of Krishna, among whom was his wife Raddha.

**Gossain** (*Sk.*). The name of a certain class of <term>ascetics</term> in India.
**Great Age.** There were several “great ages” mentioned by the ancients. In India, it embraced the whole <term>Maha-manvantara</term>, the “age of <term>Brahmâ</term>”, each “Day” of which represents the life cycle of a chain—that is, it embraces a period of seven <term>Rounds</term>. (See *Esoteric Buddhism*, by A. P. Sinnett.) Thus, while a “Day” and a “Night” represent, as <term>Manvantara</term> and <term>Pralaya</term>, 8,640,000,000 years, an “age” lasts through a period of 311,040,000,000,000 years; after which the <term>Pralaya</term>, or dissolution of the universe, becomes universal. With the Egyptians and Greeks, the “great age” referred only to the tropical or sidereal year, the duration of which is 25,868 solar years. Of the complete age—that of the gods—they say nothing, as it was a matter to be discussed and revealed only in the <term>Mysteries</term>, during the initiation ceremonies. The “great age” of the <term>Chaldeans</term> <note>Originally spelled "Chaldæes".</note> was the same in figures as that of the Hindus.
**Grihastha** (*Sk.*). Literally, “a householder”, “one who lives in a house with his family”. A <term>Brahman</term> “family priest” in popular interpretation, and the <term>sacerdotal hierarchy</term> of the Hindus.
**Guardian Wall.** A suggestive name given to the host of translated <term>adepts</term> (<term>Narjols</term>) or the <term>Saints</term> collectively, who are supposed to watch over, help, and protect Humanity. This is the so-called “<term>Nirmanakâya</term>” doctrine in Northern mystic <term>Buddhism</term>. (See *Voice of the Silence*, Part III.).
**Guff** (*Heb.*). Body; physical form; also written <term>Gof</term>.
**Guhya** (*Sk.*). Concealed, secret.
**Guhya Vidyâ** (*Sk.*). The secret knowledge of mystic <term>Mantras</term>.
**Gullweig** (*Scand.*). The personification of the “golden” ore. It is said in the <term>Edda</term> that during the Golden Age, when lust for gold and wealth was yet unknown to man, “when the gods played with golden disks, and no passion disturbed the rapture of mere existence”, the whole earth was happy. But no sooner did “<term>Gullweig</term> (Gold ore), the bewitching enchantress, come—who, thrice cast into the fire, arises each time more beautiful than before, and fills the souls of gods and men with unappeasable longing”—than everything changed. It is then that the <term>Norns</term>, the Past, Present, and Future, entered into being; the blessed peace of childhood’s dreams passed away, and <term>Sin</term> came into existence with all its evil consequences. (*Asgard and the Gods.*)
**Guñas** (*Sk.*). Qualities, attributes (See “<term>Triguna</term>”); a thread, also a cord.
**Gunavat** (*Sk.*). That which is endowed with qualities.
**Gupta Vidyâ** (*Sk.*). The same as <term>Guhya Vidyâ</term>; <term>Esoteric</term> or Secret Science; knowledge.
**Guru** (*Sk.*). Spiritual Teacher; a master in metaphysical and ethical doctrines; used also for a teacher of any science.

**Guru Deva** (*Sk.*). Literally, "divine Master".

**Gyan-Ben-Giân** (*Pers.*). The King of the Peris, the Sylphs, in the ancient mythology of Iran.

**Gyges** (*Gg.*). "The ring of Gyges" has become a familiar metaphor in European literature. Gyges was a Lydian who, after murdering King Candaules, married his widow. Plato tells us that Gyges once descended into a chasm in the earth and discovered a bronze horse; within its open side was the skeleton of a man who had a bronze ring on his finger. This ring, when placed on his own finger, made him invisible.

It is easy to recognize in these gymnosophists the Hindu <term>Aranyaka</term> of old—the learned <term>yogis</term> and <term>ascetic</term> philosophers who retired to the jungle and forest to reach, through great austerities, superhuman knowledge and experience.

**Gyn** (*Tib.*). Knowledge acquired under the tuition of an adept teacher or <term>guru</term>.

## H.

**H.**—The eighth letter and aspirate of the English alphabet, and also the eighth in the Hebrew. As a Latin numeral, it signifies 200, and with the addition of a dash, 200,000; in the Hebrew alphabet, Chêth is equivalent to *h*, corresponds to eight, and is symbolized by a Fence and *Venus* according to Seyffarth, being in affinity and connected with *Hê*, and therefore with the opening or womb. It is pre-eminently a *Yonic* letter.

**Ha** (*Sk.*). A magic syllable used in sacred formulas; it represents the power of *Akâsa Sakti*. Its efficacy lies in the expirational accent and the sound produced.

**Habal de Garmin** (*Heb.*). According to the Kabbalah, this is the Resurrection Body: a *tzelem* image or *demooth* similitude to the deceased man; an inner fundamental spiritual type remaining after death. It is the "Spirit of the Bones" mentioned in Daniel, Isaiah, and the Psalms, and is referred to in the Vision of Ezekiel regarding the clothing of the dry bones with life: consult C. de Leiningen on the Kabbalah, T. P. S. Pamphlet, Vol. II., No. 18. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**Hachoser** (*Heb.*). Literally, "reflected Lights"; a name for the minor or inferior powers in the Kabbalah.

**Hades** (*Gr.*). or *Aïdes*. The "invisible", *i.e.*, the land of the shadows, one of whose regions was Tartarus, a place of complete darkness, like the region of profound dreamless sleep in the Egyptian Amenti. Judging by the allegorical description of the various punishments inflicted there, the place was purely Karmic. Neither Hades nor Amenti was the hell still preached by some retrograde priests and clergymen; whether represented by the Elysian Fields or by Tartarus, Hades was a place of retributive justice and no more. This could only be reached by crossing the river to the "other shore", *i.e.*, by crossing the river Death, and being once reborn, for weal or for woe. As it is well expressed in Egyptian Belief: "The story of Charon, the ferryman (of the Styx) is to be found not only in Homer, but in the poetry of many lands. The *River* must be crossed before gaining the Isles of the Blest. The Ritual of Egypt described a Charon and his boat long ages before Homer. He is Khu-en-ua, the hawk-headed steersman." (See "Amenti", "Hel", and "Happy Fields".)

**Hagadah** (*Heb.*). A name given to parts of the Talmud which are legendary. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**Hahnir** (*Scand.*), or *Hönir*. One of the mighty gods (Odin,

**<term>Haima</term> *Hebrew*.** The same as the <term>Sanskrit</term> *hiranya* (golden), as in “the golden Egg,” <term>Hiranyagarbha</term>.

**<term>Hair</term>.** Occult philosophy considers the hair (whether human or animal) as the natural receptacle and *retainer* of the vital essence, which often escapes with other emanations from the body. It is closely connected with many brain functions—for instance, memory. With the ancient <term>Israelites</term>, the cutting of the hair and beard was a sign of defilement, and “the Lord said unto <term>Moses</term> . . . . They shall not make baldness upon their head,” etc. (Leviticus 21:1–5). “Baldness,” whether natural or artificial, was a sign of calamity, punishment, or grief, as when <term>Isaiah</term> (3:24) lists, “instead of well-set hair, baldness,” among the evils that are ready to befall the chosen people. And again, “On all their heads is baldness and every beard is cut” (*Ibid*. 15:2). The <term>Nazarite</term> was ordered to let his hair and beard grow, and never to permit a razor to touch them. With the <term>Egyptians</term> and <term>Buddhists</term>, it was only the initiated priest or ascetic, to whom life is a burden, who shaved. The <term>Egyptian</term> priest was supposed to have become master of his body, and hence shaved his head for cleanliness; yet the <term>Hierophants</term> wore their hair long. The <term>Buddhist</term> still shaves his head to this day—as a sign of scorn for life and health. Yet <term>Buddha</term>, after shaving his hair when he first became a mendicant, let it grow again and is always represented with the topknot of a <term>Yogi</term>. The <term>Hindu</term> priests and <term>Brahmins</term>, and almost all the castes, shave the rest of the head but leave a long lock to grow from the center of the crown. The ascetics of <term>India</term> wear their hair long, and so do the warlike <term>Sikhs</term>, and almost all of the <term>Mongolian peoples</term>. At <term>Byzantium</term> and <term>Rhodes</term>, the shaving of the beard was prohibited by law, and in <term>Sparta</term>, the shaving of the beard was a mark of slavery and servitude. Among the <term>Scandinavians</term>, we are told, it was considered a disgrace, “a mark of infamy,” to cut off the hair. The whole population of the island of <term>Ceylon</term> (the <term>Buddhist</term> <term>Singhalese</term>) wear their hair long. So do the <term>Russian</term>, <term>Greek</term>, and <term>Armenian</term> clergy and monks. <term>Jesus</term> and the <term>Apostles</term> are always represented with their hair long, but *fashion* in <term>Christendom</term> proved stronger than <term>Christianity</term>, despite the old ecclesiastical rules (*Constit. Apost. lib. I. c. 3*) enjoining the clergy “to wear their hair and beards long.” (See <term>Riddle’s Ecclesiastical Antiquities</term>.) The <term>Templars</term> were commanded to wear their beards long. <term>Samson</term> wore his hair long, and the biblical allegory shows that health, strength, and life itself are connected with the length of the hair. **<term>Hallucination</term>**. A state produced sometimes by physiological disorders, sometimes by mediumship, and at other times by drunkenness. However, the cause that produces the visions must be sought deeper than physiology. All such visions, especially when produced through mediumship, are preceded by a relaxation of the nervous system, which invariably generates an abnormal magnetic condition that attracts waves of <term>Astral Light</term> to the sufferer. It is the latter that provides the various hallucinations. These, however, are not always what physicians would claim them to be—empty and unreal dreams. No one can see that which does not exist—that is, what is not impressed—in or on the astral waves. A <term>Seer</term> may, however, perceive objects and scenes (whether past, present, or future) which have no relation at all to himself, and also perceive several things entirely disconnected from each other at the same time, thus producing the most grotesque and absurd combinations. Both the drunkard and the <term>Seer</term>, the medium and the <term>Adept</term>, see their respective visions in the <term>Astral Light</term>. But while the drunkard, the madman, and the untrained medium, or one suffering from brain fever, see because they cannot help it and evoke the jumbled visions unconsciously, the <term>Adept</term> and the trained <term>Seer</term> have the choice and the control of such visions. They know where to fix their gaze, how to steady the scenes they want to observe, and how to see beyond the upper, outward layers of the <term>Astral Light</term>. For the former, such glimpses into the *waves* are hallucinations; for the latter, they become the faithful reproduction of what actually has been, is, or will be taking place. The random glimpses caught by the medium, and his flickering visions in the deceptive light, are transformed under the guiding will of the <term>Adept</term> and <term>Seer</term> into steady pictures—the truthful representations of that which he wills to come within the focus of his perception.

**Hara (Sanskrit)**. A title of the god <term>Siva</term>.

**Hare-Worship**. The hare was sacred in many lands and especially among the Egyptians and Jews. Although the latter consider it an unclean, *hoofed* animal, unfit to eat, it was held sacred by some tribes. The reason for this was that in certain species of hare the male suckled the young. It was thus considered to be androgynous or hermaphroditic, and so typified an attribute of the <term>Demiurge</term>, or creative <term>Logos</term>. The hare was a symbol of the moon, wherein the face of the prophet Moses is to be seen to this day, say the Jews. **Hari** (*Sk*.). A title of Vishnu, but used also for other gods.
**Harikesa** (*Sk*.). The name of one of the seven rays of the Sun.
**Harivansa** (*Sk*.). A portion of the *Mahābhārata*, a poem on the genealogy of Vishnu, or Hari.
**Harmachus** (*Gr*.). The Egyptian Sphinx, called *Har-em-chu* or “Horus (the Sun) on the Horizon,” a form of Ra the sun-god; esoterically, the risen god. An inscription on a tablet reads: “O blessed Ra-Harmachus! You career by him in triumph. O shine, Amoun-Ra-Harmachus self-generated.” The temple of the Sphinx was discovered by Mariette Bey close to the Sphinx, near the great Pyramid of Gizeh. All Egyptologists agree in declaring the Sphinx and her temple the “oldest religious monument of the world”—at least in Egypt. “The principal chamber,” writes the late Mr. Fergusson, “in the form of a cross, is supported by piers, simple prisms of Syenite granite without base or capital . . . no sculpture or inscriptions of any kind are found on the walls of this temple, no ornament or symbol nor any image in the sanctuary.” This proves the enormous antiquity of both the Sphinx and the temple. “The great bearded Sphinx of the Pyramids of Gizeh is the symbol of Harmachus, the same as each Egyptian Pharaoh who bore, in the inscriptions, the name of ‘living form of the Solar Sphinx upon the Earth,’” writes Brugsch Bey. And Renan recalls that “at one time the Egyptians were said to have temples without sculptured images” (Bonwick). Not only the Egyptians but every nation of the earth began with temples devoid of idols and even of symbols. It is only when the memory of the great abstract truths and of the primordial Wisdom taught to humanity by the dynasties of the divine kings died out that men had to resort to mementos and symbology. In the story of Horus in some tablets of Edfu, Rougé found an inscription showing that the god had once assumed “the shape of a human-headed lion to gain advantage over his enemy Typhon. Certainly Horus was so adored in Leontopolis. He is the real Sphinx. That accounts, too, for the lion figure being sometimes seen on each side of Isis . . . . It was her child. (Bonwick.) And yet the story of Harmachus, or Har-em-chu, is still left untold to the world, nor is it likely to be revealed to this generation. (See “Sphinx”).

**Harpocrates** (*Gr*.). The child Horus or *Ehoou* represented with a finger on his mouth, the solar disk upon his head and golden hair. He is the “god of Silence” and of Mystery. (See “Horus”). Harpocrates was also worshipped by both Greeks and Romans in Europe as a son of Isis.

**Harshana** (*Sk.*). A deity presiding over offerings to the dead, or *Srâddha*.

**Harvîri** (*Eg.*). Horus the elder: the ancient name of a solar god; the rising sun represented as a god reclining on a blooming lotus, the symbol of the Universe.

**Haryaswas** (*Sk.*). The *fifteen thousand* sons of Daksha who, instead of peopling the world as their father desired, all became yogis as advised by the mysterious sage Narada and remained celibates. "They dispersed through the regions and have not returned." According to the secret science, this means that they had all incarnated into mortals. The name is given to natural-born mystics and celibates, who are said to be incarnations of the "Haryaswas."

**Hatchet.** In Egyptian Hieroglyphics, a symbol of power and also of death. The hatchet is called the "Severer of the Knot"—meaning of marriage or any other tie.

**Hatha Yoga** (*Sk.*). The lower form of Yoga practice; one which uses physical means for the purpose of spiritual self-development. It is the opposite of *Raja Yoga*.

**Hathor** (*Eg.*). The lower or infernal aspect of Isis, corresponding to the Hecate of Greek mythology.

**Hawk.** The Hieroglyphic symbol and type of the *Soul*. Its meaning varies with the posture of the bird. For example, when lying as if dead, it represents the transition or *larval* state—the passage from the state of one life to another. When its wings are open, it means that the deceased is resurrected in Amenti and is once again in conscious possession of his soul. The chrysalis has become a butterfly.

**Hayo Bischat** (*Heb.*). "The Beast" in the *Zohar*: the Devil and Tempter. Esoterically, our lower animal passions.

**Hay-yoth ha Qadosh** (*Hebrew*). The holy living creatures of Ezekiel’s vision of the *Merkabah*, or vehicle, or chariot. These are the four symbolic beasts, the cherubim of Ezekiel, which in the Zodiac are Taurus, Leo, Scorpio (or the Eagle), and Aquarius, the man.

This is said of the Deity of which the Head (*i.e.*, Wisdom perceived by all) is alone manifested. Of that Principle which is still higher, nothing is even predicated, except that its universal presence and actuality are a philosophical necessity.

This Heavenly Adam is the *natura naturans* (creative nature), the abstract world, while the Adam of Earth (Humanity) is the *natura naturata* (created nature) or the material universe. The former is the presence of Deity in its universal essence; the latter is the manifestation of the intelligence of that essence. **Hebdomad** Δ *(Gr.)*. The Septenary.

**Hebron or Kirjath-Arba.** The city of the Four Kebeiri, for *Kirjath-Arba* signifies "the City of the Four." It is in that city, according to the legend, that an *Isarim* or an initiate found the famous Smaragdine tablet on the dead body of Hermes.

**Hel or Hela** *(Scand.)*. The Goddess-Queen of the Land of the Dead; the inscrutable and dreadful Being who reigns over the depths of Helheim and Nifelheim. In the earlier mythology, Hel was the earth-goddess, the good and beneficent mother, the nourisher of the weary and the hungry. But in the later Skalds she became the female Pluto, the dark Queen of the Kingdom of Shades, she who brought death into this world and sorrow afterward.

**Helheim** *(Scand.)*. The Kingdom of the Dead in Norse mythology. In the Edda, Helheim surrounds the Northern Mistworld, called Nifelheim.

**Heliolatry** *(Gr.)*. Sun-Worship.

**Hell.** A term used by the Anglo-Saxons, evidently derived from the name of the goddess *Hela (q.v.)* and by the Slavonians from the Greek Hades: hell being in Russian and other Slavonic tongues—*âd*. The only difference between the Scandinavian cold hell and the hot hell of the Christians is found in their respective temperatures. But even the idea of those overheated regions is not original to Europeans, as many peoples have entertained the conception of an underworld climate; as well we might if we localize our Hell in the center of the earth. All exoteric religions—the creeds of the Brahmans, Buddhists, Zoroastrians, Mohammedans, Jews, and the rest—make their hells hot and dark, though many are more attractive than frightening. The idea of a hot hell is an afterthought, the distortion of an astronomical allegory. With the Egyptians, Hell became a place of punishment by fire no earlier than the seventeenth or eighteenth dynasty, when Typhon was transformed from a god into a devil. But at whatever time this dread superstition was implanted in the minds of the poor ignorant masses, the scheme of a burning hell and souls tormented within it is purely Egyptian. *Ra* (the Sun) became the Lord of the Furnace in Karr, the hell of the Pharaohs, and the sinner was threatened with misery "in the heat of infernal fires." "A lion was there," says Dr. Birch, "and was called the roaring monster." Another describes the place as "the bottomless pit and lake of fire, into which the victims are thrown" (compare *Revelation*). The Hebrew word *gaï-hinnom* (Gehenna) never really had the significance given to it in Christian orthodoxy.

**Hemadri** *(Sk.)*. The golden Mountain; Meru.
