# GLOSSARY

**Hemera** (Gr.). "The light of the inferior or terrestrial regions" as Ether is the light of the superior heavenly spheres. Both are born of *Erebos* (darkness) and *Nux* (night).
**Heptakis** (Gr.). "The Seven-rayed One" of the Chaldean star-worshippers: the same as Iao.
**Herakles** (Gr.). The same as Hercules.
**Heranasikha** (Sing.). From *Herana* "novice" and *Sikha* "rule" or precept: a manual of Precepts. A work written in *Elu* or the ancient Singhalese, for the use of young priests.
**Hermanubis** (Gr.). Or Hermes Anubis "the revealer of the mysteries of the lower world"—not of Hell or Hades as commonly interpreted, but of our Earth (the *lowest world of the Septenary chain of worlds*)—and also of the sexual mysteries. Creuzer must have guessed at the truth of the right interpretation, as he calls Anubis-Thoth-Hermes "a *symbol of science and of the intellectual world*." He was always represented with a cross in his hand, one of the earliest symbols of the mystery of generation, or procreation on this earth. In the Chaldean Kabbala (*Book of Numbers*) the Tat symbol, or ♁, is referred to as Adam and Eve, the latter being the transverse or horizontal bar drawn out of the side (or rib) of Hadam, the perpendicular bar. The fact is that, esoterically, Adam and Eve while representing the early third Root Race—those who, being still mindless, imitated the animals and degraded themselves with the latter—stand also as the dual symbol of the sexes. Hence Anubis, the Egyptian god of generation, is represented with the head of an animal, a dog or a jackal, and is also said to be the "Lord of the underworld" or "Hades" into which he introduces the souls of the dead (the reincarnating entities), for *Hades* is in one sense the womb, as some of the writings of the Church Fathers fully show.
**Hermaphrodite** (Gr.). Dual-sexed; a male and female Being, whether human or animal.
**Hermas** (Gr.). An ancient Greek writer of whose works only a few fragments are now extant.
**Hermes-fire**. The same as "Elmes-fire." (See *Isis Unveiled* Vol. I., p. 125).
**Hermes Sarameyas** (Greco-Sanskrit). The God Hermes, or Mercury, "he who watches over the flock of stars" in Greek mythology.
**Hermes Trismegistus** (Gr.). The "thrice great Hermes," the Egyptian. The mythical personage after whom the Hermetic philosophy was named. In Egypt, he is the God Thoth or Thot. A generic name of many ancient Greek writers on philosophy and Alchemy. Hermes Trismegistus is the name of Hermes or Thoth in his human aspect; as a god, he is far more than this. As *Hermes-Thoth-Aah*, he is Thoth, the moon, that is, his symbol is the bright side of the moon, supposed to contain the essence of creative Wisdom, "the elixir of Hermes." As such he is

<term>**Hermetic.**</term> Any doctrine or writing connected with the esoteric teachings of Hermes, who—whether as the Egyptian Thoth or the Greek Hermes—was the God of Wisdom to the ancients and, according to Plato, "discovered numbers, geometry, astronomy, and letters." Although mostly considered spurious, the Hermetic writings were nevertheless highly prized by Saint Augustine, Lactantius, Cyril, and others. In the words of Mr. J. Bonwick: "They are more or less touched up by the Platonic philosophers among the early Christians (such as Origen and Clement of Alexandria) who sought to support their Christian arguments by appealing to these ancient and revered writings, though they could not resist the temptation of making them say a little too much." Although represented by some clever and biased writers as teaching pure monotheism, the Hermetic or Trismegistic books are, nevertheless, purely pantheistic. The Deity referred to in them is defined by Paul as that in which "we live, and move, and have our being"—despite the "in Him" used by translators.

<term>**Hierogrammatists.**</term> The title given to those Egyptian priests who were entrusted with the writing and reading of the sacred and secret records; literally, the "scribes of the secret records." They were the instructors of the neophytes preparing for initiation.

<term>**Hierophant.**</term> From the Greek *Hierophantes*; literally, "one who explains sacred things." The revealer of sacred learning and the Chief of the Initiates. This was a title belonging to the highest Adepts in the temples of antiquity, who were the teachers and expounders of the Mysteries and the initiators into the final great Mysteries. The Hierophant represented the Demiurge and explained to the candidates for initiation the various phenomena of creation that were produced for their instruction. # GLOSSARY

**Hoa (Hebr.)**. That from which Ab, the "Father," proceeds; therefore, the Concealed *Logos*.
**Hoang Ty (Chin.)**. “The Great Spirit.” His Sons are said to have acquired new wisdom and imparted what they knew before to mortals by falling—like the rebellious angels—into the “Valley of Pain,” which is allegorically our Earth. In other words, they are identical to the “Fallen Angels” of exoteric religions and to the reincarnating Egos, esoterically.

**Holy of Holies**. Assyriologists, Egyptologists, and Orientalists in general show that such a place existed in every temple of antiquity. The great temple of Bel-Merodach, whose sides faced the four cardinal points, had at its extreme end a “Holy of Holies” hidden from the profane by a veil: here, “at the beginning of the year ‘the divine king of heaven and earth, the lord of the heavens, seats himself.’” According to Herodotus, here was the golden image of the god with a golden table in front, like the Hebrew table for the showbread, and upon this, food appears to have been placed. In some temples, there was also “a little coffer or ark with two engraved stone tablets on it.” (Myer’s *Qabbalah*.) In short, it is now fairly well proven that the “chosen people” had nothing original of their own, but that every detail of their ritualism and religion was borrowed from older nations. The *Hibbert Lectures* by Prof. Sayce and others show this abundantly. The story of the birth of Moses is that of Sargon the Babylonian, who preceded Moses by a couple of thousand years; and no wonder, as Dr. Sayce tells us that the name of Moses, *Mosheh*, has a connection with the name of the Babylonian sun-god as the “hero” or “leader.” (*Hib. Lect.*, p. 46 *et seq.*) Mr. J. Myer says, “The orders of the priests were divided into high priests; those attached or bound to certain deities, like the Hebrew Levites; anointers or cleaners; the *Kali*, ‘illustrious’ or ‘elders’; the soothsayers, and the *Makhkhu* or ‘great one,’ in which Prof. Delitzsch sees the *Rab-mag* of the Old Testament. . . . The Akkadians and Chaldeans kept a Sabbath day of rest every seven days; they also had thanksgiving days, and days for humiliation and prayer. There were sacrifices of vegetables and animals, of meats and wine. . . . The number seven was especially sacred. . . . The great temple of Babylon existed long before 2,250 B.C. Its ‘Holy of Holies’ was within the shrine of Nebo, the prophet god of wisdom.” It is from the Akkadians that the god Marduk passed to the Assyrians, and he had previously been Merodach, “the merciful,” of the Babylonians, the only son and interpreter of the will of Ea or *Hea*, the great Deity of Wisdom. The Assyriologists have, in short, unveiled the whole scheme of the “chosen people.”

**Holy Water.** This is one of the oldest rites practiced in Egypt, and from there in Pagan Rome. It accompanied the rite of bread and wine. “Holy water was sprinkled by the Egyptian priest both upon his gods’ images and the faithful. It was both poured and sprinkled. A brush has been found, which was supposedly used for that purpose, just as it is used today.” (*Bonwick’s Egyptian Belief*). As for the bread, “the cakes of Isis . . . were placed upon the altar.” Gliddon writes that they were identical in shape to the consecrated cake of the Roman and Eastern Churches. Melville assures us that “the Egyptians marked this holy bread with St. Andrew’s cross.” The *Presence* bread was broken before being distributed by the priests to the people, and was supposed to become the flesh and blood of the Deity. The miracle was performed by the hand of the officiating priest, who blessed the food. . . . Rougé tells us “the bread offerings bear the imprint of the *fingers*, the mark of consecration.” (*Ibid*, page 418.) (See also “Bread and Wine”.)

**Homogeneity.** From the Greek words *homos* (“the same”) and *genos* (“kind”). That which is of the same nature throughout, undifferentiated, and non-compound, as gold is *supposed to be*.

**Honir** (*Scand*.). A creative god who provided the first man with intellect and understanding after man had been created by him jointly with Odin and Lodur from an ash tree.

**Honover** (*Zned*.). The Persian *Logos*, the manifested Word.

**Hor Ammon** (*Eg*.). “The *Self-engendered*,” a term in theogony which corresponds to the Sanskrit *Anupadaka*, or parentless. Hor-Ammon is a combination of the ram-headed god of Thebes and Horus.

**Horchia** (*Chald*.). According to Berosus, the same as Vesta, the goddess of the Hearth.

**Horus** (*Eg*.). The last in the line of divine Sovereigns in Egypt, said to be the son of Osiris and Isis. He is the great god “loved by Heaven,” the “beloved of the Sun, the offspring of the gods, the subjugator of the world.” At the time of the Winter Solstice (our Christmas), his image, in the form of a small newborn infant, was brought out from the sanctuary for the adoration of the worshiping crowds. As he is the symbol of the vault of heaven, he is said to have come from the *Maem Misi*, the sacred birthplace (the womb of the World), and is, therefore, the “mystic Child of the Ark” or the *argha*, the symbol of the matrix. Cosmically, he is the *Winter Sun*. A tablet describes him as the “substance of his father,” Osiris, of whom he is an incarnation and with whom he is also identical. Horus is a chaste deity, and “like Apollo, has no love affairs. His role in the lower world is associated with the Judgment. He introduces souls to his father, the Judge” (Bonwick). An ancient hymn says of him, “By him the world is judged in all that it contains. Heaven and earth are under his immediate presence. He rules all human beings. <term>Hypnotism</term> (*Gr.*). A name given by Dr. Braid to various processes by which one person of strong willpower plunges another of weaker mind into a kind of trance; once in such a state, the latter will do anything *suggested* to him by the hypnotizer. <term>Hypocephalus</term> (*Gr.*). A kind of pillow for the head of a mummy. They are of various kinds, *e.g.*, of stone, wood, etc., and very often consist of circular disks of linen covered with cement and inscribed with magic figures and letters. They are called "rest for the dead" in the *Ritual*, and every mummy coffin has one.

<header>GLOSSARY</header>

### I.

I.—The ninth letter in the English and the tenth in the Hebrew alphabet. As a numeral, it signifies *one* in both languages, and also *ten* in Hebrew (see J), in which it corresponds to the Divine name *Jah*, the male side or aspect of the hermaphrodite being—or the male-female Adam—of which *hovah* (Jah-hovah) is the female aspect. It is symbolized by a hand with a bent forefinger to show its phallic significance.

Iacchos (Gr.). A synonym of Bacchus. Mythology mentions three persons so named: they were Greek ideals adopted later by the Romans. The word Iacchos is said to be of Phoenician origin and to mean “an infant at the breast.” Many ancient monuments represent Ceres or Demeter with Bacchus in her arms. One Iacchos was called Theban and Conqueror, son of Jupiter and Semele; his mother died before his birth and he was preserved for some time in the thigh of his father; he was killed by the Titans. Another was the son of Jupiter, appearing as a Dragon, and Persephone; this one was named Zagræus. A third was Iacchos of Eleusis, son of Ceres: he is of importance because he appeared on the sixth day of the Eleusinian Mysteries. Some see an analogy between Bacchus and Noah, both cultivators of the Vine and patrons of alcoholic excess. <note>w.w.w. - Likely William Wynn Westcott</note>

Iachus (Gr.). An Egyptian physician whose memory, according to Aelian, was venerated for many centuries on account of his wonderful occult knowledge. Iachus is credited with having stopped epidemics simply by certain *fumigations* and cured diseases by making his patients inhale herbs.

Iaho. Although this name is more fully treated under the words “Yaho” and “Iao,” a few words of explanation will not be out of place. Diodorus mentions that the God of Moses was Iao; but as the latter name denotes a “mystery god,” it cannot therefore be confused with Iaho or Yaho (*q.v.*). The Samaritans pronounced it Iabe or Yahva, and the Jews Yaho, and then Jehovah, by changing the Masoretic vowels—an adjustable system by which any change may be applied. But “Jehovah” is a later invention and invocation, as originally the name was Jah, or Iacchos (Bacchus). Aristotle shows the ancient Arabs representing Iach (Iacchos) by a horse, i.e., the horse of the Sun (Dionysus), which followed the chariot on which Ahura Mazda, the god of the Heavens, rode daily.

Iamblichus (Gr.). A great Theurgist, mystic, and writer of the third and fourth centuries; a Neo-Platonist and philosopher born at Chalcis in Coele-Syria. Correct biographies of him have never existed

<meta>This page continues the entry for Iamblichus from the previous page, detailing his contributions to Neo-Platonism, his relationship with Porphyry, and his philosophical teachings regarding theurgy and the nature of the soul.</meta>

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

because of the hatred of the Christians; but what has been gathered of his life in isolated fragments from works by impartial pagan and independent writers shows how excellent and holy his moral character was, and how great his learning was. He may be called the founder of theurgic magic among the Neo-Platonists and the reviver of the practical mysteries outside of a temple or shrine. His school was at first distinct from that of Plotinus and Porphyry, who were strongly against ceremonial magic and practical theurgy as dangerous. However, he later convinced Porphyry of its advisability on some occasions, and both master and pupil firmly believed in theurgy and magic. Of these, the former is principally the highest and most efficient mode of communication with one’s Higher Ego through the medium of one’s astral body. Theurgic is *benevolent magic*, and it becomes goëtic, or dark and evil, only when it is used for necromancy or selfish purposes; but such dark magic has never been practiced by any theurgist or philosopher whose name has come down to us unspotted by any evil deed. Porphyry (who became the teacher of Iamblichus in Neo-Platonic philosophy) was so convinced of this that although he himself never practiced theurgy, he still gave instructions for the acquisition of this sacred science.

Thus, he says in one of his writings, “Whoever is acquainted with the nature of *divinely luminous appearances* (φάσματα) also knows for what reason it is necessary to abstain from all birds (and animal food), especially for someone who hastens to be liberated from earthly concerns and to be established with the celestial gods.” (See *Select Works by T. Taylor*, p. 159.) Moreover, the same Porphyry mentions in his *Life of Plotinus* an Egyptian priest who, “at the request of a certain friend of Plotinus, exhibited to him, in the temple of Isis at Rome, the *familiar spirit* <note>The original uses "dæmon," referring to a tutelary spirit or divine guide rather than a malevolent entity.</note> of that philosopher.” In other words, he performed the theurgic invocation (see “Theurgist”) by which Egyptian Hierophants or Indian Mahatmas of old could clothe their own or any other person’s *astral double* with the appearance of its Higher Ego, or what Bulwer-Lytton terms the “Luminous Self,” the *Augoeides*, and converse with it.

This is what Iamblichus and many others, including the medieval Rosicrucians, meant by *union with Deity*. Iamblichus wrote many books, but only a few of his works are still in existence, such as his “*Egyptian Mysteries*” and a treatise “*On Spirits*,” in which he speaks very severely against any interaction with them. He was a biographer of Pythagoras and deeply versed in the latter's system, and he was also learned in the Chaldean Mysteries. He taught that the One, or universal MONAD, was the principle of all unity as well as diversity, or of homogeneity and heterogeneity; that the Duad, or two (“Principles”), was the intellect, or what we call Buddhi-Manas; and that the number three was the Soul (the lower Manas), and so on. There is much of theosophy in his teachings, and his works on the various kinds of spirits (Elementals) are a well of esoteric knowledge for the student. His austerities, purity of life, and earnestness were great. Iamblichus is credited with

**Iao** (*Gr.*). See Iaho. The highest god of the Phoenicians—“the light conceivable only by the intellect,” the physical and spiritual principle of all things, “the male essence of wisdom.” It is the ideal sunlight.

**Iao Hebdomai** (*Gr.*). The collective “Seven Heavens” (also angels) according to Irenaeus. The mystery-god of the Gnostics. The same as the Seven *Manasa-putras* (*q.v.*) of the Occultists. (See also “Yah” and “Yaho”).

**Ibis Worship.** The Ibis, in Egyptian *Hab*, was sacred to Thoth at Hermopolis. It was called the messenger of Osiris, for it is the symbol of wisdom, discrimination, and purity, as it loathes water if it is at all impure. Its usefulness in devouring the eggs of crocodiles and serpents was great, and its credentials for divine honors as a symbol were: (*a*) its black wings, which related it to primeval darkness—chaos; and (*b*) their triangular shape—the triangle being the first geometrical figure and a symbol of the trinitarian mystery. To this day, the Ibis is a sacred bird among some tribes of Copts who live along the Nile.

**Ibn Gebirol.** Solomon Ben Yehudah: a great philosopher and scholar, a Jew by birth, who lived in the eleventh century in Spain. The same as Avicenna (*q.v.*).

**Ichchha** (*Sk.*). Will, or willpower.

**Ichchha Sakti** (*Sk.*). Willpower; the force of desire; one of the occult forces of nature. That power of the will which, when exercised in occult practices, generates the nerve currents necessary to set certain muscles in motion and to paralyze others.

**Ichthus** (*Gr.*). A fish: the symbol of the fish has been frequently applied to Jesus, the Christ of the New Testament, partly because the five letters forming the word are the initials of the Greek phrase, *Iesous Christos Theou Uios Soter*, Jesus Christ the Savior, Son of God. Hence his followers in the early Christian centuries were often called fishes, and drawings of fish are found in the catacombs. Compare also the narrative that some of his early disciples were fishermen, and the assertion of Jesus—“I will make you fishers of men.” Note also that the *Vesica Piscis*, a conventional shape for fish in general, is frequently found enclosing a picture of Christ, the holy virgin, or a saint; it is a long oval with pointed ends, the space formed by the intersection of two equal circles when it is less than half the area of one. Compare this with the Christian female recluse, a Nun—this word is the Chaldean name for fish, and fish is connected with the worship of Venus, a goddess; furthermore, Roman Catholics still eat fish on the *Dies Veneris* or Friday. <note>w.w.</note>

**Ida** (*Scand.*). The plains of Ida, on which the gods assemble to hold council in the *Edda*. The field of peace and rest.

<meta>This page continues the alphabetical glossary of philosophical and religious terms, transitioning from the entry on "Ichthus" at the end of the previous page to various terms beginning with "Id-," "Ie-," and "If-," focusing heavily on Norse mythology, Gnosticism, and the Zohar.</meta>

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

**Ideos**, in Paracelsus the same as Chaos, or *Mysterium Magnum* as that philosopher calls it.

**Idises** (*Scand.*). The same as Dises, the Fairies and Valkyries, the divine women in the Norse legends; they were revered by the Teutons before the time of Tacitus, as the latter shows.

**Idæic Finger**. An iron finger strongly magnetized and used in the temples for healing purposes. It produced wonders in that direction, and therefore was said to possess *magical powers*.

**Idol**. A statue or a picture of a pagan god; or a statue or picture of a Roman Catholic Saint, or a fetish of uncivilized tribes.

**Idospati** (*Sk.*). The same as Narayana or Vishnu; resembling Poseidon in some respects.

**Idra Rabba** (*Heb.*). “The Greater Holy Assembly,” a division of the Zohar.

**Idra Suta** (*Heb.*). “The Lesser Holy Assembly,” another division of the Zohar.

**Iduna** (*Scand.*). The goddess of immortal youth. The daughter of Iwaldi, the Dwarf. She is said in the *Edda* to have hidden “life” in the depths of the ocean, and when the right time came, to have restored it to Earth once more. She was the wife of Bragi, the god of poetry, a most charming myth. Like Heimdal, who was “born of nine mothers,” Bragi at his birth rises upon the crest of the wave from the bottom of the sea (see “Bragi”). He married Iduna, the immortal goddess, who accompanies him to Asgard where every morning she feeds the gods with the apples of eternal youth and health. (See *Asgard and the Gods*.)

**Idwatsara** (*Sk.*). One of the five periods that form the Yuga. This cycle is preeminently the Vedic cycle, which is taken as the basis of calculation for larger cycles.

**Ieu**. The “first man”; a Gnostic term used in *Pistis-Sophia*.

**Iezedians** or *Iezidi* (*Pers.*). This sect came to Syria from Basrah. They use baptism and believe in the archangels, but reverence Satan at the same time. Their prophet *Iezad*, who preceded *Mahomet* by many centuries, taught that a messenger from heaven would bring them a book written from eternity.

**Ifing** (*Scand.*). The broad river that divides *Asgard*, the home of the gods, from that of the Jotuns, the great and strong magicians. Below *Asgard* was *Midgard*, where in the sunny ether was built the home of the *Light Elves*. In their layout and order of location, all these homes correspond to the *Devas* and other *Lokas* of the *Hindus*, inhabited by the various classes of *gods* and *Asuras*.

**Igaga** (*Chald.*). Celestial angels, the same as Archangels.

**I.H.S.** This triad of initials stands for the *in hoc signo* of the alleged vision of Constantine, of which no one ever knew except Eusebius, its author. I.H.S. is interpreted as *Jesus Hominum Salvator* (Jesus, Savior of Men) and *In hoc signo* (In this sign).

It is, however, well known that the Greek IHΣ was one of the most ancient names of Bacchus. **Ila** (*Sk.*). Daughter of Vaivaswata Manu; wife of Buddha, the son of Soma; one month a woman and the other a man by the degree <note>Likely "decree"</note> of Saraswati; an allusion to the androgynous second race. Ila is also Vâch in another aspect.

**Ilavriti** (*Sk.*). A region in the center of which is placed Mount Meru, the habitat of the gods.

He is the creator of our physical globe (the earth) according to the Gnostic teaching in the *Codex Nazaræus* (the Gospel of the Nazarenes and the Ebionites). The latter identifies him with Jehovah, the God of the Jews. Ildaboath is "the Son of Darkness" in a negative sense and the father of the six terrestrial "Stellar," dark spirits, the antithesis of the bright Stellar spirits. Their respective abodes are the seven spheres, the upper of which begins in the "middle space," the region of their mother Sophia Achamôth, and the lower ending on this earth—the seventh region (see *Isis Unveiled*, Vol. II., page 183.) Ilda-Baoth is the genius of Saturn, the planet; or rather the evil spirit of its ruler.

**Iliados.** In Paracelsus, the same as "Ideos" (*q.v.*). Primordial matter in the subjective state.

**Illa-ah**, *Adam* (*Heb.*). Adam Illa-ah is the celestial, superior Adam in the *Zohar*.

**Illinus.** One of the gods in the Chaldean Theogony of Damascius.

**Ilmatar** (*Finn.*). The Virgin who falls from heaven into the sea before creation. She is the "daughter of the air" and the mother of seven sons (the seven forces in nature). (See *Kalevala*, the epic poem of Finland.)

**Illusion.** In Occultism everything finite (like the universe and all in it) is called illusion or *maya*.

**Illuminati** (*Lat.*). The "Enlightened," the initiated adepts.

**<term>Illus</term>** (*Gr.*). Primordial mud or slime; also called *Hyle*.

**<term>Image</term>.** Occultism permits no other image than that of the living image of divine man (the symbol of Humanity) on earth. The *Kabbala* teaches that this living *Image*, the copy of the sublime and holy upper *Image* (the <term>Elohim</term>), has now changed into *another* likeness, owing to the development of humanity's sinful nature. It is only the *upper divine Image* (the *<term>Ego</term>*) which remains the same; the lower (personality) has changed, and man, now fearing the wild beasts, has grown to bear on his face the likeness of many of them. (*Zohar* I. fol. 71a.) In the early period of Egypt there were no images; but later, as Lenormand says, "In the sanctuaries of Egypt they divided the properties of nature and consequently of Divinity (the <term>Elohim</term>, or the <term>Egos</term>), into seven abstract qualities, each characterized by an emblem; these are matter, cohesion, fluxion, coagulation, accumulation, station and division." These were all attributes symbolized in various images.

**<term>Imagination</term>.** In Occultism this is not to be confused with fancy, as it is one of the plastic powers of the higher Soul and is the memory of preceding incarnations. However much it may be disfigured by the lower <term>Manas</term>, it always rests on a foundation of truth.

**<term>Imhot-pou</term>** or ***Imhotep*** (*Eg.*). The god of learning (the Greek Imouthes). He was the son of Ptah, and in one aspect Hermes, as he is represented as imparting wisdom with a book before him. He is a solar god; *literally*, "the god of the handsome face."

**<term>Immah</term>** (*Heb.*). Mother, as opposed to *Abba*, father.

**<term>Immah Illa-ah</term>** (*Heb.*). The upper mother; a name given to Shekinah.

**<term>In</term>** (*Chin.*). The female principle of matter, impregnated by *Yo*, the male ethereal principle, and thereafter precipitated down into the universe.

**<term>Incarnations</term> (*Divine*) or <term>Avatars</term>.** The Immaculate Conception is as pre-eminently Egyptian as it is Indian. As the author of *Egyptian Belief* states: "It is not the vulgar, coarse, and sensual story found in Greek mythology, but refined, moral, and spiritual"; and again, the idea of incarnation was found revealed on the wall of a Theban temple by Samuel Sharpe, who analyzes it thus: "First, the god Thoth... as the messenger of the gods, like the Mercury of the Greeks (or the Gabriel of the first Gospel), tells the maiden queen Mautmes that she is to give birth to a son, who is to be king Amunotaph III. Second, the god Kneph (the Spirit) and the goddess Hathor (Nature) both take hold of the queen by the hands and put into her mouth the symbol for life—a *cross*—which is to be the life of the coming child," etc., etc. Truly, divine incarnation, or the *avatar* doctrine, constituted the grandest mystery of every ancient religious system!

**<term>Incubus</term>** (*Lat.*). Something more real and dangerous than the ordinary meaning given to the word, namely, that of “nightmare.” An *Incubus* is the male Elemental, and *Succuba* the female, and these are undeniably the spooks of medieval demonology, called forth from the invisible regions by human passion and lust. They are now called “Spirit brides” and “Spirit husbands” among some benighted Spiritists and spiritual mediums. But these poetic names do not prevent them in the least from being what they are—Ghouls, Vampires, and soulless Elementals; formless centers of Life, devoid of sense; in short, subjective *protoplasms* when left alone, but called into a definite being and form by the creative and diseased imagination of certain mortals. They were known in every climate as in every age, and the Hindus can tell more than one terrible tale of the dramas enacted in the lives of young students and mystics by the Pisachas, their name in India.

**<term>Individuality</term>**. One of the names given in Theosophy and Occultism to the Human Higher Ego. We make a distinction between the immortal and divine Ego, and the mortal human Ego which perishes. The latter, or “personality” (personal Ego), survives the dead body only for a time in the Kama Loka; the Individuality prevails forever.

**<term>Indra</term>** (*Sk.*). The god of the Firmament, the King of the sidereal gods. A Vedic Deity.

These are the ten external agents; the five senses which are used for perception are called *Jnana-indriya*, and the five used for action—*Karma-indriya* <note>The OCR text lists "Karna-indriya," likely a typo for "Karma-indriya," as these are the organs of action.</note>. *Pancha-indriya* means literally, and in its occult sense, “the five roots producing life” (eternal). With the Buddhists, these are the five positive agents producing five supernal qualities.

**<term>Induvansa</term>** (*Sk.*). Also *Somavansa* or the lunar race (dynasty), from Indu, the Moon. (See “Suryavansa”).

**<term>Indwellers</term>**. A name, or the substitute for the correct Sanskrit esoteric name, given to our “inner enemies,” which are seven in the esoteric philosophy. The early Christian Church called them the “Seven Capital Sins”; the Nazarene Gnostics named them the “seven badly disposed Stellars,” and so on. Hindu exoteric teachings speak only of the “six enemies” and under the term *Arishadwarga* enumerate them as follows: (1) Personal desire, lust, or any passion (*Kama*); (2) Hatred or malice (*Krodha*); (3) Avarice or cupidity (*Lobha*); (4) Ignorance (*Moha*); (5) Pride or arrogance (*Mada*); (6) Jealousy or envy (*Matscharya*); forgetting the seventh, which is the “unpardonable sin” and the worst of all in Occultism. (See *Theosophist*, May 1890, p. 431.)

**Ineffable Name.** Among the Jews, this is the substitute for the "mystery name" of their tribal deity *Eh-yeh*, "I am," or Jehovah. Because the third commandment prohibits using the latter name "in vain," the Hebrews substituted it with *Adonai*, or "the Lord." However, Protestant Christians—who translate both Jehovah and Elohim (the latter being a substitute in itself, as well as an *inferior* deity name) without distinction as "Lord" and "God"—have in this instance become more Catholic than the Pope and include both names in the prohibition.

At the present moment, however, neither Jews nor Christians seem to remember, or even suspect, the occult reason why the designation of Jehovah or YHVH became reprehensible; most Western Kabbalists also seem to be unaware of this fact. The truth is that the name they present as "ineffable" is not so in the least. It is the "unpronounceable," or rather the name *not to be pronounced*, if anything, and this is for symbolic reasons. To begin with, the "Ineffable Name" of the true Occultist is no name at all, and it is certainly not that of Jehovah. The latter implies, even in its Kabbalistic, esoteric meaning, an androgynous nature, YHVH, or one of both male and female nature. It is simply Adam and Eve, or man and woman blended into one, and as it is now written and pronounced, it is *itself a substitute*. But the Rabbis do not care to remember the Zoharic admission that YHVH means "not as I am written am I read" (*Zohar, folio III, 230a*). One must know how to divide the Tetragrammaton *to infinity* before arriving at the sound of the truly unpronounceable name of the Jewish mystery-god. It is hardly necessary to repeat that Oriental Occultists have their own "Ineffable name."

**Initiate.** From the Latin *Initiatus*. The designation for anyone who was received into and had revealed to him the mysteries and secrets of either Masonry or Occultism. In ancient times, those who had been initiated into the arcane knowledge taught by the Hierophants of the Mysteries; and in our modern days, those who have been initiated by the adepts of mystic lore into the mysterious knowledge which, despite the passage of ages, still has a few real followers on earth.

**Initiation.** From the same root as the Latin *initia*, which means the basic or first principles of any science. The practice of initiation or admission into the sacred Mysteries, taught by the Hierophants and learned priests of the Temples, is one of the most ancient customs. This was practiced in every ancient national religion. In Europe, it was abolished with the fall of the last pagan temple. At present, there exists only one kind of initiation known to the public, namely that into the Masonic rites. Masonry, however, has no more secrets to reveal or conceal. In the flourishing days of old, the Mysteries, according to the greatest Greek and Roman philosophers, were the most sacred of all ceremonies as well as the most beneficial, and they greatly promoted virtue. The Mysteries represented the passage from mortal life into finite death, and the experiences of the disembodied Spirit and Soul in the world of subjec...

**Inner Man.** An occult term used to designate the true and immortal Entity within us, not the outward and mortal form of clay that we call our body. The term applies, strictly speaking, only to the Higher Ego; the "astral man" is the name for the Double and Kâma Rupa <note>See those entries.</note> or the surviving *eidolon*.

**Innocents.** A nickname given to the Initiates and Kabbalists before the Christian era. The "Innocents" of Bethlehem and of Lud (or Lydda) who were put to death by Alexander Janneus, numbering several thousand (around 100 B.C.), gave rise to the legend of the 40,000 innocent babies murdered by Herod while searching for the infant Jesus. The former is a little-known historical fact; the latter is a fable, as is sufficiently shown by Renan in his *Vie de Jésus*.

**Intercosmic gods.** The Planetary Spirits, Dhyan-Chohans, Devas of various degrees of spirituality, and "Archangels" in general.

It will familiarize the student with the ethics of the ancient Iranians better than many larger volumes.

**Irdhi** (*Sanskrit*). The synthesis of the ten "supernatural" occult powers in Buddhism and Brahmanism.

**Isarim** (*Hebrew*). The Essene Initiates.

**Ishim** (*Chaldean*). The B’ne-Aleim, the "beautiful sons of God," the originals and prototypes of the later "Fallen Angels."

**Ishmonia** (*Arabic*). The city near which the so-called "petrified city" is buried in the desert. Legend speaks of immense subterranean halls, chambers, passages, and libraries hidden within them. Arabs dread its vicinity after sunset.

**Ishtar** (*Chaldean*). The Babylonian Venus, called "the eldest of heaven and earth" and daughter of Anu, the god of heaven. She is the goddess of love and beauty. The planet Venus is identified with Ishtar as the evening star, and as the morning star with Anunit, the goddess of the Akkadians. There exists a most remarkable story of her descent into Hades on the sixth and seventh Assyrian tiles or tablets deciphered by the late G. Smith. Any occultist who reads of her love for Tammuz, his assassination by Izdubar, the goddess's despair and her descent through the seven gates of Hades in search of her beloved, and finally her liberation from the dark realm, will recognize the beautiful allegory of the soul in search of the Spirit.

**Isiac table.** A true monument of Egyptian art. It represents the goddess <term>Isis</term> in many of her aspects. The <term>Jesuit Kircher</term> describes it as a copper table overlaid with black enamel and silver incrustations. It was owned by <term>Cardinal Bembo</term>, and is therefore called the “<term>Tabula Bembina sive Mensa Isiaca</term>.” Under this title, it is described by <term>W. Wynn Wescott</term>, M.B., who provides its “<term>History and Occult Significance</term>” in an extremely interesting and learned volume (with photographs and illustrations). The tablet was believed to have been a votive offering to <term>Isis</term> in one of her many temples. During the sack of <term>Rome</term> in 1525, it came into the possession of a soldier who sold it to <term>Cardinal Bembo</term>. It then passed to the <term>Duke of Mantua</term> in 1630, at which time it was lost.

**Isis.** In Egyptian *<term>Issa</term>*, the goddess <term>Virgin-Mother</term>; personified Nature. In Egyptian or <term>Coptic Uasi</term>, she is the female reflection of *<term>Usar</term>* or <term>Osiris</term>. She is the “<term>woman clothed with the sun</term>” of the land of <term>Chemi</term>. <term>Isis-Latona</term> is the <term>Roman Isis</term>.

**Isitwa** (<term>Sk.</term>). The divine Power.

**Israel** (<term>Heb.</term>). The Eastern <term>Kabbalists</term> derive the name from *<term>Isaral</term>* or *<term>Asar</term>*, the <term>Sun-God</term>. “<term>Israel</term>” signifies “<term>striving with God</term>”: the “<term>sun rising upon Jacob-Israel</term>” means the <term>Sun-god Israel</term> (or <term>Isa-el</term>), striving with and seeking to fertilize matter, which has power with “<term>God</term> and with man” and often triumphs over both. <term>Esau</term>, <term>Esaou</term>, and <term>Asu</term> are also the <term>Sun</term>. <term>Esau</term> and <term>Jacob</term>, the allegorical twins, are the emblems of the ever-struggling dual principle in nature—good and evil, darkness and sunlight—and the “<term>Lord</term>” (<term>Jehovah</term>) is their archetype. <term>Jacob-Israel</term> is the feminine principle of <term>Esau</term>, just as <term>Abel</term> is that of <term>Cain</term>, with both <term>Cain</term> and <term>Esau</term> being the male principle. Hence, like <term>Malach-Iho</term>, the “<term>Lord</term>” <term>Esau</term> fights with <term>Jacob</term> and does not prevail. In *<term>Genesis</term>* 32, the <term>Sun-God</term> first strives with <term>Jacob</term>, breaks his thigh (a phallic symbol), and yet is defeated by his terrestrial type—matter; and the <term>Sun-God</term> rises upon <term>Jacob</term> and his *<term>thigh</term>* in covenant. All these biblical personages, including their “<term>Lord God</term>,” are types represented in an allegorical sequence. They are types of <term>Life</term> and <term>Death</term>, <term>Good</term> and <term>Evil</term>, <term>Light</term> and <term>Darkness</term>, and of <term>Matter</term> and <term>Spirit</term> in their synthesis, all shown under their contrasted aspects.

**Iswara** (<term>Sk.</term>). The “<term>Lord</term>” or the personal god—the *<term>divine Spirit</term>* in man. *<term>Literally</term>*, sovereign (independent) existence. A title given to <term>Siva</term> and other gods in <term>India</term>. <term>Siva</term> is also called <term>Iswaradeva</term>, or sovereign <term>deva</term>.

**Ithyphallic** (<term>Gr.</term>). Attributes of the gods as males and hermaphrodites, such as the bearded <term>Venus</term>, <term>Apollo</term> in woman’s clothes, <term>Ammon</term> the generator, the embryonic <term>Ptah</term>, and so on. Yet the <term>phallus</term>, so prominent and, according to our prudish notions, so indecent in the <term>Indian</term> and <term>Egyptian</term> religions, was associated in the earliest symbology with an idea far different and much purer than that of sexual creation. As shown by many an <term>Orientalist</term>, it expressed resurrection, the *<term>rising into life from death</term>*. **Izduhar**. A name of a hero in the fragments of Chaldean History and Theogony on the so-called Assyrian tiles, as read by the late George Smith and others. Smith seeks to identify Izduhar with Nimrod. Such may or may not be the case; but as the name of that Babylonian King itself only *appears* as Izduhar, his identification with the son of Cush may also turn out to be more apparent than real. Scholars are all too apt to check their archaeological discoveries by the far later statements found in the Mosaic books, instead of acting *vice versa*. The “chosen people” have been fond at all periods of history of helping themselves to other people’s property. From the appropriation of the early history of Sargon, King of Akkad, and its wholesale application to Moses—born (if at all) some thousands of years later—down to their “spoiling” the Egyptians under the direction and divine advice of their Lord God, the whole Pentateuch seems to be made up of unacknowledged *mosaical* <note>The author here likely uses "mosaical" as a pun, referring both to the alleged authorship of Moses and to the nature of a "mosaic"—a work made of many disparate fragments.</note> fragments from other people’s Scriptures. This ought to have made Assyriologists more cautious; but as many of these belong to the clerical caste, such coincidences as that of Sargon affect them very little. One thing is certain: Izduhar, or whatever his name may be, is shown in all the tablets as a mighty giant who towered in size above all other men as a cedar towers over brushwood—a hunter, according to cuneiform legends, who contended with and destroyed the lion, tiger, wild bull, and buffalo, the most formidable animals.

The idol is that of <term>Vishnu Krishna</term>. <term>Puri</term>, near the town of <term>Cuttack</term> in <term>Orissa</term>, is the great seat of its worship; and twice a year an immense number of pilgrims attend the festivals of the <term>Snâna-yâtra</term> and <term>Ratha-yâtra</term>. During the first, the image is bathed, and during the second it is placed on a chariot, between the images of *Balarâma* the brother and *Subhadrâ* the sister of <term>Krishna</term>, and the huge vehicle is drawn by the devotees, who consider it a blessing to be crushed to death under it.

It is followed by Chapter V as a blind; but it should be succeeded by Chapter VI, where the <term>Sons of God</term> took as their wives the daughters of men.

**<term>Jerusalem</term>**, *Jerusalem* (Septuagint) and *Hierosolyma* (Vulgate). In Hebrew, it is written *Yrshlim* or “city of peace,” but the ancient Greeks appropriately called it *Hierosalem* or “Secret Salem,” since Jerusalem is a rebirth from Salem, of which <term>Melchizedek</term> was the King-Hierophant—a declared <term>Astrolator</term> and worshipper of the Sun, “the Most High,” by the way. And no wonder, since these five kings were opposed not only by <term>Joshua</term> but by the “Lord God,” and by the Sun and the Moon also. On that day, we read, at the command of the successor of Moses, “the sun stood still and the moon stayed” (v. 13) for the whole day. No mortal man, king or commoner, could withstand, of course, such a shower “of great stones from heaven” as was cast upon them by the Lord himself . . . “from Beth-horon unto Azekah” . . . “and they died” (v. 11). After having died, they “fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah” (v. 16). It appears, however, that such undignified behavior in a God received its <term>Karmic</term> punishment afterward. At different epochs of history, the <term>Temple of the Jewish Lord</term> was sacked, ruined, and burned (See “Mount Moriah”)—holy <term>ark of the covenant</term>, <term>cherubs</term>, <term>Shekinah</term> and all—but that deity seemed as powerless to protect his property from desecration as if there were no more stones left in heaven. After <term>Pompey</term> had taken the Second Temple in 63 B.C., and the third one, built by <term>Herod the Great</term>, had been razed to the ground by the Romans in 70 A.D., no new temple was allowed to be built in the capital of the “chosen people” of the Lord. In spite of the Crusades, since the 13th century, Jerusalem has belonged to the Muslims, and almost every site holy and dear to the memory of the old Israelites, and also of the Christians, is now covered by <term>minarets</term> and <term>mosques</term>, Turkish barracks, and other monuments of <term>Islam</term>.

**<term>Jetzirah</term>** (Hebrew). See “Yetairah.”

**<term>Jetzirah</term>**, *<term>Sepher</term>*; or *Book of the Creation*. The most occult of all the Kabbalistic works now possessed by modern mystics. Its alleged origin—that it was written by <term>Abraham</term>—is, of course, nonsense, but its intrinsic value is great. It is composed of six *<term>Perakim</term>* (chapters), subdivided into thirty-three short *<term>Mishnas</term>* or Sections, and it treats the evolution of the Universe based on a system of correspondences and numbers. Deity is said in it to have formed (“created”) the Universe by means of numbers “by thirty-two paths (or ways) of secret wisdom,” these ways being made to correspond with the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet and the ten fundamental numbers. These ten are the primordial numbers from which the whole Universe proceeded, and these are followed by the twenty-two letters divided into *Three Mothers*, the seven double consonants, and the twelve simple consonants. Anyone who wishes to understand the system well is advised to read the excellent little treatise on *<term>Sepher Jetzirah</term>* by Dr. <term>W. Wynn Westcott</term>. (See “Yetairah.”)

**<term>Jhâna</term>** (Sanskrit) or *<term>Jnâna</term>*. Knowledge; Occult Wisdom.

**<term>Jhâna Bhaskara</term>** (Sanskrit). A work on *<term>Asuramâya</term>*, the <term>Atlantean</term> astronomer and magician, and other prehistoric legends.

**<term>Jigten Gonpo</term>** (Tibetan). A name of *<term>Avalokitêswara</term>*, or *<term>Chenresi Padmapani</term>*, the “Protector against Evil.”

**<term>Jishnu</term>** (Sanskrit). “Leader of the Celestial Host,” a title of <term>Indra</term>, who, in the War of the Gods with the <term>Asuras</term>, led the “host of <term>devas</term>.” He is the “<term>Michael</term>, the leader of the <term>Archangels</term>” of India.

**<term>Jiva</term>** (Sanskrit). Life, as the <term>Absolute</term>; also the <term>Monad</term> or “*<term>Atma-Buddhi</term>*.”

**<term>Jivanmukta</term>** (Sanskrit). An adept or yogi who has reached the ultimate state of holiness and separated himself from matter; a *<term>Mahatma</term>*, or *<term>Nirvanee</term>*, a “dweller in bliss” and emancipation. Virtually one who has attained <term>Nirvana</term> during life.

**<term>Jivatma</term>** (Sanskrit). The ONE universal life, generally; but also the divine Spirit in <term>Man</term>.

**<term>Jnânam</term>** (Sanskrit). The same as “*<term>Gnâna</term>*,” etc.; the same as “*<term>Jhâna</term>*” (see entry).

**<term>Jnânendriyas</term>** (Sanskrit). The five channels of knowledge.

**<term>Jnâna Sakti</term>** (Sanskrit). The power of intellect.

**<term>Jörd</term>**. In Northern Germany, the goddess of the Earth; the same as *<term>Nerthus</term>* and the Scandinavian *<term>Freya</term>* or *<term>Frigg</term>*.

**<term>Jotunheim</term>** (Scandinavian). The land of the *<term>Hrimthurse</term>* or Frost-giants.

**<term>Jotuns</term>** (Scandinavian). The <term>Titans</term> or giants. *<term>Mimir</term>*, who taught *<term>Odin</term>* magic—the “thrice wise”—was a <term>Jotun</term>.

**<term>Jul</term>** (Scandinavian). The wheel of the Sun, from which comes *<term>Yuletide</term>*, which was sacred to *<term>Freyer</term>*, or *<term>Fro</term>*, the Sun-god, the ripener of the fields and

## K.

**K.**—The eleventh letter in both the English and the Hebrew alphabets. As a numeral, it stands in the latter for 20, and in the former for 250, and with a stroke over it (K̅) for 250,000. The Kabbalists and the Masons appropriate the *Kodesh* or *Kadosh* as the name of the Jewish God under this letter.

**Ka** (*Sk.*). According to Max Müller, the interrogative pronoun “who”—raised to the dignity of a deity without cause or reason. Still, it has its esoteric significance and is a name of Brahmâ in his phallic character as generator or *Prajâpati* (*see also*).

**Kabah or Kaaba** (*Arab.*). The name of the famous Muslim temple at Mecca, a great place of pilgrimage. The building is not large but very original; it is of a cubical form, 23 by 24 cubits in length and breadth and 27 cubits high, with only one opening on the east side to admit light. In the northeast corner is the “black stone” of Kaaba, said to have been lowered down directly from heaven and to have been as white as snow, but it subsequently became black due to the sins of mankind. The “white stone,” the reputed tomb of Ishmael, is on the north side, and the place of Abraham is to the east. If, as the Muslims claim, this temple was transferred by Allah or Jehovah directly from Eden down to earth at the prayer of Adam after his exile, then the “heathen” may truly claim to have far exceeded the divine primordial architecture in the beauty of their buildings.

**Kabalist.** From Q B L H, KABALA, an unwritten or oral tradition. The Kabbalist is a student of “secret science,” one who interprets the hidden meaning of the Scriptures with the help of the symbolic *Kabala* and explains the real meaning by these means. The Tanaïm were the first Kabbalists among the Jews; they appeared in Jerusalem around the beginning of the third century before the Christian era. The books of *Ezekiel*, *Daniel*, *Enoch*, and the *Revelation* of St. John are purely Kabbalistic. This secret doctrine is identified with that of the Chaldeans and includes, at the same time, much of the Persian wisdom or “magic.” History catches glimpses of famous Kabbalists ever since the eleventh century. The Middle Ages, and even our own times, have had an enormous number of the most learned and intellectual men who were students of the *Kabala* (or Qabbalah, as some spell it). The most famous among the former were Paracelsus, Henry Khunrath, Jacob Boehme, Robert Fludd, the two Van Helmonts, Abbot John Trithemius, Cornelius Agrippa, Cardinal Nicholas of Cusa, Jerome Cardan, Pope Sixtus IV, and such Christian scholars as Raymond Lully, Giovanni Pico della Mirandola,

Guillaume Postel, the great Johannes Reuchlin, Dr. Henry More, Eugenius Philalethes (*Thomas Vaughan*), the erudite Jesuit Athanasius Kircher, Christian Knorr (*Baron*) von Rosenroth; then Sir Isaac Newton, Leibniz, Lord Bacon, Spinosa, etc., etc.—the list is almost inexhaustible. As remarked by Mr. Isaac Myer in his *Qabbalah*, the ideas of the Kabbalists have largely influenced European literature. "Upon the practical Qabbalah, the Abbé de Villars (nephew of de Montfaucon) in 1670 published his celebrated satirical novel, ‘The Count de Gabalis’, upon which Pope based his ‘Rape of the Lock’. Qabbalism ran through the medieval poems, the ‘Romance of the Rose’, and permeates the writings of Dante." No two of them, however, agreed on the origin of the Kabala, the *Zohar*, *Sepher Yetzirah*, etc. Some show it as coming from the Biblical Patriarchs, Abraham, and even Seth; others from Egypt, and others again from Chaldea. The system is certainly very old; but like all other systems, whether religious or philosophical, the Kabala is derived directly from the primeval Secret Doctrine of the East, through the Vedas, the Upanishada, Orpheus and Thales, Pythagoras, and the Egyptians. Whatever its source, its foundation is at any rate identical with that of all the other systems, from the *Book of the Dead* down to the later Gnostics. The best exponents of the Kabala in the Theosophical Society were among the earliest, Dr. S. Pancoast of Philadelphia and Mr. G. Felt; and among the latest, Dr. W. Wynn Westcott, Mr. S. L. MacGregor Mathers (both of the Rosicrucian College), and a few others. (See "Qabbalah".)

**Kabalistic Faces.** These are Nephesch, Ruach, and Neschamah, or the animal (vital), the Spiritual, and the Divine Souls in man—Body, Soul, and Mind.

**Kabalah (*Heb.*).** The hidden wisdom of the Hebrew Rabbis of the middle ages, derived from the older secret doctrines concerning divine things and cosmogony, which were combined into a theology after the time of the captivity of the Jews in Babylon. All the works that fall under the esoteric category are termed Kabalistic.

**Kabiri (*Phoen.*).** Or the Kabirim. Deities and very mysterious gods among the ancient nations, including the Israelites, some of whom—such as Terah, Abram’s father—worshiped them under the name of *Terephim*. To the Christians, however, they are now devils, although the modern Archangels are the direct transformation of these same Kabiri. In Hebrew, the latter name means "the mighty ones," *Gibborim*. At one time, all the deities connected with fire—whether they were divine, infernal, or volcanic—were called Kabirian.

**Kadmon (*Heb.*).** Archetypal man. See "Adam Kadmon".

**Kadosh (*Heb.*).** Consecrated, holy; also written *Kodesh*. Something set apart for temple worship. But between the etymological meaning of the word and its subsequent significance in application to the *Kadeshim* (the "priests" set apart for certain temple rites), there is an

# GLOSSARY

The words *Kadosh* and *Kadeshim* are used in 2 *Kings* as a rather insulting name, for the *Kadeshuth* of the Bible were identical in their office and duties to the Nautch girls of some Hindu temples. They were *Galli*, the mutilated priests of the lustful rites of Venus Astarte, who lived “by the house of the Lord.” Curiously enough, the terms *Kadosh*, etc., were appropriated and used by several degrees of Masonic knighthood.

**Kailasa** (*S*.) In metaphysics, “heaven,” the abode of gods; geographically, a mountain range in the Himalayas, north of Lake Mansaravâra, also called Lake *Manasa*.

**Kailem** (*Heb*.) *Literally*, vessels or vehicles; the vases for the source of the Waters of Life; used for the Ten Sephiroth, considered as the primeval *nuclei* of all Cosmic Forces. Some Kabbalists regard them as manifesting in the universe through twenty-two canals, which are represented by the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet, thus making, with the Ten Sephiroth, thirty-two paths of wisdom. [w.w.w.]

**Kaimarath** (*Pers*.) The last of the race of the *prehuman* kings. He is identical with Adam Kadmon; a legendary Persian hero.

**Kakodæmon** (*Gr*.) The evil genius as opposed to *Agathodæmon*, the good genius or deity. A Gnostic term.

**Kala** (*Sk*.) A measure of time; four hours, a period of thirty *Kasthas*.

**Kala** (*Sk*.) Time, fate; a cycle and a proper name, or title given to Yama, King of the underworld and Judge of the Dead.

**Kalabhana** (*Sk*.) The same as Taraka (See *The Secret Doctrine*, Vol. II, p. 382, footnote).

**Kalagni** (*Sk*.) The flame of time. A divine Being created by Siva, a monster with 1,000 heads. A title of Siva meaning “the fire of fate.”

**Kalahansa** or *Hamsa* (*Sk*.) A mystic title given to Brahma (or Parabrahman); it means “the swan in and out of time.” Brahmâ (male) is called *Hansa-Vahan*, the vehicle of the “Swan.”

**Kalavingka** (*Sk*.) also *Kuravikaya* and *Karanda*, etc. “The sweet-voiced bird of immortality.” Eitel identifies it with *cuculus melanoleicus*, though the bird itself is allegorical and non-existent. Its voice is heard at a certain stage of *Dhyana* in Yoga practice. It is said to have awakened King Bimbisara and thus saved him from the sting of a cobra. In its esoteric meaning, this sweet-voiced bird is our Higher Ego.

**Kalevala** The Finnish Epic of Creation.

**Kali** (*Sk*.) The “black,” now the name of Parvati, the consort of Siva, but originally the name of one of the seven tongues of Agni, the god of fire—“the black, fiery tongue.” Evil and wickedness.

**Kakidasa** (*Sk*.) The greatest poet and dramatist of India. <note>Likely a misspelling of Kalidasa.</note>

**Kaliya (Sk.).** The five-headed serpent killed by Krishna in his childhood. A mystical monster symbolizing human passions—the river or water being a symbol of matter.
**Kaliyuga (Sk.).** The fourth, the *black* or *iron* age, our present period, the duration of which is 432,000 years. It is the last of the ages into which the evolutionary period of man is divided by a series of such ages. It began 3,102 years B.C. at the moment of Krishna's death, and the first cycle of 5,000 years will end between the years 1897 and 1898.
**Kalki Avatar (Sk.).** The “White Horse Avatar,” which will be the last <term>manvantaric</term> incarnation of Vishnu, according to the Brahmins; of Maitreya Buddha, according to Northern Buddhists; of Sosiogh, the last hero and Savior of the Zoroastrians, as claimed by Parsis; and of the “Faithful and True” on the white Horse (*Rev.* xix., 2). In his future manifestation or tenth avatar, the heavens will open and Vishnu will appear “seated on a milk-white steed, with a drawn sword blazing like a comet for the final destruction of the wicked, the renewal of ‘creation’ and the ‘restoration of purity.’ ” (Compare *Revelation*.) This will take place at the end of the Kaliyuga, 427,000 years from now. The end of every Yuga is called “the destruction of the world,” as the earth then changes its outward form each time, submerging one set of continents and raising another set.
**Kalluka Bhatta (Sk.).** A commentator on the Hindu *Manu Smriti Scriptures*; a well-known writer and historian.
**Kalpa (Sk.).** The period of a <term>mundane revolution</term>, generally a cycle of time, but usually it represents a “day” and “night” of Brahmâ, a period of 4,320,000,000 years.
**Kama (Sk.).** Evil desire, lust, volition; the clinging to existence. Kama is generally identified with *Mara*, the tempter.
**Kamadeva (Sk.).** In popular belief, the god of love, a <term>Visvadeva</term>, in the Hindu <term>Pantheon</term>. Just as the *Eros* of Hesiod was degraded into <term>Cupid</term> by exoteric law, and still further degraded by a later popular meaning attributed to the term, so is Kama a most mysterious and metaphysical subject. The earlier Vedic description of Kama alone gives the keynote to what he symbolizes. Kama is the first conscious, *all-embracing desire* for universal good, love, and for all that lives and feels, needs help and kindness—the first feeling of infinite tender compassion and mercy that arose in the consciousness of the creative <term>ONE Force</term>, as soon as it came into life and being as a ray from the <term>ABSOLUTE</term>. The *Rig Veda* says,
> “Desire first arose in IT, which was the primal germ of mind, and which Sages, searching with their intellect, have discovered in their heart to be the bond which connects <term>Entity</term> with non-<term>Entity</term>,” or *Manas* with pure *Atma-Buddhi*. 

There is no idea of *sexual love* in the true conception. Kama is pre-eminently the divine desire for creating happiness and love; and it is only ages later, as mankind began to materialize its grandest ideals into rigid dogmas through anthropomorphization, that Kama be-

**Kamadhâtu** (*Sk.*). Also called <term>Kamâvatchara</term>, a region including <term>Kamâlôka</term>. In esoteric ideas, it is the first of the <term>Trailôkya</term>—or three regions (applied also to celestial beings) or seven planes or degrees, each broadly represented by one of the three chief characteristics: namely, <term>Kama</term>, <term>Rupa</term>, and <term>Arupa</term>, or those of desire, form, and formlessness. The first of the <term>Trailôkyas</term>, <term>Kamadhâtu</term>, is thus composed of the earth and the six inferior <term>Devalokas</term>, the earth being followed by <term>Kamaloka</term> <note>see that entry</note>. These taken together constitute the seven degrees of the material world of form and sensuous gratification. The second of the <term>Trailôkya</term> (or <term>Trilôkya</term>) is called <term>Rupadhâtu</term> or “material form” and is also composed of seven <term>Lokas</term> (or localities). The third is <term>Arupadhâtu</term> or “immaterial lokas.” “Locality,” however, is an incorrect word to use in translating the term <term>dhâtu</term>, which in some of its special applications does not mean a “place” at all. For instance, <term>Arupadhâtu</term> is a purely subjective world, a “state” rather than a place. But as European languages have no adequate metaphysical terms to express certain ideas, we can only point out the difficulty.

**Kamaloka** (*Sk.*). The semi-material plane, subjective and invisible to us, where the disembodied “personalities,” the astral forms called <term>Kamarupa</term>, remain until they fade out from it by the complete exhaustion of the effects of the mental impulses that created these images of human and animal passions and desires. (See “<term>Kamârupa</term>.”) It is the <term>Hades</term> of the ancient Greeks and the <term>Amenti</term> of the Egyptians, the land of <term>Silent Shadows</term>; a division of the first group of the <term>Trailôkya</term>. (See “<term>Kamadhâtu</term>.”)

**Kamarupa** (*Sk.*). Metaphysically, and in our esoteric philosophy, it is the subjective form created through the mental and physical desires and thoughts in connection with things of matter by all sentient beings—a form which survives the death of their bodies. After that death, three of these seven “principles”—or let us say planes of senses and consciousness on which human instincts and ideation act in turn—namely, the

**Kamea** (*Heb.*). An amulet, generally a magic square.

**Kandu** (*Sk.*). A holy sage of the second root-race, a yogi, whom <term>Pramlôcha</term>, a “nymph” sent by <term>Indra</term> for that purpose, beguiled and lived with for several centuries. Finally, the Sage, returning to his senses, repudiated and chased her away. Whereupon she gave birth to a daughter, <term>Mârishâ</term>. The story is told in an allegorical fable from the <term>Purânas</term>.

**Kanishka** (*Sk.*). A King of the <term>Tochari</term>, who reigned when the third <term>Buddhist Synod</term> met in Kashmir—that is, about the middle of the first century B.C. A great patron of Buddhism, he built the finest <term>stûpas</term> or <term>dagobas</term> in Northern India and Kabulistan.

**Kanishthas** (*Sk.*). A class of gods which will manifest in the fourteenth or last <term>manvantara</term> of our world, according to the Hindus.

**Kanya** (*Sk.*). A virgin or maiden. **Kanya Kumârî**, “the virgin-maiden,” is the title of <term>Durga-Kali</term>, worshipped by the <term>Thugs</term> and <term>Tantrikas</term>.

**Kapila Rishi** (*Sk.*). A great sage and a great adept of antiquity; the author of the <term>Sankhya philosophy</term>.

**Kapilavastu** (*Sk.*). The birth-place of the Lord Buddha; called “the yellow dwelling”; the capital of the monarch who was the father of <term>Gautama Buddha</term>.

**Karabtanos** (*Gr.*). The spirit of blind or animal desire; the symbol of <term>Kama-rupa</term>. The Spirit “without sense or judgment” in the <term>Codex of the Nazarenes</term>. He is the symbol of matter and represents the father of the seven spirits of lust fathered by him on his mother, the “Spiritus” or the <term>Astral Light</term>.

**<term>Karam</term>** (*Sk.*). A great festival in honor of the Sun-Spirit among the Kolarian tribes.

**<term>Kârana</term>** (*Sk.*). Cause (metaphysically).

**<term>Kârana Sarîra</term>** (*Sk.*). The "Causal body." It has a dual meaning. Exoterically, it is *<term>Avidya</term>*, ignorance, or that which is the cause of the evolution of a human ego and its reincarnation; hence, it represents the lower <term>Manas</term>. Esoterically, the causal body or *<term>Kâranopadhi</term>* stands in Taraka Raja Yoga as corresponding to <term>Buddhi</term> and the Higher "<term>Manas</term>," or Spiritual Soul.

**<term>Karanda</term>** (*Sk.*). The "sweet-voiced bird," the same as *Kalavingka* (see entry).

**<term>Kâranopadhi</term>** (*Sk.*). The basis or <term>upadhi</term> of Karana, the "causal soul." In Taraka Raja Yoga, it corresponds with both *<term>Manas</term>* and *<term>Buddhi</term>*. See the Table in the *Secret Doctrine*, Vol. I., p. 157.

**<term>Kardecists</term>.** The followers of the spiritual system of Allan Kardec, the Frenchman who founded the modern movement of the Spiritist School. The Spiritists of France differ from American and English Spiritualists in that their "Spirits" teach reincarnation, while those of the United States and Great Britain denounce this belief as a heretical fallacy and abuse and slander those who accept it. "When Spirits disagree..."

**<term>Karma</term>** (*Sk.*). Physically, action; metaphysically, the LAW OF RETRIBUTION, the Law of cause and effect, or Ethical Causation. It is *Nemesis* only in one sense—that of bad Karma. It is the eleventh <term>Nidana</term> in the chain of causes and effects in orthodox Buddhism; yet it is the power that controls all things, the result of moral action, the metaphysical *<term>Samskâra</term>*, or the moral effect of an act committed to attain something which gratifies a personal desire. There is the Karma of merit and the Karma of demerit. Karma neither punishes nor rewards; it is simply the *one Universal LAW* which guides unerringly and, so to speak, blindly, all other laws that produce certain effects along the paths of their respective causations. When Buddhism teaches that "Karma is that moral kernel (of any being) which alone survives death and continues in transmigration" or reincarnation, it simply means that nothing remains after each personality but the causes produced by it. These causes are undying—that is, they cannot be eliminated from the Universe until replaced and, so to speak, wiped out by their legitimate effects. Unless such causes are compensated during the life of the person who produced them with adequate effects, they will follow the reincarnated <term>Ego</term> and reach it in its subsequent reincarnation until harmony between effects and causes is fully re-established. No "personality"—a mere bundle of material atoms and of instinctual and mental characteristics—can, of course, continue as such in the world of pure Spirit. Only that which is immortal in its very nature and divine in its essence, namely the <term>Ego</term>, can exist forever.

It also distinguishes between the reincarnation-believing French Kardecists and other Spiritualist groups who reject the doctrine.</summary>

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

And as it is that Ego which chooses the personality it will inhabit after each Devachan, and which receives through these personalities the effects of the produced Karmic causes, it is therefore the Ego—that self which is the “*moral kernel*” referred to and the embodied karma—“which alone survives death.”

**<term>Karnak</term>** (*Eg.*). The ruins of the ancient temples and palaces which now stand on the site of ancient Thebes. These are the most magnificent representatives of the art and skill of the earliest Egyptians. A few lines quoted from Champollion, Denon, and an English traveler show most eloquently what these ruins are. Of Karnak, Champollion writes:—“The ground covered by the mass of remaining buildings is square, and each side measures 1,800 feet. One is astonished and *overcome* by the grandeur of the sublime remnants, and the lavishness and magnificence of workmanship to be seen everywhere. No people of ancient or modern times has conceived the art of architecture on a scale so sublime and so grandiose as it existed among the ancient Egyptians; and the imagination, which in Europe soars far above our porticos, stops and falls powerless at the foot of the 140 columns of the hypostyle of Karnak! In one of its halls, the Cathedral of Notre Dame could stand and not touch the ceiling, but would be considered a small ornament in the center of the hall.”

Another writer exclaims: “Courts, halls, gateways, pillars, obelisks, monolithic figures, sculptures, and long rows of sphinxes are found in such profusion at Karnak that the sight is too much for modern comprehension.” Denon, the French traveler, says: “It is hardly possible to believe, after seeing it, in the reality of the existence of so many buildings collected together on a single point—in their dimensions, in the resolute perseverance which their construction required, and in the incalculable expense of so much magnificence! It is necessary for the reader to imagine what is before him to be a dream, as he who views the objects themselves occasionally yields to the doubt of whether he is perfectly awake. . . . There are lakes and mountains *within the perimeter of the sanctuary*. These two edifices are selected as examples from a list that is nearly *inexhaustible*. The whole valley and delta of the Nile, from the cataracts to the sea, was covered with temples, palaces, tombs, pyramids, obelisks, and pillars. The execution of the sculptures is beyond praise. The mechanical perfection with which artists worked in granite, serpentine, breccia, and basalt is wonderful, according to all the experts . . . animals and plants look as natural as life, and artificial objects are beautifully sculpted; battles by sea and land, and scenes of domestic life are to be found in all their *bas-reliefs*.”

**<term>Karnaim</term>** (*Heb.*). Horned, an attribute of Ashtoreth and Astarte; those horns typify the male element and convert the deity into an androgyne. Isis also is at times horned. Compare also the idea of the Crescent Moon—the symbol of Isis—as being horned. <note>W.W.W.</note>

# GLOSSARY

**Hindu** "Krishna Karna." Both were Sun-gods; both "Karna" and "Karmeios" mean "radiant." (See *The Secret Doctrine* II., p. 44, note).

**Karshipta** (Mazdean). The holy bird of Heaven in the Mazdean Scriptures, of which Ahura Mazda says to Zarathustra that "he recites the *Avesta* in the language of birds" (*Bundahishn xix. and following*). The bird is the symbol of the "Soul," the Angel, and the Deva in every ancient religion. It is easy to see, therefore, that this "holy bird" refers to the divine Ego of man, or the "Soul." It is the same as Karanda (see that entry).

**Karshvare** (Zend). The "seven earths" (our seven-fold chain) over which rule the *Amesha Spenta*, the Archangels or Dhyan Chohans of the Parsis. Of these seven earths, only one—namely Hvanirata, our earth—is known to mortals. These Earths (esoterically), or seven divisions (exoterically), are our own planetary chain as described in *Esoteric Buddhism* and the *Secret Doctrine*. The doctrine is plainly stated in *Fargard* XIX., 39, of the *Vendidad*.

**Kartikeya** (Sanskrit), or *Kartika*. The Indian God of War, son of Siva, born of his seed which fell into the Ganges. He is also the personification of the power of the *Logos*. He is associated with the planet Mars. *Kartika* is a very occult figure, nursed by the Pleiades, and is a Kumâra. (See *Secret Doctrine*.)

**Karunâ-Bhâwanâ** (Sanskrit). The meditation of pity and compassion in Yoga.

**Kasbeck**. The mountain in the Caucasian range where Prometheus was bound.

**Kasi** (Sanskrit). Another and more ancient name for the holy city of Benares.

**Kasina** (Sanskrit). A mystic Yoga rite used to free the mind from all agitation and bring the *Kamic* (desire) element to a complete standstill.

**Kâsi Khanda** (Sanskrit). A long poem which forms a part of the *Skanda Purâna* and contains another version of the legend of Daksha's head. Having lost his head in a struggle, the gods replaced it with the head of a ram, *Mekha Shivas*, whereas other versions describe it as the head of a goat—a substitution that changes the allegory considerably.

**Kasyapa** (Sanskrit). A Vedic Sage; in the words of the *Atharva Veda*, he is "The self-born who sprang from Time." Besides being the father of the Adityas (headed by Indra), Kasyapa is also the forefather of serpents, reptiles, birds, and other walking, flying, and creeping beings.

**Katha** (Sanskrit). One of the Upanishads commented upon by Sankarâchârya.

**Kaumara** (Sanskrit). The "Kumara Creation," the virgin youths who sprang from the body of Brahmâ.

**Kauravya** (Sanskrit). The King of the Nâgas (Serpents) in Pâtâla; exoterically it refers to a hall, but esoterically it means something very different. There is a tribe of the *Nâgas* in Upper India; *Nagal* is the name in

# THEOSOPHICAL GLOSSARY

Mexico is still used by the chief medicine men today, as it was by the leading adepts at the dawn of history. Finally, *Patal* <note>original: "Patala," the Sanskrit name for the underworld or the opposite side of the globe</note> means the "Antipodes" and is an ancient name for America. Therefore, the story that the hero Arjuna traveled to Pâtâla and married *Ulupi*, the daughter of King Kauravvya, may be just as historical as many other legends that were first dismissed as fables and later found to be true.

**Kavanim** (*Hebrew*). Also written as Cunim; the name of certain mystical cakes offered to *Ishtar*, the Babylonian Venus. The prophet Jeremiah speaks of these "Cunim" being offered to the "Queen of Heaven" (Jeremiah 7:18). Today, we no longer offer these buns as sacrifices, but we still eat them at *Easter* <note>A reference to the origins of "Hot Cross Buns"</note>. [w.w.w.] <note>Initials for William Wynn Westcott, a prominent occultist and contributor to this glossary.</note>

**Kavyavahana** (*Sanskrit*). The sacrificial fire associated with the *Pitris* <note>The ancestors or "fathers" of humanity</note>.

**Kchana** (*Sanskrit*). An incredibly short unit of time: the 90th part of a single thought, or the 4,500th part of a minute. During this tiny fraction of time, between 90 and 100 births and as many deaths are said to occur on this earth.

**Kebar-Zivo** (*Gnostic*). One of the primary creator deities in the *Book of the Nazarenes* <note>original Latin: "Codex Nazaræus"</note>.

**Keherpas** (*Sanskrit*). An aerial or ethereal form.

**Keshara** (*Sanskrit*). "Sky Walker"; that is, a *Yogi* who has the power to travel in his astral form.

**Kether** (*Hebrew*). "The Crown," the highest of the ten *Sephiroth* <note>Divine emanations in the Kabbalah</note> and the first of the Divine Triad. It corresponds to the "Great Countenance" <note>original Latin/Greek: "Macroprosopus"</note> or the "Long Face" <note>original Aramaic: "Arikh Anpin"</note>, which then differentiates into "Wisdom" <note>original Hebrew: "Chokmah"</note> and "Understanding" <note>original Hebrew: "Binah"</note>. [w.w.w.]

**Ketu** (*Sanskrit*). In astronomy, the descending node <note>the point where the moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic</note>; mythologically, it is the tail of the celestial dragon that attacks the Sun during eclipses. The term is also used for a comet or meteor.

**Key**. A symbol of universal importance and the emblem of silence among ancient nations. When represented on the threshold of the *Adytum* <note>original: "Adytum," the innermost, most sacred shrine of a temple</note>, a key had a double meaning: it reminded the initiates of their vow of silence and promised the unlocking of mysteries that were previously hidden from the uninitiated. In the play *Oedipus at Colonus* by Sophocles, the chorus speaks of "the golden key that has been placed upon the tongue of the ministering High Priest <note>original Greek: "Hierophant"</note> in the mysteries of Eleusis" (line 1051). According to the poet Callimachus, the priestess of Ceres carried a key as her badge of office. In the Mysteries of Isis, the key symbolized the opening or revealing of the heart and conscience before the forty-two judges <note>original: "assessors"</note> of the dead (*Royal Masonic Cyclopaedia*).

**Khado** (*Tibetan*). Evil female spirits or demons in popular folklore. In Esoteric Philosophy, these represent the hidden and harmful forces of nature, known in Sanskrit as *Dakinis* (elementals).

**Khaldi**. The earliest inhabitants of Chaldea. They were originally worshippers of the Moon God <note>original Latin: "Deus Lunus"</note>, a form of worship brought to them by a great wave of early Hindu migration. Later, the term referred to a specific class of professional astrologers and initiates.

# GLOSSARY

**Kha** (*Sk.*). The same as "Akasa."

**Khamism.** A name given by Egyptologists to the ancient language of Egypt. Also called *Khami*.

**Khanda Kala** (*Sk.*). Finite or conditioned time in contrast to infinite time, or eternity—*Kala*.

**Khem** (*Eg.*). The same as Horus. "The God Khem will avenge his father Osiris," says a text in a papyrus.

**Khepra** (*Eg.*). An Egyptian god presiding over rebirth and transmigration. He is represented with a scarabaeus instead of a head.

**Khi** (*Chin.*). Literally, "breath"; meaning Buddha.

**Khnoom** (*Eg.*). The great Deep, or Primordial Space.

**Khoda** (*Pers.*). The name for the Deity.

**Khons**, or *Chons*. (*Eg.*) The Son of Maut and Ammon, the personification of morning. He is the Theban Harpocrates, according to some. Like Horus, he crushes under his foot a crocodile, an emblem of night and darkness, or Seb (Sebek) who is Typhon. But in the inscriptions, he is addressed as "the Healer of diseases and banisher of all evil." He is also the "god of the hunt," and Sir Gardner Wilkinson sees in him the Egyptian Hercules, probably because the Romans had a god named Consus who presided over horse races and was therefore called "the concealer of secrets." But the latter is a later variant of the Egyptian Khons, who is more probably an aspect of Horus, as he wears a hawk’s head and carries the whip and crook of Osiris, the *tat*, and the *crux ansata*.

**Khoom** (*Eg.*), or *Knooph*. The Soul of the World; a variant of *Khnoom*.

**Khubilkhan** (*Mong.*), or *Shabrong*. In Tibet, the names given to the supposed incarnations of Buddha; Elect Saints.

**Khunrath**, *Henry*. A famous Kabbalist, chemist, and physician born in 1502, initiated into Theosophy (Rosicrucianism) in 1544. He left some excellent Kabbalistic works, the best of which is the "Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom" (1598).

**Kimapurushas** (*Sk.*). Monstrous Devas, half-man, half-horse.

**Kings of Edom.** Esoterically, the early, tentative, malformed races of men. Some Kabbalists interpret them as "sparks"—worlds in formation that disappear as soon as they are formed.

**Kinnaras** (*Sk.*). Literally, "What men?" Fabulous creatures of the same description as the *Kim-purushas*. They are one of the four classes of beings called "Maharajas."

**Kioo-tche** (*Chin.*). An astronomical work.

**Kiratarjuniya** of *Bharavi* (*Sk.*). A Sanskrit epic celebrating the strife and prowess of Arjuna against the god Shiva, who is disguised as a forester.

**Kiver-Shans** (*Chin.*). The astral or "Thought Body."
