# THEOSOPHICAL

**Kiyun** *(Heb.)*. A deity or the god *Kivan* who was worshipped by the Israelites in the wilderness and was probably identical to Saturn and even to the god *Siva*. Indeed, as the Zendic H is S in India (their “hapta” is “sapta,” and so on) and as the letters K, H, and S are interchangeable, *Siva* may have easily become *Kiva* and *Kivan*.

**Klesha** *(Sk.)*. Love of life, but literally “pain and misery.” The clinging to existence, which is almost the same as *Kama*.

**Klikoosha** *(Russ.)*. One possessed by the Evil One. *Literally*, a “crier out” or a “screamer,” as such unfortunate people are periodically attacked with fits during which they crow like cocks, neigh, bray, and prophesy.

**Klippoth** *(Heb.)*. Shells; used in the Kabbalah in several senses: (1) evil spirits or demons; (2) the shells of dead human beings—not the physical body, but the remnant of the personality after the spirit has departed; (3) the Elementaries of **some authors**. [w.w.w.]

**Kneph** *(Eg.)*. Also *Cneph* and *Nef*, endowed with the same attributes as Khem. One of the gods of creative force, for he is connected with the Mundane Egg. He is called by Porphyry “the creator of the world”; by Plutarch the “unmade and eternal deity”; by Eusebius he is identified with the *Logos*; and Iamblichus goes so far as almost to identify him with Brahmâ, since he says of him that “this god is intellect itself, intellectually perceiving itself, and consecrating intellection to itself; and is to be worshipped in silence.” One form of him, adds Mr. Bonwick, “was *Av*, meaning *flesh*. He was <note>criocephalus means ram-headed</note> criocephalus, with a solar disk on his head, and standing on the serpent *Mehen*. In his left hand was a viper, and a cross was in his right. He was actively engaged in the underworld upon a mission of creation.” Deveria writes: “‘His journey to the lower hemisphere appears to symbolize the evolution of substances which are born to die and to be reborn.’” Thousands of years before Kardec, Swedenborg, and Darwin appeared, the ancient Egyptians entertained their various philosophies. (*Egyptian Belief and Modern Thought*.)

**Koinobi** *(Gr.)*. A sect which lived in Egypt in the early part of the first Christian century; usually confused with the *Therapeutæ*. They were known as magicians.

**Kokab** *(Chald.)*. The Kabbalistic name associated with the planet Mercury; also the stellar light. [w.w.w.]

**Kol** *(Heb.)*. A voice; in Hebrew letters QUL. The voice of the divine. (See “*Bath Kol*” and “*Vâch*”). [w.w.w.]

**Kols**. One of the tribes in central India, much given to magic. They are considered to be great sorcerers.

**Konx-Om-Pax** *(Gr.)*. Mystic words used in the Eleusinian mysteries. It is believed that these words are the Greek imitation of ancient Egyptian words once used in the secret ceremonies of the Isiac cult. Several modern authors give fanciful translations, but they are all only guesses at the truth. [w.w.w.]

<header>GLOSSARY</header>

**Koorgan** (*Russ.*). An artificial mound, generally an old tomb. Traditions of a supernatural or magical character are often attached to such mounds.

**Koran** (*Arab.*), or *Quran*. The sacred Scripture of the Muslims, revealed to the Prophet Mohammed by Allah (God) himself. This revelation differs, however, from that given by Jehovah to Moses. Christians abuse the Koran, calling it a hallucination and the work of an Arabian impostor. However, Mohammed preaches in his Scripture the unity of Deity and renders honor to the Christian prophet “*Issa Ben Yussuf*” (Jesus, son of Joseph). The Koran is a grand poem, filled with ethical teachings proclaiming loudly Faith, Hope, and Charity.

**Kosmos** (*Gr.*). The Universe, as distinguished from the world, which may mean our globe or earth.

**Kounboum** (*Tib.*). The sacred Tree of Tibet, the tree of the “10,000 images,” as Huc describes it. It grows in an enclosure on the monastery lands of the Lamasery of the same name and is well cared for. Tradition has it that it grew out of the hair of Tson-ka-pa, who was buried on that spot. This “Lama” was the great Reformer of Tibetan Buddhism and is regarded as an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha. In the words of the Abbé Huc, who lived several months with another missionary named Gabet near this phenomenal tree: “Each of its leaves, in opening, bears either a letter or a religious sentence written in sacred characters, and these letters are, of their kind, of such perfection that the type-foundries of Didot contain nothing to excel them. Open the leaves which the plant is about to unroll, and you will discover there, at the moment of appearing, the letters or the distinct words which are the marvel of this unique tree! Turn your attention from the leaves of the plant to the bark of its branches, and new characters will meet your eyes! Do not allow your interest to flag; lift the layers of this bark, and still other CHARACTERS will show themselves below those whose beauty had surprised you. For, do not fancy that these layered layers repeat the same *printing*. No, quite the contrary; for each layer you lift presents to view its own distinct type. How, then, can we suspect trickery? I have done my best in that direction to discover the slightest trace of human trick, and my baffled mind could not retain the slightest suspicion.” Yet, the kind French Abbé promptly suspects—the *Devil*.

**Kratudwishas** (*Sk.*). The enemies of the Sacrifices; the Daityas, Danavas, Kinnaras, etc., all represented as great ascetics and Yogis. This shows who are really meant. They were the enemies of religious rituals and empty ceremonies.

**Kravyâd** (*Sk.*). A flesh-eater; a carnivorous man or animal.

**Krisâswas, Sons of** (*Sk.*). The weapons called *Agneyâstra*. The magical living weapons endowed with intelligence, spoken of in the *Ramayana* and elsewhere. An occult allegory.

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

**Krishna** (*Sk.*). The most celebrated <term>avatar</term> of <term>Vishnu</term>, the "Savior" of the <term>Hindus</term> and their most popular god. He is the eighth <term>Avatar</term>, the son of <term>Devaki</term>, and the nephew of <term>Kansa</term>, the Indian King <term>Herod</term>, who while seeking for him among the shepherds and cowherds who concealed him, killed thousands of their newborn babes. The story of <term>Krishna</term>'s conception, birth, and childhood are the exact prototype of the New Testament story. The missionaries, of course, try to show that the <term>Hindus</term> stole the story of the Nativity from the early Christians who came to India.

**Krita-Yuga** (*Sk.*). The first of the four <term>Yugas</term> or Ages of the <term>Brahmans</term>; also called *Satya-Yuga*, a period lasting 1,728,000 years.

**Krittika** (*Sk.*). The <term>Pleiades</term>. The seven nurses of <term>Karttikiya</term>, the god of war.

**Kriyasakti** (*Gr.*). The power of thought; one of the seven forces of <term>Nature</term>. Creative potency of the *Siddhis* (powers) of the full <term>Yogis</term>.

**Kronos** (*Gr.*). <term>Saturn</term>. The God of Boundless Time and of the <term>Cycles</term>.

**Krura-lochana** (*Sk.*). The "evil-eyed"; used for <term>Sani</term>, the <term>Hindu Saturn</term>, the planet.

**Kshanti** (*Sk.*). Patience, one of the <term>Paramitas</term> of perfection.

**Kshatriya** (*Sk.*). The second of the four <term>castes</term> into which the <term>Hindus</term> were originally divided.

**Kshetrajna** or *Kshetrajneswara* (*Sk.*). Embodied spirit, the Conscious <term>Ego</term> in its highest manifestations; the reincarnating <term>Principle</term>; the "Lord" in us.

**Kshetram** (*Sk.*). The "Great Deep" of the <term>Bible</term> and <term>Kabala</term>. <term>Chaos</term>, <term>Yoni</term>; <term>Prakriti</term>, <term>Space</term>.

**Kshira Samudra** (*Sk.*). Ocean of milk, churned by the gods.

**Kuch-ha-guf** (*Heb.*). The astral body of a man. In <term>Franz Lambert</term> it is written "<term>Coach-ha-guf</term>." But the <term>Hebrew</term> word is <term>Kuch</term>, meaning *vis* <note>Latin for "force" or "power"</note>, the motive origin of the earthly body. [w.w.w.]

**Kuklos Anagkês** (*Gr.*). *Lit.*, "The Unavoidable Cycle" or the "Circle of Necessity." Of the numerous <term>catacombs</term> in <term>Egypt</term> and <term>Chaldea</term>, the most renowned were the subterranean crypts of <term>Thebes</term> and <term>Memphis</term>. The former began on the western side of the <term>Nile</term>, extending toward the <term>Libyan</term> desert, and were known as the *serpents'* (<term>Initiated Adepts</term>) catacombs. It was there that the <term>Sacred Mysteries</term> of the *Kuklos Anagkês* were performed, and the candidates were made acquainted with the inexorable laws traced for every disembodied soul from the beginning of time. These laws were that every reincarnating <term>Entity</term>, casting away its body, should pass from this life on earth into another life on a more subjective plane, a state of bliss, unless the sins of the personality brought on a complete separation of the higher from the lower "principles"; that the "circle of necessity" or the unavoidable cycle should last a given

The Egyptian and Chaldean teachings were those of the “Secret Doctrine” of the Theosophists. The Mexicans held the same beliefs. Their demi-god, <term>Votan</term>, is described in the *Popol Vuh* (see de Bourbourg's work) as mentioning the *ahugero de colubra*, which is identical with the “<term>Serpent's Catacombs</term>” or passage; he adds that it ran underground and “terminated at the root of heaven.” <term>Votan</term> was admitted into this <term>serpent's hole</term> because he was himself “a son of the Serpents,” or a <term>Dragon of Wisdom</term>—meaning an <term>Initiate</term>. Throughout the world, the <term>priest-adepts</term> called themselves “Sons of the Dragon” and “Sons of the Serpent-dog.”

**Kukkuta Padagiri** (Sk.), also called *Gurupadagiri*, the “teacher's mountain.” It is situated about seven miles from Gaya and is famous due to a persistent report that <term>Arhat Mahâkâsyapa</term> dwells in its caves even to this day.

**Kumâra** (Sk.). A virgin boy or young celibate. The first <term>Kumâras</term> are the seven sons of <term>Brahmâ</term>, born from the limbs of the god in the so-called <term>ninth creation</term>. It is stated that the name was given to them because of their formal refusal to “procreate their species,” and so, as the legend says, they “remained <term>Yogis</term>.”

**Kumârâbudhi** (Sk.). A title given to the human “<term>Ego</term>.”

**Kumâra guha** (Sk.). Literally, “the mysterious <term>virgin youth</term>.” A title given to <term>Kârtikeya</term> because of his strange origin.

**Kumbhaka** (Sk.). The retention of breath according to the regulations of the <term>Hatha Yoga</term> system.

**Kumbhakarna** (Sk.). The brother of King <term>Ravana</term> of Lanka, the abductor of <term>Rama</term>'s wife, <term>Sita</term>. As shown in the *Ramayana*, <term>Kumbhakarna</term> slept for six months under a curse from <term>Brahmâ</term>, then remained awake for one day before falling asleep again, and so on for many hundreds of years. He was awakened to take part in the war between <term>Rama</term> and <term>Ravana</term>; he captured <term>Hanuman</term> but was finally killed himself.

**Kundalini Sakti** (Sk.). The power of life; one of the <term>Forces of Nature</term>; the power that generates a specific light in those who practice spiritual and clairvoyant development. It is a power known only to those who practice <term>concentration</term> and <term>Yoga</term>.

**Kuntî** (Sk.). The wife of <term>Pandu</term> and the mother of the <term>Pandavas</term>—the heroes and the enemies of their cousins, the <term>Kauravas</term>, in the *Bhagavad-gita*. It is an allegory of the <term>Spirit-Soul</term> or <term>Buddhi</term>. Some think that <term>Draupadi</term>, the common wife of the five brothers (the <term>Pandavas</term>), is meant to represent <term>Buddhi</term>, but this is not so; <term>Draupadi</term> represents the <term>terrestrial life</term> of the <term>Personality</term>. As such, she is seen as being treated as insignificant, allowed to be insulted, and even taken into slavery by <term>Yudhishthira</term>, the eldest of the <term>Pandavas</term> and her chief husband, who represents the <term>Higher Ego</term> with all its qualifications.

**Kurios** (*Gr.*). The Lord, the Master.

**Kwan-yin** (*Chin.*). The female <term>logos</term>, the “Mother of Mercy.”

**Kwan-yin-tien** (*Chin.*). The heaven where <term>Kwan-yin</term> and the other <term>logoi</term> dwell.

<header>GLOSSARY</header>

## L.
L.—The twelfth letter of the English Alphabet, and also of the Hebrew, where <term>Lamed</term> signifies an ox-goad, the sign of a fold. The letter is an equivalent of the number 30. The Hebrew divine name corresponding to L is <term>Limmud</term>, or *Doctus*.

**Labarum** (*Lat.*). The standard carried before the ancient Roman Emperors, having an eagle upon it as an emblem of sovereignty. It was a long lance with a cross staff at right angles. <term>Constantine</term> replaced the eagle with the Christian monogram and the motto *εν τουτω νικα*, which was later interpreted as *In hoc signo vinces* <note>"In this sign you shall conquer."</note>. As for the monogram, it was a combination of the letter <term>X, Chi</term>, and <term>P, Rho</term>, the initial syllable of <term>Christos</term>. However, the <term>Labarum</term> had been an emblem of <term>Etruria</term> ages before Constantine and the Christian era. It was also the sign of <term>Osiris</term> and of <term>Horus</term>, who is often represented with the long Latin cross, while the Greek pectoral cross is purely Egyptian. In his “Decline and Fall,” <term>Gibbon</term> has exposed the Constantine imposture. The emperor, if he ever had a vision at all, must have seen the <term>Olympian Jupiter</term>, in whose faith he died.

**Labro**. A Roman saint, solemnly beatified a few years ago. His great holiness consisted in sitting at one of the gates of Rome night and day for forty years, and remaining unwashed through that entire time. He was eaten by vermin to the bone.

**Labyrinth** (*Gr.*). Egypt had the “celestial labyrinth” into which the souls of the departed plunged, and also its type on earth, the famous Labyrinth, a subterranean series of halls and passages with the most extraordinary windings. <term>Herodotus</term> describes it as consisting of 3,000 chambers, half below and half above ground. Even in his day, strangers were not allowed into the subterranean portions of it, as they contained the sepulchers of the kings who built it and other mysteries. The “Father of History” found the Labyrinth already almost in ruins, yet regarded it, even in its state of dilapidation, as far more marvelous than the pyramids.

**Lactantius**. A Church Father who declared the heliocentric system a heretical doctrine, and that of the antipodes as a “fallacy invented by the devil.”

**Ladakh**. The upper valley of the <term>Indus</term>, inhabited by <term>Tibetans</term>, but belonging to the <term>Rajah of Kashmir</term>.

**Ladder**. There are many “ladders” in the mystic philosophies and schemes, all of which were, and some still are, used in their respective

The *Brahmanical Ladder* symbolizes the *Seven Worlds* or *Sapta Loka*; the *Kabalistical Ladder* symbolizes the seven lower Sephiroth; *Jacob's Ladder* is spoken of in the Bible; the *Mithraic Ladder* is also known as the "Mysterious Ladder." Then there are the Rosicrucian, the Scandinavian, and the Borsippa Ladders, and so on; and finally the *Theological Ladder* which, according to Brother Kenneth Mackenzie, consists of the four cardinal and three theological virtues.

**Lady of the Sycamore**. A title of the Egyptian goddess Neïth, who is often represented as appearing in a tree and handing from it the fruit of the Tree of Life, as well as the Water of Life, to her worshippers.

**Laena** (Lat.). A robe worn by the Roman Augurs with which they covered their heads while sitting in contemplation on the flight of birds.

**Lahgash** (*Kab.*). Secret speech; esoteric incantation; almost identical to the mystical meaning of Vâch.

**Lajja** (*Sk.*). "Modesty"; a demi-goddess, daughter of Daksha.

**Lakh** (*Sk.*). 100,000 units, whether in currency or anything else.

**Lakshana** (*Sk.*). The thirty-two bodily signs of a Buddha, which are the marks by which he is recognized.

**Lakshmi** (*Sk.*). "Prosperity," fortune; the Indian Venus, born of the churning of the ocean by the gods; the goddess of beauty and wife of Vishnu.

**Lalita Vistara** (*Sk.*). A celebrated biography of Sakya Muni, the Lord Buddha, by Dharmarakcha, A.D. 308.

**Lama** (*Tib.*). Written "Clama." The title, if correctly applied, belongs only to the priests of superior grades—those who can hold office as gurus in the monasteries. Unfortunately, every common member of the *gedun* (clergy) calls himself or allows himself to be called "Lama." A real Lama is an ordained and thrice-ordained Gelong. Since the reform produced by Tsong-ka-pa, many abuses have again crept into the theocracy of the land. There are "Lama-astrologers"—the *Chakhan*, or common *Tsikhan* (from *tsigan*, "gypsy")—and Lama-soothsayers, even some who are allowed to marry and do not belong to the clergy at all. They are very scarce, however, in Eastern Tibet, belonging principally to Western Tibet and to sects which have nothing to do with the *Gelukpas* (yellow caps). Unfortunately, Orientalists, knowing next to nothing of the true state of affairs in Tibet, confuse the Choichong of the Gurmakhayas Lamasery (Lhasa)—the initiated esotericists—with the charlatans and *Dugpas* (sorcerers) of the Bhon sects. No wonder if—as Schagintweit <note>Referring to the orientalist Emil Schlagintweit.</note> says in his *Buddhism in Tibet*—"though the images of King Choichong (the 'god of astrology') are met with in most monasteries of Western Tibet and the Himalayas, my brothers never saw a Lama Choichong." This is only natural. Neither the Choichong nor the *Kubilkhan* (*q.v.*) overrun the country. As to the "God" or "King Choichong," he is no more a "god of astrology" than any other "Planetary" Dhyan Chohan.

<term>**Lamrin**</term> (*Tib.*). A sacred volume of precepts and rules, written by Tson-kha-pa, “for the advancement of knowledge.”

<term>**Land of the Eternal Sun**</term>. Tradition places it beyond the Arctic regions at the North Pole. It is “the land of the gods where the sun never sets.”

<term>**Lang-Shu**</term> (*Chin.*). The title of the translation of Nagarjuna’s work, the *Ekasloka-Shastra*.

<term>**Lanka**</term> (*Sk.*). The ancient name of the island now called Ceylon. It is also the name of a mountain in the Southeast of Ceylon, where, as tradition says, there was a town peopled with demons named Lankapuri. It is described in the epic of the *Ramayana* as being of gigantic size and magnificence, “with seven broad moats and seven stupendous walls of stone and metal.” Its foundation is attributed to Visva-Karma, who built it for Kuvera, the king of the demons, from whom it was taken by Ravana, the abductor of Sita. The *Bhâgavat Purâna* depicts Lanka or Ceylon as originally the summit of Mount Meru, which was broken off by Vayu, the god of the wind, and hurled into the ocean. It has since become the seat of the Southern Buddhist Church and the Siamese Sect (headed at present by the High Priest Sumangala), representing the purest exoteric Buddhism on this side of the Himalayas.

<term>**Lanoo**</term> (*Sk.*). A disciple, the same as a “chela.”

<term>**Lao-tze**</term> (*Chin.*). A great sage, saint, and philosopher who preceded Confucius.

<term>**Lapis philosophorum**</term> (*Lat.*). The “Philosopher’s Stone”; a mystic term in alchemy, having a very different meaning from the one usually attributed to it.

<term>**Lararium**</term> (*Lat.*). A room in the houses of ancient Romans where the *Lares*, or household gods, were kept along with other family relics.

<term>**Lares**</term> (*Lat.*). These were of three kinds: *Lares familiares*, the guardians and invisible overseers of the family circle; *Lares parvi*, small idols used for divination and augury; and *Lares præstites*, which were supposed to maintain order among the others. The Lares are the *manes*, or the ghosts of disembodied people. Apuleius says that the tomb inscription, *To the gods manes who lived*, meant that the Soul had been transformed into a *Lemure*. He adds that though “the human Soul is a demon that our languages may name a genius,” and “is an immortal god, though in a certain sense it is born at the same time as the person in whom it exists, yet we may say that it dies in the same way that it is born.” This means, in simpler language, that *Lares* and *Lemures* are simply the shells cast off by the Ego—the high spiritual and immortal Soul—whose shell and its astral reflection, the animal Soul, die, whereas the higher Soul lasts throughout eternity.

<term>**Larva**</term> (*Lat.*). The animal Soul. *Larvæ* are the shadows of people who have lived and died.

## **Law of Retribution.** (See “Karma”).

## **Laya** or *Layam* (*Sk.*). From the root *Li*, "to dissolve, to disintegrate," it is a point of equilibrium (zero-point) in physics and chemistry. In occultism, it is that point where substance becomes homogeneous and is unable to act or differentiate.

## **Lebanon** (*Heb.*). A range of mountains in Syria, with a few remnants of the gigantic cedar trees, a forest of which once crowned its summit. Tradition says that it is here that the timber for King Solomon’s temple was obtained. (See “Druzes”).

## **Lemuria**. A modern term first used by some naturalists and now adopted by Theosophists to indicate a continent that, according to the *Secret Doctrine* of the East, preceded Atlantis. Its Eastern name would not reveal much to European ears.

## **Leon, Moses de**. The name of a Jewish Rabbi in the 13th century, accused of having composed the *Zohar*, which he presented as the true work of Simeon Ben Jachai. His full name is given in Myer’s *Qabbalah* as Rabbi Moses ben-Shem-Tob de Leon of Spain; the same author proves very cleverly that de Leon was *not* the author of the *Zohar*. Few will say he was, but everyone must suspect Moses de Leon of considerably perverting the original *Book of Splendour* (*Zohar*). This sin, however, may be shared by him with the Medieval “Christian Kabbalists” and by Knorr von Rosenroth especially. Surely, neither Rabbi Simeon (condemned to death by Titus), nor his son Rabbi Eliezer, nor his secretary Rabbi Abba, can be charged with introducing into the *Zohar* purely Christian dogmas and doctrines invented by the Church Fathers several centuries after the death of the former Rabbis. This would be stretching alleged divine prophecy a little too far.

## **Lévi, Eliphas**. The real name of this learned Kabbalist was Abbé Alphonse Louis Constant. Eliphas Lévi Zahed was the author of several works on philosophical magic. A member of the *Fratres Lucis* (Brothers of Light), he was also once a priest—an abbé of the Roman Catholic Church—which promptly proceeded to unfrock him when he acquired fame as a Kabbalist. He died about twenty years ago, leaving five famous works: *Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie* (1856), *Histoire de la Magie* (1860), *La Clef des grands Mystères* (1861), *Legendes et Symboles* (1862), and *La Science des Esprits* (1865), besides some other works of minor importance. His style is extremely light and fascinating, but with a characteristic of mockery and paradox that is a bit too strong to be the ideal for a serious Kabbalist.

## **Leviathan**. In biblical esotericism, Deity in its double manifestation of good and evil. The meaning may be found in the *Zohar* (II. 34b). “Rabbi Shimeon said: The companions (candidates) study and understand the work of the beginning (or ‘creation’); but the *little ones* (the full or perfect Initiates) are those who understand the allusion to the

**Levânah** (*Hebrew*). The moon, as a planet and an astrological influence.

**Lha** (*Tibetan*). Spirits of the highest spheres, from which comes the name of Lhasa, the residence of the Dalai Lama. The title of Lha is often given in Tibet to certain *Narjôls* (Saints and Yogi adepts) who have attained great occult powers.

**Lhagpa** (*Tibetan*). Mercury, the planet.

**Lhakang** (*Tibetan*). A temple; a crypt, especially a subterranean temple for mystic ceremonies.

**Lhamayin** (*Tibetan*). Elemental spirits of the lower terrestrial plane. Popular imagination turns them into demons and devils.

**Lif** (*Scandinavian*). Lif and Lifthresir, the only two human beings who were allowed to be present at the “Renewal of the World.” Being “pure and innocent and free from sinful desires, they are permitted to enter the world where peace now reigns.” The *Edda* shows them hidden in Hoddmimir’s forest dreaming the dreams of childhood while the last conflict was taking place. These two creatures, and the allegory in which they take part, are allusions to the few nations of the Fourth Root Race, who, surviving the great submersion of their continent and the majority of their Race, passed into the Fifth and continued their ethnic evolution in our present Human Race.

**Light, Brothers of.** This is what the great authority on secret societies, Brother Kenneth R. H. Mackenzie IX., says of this Brotherhood: “A mystic order, *Fratres Lucis*, established in Florence in 1498. Among the members of this order were Pasqualis, Cagliostro, Swedenborg, St. Martin, Eliphaz Lévi, and many other eminent mystics. Its members were very much persecuted by the Inquisition. It is a small but compact body, the members being spread all over the world.”

**Lila** (*Sanskrit*). Literally sport, or pastime. In the orthodox Hindu Scriptures it is explained that “the acts of the divinity are *lila*,” or sport.

**Lilith** (*Hebrew*). According to Jewish tradition, a demon who was the first wife of Adam, before Eve was created: she is supposed to have a fatal influence on mothers and newborn infants. LIL means night, and LILITH is also the owl: and in medieval works she is a synonym of Lamia or a female demon. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**Lil-in** (*Hebrew*). The children of Lilith, and their descendants. “Lilith is the Mother of the *Shedim* and the *Muquishim* (the ensnarers).” Every class of the Lil-in, therefore, are devils in the demonology of the Jews. (See *Zohar* ii. 268a).

**Limbus Major** (*Latin*). A term used by Paracelsus to denote primordial (alchemical) matter; “Adam’s earth.”

# THEOSOPHICAL

**Linga** or *Lingam* (*Sk.*). A sign or a symbol of abstract creation. Force becomes the organ of procreation only on this earth. In India, there are 12 great *Lingams* of Siva, some of which are on mountains and rocks, and also in temples. One such is the *Kedâresa* in the Himalayas, a huge and shapeless mass of rock. In its origin, the *Lingam* never had the gross meaning connected with the phallus, an idea that is entirely of a later date. The symbol in India has the same meaning it had in Egypt, which is simply that the creative or procreative Force is divine. It also denotes the dual Creator—male and female, Siva and his *Sakti*. The gross and immodest idea connected with the phallus is not Indian, but Greek and pre-eminently Jewish. The Biblical *Bethels* were real priapic stones, the “Beth-el” (phallus) in which God dwells. The same symbol was concealed within the Ark of the Covenant, the “Holy of Holies.” Therefore, the “*Lingam*,” even as a phallus, is not a “symbol of Siva” only, but that of every “Creator” or creative god in every nation, including the Israelites and their “God of Abraham and Jacob.”

**Linga Purâna** (*Sk.*). A scripture of the Saivas, or worshippers of Siva. In it, *Maheswara*, “the great Lord,” concealed in the *Agni Linga*, explains the ethics of life—duty, virtue, self-sacrifice, and finally liberation by and through an ascetic life at the end of the *Agni Kalpa* (the Seventh Round). As Professor Wilson justly observed, “the spirit of the worship (phallic) is as little influenced by the character of the type as can well be imagined. There is nothing like the phallic orgies of antiquity; it is all mystical and spiritual.”

**Linga Sharîra** (*Sk.*). The “body,” that is, the aerial symbol of the body. This term designates the *doppelganger* or the “astral body” of man or animal. It is the *eidolon* of the Greeks, the vital and prototypal body, and the reflection of the men of flesh. It is born before the physical body and dies or fades out with the disappearance of the last atom of the body.

**Lipi** (*Sk.*). To write. See “*Lipikas*” in Volume I of the *Secret Doctrine*.

**Lipikas** (*Sk.*). The celestial recorders, the “Scribes,” those who record every word and deed said or done by man while on this earth. As Occultism teaches, they are the agents of Karma—the retributive Law.

**Lobha** (*Sk.*). Covetousness; cupidity, a son born from Brahmâ in an evil hour.

**Lodur** (*Scand.*). The second personage in the trinity of gods in the *Edda* of the Norsemen, and the father of the twelve great gods. It is Lodur who endows the first man—made from the ash tree (*Ask*)—with blood and color.

**Logi** (*Scand.*). Literally, “flame.” This giant, along with his sons and relatives, finally made themselves known as the authors of every cataclysm and conflagration in heaven or on earth by letting mortals perceive them.

*   **<term>Logia</term>** (*Gr.*). The secret discourses and teachings of Jesus contained in the Gospel of Matthew—in the original Hebrew, not the spurious Greek text we have—and preserved by the Ebionites and the Nazarenes in the library collected by Pamphiluis at Caesarea. This “Gospel,” called by many writers “the genuine Gospel of Matthew,” was used, according to (St.) Jerome, by the Nazarenes and Ebionites of Beroea, Syria, in his own day (4th century). Like the <term>Apokrheta</term>, or secret discourses of the Mysteries, these *Logia* could only be understood with a key. Sent by the Bishops Chromatius and Heliodorus, Jerome, after having obtained permission, translated them but found it “a difficult task” (truly so!) to reconcile the text of the “genuine” with that of the spurious Greek gospel he was familiar with. *   **<term>Logos</term>** (*Gr.*). The manifested deity in every nation and people; the outward expression, or the effect of the cause which is ever concealed. Thus, speech is the *Logos* of thought; hence it is aptly translated as the “*Verbum*” and “*Word*” in its metaphysical sense.
*   **<term>Lohitanga</term>** (*Sk.*). The planet Mars.
*   **<term>Loka</term>** (*Sk.*). A region or defined place. In metaphysics, a world, sphere, or plane. The *Puranas* of India speak incessantly of seven and fourteen *Lokas*—above and below our earth, representing heavens and hells.

*   **<term>Loka Palas</term>** (*Sk.*). The supporters, rulers, and guardians of the world. The deities (planetary gods) who preside over the eight cardinal points, among which are the *Tchatur* (Four) *Maharajahs*.
*   **<term>Loki</term>** (*Scand.*). The Scandinavian Evil Spirit from an exoteric perspective. In esoteric philosophy, he is “an opposing power” only because he differentiates himself from primordial harmony. In the *Edda*, he is the father of the terrible *Fenris Wolf* and of the *Midgard Snake*. By blood, he is the brother of Odin, the good and valiant god; but in nature, he is his opposite. Loki and Odin are simply two in one. As Odin is, in one sense, vital heat, so Loki is the symbol of the passions produced by the intensity of that heat.
*   **<term>Loreley</term>**. The German version of the Scandinavian “Lake Maiden.” <term>Undine</term> is one of the names given to these maidens, who are known in exoteric Magic and Occultism as the Water-Elementals.
*   **<term>Lost Word</term>** (*Masonic*). This should be understood as “lost words” and lost secrets in general, for what is termed the lost “Word” is no word at all, as is the case with the Ineffable Name (*q.v.*). **Lotus** (*Gr.*). A highly occult plant, sacred in Egypt, India, and elsewhere; called "the child of the Universe bearing the likeness of its mother in its heart." There was a time "when the world was a golden lotus" (*padma*), according to the allegory. A great variety of these plants—from the majestic Indian lotus down to the marsh-lotus (bird's foot trefoil) and the Greek "Dioscoridis"—is eaten in Crete and other islands. It is a species of *nymphæa*, first introduced from India to Egypt, where it was not native. See the text of *Archaic Symbolism* in Appendix VIII: "The Lotus as a Universal Symbol."

**Lotus, Lord of the.** A title applied to various creative gods, as well as to the Lords of the Universe, of which this plant is the symbol. (See "Lotus").

**Love Feasts, Agapæ** (*Gr.*). These charitable banquets held by the earliest Christians were established in Rome by Clement during the reign of Domitian. Professor A. Kestner’s *The Agapæ or the Secret World Society (Weltbund) of the Primitive Christians* (published 1819 at Jena) describes these Love Feasts as "having a hierarchical structure and a foundation of Masonic symbolism and Mysteries"; it shows a direct connection between the ancient Agapæ and the Table Lodges or Banquets of the Freemasons. However, having excluded the "holy kiss" and women from their suppers, the banquets of the latter are more like "drinking" than "love" feasts. The early Agapæ were certainly the same as the *Phallica*, which "were once as pure as the Love Feasts of early Christians," as Mr. Bonwick very rightly remarks, "though like them, they rapidly degenerated into licentiousness." (*Egyptian Belief and Modern Thought*, p. 260).

**Lower Face** or *Lower Countenance* (*Kab.*). A term applied to Microprosopus, just as "Higher Face" is applied to Macroprosopus. These two are identical to the *Long Face* and *Short Face*.

**Lubara** (*Chald.*). The god of Pestilence and Disease.

**Lucifer** (*Lat.*). The planet Venus, as the bright "Morning Star." Before Milton, Lucifer had never been a name for the Devil. Quite the opposite, since the Christian Savior is made to say of himself in *Revelation* (xvi. 22), "I am . . . the bright morning star" or Lucifer. One of the early Popes of Rome bore that name; and there was even a Christian sect in the fourth century called the *Luciferians*.

# GLOSSARY

In a moment of need, he made several million gold "rose nobles" for King Edward III of England, and thus helped him to carry on war victoriously. He founded several colleges for the study of Oriental languages, and Cardinal Ximenes was one of his patrons and held him in great esteem, as did Pope John XXI. He died in 1314 at a good old age. Literature has preserved many wild stories about Raymond Lully, which would form a most extraordinary romance. He was the elder son of the Seneschal of Majorca and inherited great wealth from his father.

**Lunar Gods.** Called in India the Fathers, "Pitris," or the lunar ancestors. They are subdivided, like the rest, into seven classes or hierarchies. In Egypt, although the moon received less worship than in Chaldea or India, Isis still stands as the representative of Luna-Lunus, "the celestial Hermaphrodite." Strangely enough, while modern people connect the moon only with lunacy and generation, the ancient nations, who knew better, individually and collectively connected their "wisdom gods" with it. Thus, in Egypt, the lunar gods are Thoth-Hermes and Chons; in India, it is Budha, the son of *Soma* (the moon); in Chaldea, Nebo is the lunar god of Secret Wisdom, and so on. The wife of Thoth, *Sifix*, the lunar goddess, holds a pole with fire rays or the five-pointed star—the symbol of man, the *Microcosm*, in distinction from the Septenary Macrocosm. As in all theogonies a goddess precedes a god (most likely on the principle that the chick can hardly precede its egg), in Chaldea the moon was held as older and more venerable than the sun because, as they said, darkness precedes light at every periodical rebirth (or "creation") of the universe. Although Osiris is connected with the sun and is a solar god, he is nevertheless born on Mount *Sinai*, because *Sin* is the Chaldeo-Assyrian word for the moon; so was Dionysos, god of Nyssi or *Nisi*, which latter appellation was that of Sinai in Egypt, where it was called Mount *Nissa*. The crescent is not—as proven by many writers—an emblem of the Turks, but was adopted by Christians as their symbol before the Muslims. For ages, the crescent was the emblem of the Chaldean Astarte, the Egyptian Isis, and the Greek Diana—all of them Queens of Heaven—and finally became the emblem of Mary the Virgin. "The Greek Christian Empire of Constantinople held it as their palladium. Upon the conquest by the Turks, the Sultan adopted it . . . and since then, the crescent has been made to oppose the idea of the cross" (*Egyptian Belief*).

**Lupercalia** (*Lat.*). Magnificent popular festivals celebrated in ancient Rome on February 15th in honor of the god Pan. During these, the *Luperci* (the most ancient and respectable among the priestly officials) sacrificed two goats and a dog, and two of the most illustrious youths were compelled to run about the city naked (except for their loins), whipping all those whom they met. Pope Gelasius abolished the Lupercalia in 496, but substituted for them on the same day the procession of lighted candles.

### Luxor (Occ.).
A compound word from *lux* (light) and *aur* (fire), thus meaning the “Light of (divine) Fire.”

### Luxor, Brotherhood of.
A certain Brotherhood of mystics. It would have been much better if its name had never been divulged, as it led to a great number of well-meaning people being deceived and robbed of their money by a certain bogus Mystic Society of speculators, which started in Europe only to be exposed and flee to America. The name is derived from the ancient *Lookshur* in Balochistan, lying between Bela and Kedjee. The order is very ancient and the most secret of all. It is unnecessary to repeat that its members disclaim all connection with the “H.B. of L.” and the *tutti quanti* <note>Italian for "all the rest" or "the whole lot"</note> of commercial mystics, whether from Glasgow or Boston.

### Lycanthropy (Gr.).
Physiologically, a disease or mania during which a person imagines he is a wolf and acts as such. Occultly, it means the same as “werewolf”: the psychological faculty of certain sorcerers to *appear* as wolves. Voltaire states that in the district of Jura, in the two years between 1598 and 1600, more than 600 lycanthropes were put to death by an overly zealous Christian judge. This does not mean that shepherds accused of sorcery, and seen as wolves, actually had the power of physically changing themselves into such; but simply that they had the hypnotizing power of making people (or those they regarded as enemies) believe they saw a wolf when there was, in fact, none. The exercise of such power is truly sorcery. “Demoniacal” possession is *true* at its core, *without* the devils of Christian theology. However, this is no place for a long discussion upon occult mysteries and magic powers.

## M.

M.—The thirteenth letter of the Hebrew and the English alphabets, and the twenty-fourth of the Arabic. As a Roman numeral, this letter stands for 1,000, and with a bar over it (M̄), it signifies one million. In the Hebrew alphabet, *Mem* symbolized water and, as a numeral, is equivalent to 40. The Sanskrit *ma* is equivalent to the number 5 and is also connected with water through the sign of the Zodiac called Makâra (see entry). Moreover, in the Hebrew and Latin numerals, the *m* stands “as the definite numeral for an indeterminate number” (Mackenzie’s *Masonic Cyclopaedia*), and “the Hebrew sacred name of God applied to this letter is *Meborach, Benedictus*.” According to Esotericists, *M* is the symbol of the Higher Ego—*Manas*, the *Mind*.

**Mâ** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, “five.” A name of Lakshmi.

**Ma, Mut** (*Egyptian*). The goddess of the lower world, another form of Isis, as she represents nature, the eternal mother. She was the sovereign and ruler of the North Wind, the precursor of the Nile’s flooding, and was thus called “the opener of the nostrils of the living.” She is represented as offering the *ankh*, or cross—the emblem of physical life—to her worshippers, and is called the “Lady of Heaven.”

**Machagistia**. Magic, as it was once taught in Persia and Chaldea, and elevated in its occult practices into a religious magianism. Plato, speaking of Machagistia or Magianism, remarks that it is the purest form of the worship of divine things.

**Macrocosm** (*Greek*). Literally the “Great Universe,” or Cosmos.

**Macroprosopus** (*Greek*). A Kabbalistic term made of a compound Greek word meaning the Vast or Great Countenance (See “Kabbalistic Faces”); a title of Kether, the Crown, the highest Sephira. It is the name of the Universe, called *Arikh-Anpin*, the totality of which Microprosopus or *Zauir-Anpin*, “the lesser countenance,” is the component part and antithesis. In its highest or abstract metaphysical sense, Microprosopus is Adam Kadmon, the vehicle of *Ain-Suph* and the crown of the Sephirothal Tree; though since Sephira and Adam Kadmon are in fact one under two aspects, it amounts to the same thing. Interpretations are many, and they differ.

**Madhasadana** or *Madhu-Sûdana* (*Sanskrit*). “Slayer of Madhu” (a demon), a title of Krishna given because he killed that demon.

**Mâdhava** (*Sanskrit*). (1) A name of Vishnu or Krishna; (2) The month of April; (3) A title of Lakshmi when written as *Mâdhavi*.

**Madhya** (*Sanskrit*). Ten thousand billions.

THEOSOPHICAL

**Madhyama** (_Sk._). Used to describe something without beginning or end. Thus *Vâch* (Sound, the female *Logos*, or the female counterpart of *Brahmâ*) is said to exist in several states, one of which is *Mâdhyama*. This is equivalent to saying that *Vâch* is *eternal* in one sense: “the Word (*Vâch*) was with God, and *in* God,” for the two are one.

**Mâdhyamikas** (_Sk._). A sect mentioned in the *Vishnu Purâna*. According to Orientalists, it is a “Buddhist” sect, which is an anachronism. It was probably at first a sect of Hindu atheists. A later school of that name, teaching a system of sophistic nihilism—which reduces every proposition into a thesis and its antithesis and then denies both—was started in Tibet and China. It adopts a few principles of *Nâgârjuna*, who was one of the founders of the esoteric Mahâyâna systems, not their *exoteric* travesties. The allegory that regarded *Nâgârjuna’s* “*Paramârtha*” as a gift from the *Nâgas* (Serpents) shows that he received his teachings from the secret school of adepts, and that the real tenets are therefore kept secret.

**Maga** (_Sk._). The priests of the Sun, mentioned in the *Vishnu Purâna*. They are the later *Magi* of Chaldea and Iran, the ancestors of the modern Parsis.

**Magadha** (_Sk._). An ancient country in India, under Buddhist Kings.

**Mage**, or **Magian**. From *Mag* or *Maha*. The word is the root of the word magician. *Maha-âtma* (the great Soul or Spirit) in India had its priests in pre-Vedic times. The Magians were priests of the fire-god; we find them among the Assyrians and Babylonians, as well as among the Persian fire-worshippers. The three *Magi*, also called kings, who are said to have given gifts of gold, incense, and myrrh to the infant Jesus, were fire-worshippers like the rest, and astrologers; for they saw his star. The high priest of the Parsis, at Surat, is called *Mobêd*. Others derive the name from *Megh*; *Meh-ab* signifying something grand and noble. *Zoroaster’s* disciples were called *Meghêstom*, according to Kleuker.

**Magi** (_Lat._). The name of the ancient hereditary priests and learned adepts in Persia and Media, a word derived from *Mâha* (great), which later became *mog* or *mag*, a priest in Pehlevi. Porphyry describes them (*Abst. iv. 16*) as: “The learned men who are engaged among the Persians in the service of the Deity are called *Magi*,” and Suidas informs us that “among the Persians the lovers of wisdom (*philalethai*) are called *Magi*.” The *Zendavesta* (ii. 171, 261) divides them into three degrees: (1) The *Herbeds* or “Novitiates”; (2) *Mobeds* or “Masters”; (3) *Destur Mobeds*, or “Perfect Masters.” The Chaldeans had similar colleges, as did the Egyptians. *Destur Mobeds* were identical with the Hierophants of the mysteries, as practiced in Greece and Egypt.

They applied both celestial and earthly natures for occult purposes, by means of which, through a certain likeness, they drew divine virtues down into this lower realm.”

**Magic, White**, or “Beneficent Magic,” as it is called, is *divine magic*, devoid of selfishness, love of power, ambition, or greed, and focused only on doing good for the world in general and one’s neighbor in particular. The smallest attempt to use one’s abnormal powers for self-gratification turns these powers into sorcery or black magic.

**Magic, Black**. (See above.)

**Magician**. This term, once a title of renown and distinction, has become completely perverted from its true meaning. Once the synonym of everything honorable and reverent—of a person possessing learning and wisdom—it has been degraded into an epithet used to designate someone who is a pretender and a juggler; in short, a charlatan, or someone who has “sold his soul to the Evil One,” who misuses his knowledge and employs it for low and dangerous purposes, according to the teachings of the clergy and a mass of superstitious fools who believe the magician to be a sorcerer and an “Enchanter.” The word is derived from *Magh* or *Mah*; in Sanskrit, *Mâha* means “great”; it refers to a man well-versed in esoteric knowledge. (*Isis Unveiled*).

**Magna Mater** (*Latin*). “Great Mother.” A title given in ancient times to all the chief goddesses of the nations, such as Diana of Ephesus, Isis, Mauth, and many others.

**Magnes**. An expression used by Paracelsus and the medieval Theosophists. It is the spirit of light, or *Akâsa*. This word was much used by the medieval Alchemists.

**Magnetic Masonry**. Also called “*Iatric*” masonry. It is described as a Brotherhood of Healers (from *iatrikê*, a Greek word meaning “the art of healing”) and is frequently mentioned by the “Brothers of Light,” as Kenneth Mackenzie states in the *Royal Masonic Cyclopedia*. There appears to be a tradition in some secret Masonic works—according to Ragon, at least, the great Masonic authority—that there was a Masonic degree called the Oracle of Cos, established in the eighteenth century B.C. because Cos was the birthplace of Hippocrates. The *iatrikê* was a distinct characteristic of the priests who took charge of the patients in the ancient *Asclepia*—the temples where the god Asclepios (Aesculapius) was said to heal the sick and the lame.

**Magnetism.** A force in nature and in man. When it is the former, it is an agent that gives rise to various phenomena of attraction, polarity, etc. When the latter, it becomes “animal” magnetism, in contrast to cosmic and terrestrial magnetism.

Animal magnetism is a *fluid*, an emanation. Some people can emit it for curative purposes through their eyes and the tips of their fingers, while all other creatures—mankind, animals, and even every inanimate object—emanate it either as an *aura* or a varying light, whether consciously or not. When acted upon by contact with a patient or by the will of a human operator, it is called “Mesmerism” (*see entry*).

**Magus** (*Lat.*). In the New Testament, it means a Sage, a wise man of the Chaldeans; in English, it is often used for a Magician or any wonder-worker. In the Rosicrucian Society, it is the title of the highest members, the IXth grade; the Supreme Magus is the Head of the Order in the “Outer”; the Magi of the “Inner” are unknown except to those of the VIIIth grade. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Mahâ Chohan** (*Sk.*). The chief of a spiritual hierarchy, or of a school of Occultism; the head of the trans-Himalayan mystics.
**Mahâ Deva** (*Sk.*). Literally, “great god”; a title of Siva.

**Mahâjwala** (*Sk.*). A certain hell.

**Mahâ Kalpa** (*Sk.*). The “great age.”
**Mahâ Manvantara** (*Sk.*). Literally, the great interludes between the “Manus.” The period of universal activity. “Manvantara” implies here simply a period of activity, as opposed to Pralaya, or rest—without reference to the length of the cycle.

Literally, the “great war”; the celebrated epic poem of India (probably the longest poem in the world) which includes both the *Ramayana* and the *Bhagavad Gîtâ*, “the Song Celestial.” No two Orientalists <note>Scholars who study the languages, literatures, and cultures of the Orient.</note> agree on its date. Exoteric or popular teaching, which makes slight variations on the esoteric doctrine, states that Sakyamuni (Gautama Buddha) visited him in Tushita (a celestial abode) and commissioned him to go to earth as his successor five thousand years after his (Buddha’s) death. This would be in less than 3,000 years from now. Esoteric philosophy teaches that the next Buddha will appear during the seventh (sub) race of this Round. The fact is that Maitreya was a follower of Buddha, a well-known Arhat, though not his direct disciple, and he was the founder of an esoteric philosophical school. As shown by Eitel (*Sanskrit-Chinese Dict.*), “statues were erected in his honor as early as 350 B.C.”

**Makâra** (*Sk.*). “The Crocodile.” In Europe, the same as Capricorn; the tenth sign of the Zodiac. Esoterically, it refers to a mystic class of devas. To the Hindus, it is the vehicle of Varuna, the water-god.

**Mantra Period** (*Sk.*). One of the four periods into which Vedic literature has been divided.

**Maquom** (*Chald.*). “A secret place” in the terminology of the *Zohar*; a concealed spot, whether referring to a sacred shrine in a temple, to the “Womb of the World,” or the human womb. A Kabbalistic term.

An ancient <term>Gnostic Sect</term> founded by <term>Marcion</term>, who was a devout <term>Christian</term> as long as no <term>dogma</term> of <term>human creation</term> came to mar the purely <term>transcendental</term> and <term>metaphysical concepts</term> and the *original beliefs* of the <term>early Christians</term>. Such <term>primitive beliefs</term> were those of <term>Marcion</term>. He denied the *historical facts* (as now found in the <term>Gospels</term>) of <term>Christ’s birth</term>, <term>incarnation</term>, and <term>passion</term>, and also the <term>resurrection</term> of the <term>body</term> of <term>Jesus</term>. He maintained that such statements were simply the <term>carnalization</term> of <term>metaphysical allegories</term> and <term>symbolism</term>, and a <term>degradation</term> of the true <term>spiritual idea</term>. Along with all the other <term>Gnostics</term>, <term>Marcion</term> accused the “<term>Church Fathers</term>”—as <term>Irenæus</term> himself complains—of “framing their (<term>Christian</term>) <term>doctrine</term> according to the capacity of their <term>hearers</term>, inventing blind fables for the blind, according to their blindness; for the dull, according to their dullness; and for those in error, according to their errors.”

**Mârga** (*Sk.*). The “<term>Path</term>.” The <term>Ashthânga m\^arga</term>, the “<term>holy</term>” or <term>sacred path</term>, is the one that leads to <term>Nirvâna</term>. The <term>eight-fold path</term> has grown out of the <term>seven-fold path</term> by the addition of the (now) first of the eight <term>Mârga</term>—that is, “<term>the possession of orthodox views</term>”—with which a real *Yogâchârya* would have nothing to do.

**Mârîchi** (*Sk.*). One of the “<term>mind-born</term>” sons of <term>Brahmâ</term> in the *Purânas*. <term>Brahmans</term> consider him to be the <term>personified light</term>, the <term>parent</term> of <term>Sûrya</term> (the <term>Sun</term>), and the direct <term>ancestor</term> of <term>Mahâkâsyapa</term>. The <term>Northern Buddhists</term> of the *Yogachârya School* see in <term>Mârîchi Deva</term> a *Bodhisattva*, while <term>Chinese Buddhists</term> (especially the <term>Fausta</term>) have made of this conception the <term>Queen of Heaven</term>, the <term>goddess of light</term>, and the <term>ruler of the sun and moon</term>. For pious but illiterate <term>Buddhists</term>, her magic <term>formula</term> “*Om Mârîchi svâha*” is very powerful. Speaking of <term>Mârîchi</term>, <term>Eitel</term> mentions “<term>Georgi</term>, who explains the name as a ‘<term>Chinese transcription</term>’ of the name of the <term>holy Virgin Mary</term>” (!!). As <term>Mârîchi</term> is the <term>chief of the Maruts</term> and one of the <term>seven primitive Rishis</term>, this supposed <term>derivation</term> does seem a little far-fetched.

**Mârishâ** (*Sk.*). The daughter of the <term>Sage Kanda</term> and <term>Pramlochâ</term>, the *Apsara-demon* from <term>Indra’s heaven</term>. She was the mother of <term>Daksha</term>.

An allegory referring to the Mystery of the Second and Third human Races.

**<term>Martinists</term>.** A Society in France, founded by a great mystic named the Marquis de St. Martin, a disciple of Martinez Pasqualis. It was first established at Lyons as a kind of occult Masonic Society; its members believed in the possibility of communicating with Planetary Spirits and minor Gods and genii of the ultramundane Spheres. Louis Claude de St. Martin, born in 1743, began his life as a brilliant officer in the army, but he left it to devote himself to study and literature (*belles-lettres*), ending his career by becoming an ardent Theosophist and a disciple of Jacob Boehmen. He tried to return Masonry to its primeval character of Occultism and Theurgy, but he failed. He initially designed his “Rectified Rite” to consist of ten degrees, but these were reduced to seven due to the study of the original Masonic orders. Masons complain that he introduced certain ideas and adopted rites “at variance with the archaeological history of Masonry”; however, so did Cagliostro and St. Germain before him, as did all those who knew the origins of Freemasonry well.

**<term>Mârttanda</term>** (*Sk.*). The Vedic name of the Sun.

**<term>Mârut Jivas</term>** (*Sk.*). The monads of Adepts who have attained final liberation but prefer to reincarnate on earth for the sake of Humanity. They should not be confused, however, with the *Nirmânakâyas*, who are far higher.

**<term>Mâruṭs</term>** (*Sk.*). To Orientalists, these are Storm-Gods, but in the *Veda*, they are something very mystical. In the esoteric teachings, as they incarnate in every round, they are simply identical to some of the Agnishwatta Pitris, the Human Intelligent Egos. Hence, the allegory of Siva transforming *lumps of flesh into boys* and calling them Maruts shows senseless men being transformed by becoming the Vehicles of the Pitris or Fire Maruts, and thus becoming rational beings.

**<term>Masben</term> .'.** (*Chald.*). A Masonic term meaning “the Sun in putrefaction.” It has a direct reference—perhaps forgotten by the Masons—to their “Word at Low Breath.”

**<term>Mash-Mak</term>.** By tradition, an Atlantean word of the fourth Race used to denote a mysterious Cosmic fire, or rather Force, which was said to be able to pulverize entire cities in a second and disintegrate the world.

**<term>Masorah</term>** (*Heb.*). The name is especially applied to a collection of explanatory, grammatical, and critical notes found on the margins of ancient Hebrew manuscripts or scrolls of the Old Testament. The Masoretes were also called Melchites.

**<term>Masoretic Points</term>**, or *Vowels* (*Heb.*). Or, as the system is now called, *Masôra* from *Massoreh* or *Massoreth* (“tradition”) and *Māsâr* (“to hand down”). ### Mastaba (*Eg.*). The upper portion of an Egyptian tomb which, according to Egyptologists, always consisted of three parts: namely (1) the <term>Mastaba</term> or memorial chapel above ground; (2) a Pit from twenty to ninety feet in depth, which led by a passage to (3) the *Burial Chamber*, where the <term>Sarcophagus</term> stood, containing the mummy sleeping its sleep of long ages. Once the mummy was interred, the pit was filled up and the entrance to it was concealed. So say the Orientalists, who divide the last resting place of the mummy based on almost the same principles as theologians divide man—into body, soul, and spirit or mind. The fact is that these tombs of the ancients were symbolical, like the rest of their sacred buildings, and this symbolism points directly to the septenary division of man. But in death, the order is reversed; and while the <term>Mastaba</term>—with its scenes of daily life painted on the walls and its *table of offerings* to the <term>Larva</term>, the *ghost*, or "Linga Sarira"—was a memorial raised to the two Principles and Life which had left what was a lower trio on earth, the Pit, the Passage, the Burial Chambers, and the mummy in the <term>Sarcophagus</term> were the objective symbols raised to the two perishable "principles" (the personal mind and <term>Kama</term>) and the three imperishable ones (the higher Triad, now merged into one). This "One" was the Spirit of the Blessed now resting in the Happy Circle of <term>Aanroo</term>.

### Matari Svan (*Sk.*). An aerial being shown in the *Rig-Veda* bringing down <term>agni</term> (fire) to the <term>Bhrigus</term>, who are called "The Consumers" and are described by Orientalists as "a class of mythical beings who belonged to the middle or aerial class of gods." In Occultism, the <term>Bhrigus</term> are simply the "Salamanders" of the Rosicrucians and Kabbalists.

### Materializations. In Spiritualism, the word signifies the objective appearance of the so-called "Spirits" of the dead, who occasionally reclothe themselves in matter; that is, they form a temporary body for themselves out of the materials at hand, which are found in the atmosphere and the emanations of those present. This body bears the human likeness of the deceased as they appeared when alive. Theosophists accept the phenomenon of "materialization," but they reject the theory that it is produced by "Spirits"—that is, the immortal principles of disembodied persons. Theosophists hold that when the phenomenon is genuine—and it is a fact of rarer occurrence than is generally believed—it is produced by the <term>larvæ</term>, the <term>eidola</term>, or <term>Kamalokic</term> "ghosts" of the dead personalities. (See "<term>Kāmadhâtu</term>", "<term>Kāmaloka</term>" and "<term>Kāmarupa</term>"). As <term>Kāmaloka</term> is on the earth plane and differs from it in its degree of materiality only in the

The occasional appearance of such shells is as natural as that of electric balls and other atmospheric phenomena. Electricity as a fluid, or atomic matter (for Theosophists agree with Maxwell that it *is* atomic), though invisible, is always present in the air and manifests under various shapes, but only when certain conditions exist to “materialize” the fluid—when it passes from its own plane onto ours and becomes objective. It is the same with the *eidola* of the dead. They are present around us, but being on another plane, they do not see us any more than we see them. But whenever the strong desires of living men and the conditions provided by the abnormal constitutions of mediums are combined, these *eidola* are drawn—indeed, pulled down—from their plane onto ours and made objective. This is *necromancy*; it does no good for the dead and great harm to the living, in addition to the fact that it interferes with a law of nature. The occasional materialization of the “astral bodies” or doubles of living persons is quite another matter. These “astrals” are often mistaken for the apparitions of the dead since, like a chameleon, our own “Elementaries,” along with those of the disembodied and cosmic Elementals, will often assume the appearance of those images which are strongest in our thoughts. In short, at so-called “materialization” séances, it is those present and the medium who create the peculiar likeness of the apparitions. Independent “apparitions” belong to another kind of psychic phenomena. Materializations are also called “form-manifestations” and “portrait statues.” To call them materialized spirits is inadmissible, for they are not spirits but, indeed, animated portrait-statues.

**Matsya** (*Sk.*). “A fish.” *Matsya avatar* was one of the earliest incarnations of Vishnu.

**Matsya Purâna** (*Sk.*). The Scripture or Purâna which treats of that incarnation.

**Mâyâ Moha** (*Sanskrit*). An illusive form assumed by Vishnu in order to deceive ascetic Daityas who were becoming too holy through austerities and therefore too dangerous in power, as stated in the *Vishnu Purâna*.

**Mâyâvi Rûpa** (*Sanskrit*). “Illusive form”; the “double” in esoteric philosophy; *doppelganger* or *perisprit* in German and French.

**Mayavic Upadhi** (*Sanskrit*). The covering of illusion, phenomenal appearance.

**Mazdeans**. From (Ahura) Mazda. (See Spiegel’s *Yasna*, xl). They were the ancient Persian nobles who worshiped Ormazd and, by rejecting images, inspired the Jews with the same horror for every concrete representation of the Deity. **Mazdiasnian**. Zoroastrian; literally, “worshiping God.”

**M’bul** (*Hebrew*). The “waters of the flood.” Esoterically, the periodical outpourings of astral impurities upon the earth; periods of psychic crimes and iniquities, or of regular moral cataclysms.

**Medinî** (*Sanskrit*). The earth; so-called from the marrow (*medas*) of two demons. These monsters, springing from the ear of the sleeping Vishnu, were preparing to kill Brahmâ, who was lying on the lotus that grows from Vishnu’s navel, when the god of Preservation awoke and killed them. Their bodies, being thrown into the sea, produced such a quantity of fat and marrow that Nârâyana used it to form the earth.

**Megacosm** (*Greek*). The world of the Astral light; or, as explained by a puzzled Mason, “a great world, not identical with the Macrocosm (the Universe), but something between it and the Microcosm (the little world)” or man.

**Mehen** (*Egyptian*). In popular myths, the great serpent which represents the lower atmosphere. In Occultism, the world of the *Astral light*, symbolically called the *Cosmic Dragon* and the *Serpent*. (See the works of Eliphaz Lévi, who called this light *le Serpent du Mal* and other names, attributing to it all the evil influences on the earth).

**Melekh** (*Hebrew*). Literally, “a King.” A title of the Sephira *Tiphereth*, the *V*, or *vau* in the tetragrammaton—the son or *Microprosopus* (the Lesser Face).

**Melhas** (*Sanskrit*). A class of fire-gods or Salamanders.

**Memrab** (*Hebrew*). In the Kabala, “the voice of the will”; that is, the collective forces of nature in activity, called the “Word” or *Logos* by the Jewish Kabbalists.

### Mendaeans (Gr.).
Also called *Sabians* and St. John Christians. The latter name is absurd since, according to all accounts and even their own, they have nothing at all to do with Christianity, *which they abhor*. The modern sect of the Mendaeans is widely scattered over Asia Minor and elsewhere, and several Orientalists rightly believe it to be a direct surviving relic of the Gnostics. For as explained in the *Dictionnaire des Apocryphes* by the Abbé Migne (in the article “Le Code Nazaréan,” commonly called the *Livre d’Adam*), the name Mendaeans (written in French as *Mandaïtes*, a name they pronounce as *Mandai*) “properly signifies science, knowledge, or *Gnosis*. Thus, it is the equivalent of *Gnostics*” (cited source, note p. 3). As the work cited above shows, although many travelers have spoken of a sect whose followers are variously named *Sabians*, St. John’s Christians, and *Mendaeans*, and who are scattered around Schat-*Elarab* <note>The Shatt al-Arab river</note> at the junction of the Tigris and Euphrates (principally at Basra, Hoveïza, Korna, etc.), it was Norberg who was the first to point out a tribe belonging to the same sect established in Syria. And they are the most interesting of all. This tribe, numbering some 14,000 or 15,000, lives a day’s march east of Mount Lebanon, principally at Elmerkah (Latakia). They call themselves both Nazarenes and Galileans, as they originally came to Syria from Galilee. They claim that their religion is the same as that of St. John the Baptist and that it has not changed at all since his day. On festival days, they clothe themselves in camel skins, sleep on camel skins, and eat locusts and honey just as their “Father, St. John the Baptist” did. Yet they call Jesus Christ an *imposter*, a *false Messiah*, and *Nebso* (or the planet Mercury in its evil aspect), and represent him as a product of the Spirit of the “seven ill-disposed stellars” (or planets). See *Codex Nazaraeus*, which is their Scripture.

### Mendes (Gr.).
The name of the demon-goat alleged by the Church of Rome to have been worshiped by the Templars and other Masons. But this goat was a myth created by the malicious imagination of *theological hatred*. There never was such a creature, nor was its worship known among the Templars or their predecessors, the Gnostics. The god of Mendes (or the Greek *Mendesius*, a name given to Lower Egypt in pre-Christian days) was the ram-headed god Ammon, the living and holy spirit of *Ra*, the life-giving sun. This led certain Greek authors into the error of claiming that the Egyptians called the “goat” (or the ram-headed god) himself Mendes. Ammon was for ages the chief deity of Egypt, the supreme god; *Amon-Ra* the “hidden god,” or *Amen* (the concealed), the *Self-engendered* who is “his own father and his own son.” Esoterically, he was *Pan*, the god of nature or nature personified, and the cloven foot of the *goat-footed* Pan probably helped to produce the error of this god being a goat. As Ammon’s shrine was at *Pa-bi-neb-tat*, “the dwelling of Tat or Spirit, Lord of Tat” (*Bindedi* in the Assyrian inscriptions), the Greeks first corrupted the name to *Bendes* and then

**Metatron** (*Hebrew*). The Kabbalistic "Prince of Faces," the Intelligence of the First Sephira, and the reputed ruler of Moses. His numeration is 314, the same as the deity title "Shaddai," Almighty. He is also the Angel of the world of Briah, and the one who led the Israelites through the Wilderness; therefore, he is the same as "the Lord God" Jehovah. The name resembles the Greek words *metathronon* or "beside the Throne." [w.w.w.]

**Metempsychosis.** The progress of the soul from one stage of existence to another. It is symbolized as, and commonly believed to be, rebirths in animal bodies. This is a term generally misunderstood by every class of European and American society, including many scientists. *Metempsychosis* should apply to animals alone. The Kabbalistic axiom, "A stone becomes a plant, a plant an animal, an animal a man, a man a spirit, and a spirit a god," receives an explanation in Manu's *Mânava-Dharma-Shâstra* and other Brahmanical books.

**Metis** (*Greek*). Wisdom. Greek theology associated Metis, Divine Wisdom, with Eros—Divine Love. The word is also said to form part of the Templars' deity or idol Baphomet, which some authorities derive from *Baphe*, baptism, and *Metis*, wisdom; while others say that the idol represented the two teachers whom the Templars equally denied, namely, the Pope and Mahomet. [w.w.w.]

**Midgard** (*Scandinavian*). The great snake in the *Eddas* which gnaws the roots of the *Yggdrasil*—the Tree of Life and the Universe in the legend of the Norsemen. Midgard is the Mundane Snake of Evil.

**Midrashim** (*Hebrew*). "Ancient"—the same as *Purâna*; the ancient writings of the Jews, just as the *Purânas* are called the "Ancient" Scriptures of India.

**Migmar** (*Tibetan*). The planet Mars.

**Mîmânsâ** (*Sanskrit*). A school of philosophy; one of the six in India. There are two Mîmânsâ schools, the older and the younger. The first, the "Pûrva-Mîmânsâ," was founded by Jamini; the latter, or "Uttara-Mîmânsâ," was founded by a Vyasa and is now called the Vedânta school. Sankarâchârya was the most prominent apostle of the latter. The Vedânta school is the oldest of all the six Darshana (literally, "demonstrations"), but even the Pûrva-Mîmânsâ is dated no earlier than 500 <term>B.C.</term> Orientalists who support the absurd idea that all these schools are "due to Greek influence" would date them even later to fit their theory. The *Shad-darshana* (or Six Demonstrations) all have a common starting point and maintain that *ex nihilo nihil fit* <note>out of nothing, nothing comes</note>.

**Minas** (*Sanskrit*). The same as Meenam, the Zodiacal sign *Pisces* or Fishes.

**Miölner** (*Scandinavian*). The storm-hammer of Thor (See “Svâstica”) made for him by the Dwarfs; with it, the God conquered men and gods alike. It is the same kind of magic weapon as the Hindu <term>Agneyastra</term>, the fire-weapon.

**Mirror**. The Luminous Mirror, <term>Aspaqularia nêra</term>, a Kabbalistic term, means the power of foresight and farsight—prophecy such as Moses had. A parallel symbolism is that of the conception of the Tree of Life, compared to that only of the Tree of Knowledge. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Mishnah** (*Hebrew*). The older portion of the Jewish <term>Talmud</term>, or oral law, consisting of supplementary regulations for the guidance of the Jews with an ample commentary. The contents are arranged in six sections, treating of Seeds, Feasts, Women, Damages, Sacred Things, and Purification. Rabbi Judah Ha-Nasi codified the Mishnah about A.D. 140. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Mistletoe**. This curious plant, which grows only as a parasite upon other trees such as the apple and the oak, was a mystic plant in several ancient religions, notably that of the Celtic <term>Druids</term>. Their priests cut the Mistletoe with much ceremony at certain seasons, and then only with a specially consecrated golden knife. Hislop suggests as a religious explanation that the Mistletoe, being a branch growing out of a mother tree, was worshiped as a Divine Branch out of an Earthly Tree—the union of deity and humanity. The name in German means “all-heal.” Compare the <term>Golden Branch</term> in Virgil's *Æneid*, vi. 126, and Pliny, *Natural History*, xvii. 44: “A priest clothed in white vestments climbs the tree and cuts it with a golden sickle.” <note>Original Latin: Sacerdos candida vesta cultus arborem scandit, falce aurea demetit</note> <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Mitra** or **Mithra**. (*Persian*). An ancient Iranian deity and sun-god, as evidenced by his being lion-headed. The name also exists in India and refers to a form of the sun. The Persian Mithra, who drove <term>Ahriman</term> out of heaven, is a kind of <term>Messiah</term> who is expected to return as the judge of men, and is a sin-bearing god who atones for the iniquities of mankind. As such, however, he is directly connected with the highest Occultism, the tenets of which were expounded during the <term>Mithraic</term> Mysteries which bore his name.

**Mitre**. The head-dress of a religious dignitary, such as a Roman Catholic Bishop; a cap ending upwards in two lips, like a fish’s head with an open mouth—*os tincæ*—associated with <term>Dagon</term>, the Babylonian deity, the word *dag* meaning fish. **Moon**. The earth’s satellite has featured very prominently as an emblem in the religions of antiquity. Most commonly, it has been represented as female, but this is not universal; in the myths of the Teutons and Arabs, as well as in the conceptions of the Rajputs of India (see *Tod, Hist.*) and in Tartary, the moon was male. Latin authors speak of Luna and also of Lunus, though very rarely. The Greek name is Selene; the Hebrew is Lebanon and also Yarcah. In Egypt, the moon was associated with Isis; in Phoenicia, with Astarte; and in Babylon, with Ishtar. From certain points of view, the ancients also regarded the moon as androgynous. Astrologers assign an influence to the moon over the various parts of a person, according to the different Zodiacal signs she traverses, as well as a special influence produced by the house she occupies in a chart.

**Mumukshatwa** (*Sk.*). Desire for liberation (from reincarnation and the bondage of matter).

**Mystagogy** (*Gr.*). The doctrines or interpretations of the sacred mysteries.

**Mysterium Magnum** (*Lat.*). "The great Mystery," a term used in Alchemy in connection with the creation of the "Philosopher's Stone" and the "Elixir of Life."

**Mysteries.** Greek *teletai*, or finishings; celebrations of initiation or the Mysteries. They were observances, generally kept secret from the uninitiated, in which the origin of things, the nature of human spirits, their relation to the body, and the method of their purification and restoration to a higher life were taught through dramatic representation and other methods. Physical science, medicine, the laws of music, and divination were all taught in the same manner. The Hippocratic oath

was only a mystic obligation. Hippocrates was a priest of Asklepios <note>OCR text: Asklepois</note>, some of whose writings happened to become public. But the Asclepiades were initiates of the Aesculapian serpent-worship, just as the Bacchantes were of the Dionysia; and both rites were eventually incorporated into the Eleusinia. The Sacred Mysteries were performed in the ancient Temples by the initiated Hierophants for the benefit and instruction of the candidates. The most solemn and occult Mysteries were certainly those performed in Egypt by “the band of secret-keepers,” as Mr. Bonwick calls the Hierophants. Maurice describes their nature very graphically in a few lines. Speaking of the Mysteries performed in Philae (the Nile island), he says that “it was in these gloomy caverns that the grand and mystic secrets of the goddess (Isis) were revealed to the adoring aspirant, while the solemn hymn of initiation resounded through the long extent of these stony recesses.” The word “mysteries” is derived from the Greek μυῶ, “to close the mouth,” and every symbol connected with them had a hidden meaning. As Plato and many other sages of antiquity affirm, the Mysteries were highly religious, moral, and beneficial as a school of ethics. The Greek mysteries, those of Ceres and Bacchus, were only imitations of the Egyptian ones; and the author of *Egyptian Belief and Modern Thought* informs us that our own “word chapel or *capella* is said to be the *Cap-El* or college of *El*, the Solar divinity.” The well-known Kabiri are associated with the Mysteries. In short, the Mysteries were in every country a series of dramatic performances, in which the mysteries of cosmogony and nature, in general, were personified by the priests and neophytes, who enacted the parts of various gods and goddesses, repeating supposed scenes (allegories) from their respective lives. These were explained in their hidden meaning to the candidates for initiation and incorporated into philosophical doctrines.

**Mystery Language.** The priestly secret jargon employed by the initiated priests, and used only when discussing sacred things. Every nation had its own “mystery” tongue, unknown except to those admitted to the Mysteries.

**Mystes** (Gr.). In antiquity, the name for the Initiates; today it is that of Roman Cardinals, who, having borrowed all their other rites and dogmas from Aryan, Egyptian, and Hellenic “heathen,” have also helped themselves to the <term>μῦσις</term> of the neophytes. They must keep their eyes and mouths shut during their consecration and are, therefore, called *Mystae*.

**Mystica Vannus Iacchi.** Commonly translated as the mystic *Fan*; but in an ancient terracotta in the British Museum, the fan is a Basket such as the ancient Mysteries displayed with mystic contents: Inman says with symbolic testes. [w.w.w.]

# N.

**N.** — The 14th letter in both the English and the Hebrew alphabets. In the latter language, the *N* is called Nûn and signifies a fish. It is the symbol of the female principle or the womb. Its numerical value is 50 in the Kabbalistic system, but the Peripatetics made it equivalent to 900, and with a stroke over it ($\overline{900}$), 9,000. With the Hebrews, however, the final Nun was 700.

**Naaseni.** The Christian Gnostic sect, called Naasenians or serpent worshippers, who considered the constellation of the Dragon as the symbol of their Logos or Christ.

**Nabatheans.** A sect almost identical in their beliefs with the Nazarenes and Sabeans, who had more reverence for John the Baptist than for Jesus. Maimonides identifies them with the star-worshippers.
> "Concerning the beliefs of the *Sabeans*," he says, "the most famous is the book, *The Agriculture of the Nabatheans*." And we know that the Ebionites—the first of whom were the friends and relatives of Jesus according to tradition, or in other words, the earliest and first Christians—"were the direct followers and disciples of the Nazarene sect," according to Epiphanius and Theodoret (See the *Contra Ebionites* of Epiphanius, and also "Galileans" and "Nazarenes").

**Nabhi** (*Sk.*). The father of Bhârata, who gave his name to *Bhârata Varsha* (the land) or India.

**Nabia** (*Heb.*). Seership, soothsaying. This oldest and most respected of mystic phenomena is the name given to prophecy in the *Bible*, and is correctly included among the spiritual powers, such as divination, clairvoyant visions, trance conditions, and oracles. But while enchanters, diviners, and even astrologers are strictly condemned in the Mosaic books, prophecy, seership, and nabia appear as the special gifts of heaven. In early ages they were all termed Epoptai (Seers), the Greek word for Initiates; they were also designated *Nebim*, "the plural of Nebo, the Babylonian god of wisdom." The Kabbalist distinguishes between the *seer* and the *magician*; one is passive, the other active. *Nebirah* is one who looks into the future and a clairvoyant; *Nebi-poel* is he who possesses magic powers. We notice that Elijah and Apollonius used the same methods to isolate themselves from the disturbing influences of the outer world: namely, wrapping their heads entirely in a woollen mantle—supposedly because it is an electric non-conductor.
