<term>**Pratyâbhâva**</term> (*Sk.*). The state of the Ego under the necessity of repeated births.
<term>**Pratyagâtmâ**</term> (*Sk.*). The same as *Jîvâtmâ*, or the one living Universal Soul—*Alaya*.
<term>**Pratyâhâra**</term> (*Sk.*). The same as “*Mahâpralaya*.”
<term>**Pratyâharana**</term> (*Sk.*). The preliminary training in practical *Râj-Yoga*.
<term>**Pratyaksha**</term> (*Sk.*). Spiritual perception by means of the senses.
<term>**Pratyasarga**</term> (*Sk.*). In *Sankhya* philosophy, the “intellectual evolution of the Universe”; in the *Purânas*, it is the 8th creation.
<term>**Pratyêka Buddha**</term> (*Sk.*). The same as “*Pasî-Buddha*.” The *Pratyêka Buddha* is a degree that belongs exclusively to the *Yogâ-chârya* school, yet it represents only a high level of intellectual development with no true spirituality. It is the *dead-letter* of the *Yoga* laws, in which intellect and comprehension play the greatest part, added to the strict observance of the rules of inner development. It is the lowest of the three paths to *Nirvâna*, in which a *Yogî*—“without a teacher and without saving others”—attains a kind of nominal *Buddhaship* individually through the mere force of will and technical observances. He does no good to anyone, but works selfishly for his own salvation alone. The *Pratyêkas* are respected outwardly but are despised inwardly by those of keen or spiritual appreciation. A *Pratyêka* is generally compared to a “*Khadga*,” or solitary rhinoceros, and called *Ekashringa Rishi*, a selfish solitary *Rishi* (or saint). “By crossing *Sansâra* (‘the ocean of birth and death’ or the series of incarnations), suppressing errors, and yet not attaining absolute perfection, the *Pratyêka Buddha* is compared to a horse that swims across a river without touching the ground” (*Sanskrit-Chinese Dictionary*). He is far below a true “Buddha of Compassion.” He strives only to reach *Nirvâna*.
<term>**Pre-existence**</term>. The term used to denote that we have lived before; the same as reincarnation in the past. This idea is derided by some, rejected by others, and called absurd and inconsistent by a third group; yet it is the oldest and most universally accepted belief from immemorial antiquity. And if this belief was universally accepted by the most subtle philosophical minds of the pre-Christian world, it is certainly not out of place for some of our modern intellectual men to also believe in it, or at least give the doctrine the benefit of the doubt. Even the Bible hints at it more than once: St. John the Baptist is regarded as the reincarnation of Elijah, and the Disciples asked whether the *blind man was born blind because of his sins*, which is equivalent to saying that he had *lived and sinned before being born blind*. As Mr. Bonwick rightly says, it was “the work of spiritual progression and soul discipline. Truly, "an evil act follows a man, passing through one hundred thousand transmigrations" (*Panchatantra*). "All souls have a subtle vehicle, an image of the body, which carries the passive soul from one material dwelling to another," says Kapila; while Basnage explains regarding the Jews: "By this 'second death' they do not mean hell, but that which happens when a soul has animated a body for a second time." **Prêtas** (Sk.). "Hungry demons" in popular folklore. "Shells" of the avaricious and selfish man after death; "Elementaries" reborn as Prêtas in Kâma-loka, according to the esoteric teachings.

**Priestesses**. Every ancient religion had its priestesses in the temples. In Egypt, they were called the *Sâ* and served the altar of Isis and in the temples of other goddesses. *Canéphorae* was the name given by the Greeks to those consecrated priestesses who carried the baskets of the gods during the public festivals of the Eleusinian Mysteries. There were female prophets in Israel as in Egypt, diviners of dreams and oracles; and Herodotus mentions the *Hierodules*, the virgins or nuns dedicated to the Theban Jove, who were generally the Pharaoh's daughters and other Princesses of the Royal House. Orientalists speak of the wife of Cephrenes, the builder of the so-called second Pyramid, who was a priestess of Thoth. (See "Nuns".)

**Primordial Light**. In Occultism, the light which is born in and through the preternatural darkness of chaos, which contains "the all in all"—the seven rays that later become the seven Principles in Nature.

**Principles**. The Elements or original essences, the basic differentiations upon and of which all things are built up. We use the term to denote the seven individual and fundamental aspects of the One Universal Reality in the Cosmos and in man. Hence also the seven aspects in their manifestation in the human being—divine, spiritual, psychic, astral, physiological, and simply physical.

**Priyavrata** (Sk.). The name of the son of Swâyambhuva Manu in exoteric Hinduism. The occult designation of one of the primeval races in Occultism.

**Psychometry.** Literally, “Soul-measuring”; reading or seeing, not with the physical eyes, but with the soul or *inner Sight*.

**Psychophobia.** Literally, “Soul-fear,” applied to materialists and certain atheists, who become struck with madness at the very mention of Soul or Spirit.

**Psylli** (*Gr.*). Serpent-charmers of Africa and Egypt.

**Ptah**, or *Phthah* (*Eg.*). The son of <term>Kneph</term> in the Egyptian Pantheon. He is the <term>Principle of Light and Life</term> through which “creation”—or rather, evolution—took place. The Egyptian <term>logos</term> and creator, the *Demiurgos*. A very old deity, as, according to <term>Herodotus</term>, he had a temple erected to him by <term>Menes</term>, the first king of Egypt. He is the “giver of life” and the self-born, and the father of <term>Apis</term>, the sacred bull, conceived through a ray from the Sun. <term>Ptah</term> is thus the prototype of <term>Osiris</term>, a later deity. <term>Herodotus</term> makes him a father of the <term>Kabiri</term>, the mystery-gods; and the *Targum of Jerusalem* says: “Egyptians called the wisdom of the <term>First Intellect Ptah</term>”; hence he is *Mahat*, the “divine wisdom”; though from another aspect he is *Swabhâvat*, the self-created substance, as a prayer addressed to him in the *Ritual of the Dead* says, after calling <term>Ptah</term> “father of fathers and of all gods, generator of all men produced from his substance”: “Thou art without father, being engendered by thy own will; thou art without mother, being born by the renewal of thine own substance from whom proceeds substance.”

**Pûjâ** (*Sk.*). An offering; worship and divine honors offered to an idol or something sacred.

**Pulastya** (*Sk.*). One of the seven “<term>mind-born sons</term>” of <term>Brahmâ</term>; the reputed father of the <term>Nâgas</term> (serpents, also *Initiates*) and other symbolical creatures.

**Pums** (*Sk.*). Spirit, supreme <term>Purusha</term>, Man.

**Punarjanma** (*Sk.*). The power of evolving objective manifestations; motion of forms; also, re-birth.

**Pundarîk-aksha** (*Sk.*). Literally, “lotus-eyed”, a title of <term>Vishnu</term>. “Supreme and imperishable glory”, as translated by some Orientalists.

**Pûraka** (*Sk.*). Inbreathing process; a way of breathing as regulated according to the prescribed rules of <term>Hatha Yoga</term>.

**Purânas** (*Sk.*). Literally, “ancient.” A collection of symbolical and allegorical writings—eighteen in number now—supposed to have been composed by <term>Vyâsa</term>, the author of the *Mahâbhârata*.

**Purohitas** (*Sk.*). Family priests; Brahmans.

**Pururavas** (*Sk.*). The son of <term>Budha</term>, the son of <term>Soma</term> (the moon), and of <term>Ila</term>; famous for being the first to produce fire by the friction of two pieces of wood, and making it (the fire) triple. An occult character.

**Purusha** (Sk.). Man, “heavenly man.” Spirit, the same as Narayana in another aspect. “The Spiritual Self.”

**Purusha Nârâyana** (Sk.). Primordial male—Brahma.

**Purushottama** (Sk.). *Literally*, “best of men”; metaphysically, however, it is spirit, the Supreme Soul of the universe; a title of Vishnu.

**Pûrvoja** (Sk.). “Pregenetic,” the same as the *Orphic Protologos*; a title of Vishnu.

**Purushadha** (Sk.). An asterism.

**Pûshan** (Sk.). A Vedic deity, the real meaning of which remains unknown to Orientalists. It is described as the “Nourisher,” the feeder of all (helpless) beings. Esoteric philosophy explains the meaning. Speaking of it, the *Taittirîya Brâhmana* says that, “When Prajâpati formed living beings, Pûshan nourished them.” This, then, is the same mysterious force that nourishes the fetus and unborn babe by *osmosis*, and which is called the “atmospheric (or *akasic*) nurse,” and the “father nourisher.” When the lunar Pitris had evolved men, these remained senseless and helpless, and it is “Pûshan who fed primeval man.” Also a name of the Sun.

**Pushkala** (Sk.) or *Puskola*. A palm leaf prepared for writing on, used in Ceylon <note>Now Sri Lanka</note>. All the native books are written on such palm leaves, and last for centuries.

**Pushkara** (Sk.). A blue lotus; the seventh *Dwîpa* or zone of *Bhâratavarsha* (India). A famous lake near Ajmere; also the proper name of several persons.

**Pûto** (Sk.). An island in China where Kwan-Shai-Yin and Kwan-Yin have a number of temples and monasteries.

**Putra** (Sk.). A son.

**Pu-tsi K’iun-ling** (Chin.). *Literally*, “the Universal Savior of all beings.” A title of Avalokiteswara, and also of Buddha.

**Pygmalion** (Gr.). A celebrated sculptor and statue-maker on the island of Cyprus, who became enamored of a statue he had made. So the Goddess of beauty, taking pity on him, changed it into a living woman (*Ovid, Metamorphoses*). The above is an allegory of the soul.

**Pymander** (Gr.). The “Thought divine.” The Egyptian Prometheus and the personified *Nous* or divine light which appears to and instructs Hermes Trismegistus, in a Hermetic work called “Pymander.”

**Pyrrha** (Gr.). A daughter of Epimetheus and Pandora, who was married to Deucalion. After a deluge when mankind was almost annihilated, Pyrrha and Deucalion made men and women out of stones which they threw behind them.

**Pyrrhonism** (Gr.). The doctrine of Skepticism as first taught by Pyrrho, though his system was far more philosophical than the blank denial of our modern Pyrrhonists.

# THEOSOPHICAL

**Pythagoras** *(Gr.).* The most famous of mystic philosophers, born at Samos, about 586 <term>B.C.</term> He seems to have traveled all over the world and to have gathered his philosophy from the various systems to which he had access. Thus, he studied the esoteric sciences with the Brahmins of India, and astronomy and astrology in Chaldea and Egypt. He is known to this day in India under the name of Yavanâchârya (“Ionian teacher”). After returning, he settled in Crotona, in Magna Graecia, where he established a college that was soon attended by all the best intellects of the civilized centers. His father was a certain Mnesarchus of Samos, a man of noble birth and learning. It was Pythagoras who was the first to teach the heliocentric system, and who was the most proficient expert in geometry of his century. It was he also who created the word “philosopher,” composed of two words meaning a “lover of wisdom”—*philo-sophos*. As the greatest mathematician, geometer, and astronomer of historical antiquity, and also the greatest of the metaphysicians and scholars, Pythagoras has won imperishable fame. He taught reincarnation as it is practiced in India, along with much else of the Secret Wisdom.

**Pythagorean Pentacle** *(Gr.).* A Kabbalistic six-pointed star with an eagle at the apex and a bull and a lion under the face of a man; a mystic symbol adopted by the Eastern and Roman Christians, who place these animals beside the four Evangelists.

**Pythia** or **Pythoness** *(Gr.).* Modern dictionaries inform us that the term means one who delivered the oracles at the temple of Delphi, and “any female supposed to have the spirit of divination in her—a witch” (Webster). This is neither true, just, nor correct. On the authority of Iamblichus, Plutarch, and others, a Pythia was a priestess chosen from among the psychically sensitive people of the poorer classes and placed in a temple where oracular powers were exercised. There she had a room secluded from everyone except the chief Hierophant and Seer, and once admitted, was, like a nun, lost to the world. Sitting on a brass tripod placed over a fissure in the ground, through which intoxicating vapors arose, these subterranean exhalations penetrated her whole system and produced a prophetic mania; in this abnormal state, she delivered oracles. Aristophanes in “Væstas” <note>Likely referring to the play *The Wasps* (Vespae)</note> I., reg. 28, calls the Pythia *ventriloqua vates* or the “ventriloquial prophetess,” because of her stomach-voice. The ancients placed the soul of man (the lower *Manas*) or his personal self-consciousness in the pit of his stomach. We find in the fourth verse of the second *Nâbhânedishta* hymn of the Brahmins: “Hear, O sons of the gods, one who speaks through his name (*nâbha*), for he hails you in your dwellings!” This is a modern somnambulic phenomenon. The navel was regarded in antiquity as “the circle of the sun,” the seat of divine internal light. Therefore, the oracle of Apollo was at Delphi, the city of *Delphus*—meaning the womb or abdomen—while the seat of the temple was called the *omphalos*, or navel. As is well known, a number of mesmerized subjects can read letters, hear, smell, and see through that part of their body. In

**Quadrivium** (*Lat.*). A term used by the Scholastics during the Middle Ages to designate the last four paths of learning—of which there were originally seven. Thus grammar, rhetoric, and logic were called the *trivium*, and arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy (the obligatory Pythagorean sciences) went under the name of *quadrivium*.

**Quetzo-Cohuatl** (*Mex.*). The serpent-god in the Mexican Scriptures and legends. His "landmarks" and other signs show him to be some great Initiate of antiquity, who received the name of “Serpent” because of his wisdom, long life, and powers. To this day, the indigenous tribes of Mexico call themselves by the names of various reptiles, animals, and birds.

**Quiche Cosmogony**. Called the *Popol Vuh*; discovered by the Abbé Brasseur de Bourbourg. (See “Popol Vuh”.)

**Quietists**. A religious sect founded by a Spanish monk named Molinos. Their chief doctrine was that contemplation (an internal state of complete rest and passivity) was the only religious practice possible and constituted the whole of religious observance. They were the Western *Hatha Yogis* and spent their time trying to separate their minds from the objects of the senses. This practice became fashionable in France and also in Russia during the early part of this century.

**Quinanes**. A very ancient race of giants, of whom there are many traditions, not only in folklore but in the history of Central America. Occult science teaches that the race which preceded our own human race was one of giants which gradually decreased—after the Atlantean deluge had almost swept them off the face of the earth—to the present size of man.

**Quindecemvir** (*Lat.*). The Roman priest who was in charge of the Sibylline books.

**Qû-tamy** (*Chald.*). The name of the mystic who receives the revelations of the moon-goddess in the ancient Chaldean work, which was translated into Arabic and retranslated by Chwolsôhn into German under the title *Nabathaean Agriculture*.

## R.

R.—The eighteenth letter of the alphabet; it is called "the canine" because its sound reminds one of a snarl. In the Hebrew alphabet it is the twentieth, and its numerical value is 200. As <term>Resh</term>, it is equivalent to the divine name <term>Rahim</term> (clemency); and its symbols are a sphere, a head, or a circle.

**Ra** (*Eg*.). The divine Universal Soul in its manifested aspect—the ever-burning light; also the personified Sun.

**Rabbis** (*Heb*.). Originally teachers of the Secret Mysteries, the <term>Qabbalah</term>; later, every Levite of the priestly caste became a teacher and a Rabbi. (See the series of <term>Kabbalistic Rabbis</term> by w.w.w.)

1 **Rabbi Abulafia** of Saragossa, born in 1240, formed a school of <term>Kabbalah</term> named after him; his chief works were *The Seven Paths of the Law* and *The Epistle to Rabbi Solomon*.

2 **Rabbi Akiba**. Author of a famous <term>Kabbalistic</term> work, the "Alphabet of R. A.," which treats every letter as a symbol of an idea and an emblem of some sentiment; the *Book of Enoch* was originally a portion of this work, and appeared at the close of the eighth century. It was not a purely <term>Kabbalistic</term> treatise.

3 **Rabbi Azariel ben Menachem** (A.D. 1160). The author of the *Commentary on the Ten Sephiroth*, which is the oldest purely <term>Kabbalistic</term> work in existence, setting aside the *Sepher Yetzirah*, which, although older, is not concerned with the <term>Kabbalistic Sephiroth</term>. He was the pupil of <term>Isaac the Blind</term>, who is the reputed author of the European <term>Kabbalah</term>, and he was the teacher of the equally famous R. <term>Moses Nachmanides</term>.

4 **Rabbi Moses Botarel** (1480). Author of a famous commentary on *the Sepher Yetzirah*; he taught that through an ascetic life and the use of invocation, a man's dreams might be made prophetic.

5 **Rabbi Chajim Vital** (1600). The great exponent of the <term>Kabbalah</term> as taught by R. <term>Isaac Loria</term>: author of one of the most famous works, *Otz Chijm*, or *Tree of Life*; from this, <term>Knorr von Rosenroth</term> has taken the *Book on the Rashith ha Gilgalim*, which deals with the revolutions of souls or the scheme of reincarnations.

6 **Rabbi Ibn Gebirol**. A famous Hebrew Rabbi and author of the hymn *Kether Malchuth*, or *Royal Diadem*, which appeared about 1050; it is a beautiful poem embodying the cosmic doctrines of <term>Aristotle</term>, and it even now forms part of the special Jewish service for the evening preceding the great annual <term>Day of Atonement</term>. (See <term>Ginsburg</term> and <term>Sachs</term> on the *Religious Poetry of the Spanish Jews*). This author is also known as <term>Avicebron</term>.

**7 Rabbi Gikatilla.** A distinguished <term>Kabbalist</term> who thrived about 1300: he wrote the famous books, *The Garden of Nuts, The Gate to the Vowel Points, The Mystery of the Shining Metal, and The Gates of Righteousness*. He laid special emphasis on the use of <term>Gematria</term>, <term>Notaricon</term> and <term>Temura</term>.

**8 Rabbi Isaac the Blind** of Posquiero. The first who publicly taught in Europe, about 1200 A.D., the <term>Theosophic</term> doctrines of the <term>Kabbalah</term>.

**9 Rabbi Loria** (also written *Luria*, and also named *Ari* from his initials). Founded a school of the <term>Kabbalah</term> around 1560. He did not write any works, but his disciples treasured his teachings, and Rabbi Chajim Vital published them.

**10 Rabbi Moses Cordovero** (1550 A.D.). The author of several Kabbalistic works of a wide reputation, namely, *A Sweet Light, The Book of Retirement*, and *The Garden of Pomegranates*; this latter can be read in Latin in Knorr von Rosenroth's *Kabbalah Denudata*, entitled *Tractatus de Animo, ex libro Pardes Rimmonim*. Cordovero is notable for his adherence to the strictly metaphysical part, ignoring the miracle-working branch which Rabbi Sabbatai Zevi practiced, and almost perished in the pursuit of.

**11 Rabbi Moses de Leon** (around 1290 A.D.). The editor and first publisher of the first <term>Zohar</term> or “<term>Splendor</term>”, the most famous of all the Kabbalistic volumes, and almost the only one of which any large part has been translated into English. This <term>Zohar</term> is asserted to be mainly the production of the still more famous Rabbi Simon ben Jochai, who lived during the reign of the Emperor Titus.

**12 Rabbi Moses Maimonides** (died 1304). A famous Hebrew Rabbi and author, who condemned the use of charms and amulets, and objected to the Kabbalistic use of the divine names.

**13 Rabbi Sabbatai Zevi** (born 1641). A very famous <term>Kabbalist</term>, who, passing beyond dogma, became of great reputation as a miracle-worker, performing wonders by the divine names. Later in life he claimed to be the Messiah and fell into the hands of the Sultan Mohammed IV of Turkey; he would have been executed, but saved his life by adopting the Islamic religion. (See Jost on *Judaism and its Sects*.)

**14 Rabbi Simon ben Jochai** (around 70-80 A.D.). It is around this name that the mystery and poetry of the origin of the <term>Kabbalah</term> cluster as a gift from the deity to mankind. Tradition has it that the <term>Kabbalah</term> was a divine theosophy first taught by God to a company of angels, and that some glimpses of its perfection were granted to Adam; that the wisdom passed from him to Noah; from there to Abraham, from whom the Egyptians of his era learned a portion of the doctrine. Moses derived a partial initiation from the land of his birth, and this was perfected by direct communications with the deity. From Moses it passed to the seventy elders of the Jewish nation, and from them the theosophic system was handed from generation to generation; David and Solomon especially became masters of this hidden doctrine. **Râdhâ** (*Sk*.). The shepherdess among the *Gopis* (shepherdesses) of Krishna, who was the wife of the god.

**Râga** (*Sk*.). One of the five *Kleshas* (afflictions) in Patânjali’s Yoga philosophy. In *Sânkhya Kârikâ* it is the “obstruction” called love and desire in the physical or earthly sense. The five *Kleshas* are: *Avidyâ*, or ignorance; *Asmitâ*, selfishness, or “I-am-ness”; *Râga*, love; *Dwesha*, hatred; and *Abhinivesa*, dread of suffering.

**Ragnarök** (*Scand*.). A kind of metaphysical entity called the “Destroyer,” and the “Twilight of the Gods,” two-thirds of whom are destroyed at the “Last Battle” in the *Edda*. Ragnarök lies in chains on the ledge of a rock as long as there are some good men in the world; but when all laws are broken and all virtue and goodness vanish from it, then Ragnarök will be unbound and allowed to bring every imaginable evil and disaster upon the doomed world.

**Ragon, J. M.** A French Mason, a distinguished writer and great symbologist, who tried to restore Masonry to its original purity. He was born at Bruges in 1789, was admitted when quite a boy into the Lodge and Chapter of the “*Vrais Amis*,” and upon moving to Paris founded the Society of the Trinosophes. It is rumored that he possessed a number of papers given to him by the famous Count de St. Germain, from which he gained all his remarkable knowledge of early Masonry. He died at Paris in 1866, leaving a number of books written by himself and masses of manuscripts, which he bequeathed to the “Grand Orient.” Of the mass of his published works very few are obtainable, while others have entirely disappeared. This is due to mysterious persons (believed to be Jesuits) who hurried to buy up every edition they could find after his death. In short, his works are now extremely rare.

**Rahasya** (*Sk*.). A name for the Upanishads. *Lit*., secret essence of knowledge.

**Rahat**. The same as “Arhat”; the adept who becomes entirely free from any desire on this plane by acquiring divine knowledge and powers.

<header>GLOSSARY</header>

**Ra'hmin Seth** (*Heb*.). According to the *Kabala* (or *Qabbalah*), the “soul-sparks” contained in Adam (Kadmon) went into three sources, the heads of which were his three sons. Thus, while the “soul-spark” (or *Ego*) called Chesed went into Habel, and Geboor-ah into Qai-yin (Cain)—Ra'hmin went into Seth, and these three sons were divided into seventy human species called “the principal roots of the human race.”

**Râhu** (*Sk*.). A *Daitya* (demon) whose lower parts were like a dragon's tail. He made himself immortal by robbing the gods of some *Amrita*—the elixir of divine life—for which they were churning the ocean of milk. Unable to deprive him of his immortality, Vishnu exiled him from the earth and made of him the constellation Draco, his head being called Râhu and his tail Ketu—astronomically, the ascending and descending nodes. With the latter appendage, he has ever since waged a destructive war on the denouncers of his robbery, the sun and the moon, and (during the eclipse) is said to swallow them. Of course, the fable has a mystic and occult meaning.

**Rahula** (*Sk*.). The name of Gautama Buddha's son.

**Raibhyas** (*Sk*.). A class of gods in the 5th Manvantara.

**Raivata Manvantara** (*Sk*.). The life-cycle presided over by Raivata Manu. As he is the fifth of the fourteen Manus (in Esotericism, *Dhyan Chohans*), there being seven *root*-Manus and seven *seed*-Manus for the seven Rounds of our terrestrial chain of globes (See *Esot. Buddhism* by A. P. Sinnett, and *the Secret Doctrine*, Vol. I., “Brahminical Chronology”), Raivata presided over the third Round and was its *root*-Manu.

**Râjâ** (*Sk*.). A Prince or King in India.

**Râjagriha** (*Sk*.). A city in Magadha famous for its conversion to Buddhism in the days of the Buddhist kings. It was their residence from Bimbisara to Asoka, and was the seat of the first Synod, or Buddhist Council, held 510 B.C.

**Râjârshis** (*Sk*.). The King-Rishis or King-Adepts, one of the three classes of Rishis in India; the same as the King-Hierophants of ancient Egypt.

**Râjas** (*Sk*.). The “quality of foulness” (*i.e.*, differentiation) and activity in the *Purânas*. One of the three *Gunas* or divisions in the correlations of matter and nature, representing form and change.

**Rajasâs** (*Sk*.). The elder *Agnishwâttas*—the Fire-Pitris, “fire” standing as a symbol of enlightenment and intellect.

**Râja-Yoga** (*Sk*.). The true system of developing psychic and spiritual powers and union with one's *Higher Self*—or the Supreme Spirit, as the profane express it. The exercise, regulation, and concentration of thought. Râja-Yoga is opposed to Hatha-Yoga, the physical or psycho-physiological training in asceticism.

**Râkâ** (*Sk*.). The day of the full moon: a day for occult practices.

**Râkshâ** (*Sk*.). An amulet prepared during the full or new moon.

**Râkshasas** (*Sk.*). Literally, “raw eaters,” and in popular superstition, these are evil spirits or demons. Esoterically, however, they are the *Gibborim* (giants) of the Bible, representing the Fourth Race or the Atlanteans. (See *The Secret Doctrine*, II, 165.)

**Râkshasi-Bhâshâ** (*Sk.*). Literally, the language of the Râkshasas. In reality, this is the speech of the Atlanteans, our gigantic forefathers of the fourth Root-race.

**Ram Mohum Roy** (*Sk.*). The well-known Indian reformer who traveled to England in 1833 and died there.

**Râma** (*Sk.*). The seventh *avatar* or incarnation of Vishnu; the eldest son of King Dasaratha, of the Solar Race. His full name is Râma-Chandra, and he is the hero of the *Râmâyana*. He married Sîta, who was the female *avatar* of Lakshmî, Vishnu’s wife. She was carried away by Râvana, the Demon-King of Lanka, an act that led to the famous war.

**Râmâyana** (*Sk.*). The famous epic poem associated with the *Mahâbhârata*. It appears as if this poem was either the original source of the *Iliad* or vice versa, except that in the *Râmâyana*, the allies of Râma are monkeys led by Hanuman, along with monster birds and other animals, all of whom fight against the *Râkshasas*, or the demons and giants of Lankâ.

**Râsa** (*Sk.*). The mystery-dance performed by Krishna and his *Gopis* (the shepherdesses), which is represented in a yearly festival to this day, especially in Rajasthan. Astronomically, it represents Krishna—the *Sun*—around whom circle the planets and the signs of the Zodiac, symbolized by the *Gopis*. This is the same as the “<term>circle-dance</term>” of the Amazons around the phallic image, the dance of the daughters of Shiloh (*Judges* xxi.), and the dance of King David around the ark. (See *Isis Unveiled*, II, pages 45, 331, and 332.)

**Râshi** (*Sk.*). An astrological division; specifically the sixth, relating to Kanya (*Virgo*), the sixth sign in the Zodiac.

**Rashi-Chakra** (*Sk.*). The Zodiac.

**Rasit** (*Heb.*). Wisdom.

**Rasollâsâ** (*Sk.*). The first of the eight physical perfections, or *Siddhis* (*phenomena*), of the Hatha Yogis. Rasollâsâ is the rapid development at will of the fluids of the body, independent of any external nutrition.

**Rasshoo** (*Eg.*). The solar fires formed in and out of the primordial “waters,” or substance, of Space.

**Ratnâvabhâsa Kalpa** (*Sk.*). The age in which all sexual differences will have ceased to exist and birth will take place in the *Anupâdaka* mode, as it did in the second and third Root-races. Esoteric philosophy teaches that this will take place at the end of the sixth and during the seventh and last Root-race in this Round.

**Râtri** (*Sk.*). Night; the body that Brahmâ assumed for the purposes of creating the Râkshasas or supposed giant-demons.

**Ravail.** The true name of the founder of modern Spiritism in France, who is better known under the pseudonym *Allan Kardec*.

**Râvana** (*Sk.*). The Demon-King (of the *Râkshasas*), the Sovereign of Lankâ (Ceylon), who kidnapped Sîta, Râma’s wife; this led to the great war described in the *Râmâyana*.

**Rechaka** (*Sk.*). A practice in Hatha Yoga performed during *Prânâyâma*, or the regulation of breath: specifically, the act of opening one nostril and exhaling through it while keeping the other closed. This is one of the three operations known as Pûraka, Kumbhaka, and Rechaka—practices that are very harmful to health.

**Red Colour.** This has always been associated with male characteristics, especially by the Etruscans and Hindus. In Hebrew, it is Adam, which is the same as the word for “earth” and “the first man.” It seems that nearly all myths represent the first perfect man as white. The same word without the initial 'A' is *Dam* or *Dem*, which means blood, also red in color. <note>w.w.w.</note>

The color of the fourth Principle in man—*Kâma*, the seat of desires—is represented as red.

**Reincarnation.** The doctrine of rebirth, believed in by Jesus and the Apostles, as it was by all men in those days, but now denied by Christians. All the Egyptian converts to Christianity, Church Fathers, and others believed in this doctrine, as shown by the writings of several of them. In the still-existing symbols, the human-headed bird flying toward a mummy, a body, or “the soul uniting itself with its *sahou*” (the glorified body of the Ego, and also the *kâmalokic* shell) proves this belief.

> “The Song of the Resurrection” chanted by Isis to recall her dead husband to life might be translated as the “Song of Rebirth,” as Osiris represents collective Humanity. “Oh! Osiris <note>here follows the name of the Osirified mummy, or the deceased</note>, rise again in holy earth (matter), majestic mummy in the coffin, beneath your physical substances,” was the funeral prayer of the priest over the deceased. “Resurrection” to the Egyptians never meant the resurrection of the mutilated mummy, but of the *Soul* that animated it—the Ego in a new body. The Soul or Ego periodically putting on flesh was a universal belief; nor can anything be more consistent with justice and Karmic law. (See “Pre-existence.”)

**Rephaim** (*Hebrew*). Specters, phantoms. (*Secret Doctrine*, II., 279.)

**Resha-havurah** (*Hebrew, Kabbalah*). Literally, the "White Head," from which flows the fiery fluid of life and intelligence in three hundred and seventy streams, in all the directions of the Universe. The "White Head" is the first Sephira, the Crown, or first active light.

**Reuchlin, John.** Nicknamed the "Father of the Reformation"; the friend of Pico della Mirandola, and the teacher and instructor of Erasmus, Luther, and Melanchthon. He was a great Kabbalist and Occultist.

**Rig Veda** (*Sanskrit*). The first and most important of the four Vedas. Fabled to have been "created" from the Eastern mouth of Brahmâ; recorded in Occultism as having been delivered by great sages on Lake Manasarovara beyond the Himalayas, tens of thousands of years ago.

**Rik** (*Sanskrit*). A verse of the *Rig-Veda*.

**Riksha** (*Sanskrit*). Each of the twenty-seven constellations forming the Zodiac. Any fixed star, or constellation of stars.

**Rimmon** (*Hebrew*). A Pomegranate, the type of abundant fertility; occurs in the Old Testament; it figures in Syrian temples and was deified there as an emblem of the celestial prolific mother of all; also a type of the full womb. <note>w.w.w.</note>

**Rings, Magic.** These existed as talismans in all folklore. In Scandinavia, such rings are always connected with the elves and dwarfs who were alleged to be the possessors of talismans and who gave them occasionally to human beings whom they wished to protect. In the words of the chronicler: "These magic rings brought good luck to the owner so long as they were carefully preserved; but their loss was attended with terrible misfortunes and unspeakable misery."

**Rings and Rounds.** Terms employed by Theosophists in the explanation of Eastern cosmogony. They are used to denote the various evolutionary cycles in the Elemental, Mineral, etc., Kingdoms, through which the Monad passes on any one globe; the term Round is used only to denote the cyclic passage of the Monad around the complete chain of seven globes. Generally speaking, Theosophists use the term ring as a synonym for cycles, whether cosmic, geological, metaphysical, or any other.

**Riphæus** (*Greek*). In mythology, a mountain chain upon which slept the frozen-hearted god of snows and hurricanes. In Esoteric philosophy, a real prehistoric continent which, from a tropical, ever-sunlit land, has now become a desolate region beyond the Arctic Circle.

**Rishabha** (*Sanskrit*). A sage supposed to have been the first teacher of the Jain doctrines in India.

**Rishabham** (*Sanskrit*). The Zodiacal sign Taurus.

**Rishi-Prajâpati** (*Sanskrit*). *Literally*, “revealers,” holy sages in the religious history of Âryavarta. Esoterically, the highest of them are the Hierarchies of “Builders” and Architects of the Universe and of living things on earth; they are generally called Dhyan Chohans, Devas, and gods.

**Rishis** (*Sanskrit*). Adepts; the inspired ones. In Vedic literature, the term is employed to denote those persons through whom the various Mantras were revealed.

**Ri-thlen**. *Literally*, “snake-keeping.” It is a terrible kind of sorcery practiced at Cherrapunji in the Khasi Hills. The former is the ancient capital of the latter. As the legend tells us, ages ago a *thlen* (serpent-dragon) which inhabited a cavern and devoured men and cattle was put to death by a local St. George and cut to pieces, with every piece being sent to a different district to be burned. But the piece received by the Khasis was preserved by them and became a kind of household god, and their descendants developed into *Ri-thlens* or “snake-keepers,” for the piece they preserved grew into a dragon (*thlen*) and ever since has obsessed certain Brahmin families of that district. To acquire the good grace of their *thlen* and save their own lives, these “keepers” often have to commit murders of women and children, from whose bodies they cut out the toe and finger nails, which they bring to their *thlen*, and thus indulge in a number of black magic practices connected with sorcery and necromancy.

**Roger Bacon**. A very famous Franciscan monk who lived in England in the thirteenth century. He was an alchemist who firmly believed in the existence of the Philosopher’s Stone, and was a great mechanician, chemist, physicist, and astrologer. In his treatise on the *Admirable Force of Art and Nature*, he gives hints about gunpowder and predicts the use of steam as a propelling power, describing also the hydraulic press, the diving-bell, and the kaleidoscope. He also made a famous brazen head fitted with an acoustic apparatus which gave out oracles.

**Ro and Ru** (*Egyptian*). The gate or outlet, the spot in the heavens from which proceeded or was born primeval light; synonymous with “cosmic womb.”

**Rohinilâ** (*Sanskrit*). The ancient name of a monastery visited by Buddha Sâkyamuni, now called Roynallah, near Balgada, in Eastern Bihar.

**Rohit** (*Sanskrit*). A female deer, a hind; the form assumed by Vâch (the female Logos and female aspect of Brahmâ, who created her out of one half of his body) to escape the amorous pursuits of her “father,” who transformed himself for that purpose into a buck or red deer (the color of Brahmâ being red).

**Rohitaka Stupa** (*Sanskrit*). The “red stupa,” or dagoba, built by King Ashoka, and on which Maitribala-râjâ fed starving Yakshas with his blood. The Yakshas are inoffensive demons (Elementaries) called *pûnya-janas* or “good people.”

<term>Rosicrucians</term> (Mystical). The name was first given to the disciples of a learned Adept named Christian Rosenkreuz, who flourished in Germany around 1460. He founded an Order of mystical students whose early history is to be found in the German work, *Fama Fraternitatis* (1614), which has been published in several languages. The members of the Order maintained their secrecy, but traces of them have been found in various places every half century since these dates. The *Societas Rosicruciana in Anglia* is a Masonic Order which has adopted membership in the "outer" order of the Chabrath Zereh Aur Bokher, or Order of the G.D. <note>Order of the Golden Dawn</note>, which has a very complete scheme of initiation into the Kabbalah and the Higher Magic of the Western or Hermetic type, and admits both sexes. It is a direct descendant from medieval societies of Rosicrucians, who were themselves descended from the Egyptian Mysteries. [w.w.w.]

<term>Rostan</term>. Book of the Mysteries of Rostan; an occult work in manuscript.

<term>Rowhanee</term> (Egyptian), or *Er-Roohanee*. This is the Magic of modern Egypt, supposed to proceed from Angels and Spirits (that is, Genii) and through the use of the mystery names of Allah. They distinguish two forms—*Ilwee*, which is the Higher or White Magic, and *Suflee* and *Sheytanee*, the Lower or Black Demonic Magic. There is also *Es-Seemuja*, which is deception or conjuring. Opinions differ as to the importance of a branch of Magic called *Darb el Mendel*, or as Barker calls it in English, the Mendel; by this is meant a form of artificial clairvoyance exhibited by a young boy before puberty, or a virgin, who—as the result of self-fascination by gazing at a pool of ink in the hand, alongside the use of incense and incantation—sees certain scenes of real life passing over its surface. Many Eastern travelers have narrated instances, such as E. W. Lane in his *Modern Egyptians* and his *Thousand and One Nights*, and E. B. Barker; the incidents have also been introduced into many works of fiction, such as Marryat's *Phantom Ship*, and a similar idea is interwoven with the story of Rose Mary and the Beryl stone, a poem by Rossetti. For a superficial attempt at an explanation, see the *Quarterly Review*, No. 117. [w.w.w.]

<term>Ruach</term> (Hebrew). Air, also Spirit; the Spirit, one of the "human principles" (Buddha-Manas).

<term>Ruach Elohim</term> (Hebrew). The Spirit of the gods; corresponds to the Holy Ghost of the Christians. Also the wind, breath, and rushing water. [w.w.w.]

<term>Rudra</term> (Sanskrit). A title of Siva, the Destroyer.

<term>Rudras</term> (Sanskrit). The mighty ones; the lords of the three upper worlds. One of the classes of the "fallen" or incarnating spirits; they are all born of Brahmâ.

<term>Runes</term> (Scandinavian). The Runic language and characters are the mystery or priestly tongue and alphabet of the ancient Scandinavians. *Runes* are derived from the word *rûna* (secret). Therefore, both the language and the character could neither be understood nor interpreted without having

## S.

**S.**—The nineteenth letter; numerically, *sixty*. In Hebrew it is the fifteenth letter, *Samech*, held as holy because “the sacred name of God is *Samech*.” Its symbol is a prop, or a pillar, and a phallic egg. In occult geometry, it is represented as a circle divided by a cross. ⊗ In the *Kabbalah*, the “divisions of *Gan-Eden* or *paradise*” are similarly divided.
**Sa** or **Hea** (*Chaldean*). The synthesis of the seven Gods in Babylonian mythology.
**Sabalâswâs** (*Sanskrit*). Sons of Daksha (*Secret Doctrine*, II., 275).
**Sabao** (*Greek*). The Gnostic name of the genius of Mars.
**Sabaoth** (*Hebrew*). An army or host from *Sâbâ*—to go to war; hence the name of the fighting god—the “Lord of Sabaoth.”
**Sabda** (*Sanskrit*). The Word, or Logos.
**Sabda Brahmam** (*Sanskrit*). “The Unmanifested Logos.” The *Vedas*; “Ethereal Vibrations diffused throughout Space.”
**Sabhâ** (*Sanskrit*). An assembly; a place for meetings, social or political. Also *Mahâsabhâ*, “the bundle of wonderful (mayavic or illusionary) things,” the gift of Mayâsur to the Pândavas (*Mahâbhârata*.)
**Sabianism.** The religion of the ancient Chaldeans. The latter, believing in one impersonal, universal, divine Principle, never mentioned It, but offered worship to the solar, lunar, and planetary gods and rulers, regarding the stars and other celestial bodies as their respective symbols.
**Sabians.** So-called astrolaters; those who worshipped the stars, or rather their “regents.” (See “Sabianism.”)
**Sacha Kiriya** (*Sanskrit*). A power among the Buddhists akin to a magic *mantram* used by the Brahmans. It is a miraculous energy which can be exercised by any adept, whether priest or layman, and is “most efficient when accompanied by *bhâwanâ*” (meditation). It consists in a recitation of one’s “acts of merit done either in this or some former birth”—as the Rev. Mr. Hardy thinks and describes it—but in reality it depends on the intensity of one’s will, added to an absolute faith in one’s own powers, whether of *yoga*—willing—or of prayer, as in the case of Muslims and Christians. *Sacha* means “true,” and *Kiriyang* means “action.” It is the power of merit, or of a saintly life.
**Sacrarium** (*Latin*). The name of the room in the houses of the ancient Romans which contained the particular deity worshipped by the family; also the adytum <note>The innermost sanctuary or shrine</note> of a temple.

**Sacred Heart.** In Egypt, the heart of Horus; in Babylon, the heart of the god Bel; and the lacerated heart of Bacchus in Greece and elsewhere. Its symbol was the persea. The pear-like shape of its fruit, and especially of its kernel, resembles the form of the heart. It is sometimes seen on the head of Isis, the mother of Horus, where the fruit is cut open and the heart-like kernel is exposed to full view. Roman Catholics have since adopted the worship of the "Sacred Heart" of Jesus and of the Virgin Mary.

**Sacred Science.** The name given to the *inner* esoteric philosophy—the secrets taught in ancient days to the initiated candidates and revealed during the final and supreme initiation by the Hierophants.

**Sadaikarûpa** (*Sanskrit*). The essence of the immutable nature.

**Sadducees.** A sect consisting of the followers of Zadok, a disciple of Antigonus Saccho. They are accused of denying the immortality of the (personal) soul and the resurrection of the (physical and personal) body. Theosophists do the same, although they deny neither the immortality of the Ego nor the resurrection of all its numerous and successive lives, which survive in the memory of the Ego. However, along with the Sadducees—a sect of learned philosophers who were to the other Jews what the polished and learned Gnostics were to the rest of the Greeks during the early centuries of our era—we certainly deny the immortality of the *animal* soul and the resurrection of the physical body. The Sadducees were the scientists and the learned men of Jerusalem and held the highest offices, such as high priests and judges, while the Pharisees were almost entirely the hypocrites <note>The original text uses "Pecksniffs," a reference to a hypocritical character in Charles Dickens' *Martin Chuzzlewit*.</note> of Judea.

**Sâdhyas** (*Sanskrit*). One of the names of the "twelve great gods" created by Brahmâ. They are cosmic gods; literally, "divine sacrificers." The Sâdhyas are important in Occultism.

**Sadik.** The same as the Biblical Melchizedec, identified by mystic Bible-worshippers with Jehovah and Jesus Christ. But since Father Sadik’s identity with Noah has been proven, he can be further identified with Kronos-Saturn.

**Safekh** (*Egyptian*). Written also as *Sebek* and *Sebakh*, the god of darkness and night, with the crocodile as his emblem. In the Typhonic legend and transformation, he is the same as Typhon. He is connected with both Osiris and Horus and is their great enemy on earth. We often find him called the "triple crocodile." In astronomy, he is the same as Mâkâra or Capricorn, the most mystical of the signs of the Zodiac.

**Saga** (*Scandinavian*). The goddess "who sings of the deeds of gods and heroes," and to whom the black ravens of Odin reveal the history of the Past and of the Future in the Norsemen’s *Edda*.

**Sâgara** (*Sanskrit*). Literally, "the Ocean"; a king, the father of 60,000 sons, who were reduced to ashes by a single glance from the eye of the sage Kapila for the disrespect they showed him.

**Sagardagan.** One of the four paths to Nirvâna.

**Saha** (*Sk.*). “The world of suffering”; any inhabited world in the chilio-cosmos.

**Sahampati** (*Sk.*). Maha or Parabrahm.

**Saharaksha** (*Sk.*). The fire of the Asuras; the name of a son of Pavamâna, one of the three chief occult fires.

**Saint Martin**, *Louis Claude de*. Born in France (Amboise) in 1743. A great mystic and writer who pursued his philosophical and theosophical studies in Paris during the Revolution. He was an ardent disciple of Jacob Boehme and studied under Martinez Paschalis, eventually founding a mystical semi-Masonic Lodge, “the Rectified Rite of St. Martin,” with seven degrees. He was a true <term>Theosophist</term>. At the present moment, some ambitious charlatans in Paris are caricaturing him and passing themselves off as initiated Martinists, and thus dishonoring the name of the late Adept.

**Sais** (*Eg.*). The place where the celebrated temple of Isis-Neith was found, which contained the ever-veiled statue of Neith (Neith and Isis being interchangeable), with the famous inscription,
->“I am all that has been, and is, and shall be, and no mortal has withdrawn my peplum”<-
(See “Sirius.”)

**Saka** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, “the One,” or the *Eka*; used for the “Dragon of Wisdom” or the manifesting deities, taken collectively.

**Saka** (*Sk.*). According to the Orientalists, the same as the classical *Sacæ*. It was during the reign of their King Yudishthira that the *Kali Yuga* began.

**Sâka Dwîpa** (*Sk.*). One of the seven islands or continents mentioned in the *Purânas* (ancient works).

**Sakkayaditthi**. Delusion of personality; the mistaken idea that
->“I am I,”<-
a man or a woman with a special name, instead of being an inseparable part of the whole.

**Sakradagamin** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, “he who will be born only once more” before he reaches *Nirvâna*; he who has entered the second of the four paths which lead to *Nirvâna* and has almost reached perfection.

**Sakshi** (*Sk.*). The name of the hare who, in the legend of the “moon and the hare,” threw himself into the fire to save some starving pilgrims who would not kill him. For this sacrifice, *Indra* is said to have transferred him to the center of the moon.

**Sakti** (*Sk.*). The active female energy of the gods; in popular Hinduism, their wives and goddesses; in Occultism, the crown of the astral light. Force and the six forces of nature synthesized. Universal Energy.

**Sakti-Dhara** (*Sk.*). *Lit.*, the “Spear-holder,” a title given to *Kartikeya* for killing *Târaka*, a *Daitya* or giant-demon. The latter, demon though he was, seems to have been such a great *Yogin*, owing to his religious austerities and holiness, that he made all the gods tremble before him. This makes *Kartikeya*, the war god, a kind of St. Michael.

**Sakwala.** This is a *bana* or "word" uttered by Gautama Buddha in his oral instructions. A Sakwala is a mundane world, or rather a solar system, of which there is an indefinite number in the universe; it denotes that space to which the light of every sun extends. Each Sakwala contains earths, hells, and heavens (meaning good and bad spheres, our earth being considered a hell in Occultism); it reaches its prime, then falls into decay, and is finally destroyed at regularly recurring periods by virtue of one immutable law. Upon the earth, the Master taught that there have already been four great "continents" (the Land of the Gods, Lemuria, Atlantis, and the present "continent" divided into five parts in the *Secret Doctrine*), and that three more are yet to appear. The former "did not communicate with each other," a phrase showing that Buddha was not speaking of the actual continents known in his day (for *Pâtâla*, or America, was perfectly familiar to the ancient Hindus), but of the four geological formations of the earth, with their four distinct *root-races* which had already disappeared.

**Sâkya** (*Sk.*). A family name of Gautama Buddha.

**Sâkyamuni Buddha** (*Sk.*). A name for the founder of Buddhism, the great Sage, the Lord Gautama.

**Salamanders.** The Rosicrucian name for the Elementals of Fire. The animal, as well as its name, is of great occult significance and is widely used in poetry. The name is almost identical in all languages. Thus, in Greek, Latin, French, Spanish, Italian, and others, it is *Salamandra*; in Persian, it is *Samandel*; and in Sanskrit, it is *Salamandala*.

**Salmalî** (*Sk.*). One of the seven zones; also a type of tree.

**Sama** (*Sk.*). One of the *bhâva pushpas*, or "flowers of sanctity." Sama is the fifth flower, or "resignation." There are eight such flowers: clemency or charity, self-restraint, affection (or love for others), patience, resignation, devotion, meditation, and truthfulness. Sama is also the repression of any mental disturbance.

**Sâma Veda** (*Sk.*). *Literally*, "the Scripture, or *Shâstra*, of peace." One of the four Vedas.

**Samâdhâna** (*Sk.*). That state in which a Yogi can no longer stray from the path of spiritual progress; when everything terrestrial, except for the visible body, has ceased to exist for him.

**Samâdhi** (*Sk.*). A state of ecstatic and complete trance. The term comes from the words *Sam-âdha*, meaning "self-possession." He who possesses this power is able to exercise absolute control over all his faculties, whether physical or mental; it is the highest state of Yoga.

**Samâdhindriya** (*Sk.*). *Literally*, "the root of concentration"; the fourth of the five roots called Pancha Indriyâni. In esoteric philosophy, these are said to be the agents that produce a highly moral life leading to sanctity and liberation. When these are reached, the two spiritual roots lying dormant in the body (*Atmâ* and *Buddhi*) will send out shoots and blossom. Samâdhindriya is the organ of ecstatic meditation in Râj-yoga practices.

**<term>Samael</term>** (*Heb.*). The Kabbalistic title of the Prince of those evil spirits who represent incarnations of human vices; the angel of Death. From this, the idea of Satan has evolved. [w.w.w.]

**<term>Samajna</term>** (*Sk.*). Literally, "an enlightened (or luminous) Sage". Translated literally, *Samgharana Samajna*, the famous *Vihara* near Kustana (China), means "the monastery of the luminous Sage".

**<term>Samâna</term>** (*Sk.*). One of the five breaths (*Pranas*) which carry on the chemical action in the animal body.

**<term>Sâmanêra.</term>** A novice; a postulant for the Buddhist priesthood.

**<term>Samanta Bhadra</term>** (*Sk.*). Literally, "Universal Sage". The name of one of the four Bodhisattvas of the Yogachara School, of the Mahayana (the Great Vehicle) of Wisdom of that system. There are four terrestrial and three celestial Bodhisattvas: the first four only act in the present races, but in the middle of the fifth Root-race the fifth Bodhisattva appeared, who, according to <unclear>an</unclear> esoteric legend, was Gautama Buddha, but who, having appeared too early, had to disappear physically from the world for a while.

**<term>Sâmanta Prabhâsa</term>** (*Sk.*). Literally, "universal brightness" or dazzling light. The name under which each of the 500 perfected Arhats reappears on earth as Buddha.

**<term>Sâmânya</term>** (*Sk.*). Community, or the mingling of qualities; an abstract notion of genus, such as humanity.

**<term>Samâpatti</term>** (*Sk.*). Absolute concentration in Raja-Yoga; the process of development by which perfect indifference (*Sams*) is reached (*apatti*). This state is the last stage of development before the possibility of entering into Samadhi is reached.

**<term>Samaya</term>** (*Sk.*). A religious precept.

**<term>S'ambhala</term>** (*Sk.*). A very mysterious locality due to its future associations. A town or village mentioned in the Puranas, from which, it is prophesied, the Kalki Avatar will appear. The "Kalki" is Vishnu, the *Messiah on the White Horse* of the Brahmins; the Maitreya Buddha of the Buddhists, Sosiosh of the Parsis, and Jesus of the Christians (See *Revelations*). All these "messengers" are to appear "before the destruction of the world", says the one; before the end of Kali Yuga, say the others. It is in Shambhala that the future Messiah will be born. Some Orientalists identify modern Muradabad in Rohilkhand (N.W.P.) with Shambhala, while Occultism places it in the Himalayas. It is pronounced *Shambhala*.

**<term>Sambhogakâya</term>** (*Sk.*). One of the three "Vestures" of glory, or bodies, attained by ascetics on the "Path". Some sects hold it as the second, while others as the third of the *Buddhakshêtras*, or forms of Buddha. Literally, the "Body of Compensation" (See *Voice of the Silence*, Glossary iii). Of such *Buddhakshêtras* there are seven; those of Nirmanakaya, Sambhogakaya, and Dharmakaya belong to the Trikaya, or three-fold quality.

<header>GLOSSARY</header>

**<term>Samgha</term> (*Sk.*).** The corporate assembly or a quorum of priests; also called *Bhikshu Samgha*. The word “church” used in translation does not at all express the real meaning.

**<term>Samkhara</term> (*Pali*).** One of the five *Skandhas* or attributes in Buddhism.

**<term>Samkhara</term> (*Pali*).** “Tendencies of mind” (See “*Skandhas*”).

**<term>Samma Sambuddha</term> (*Pali*).** The recollection of all of one’s past incarnations; a yoga phenomenon.

**<term>Samma Sambuddha</term> (*Pali*).** A title of the Lord Buddha, the “Lord of meekness and resignation”; it means “perfect illumination.”

**<term>Samothrace</term> (*Gr.*).** An island famous for its Mysteries, perhaps the oldest ever established in our present race. The Samothracian Mysteries were renowned all over the world.

**<term>Samothraces</term> (*Gr.*).** A designation of the five gods worshipped at the island of that name during the Mysteries. They are considered identical to the Cabeiri, Dioscuri, and Corybantes. Their names were mystical, denoting Pluto, Ceres or Proserpine, Bacchus and Aesculapius, or Hermes.

**<term>Sampajnâna</term> (*Sk.*).** A power of internal illumination.

**<term>Samskâra</term> (*Sk.*).** *Literally*, from *Sam* and *Kri*, meaning to improve, refine, or impress. In Hindu philosophy, the term is used to denote the impressions left upon the mind by individual actions or external circumstances, which are capable of being developed on any future favorable occasion—even in a future birth. The *Samskâra* denotes, therefore, the seeds of propensities and impulses from previous births to be developed in this one, or in coming *janmâs* (reincarnations). In Tibet, *Samskâra* is called Doodyed, and in China it is defined as—or at least connected with—action or Karma. Strictly speaking, it is a metaphysical term that is variously defined in exoteric philosophies; for example, in Nepal as illusion, in Tibet as a notion, and in Ceylon <note>modern Sri Lanka</note> as discrimination. The true meaning is as given above, and as such, it is connected with Karma and its operation.

**<term>Samtan</term> (*Tib.*).** The same as *Dhyâna* or meditation.

**<term>Samvara</term> (*Sk.*).** A deity worshipped by the Tantrikas.

**<term>Samvarta</term> (*Sk.*).** A minor *Kalpa*. A period in creation after which a partial annihilation of the world occurs.

**<term>Samvartta Kalpa</term> (*Sk.*).** The *Kalpa* or period of destruction, the same as *Pralaya*. Every root-race and sub-race is subject to such *Kalpas* of destruction; the fifth root-race has sixty-four such periodic cataclysms: fifty-six by fire, seven by water, and one small *Kalpa* by winds or cyclones.

**<term>Samvat</term> (*Sk.*).** The name of an Indian chronological era, supposed to have begun in 57 B.C.

**<term>Samvriti</term> (*Sk.*).** False conception—the origin of illusion.

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

**<term>Samvritisatya</term> (*Sk.*).** Truth mixed with false conceptions (Samvriti); the opposite of absolute truth—or **<term>Paramârthasatya</term>**, which is self-consciousness in absolute truth or reality.

**<term>Samyagâjiva</term> (*Sk.*).** Religious mendicancy <note>the practice of begging for alms</note>: the correct profession. It is the fourth Mârga (path), the vow of poverty, which is obligatory for every Arhat and monk.

**<term>Samyagdrîshti</term> (*Sk.*).** The ability to discuss truth. The first of the eight Mârgas (paths) of the ascetic.

**<term>Samyakkarmânta</term> (*Sk.*).** The last of the eight Mârgas. Strict purity and the observance of honesty, disinterestedness, and unselfishness, which are the characteristics of every Arhat.

**<term>Samyaksamâdhi</term> (*Sk.*).** Absolute mental coma <note>a state of profound meditative absorption or trance</note>. The sixth of the eight Mârgas; the full attainment of Samâdhi.

**<term>Samyaksambuddha</term> (*Sk.*) or <term>Sammâsambuddha</term>,** as pronounced in Ceylon. *Literally*, the Buddha of correct and harmonious knowledge; the third of the ten titles of Sâkyamuni.

**<term>Samyattaka Nikaya</term> (*Pali*).** A Buddhist work composed mostly of dialogues between the Buddha and his disciples.

**<term>Sana</term> (*Sk.*).** One of the three *esoteric* Kumâras, whose names are Sana, Kapila, and Sanatsujâta; this is the mysterious triad that contains the mystery of generation and reincarnation.

**<term>Sana</term> or <term>Sanaischarâ</term> (*Sk.*).** The same as Sani or the planet Saturn. In the Hindu Pantheon, he is the son of Surya (the Sun) and Sanjna (Spiritual Consciousness), who is the daughter of Visva-Karman—or rather, he is the son of Chhâyâ, the shadow left behind by Sanjna. Sanaischara means the "slow-moving."

**<term>Sanaka</term> (*Sk.*).** A sacred plant whose fibers are woven into yellow robes for Buddhist priests.

**<term>Sanat Kumâra</term> (*Sk.*).** The most prominent of the seven Kumâras, the Vaidhâtra, the first of whom are called Sanaka, Sananda, Sanâtana, and Sanat Kumâra; these names are all significant descriptions of the degrees of human intellect.

**<term>Sanat Sujâtiya</term> (*Sk.*).** A work treating Krishna’s teachings, similar to those in the *Bhagavad Gîtâ* and *Anugîtâ*.

**<term>Sancha-Dwîpa</term> (*Sk.*).** One of the seven great islands, the *Sapta-Dwîpa*.

**<term>Sanchoniathon</term> (*Gr.*).** A pre-Christian writer on Phoenician Cosmogony whose works are no longer extant <note>no longer in existence</note>. Philo of Byblos provides only the so-called fragments of Sanchoniathon.

**<term>Sandalphon</term> (*Heb.*).** The Kabbalistic Prince of Angels, emblematically represented by one of the Cherubim of the Ark.

**<term>Sandhyâ</term> (*Sk.*).** A period between two Yugas, morning or evening; anything that comes between and joins two others. *Literally*, "twilight"; the period between a full Manvantara (a "Day") and a full Pralaya (a "Night") of "Brahmâ."

**<term>Sandhyâmsa</term> (*Sk.*).** A period following a Yuga.

**<term>Sanghai Dag-po</term> (*Tib.*).** The “concealed Lord”; a title of those who have merged into and identified themselves with the Absolute. It is used for the “Nirvânees” and the “Jîvanmuktâs.”

**<term>Sangye Khado</term> (*Sk.*).** The Queen of the *Khado* or female genii; the *Dâkinî* of the Hindus and the *Lilith* of the Hebrews.

**<term>Sanjnâ</term> (*Sk.*).** Spiritual Consciousness. The wife of *Surya*, the Sun.

**<term>Sankara</term> (*Sk.*).** The name of Siva. Also a great Vedantic philosopher.

**<term>Sânkhya</term> (*Sk.*).** The system of philosophy founded by Kapila Rishi; a system of analytical metaphysics and one of the six *Darshanas* or schools of philosophy. It discusses numerical categories and the meaning of the twenty-five *tatwas* (the forces of nature in various degrees). This “atomistic school,” as some call it, explains nature by the interaction of twenty-four elements with *purusha* (spirit) modified by the three *gunas* (qualities). It teaches the eternity of *pradhâna* (primordial, homogeneous matter), or the self-transformation of nature and the eternity of human Egos.

**<term>Sânkhya Kârikâ</term> (*Sk.*).** A work by Kapila containing his aphorisms.

**<term>Sânkhya Yoga</term> (*Sk.*).** The system of Yoga as established by the school mentioned above.

**<term>Sanna</term> (*Pali*).** One of the five *Skandhas*, specifically the attribute of abstract ideas.

**<term>Sannyâsi</term> (*Sk.*).** A Hindu ascetic who has reached the highest mystic knowledge, whose mind is focused only on the supreme truth, and who has entirely renounced everything terrestrial and worldly.

**<term>Sansâra</term> (*Sk.*).** *Literally*, “rotation”; the ocean of births and deaths. Human rebirths are represented as a continuous circle—a wheel that is always in motion.

**<term>Sanskrit</term> (*Sk.*).** The classical language of the Brahmans; it was *never known or spoken in its true systematized form* (which was later given approximately by Pânini) except by initiated Brahmans, as it was pre-eminently a “mystery language.” It has now degenerated into the so-called *Prâkrita*.

**<term>Santa</term> (*Sk.*).** *Literally*, “placidity.” The primeval quality of the latent, undifferentiated state of elementary matter.

**<term>Santatih</term> (*Sk.*).** The “offspring.”

**<term>Saphar</term> (*Heb.*).** Sepharim; one of those called in the Kabbalah—Sepher, Saphar, and Sipur, or “Number, Numbers, and Numbered”—by whose agency the world was formed.

**<term>Sapta</term> (*Sk.*).** Seven.

**<term>Sapta Buddhaka</term> (*Sk.*).** An account in the *Mahânidâna Sûtra* of the *Sapta Buddha*, the seven Buddhas of our Round, of which Gautama Sâkyamuni is esoterically the fifth, and exoterically (as a blind <note>a term used to conceal a deeper truth from the uninitiated</note>), the seventh.

**<term>Sapta Samudra</term> (*Sk.*).** The "seven oceans." These have an occult significance on a higher plane.

**<term>Sapta Sindhava</term> (*Sk.*).** The "seven sacred rivers." A Vedic term. In Zend works, they are called *Hapta Heando*. These rivers are closely united with the esoteric teachings of the Eastern schools, having a very occult significance.

**<term>Sapta Tathâgata</term> (*Sk.*).** The chief seven Nirmânakâyas among the countless ancient world-guardians. Their names are inscribed on a seven-sided pillar kept in a secret chamber in almost all Buddhist temples in China and Tibet. Orientalists are wrong to think that these are "the seven Buddhist substitutes for the Rishis of the Brahmans." (See "Tathâgata-gupta").

**<term>Saptadwipa</term> (*Sk.*).** The seven sacred islands or "continents" in the *Purânas*.

**<term>Saptaloka</term> (*Sk.*).** The seven higher regions, beginning from the earth and moving upwards.

**<term>Saptaparna</term> (*Sk.*).** The "sevenfold." A plant which gave its name to a famous cave, a *Vihâra*, in Râjâgriha, now near Buddhagaya, where the Lord Buddha used to meditate and teach his Arhats, and where the first Synod was held after his death. This cave had seven chambers, which is the source of the name. In Esotericism, *Saptaparna* is the symbol of the "sevenfold Man-Plant."

**<term>Saptarshi</term> (*Sk.*).** The seven Rishis. As stars, they are the constellation of the Great Bear, and are called as such the *Riksha* and *Chitrasikhandinas*, meaning "bright-crested."

**<term>Sar</term> or <term>Saros</term> (*Chald.*).** A Chaldean god from whose name, represented by a circular horizon, the Greeks borrowed their word *Saros*, the cycle.

**<term>Saramâ</term> (*Sk.*).** In the Vedas, the dog of Indra and mother of the two dogs called *Sârameyas*. Saramâ is the "divine watchman" of the god and the same as the one who watched "over the golden flock of stars and solar rays"; she is the same as the planet Mercury and the Greek Hermes, who is called *Sârameyas*.

**<term>Saraph</term> (*Heb.*).** A flying serpent.

**<term>Sarasvati</term> (*Sk.*).** The same as Vâch, the wife and daughter of Brahmâ, produced from one of the two halves of his body. She is the goddess of speech and of sacred or esoteric knowledge and wisdom. She is also called *Sri*.

**<term>Sarcophagus</term> (*Gr.*).** A stone tomb, a receptacle for the dead; *sarc* means flesh, and *phagein* means to eat. *Lapis assius*, the stone from which sarcophagi were made, is found in Lycia and has the property of consuming bodies in a very few weeks. In Egypt, sarcophagi were made of various other stones, such as black basalt, red granite, alabaster, and other materials, as they served only as outward containers for the wooden coffins holding the mummies. **<term>Satti</term>** or **<term>Suttee</term>**, (*Sk.*). The burning of living widows together with their dead husbands—a custom now happily abolished in India; *literally*, "a chaste and devoted wife."

**<term>Sattva</term>** (*Sk.*). Understanding; quiescence in divine knowledge. It generally follows the word *Bodhi* when used as a compound word, *e.g.*, "Bodhisattva."

**<term>Sattva</term>** or **<term>Satwa</term>**, (*Sk.*). Goodness; the same as *Sattva*, or purity, one of the *trigunas* or three divisions of nature.

**<term>Satya</term>** (*Sk.*). Supreme truth.

**<term>Satya Loka</term>** (*Sk.*). The world of infinite purity and wisdom, the celestial abode of Brahma and the gods.

**<term>Scarabæus.</term>** In Egypt, the symbol of resurrection, and also of rebirth; of resurrection for the mummy—or rather of the highest aspects of the personality which animated it—and of rebirth of the Ego, the "spiritual body" of the lower, human Soul. Egyptologists give us but half of the truth when, in speculating upon the meaning of certain inscriptions, they say, "the justified soul, once arrived at a certain period of its wanderings (simply at the death of the physical body) should be united to its body (*i.e.*, the Ego) never more to be separated from it." (Rougé.) What is this so-called body? Can it be the mummy? Certainly not, for the emptied mummified corpse can never resurrect. It can only be the eternal, spiritual vestment, the Ego that never dies but gives immortality to whatsoever becomes united with it. "The delivered Intelligence (which) retakes its luminous envelope and (re)becomes Daimon," as Prof. Maspero says, is the spiritual Ego; the personal Ego or *Kama Manas*, its direct ray, or the lower soul, is that which aspires to become *Osirified*, *i.e.*, to unite itself with its "god"; and that portion of it which will succeed in so doing, will *never more be separated from it* (the god), not even when the latter incarnates again and again, descending periodically on earth in its pilgrimage, in search of further experiences and following the decrees of Karma. Khem, "the sower of seed," is shown on a stele in a picture of Resurrection after physical death, as the creator and the sower of the grain of corn, which after corruption, springs up afresh each time into a new ear, on which a scarabæus beetle is seen poised; and Deveria shows very justly that "Ptah is the inert, material form of Osiris, who will become Sokari (the eternal Ego) to be reborn, and afterwards be Harmachus," or Horus in his transformation, the risen god. The prayer so often found in the tomb inscriptions, "the wish for the resurrection in one's *living soul*" or the Higher Ego, always has a scarabæus at the end, standing for the personal soul. The scarabæus is the most honored, as the most frequent and familiar, of all Egyptian symbols. No mummy is without several of them; the favorite ornament on engravings, household fur-

It is written in the Neo-Hebrew of the *Mishnah*. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**<term>Sephira</term>** (*Hebrew*). An emanation of Deity; the parent and synthesis of the ten Sephiroth when she stands at the head of the Sephirothal Tree. In the *Kabbalah*, Sephira, or the “Sacred Aged,” is the divine Intelligence (the same as Sophia or Metis), the first emanation from the “Endless” or <term>Ain-Suph</term>.

**<term>Sephiroth</term>** (*Hebrew*). The ten emanations of Deity; the highest is formed by the concentration of the Ain Soph Aur, or the Limitless Light, and each Sephira produces another Sephira by emanation. The names of the Ten Sephiroth are: 1. <term>Kether</term>—The Crown; 2. <term>Chokmah</term>—Wisdom; 3. <term>Binah</term>—Understanding; 4. <term>Chesed</term>—Mercy; 5. <term>Geburah</term>—Power; 6. <term>Tiphereth</term>—Beauty; 7. <term>Netzach</term>—Victory; 8. <term>Hod</term>—Splendor; 9. <term>Jesod</term>—Foundation; and 10. <term>Malkuth</term>—The Kingdom.

The conception of Deity embodied in the Ten Sephiroth is a very sublime one, and each Sephira represents to the Kabbalist a group of exalted ideas, titles, and attributes that the name only faintly represents. Each Sephira is called either active or passive, though this classification may lead to error; “passive” does not mean a return to negative existence, and the two words only express the relation between individual Sephiroth rather than any absolute quality. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**<term>Septerium</term>** (*Latin*). A great religious festival held in ancient times every ninth year at Delphi in honor of Helios (the Sun) or Apollo, to commemorate his triumph over darkness (Python); Apollo-Python is the same as Osiris-Typhon in Egypt.

**<term>Seraphim</term>** (*Hebrew*). Celestial beings described by Isaiah (6:2) as having a human form with the addition of three pairs of wings. The Hebrew word is ShRPIM and, aside from the instance mentioned above, it is translated as "serpents" and is related to the verbal root ShRP, *to burn up*. The word is used for serpents in the books of Numbers and Deuteronomy. Moses is said to

In the *Kabbalah*, the Seraphim are a group of angelic powers assigned to the Sephira Geburah—Severity. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**<term>Serapis</term>** (*Egyptian*). A great solar god who replaced Osiris in popular worship, and in whose honor the seven vowels were sung. He was often depicted in representations as a serpent, a “Dragon of Wisdom.” He was the greatest god of Egypt during the first centuries of Christianity.

**<term>Sesha</term>** (*Sanskrit*). *Ananta*, the great Serpent of Eternity, the couch of Vishnu; the symbol of infinite Time in Space. In popular beliefs, Sesha is represented as a thousand-headed and seven-headed cobra; the former being the king of the underworld, called Pâtâla, and the latter being the carrier or support of Vishnu on the Ocean of Space.

**<term>Set</term>** or **<term>Seth</term>** (*Egyptian*). The same as the Son of Noah and Typhon—who is the dark side of Osiris. He is the same as Thoth and Satan, the adversary, though not the devil as represented by Christians.

**<term>Sevekh</term>** (*Egyptian*). The god of time; Chronos; the same as *Sefekh*. Some scholars of the East translate it as the “Seventh.”

**<term>Shaberon</term>** (*Tibetan*). The Mongolian Shaberon or Khubilgan (or Khubilkhans) are the reincarnations of Buddha, according to the Lamaists; they are great Saints and *Avatars*, so to speak.

**<term>Shaddai</term>**, *El* (*Hebrew*). A name of the Hebrew Deity, usually translated as God Almighty, found in *Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Ruth*, and *Job*. Its Greek equivalent is Kurios Pantokrator; but by Hebrew derivation it means rather “the pourer forth,” as *shad* means a breast, and indeed *shdi* is also used for “a nursing mother.” <note>W.W.W.</note>

**<term>Shamans</term>**. An order of Tartar or Mongolian priest-magicians, or as some say, priest-sorcerers. They are not Buddhists, but a sect of the old *Bhon* religion of Tibet. They live mostly in Siberia and its borderlands. Both men and women may be Shamans. They are all magicians, or rather psychics or mediums developed through artificial means. At present, those who act as priests among the Tartars are generally very uneducated and far below the fakirs in knowledge and training.

**<term>Shânâh</term>** (*Hebrew*). The Lunar Year.

**<term>Shangna</term>** (*Sanskrit*). A mysterious epithet given to a robe or “vesture” in a metaphorical sense. To put on the “Shangna robe” means the acquisition of Secret Wisdom and Initiation. (See *Voice of the Silence*, pp. 84 and 85, Glossary.)

<header>THEOSOPHICAL</header>

**Shâstra** or *S’âstra* (*Sanskrit*). A treatise or book; any work of divine or accepted authority, including law books. A *Shâstrî* means to this day, in India, a man learned in divine and human law.

**Shedim** (*Hebrew*). See “*Siddim*”.

**Shekinah** (*Hebrew*). A title applied to Malkuth, the tenth Sephira, by the *Kabbalists*; but used by the Jews to refer to the cloud of glory which rested on the Mercy-seat in the Holy of Holies. As taught, however, by all the rabbis of Asia Minor, its nature is of a more exalted kind: Shekinah being the veil of Ain-Soph, the Endless and the Absolute; hence a kind of Kabbalistic *Mûlaprakriti*. <note>W.W.W.</note>

**Shells**. A Kabbalistic name for the phantoms of the dead—the “spirits” of the Spiritualists who appear in physical phenomena. They are so named because they are simply illusory forms, *empty* of their higher principles.

**Shemal** (*Chaldean*). Samâel, the spirit of the earth, its presiding ruler and genius.

**Shemhamphorash** (*Hebrew*). The separated name. The marvelous name derived from the substance of deity and showing its self-existent essence. Jesus was accused by the Jews of having stolen this name from the Temple through magic arts and of using it to produce his miracles.

**Sheol** (*Hebrew*). The hell of the Hebrew Pantheon; a region of stillness and inactivity as distinguished from Gehenna (*see also*).

**Shien-Sien** (*Chinese*). A state of bliss and soul-freedom, during which a person can travel in spirit wherever they like.

**Shiites** (*Persian*). A sect of Muslims who place the prophet Ali higher than Muhammad, rejecting Sunnah or tradition.

**Shîla** (*Pali*). The second virtue of the ten Pâramitâs of perfection. Perfect harmony in words and acts.

**Shinto** (*Japanese*). The ancient religion of Japan before Buddhism, based upon the worship of spirits and ancestors.

**Shoel-ob** (*Hebrew*). One who consults with familiar “spirits”; a necromancer, or one who raises the dead or their phantoms.

**Shoo** (*Egyptian*). A personification of the god Ra; represented as the “great cat of the Basin of Persea in Anu.”

**Shudâla Mâdan** (*Tamil*). The vampire, the ghoul, or graveyard spook.

**Shûle Mâdan** (*Tamil*). The elemental spirit which is said to help “magicians” grow mango trees and perform other wonders.

**Shutukt** (*Tibetan*). A collegiate monastery in Tibet of great fame, containing over 30,000 monks and students.

**Sibac** (*Quiché*). The reed from whose pith the third race of humans was created, according to the scripture of the Guatemalans called the *Popol Vuh*.

**Sibikâ** (*Sanskrit*). The weapon of Kuvera, the god of wealth (a Vedic deity living in the underworld, and thus a kind of Pluto), made out of the parts of the

**Siddhânta** (*Sk*.). Any learned work on astronomy or mathematics in India.

**Siddhârtha** (*Sk*.). A name given to Gautama Buddha.

**Siddhas** (*Sk*.). Saints and sages who have become almost divine; also a hierarchy of Dhyan Chohans.

**Siddhâsana** (*Sk*.). A posture in Hatha-yoga practices.

**Siddha-Sena** (*Sk*.). Literally, “the leader of *Siddhas*”; a title of Karttikeya, the “mysterious youth” (*kumâra guha*).

**Siddhis** (*Sk*.). Literally, “attributes of perfection”; phenomenal powers acquired through holiness by Yogis.

**Siddim** (*Heb*.). The Canaanites, we are told, worshiped these evil powers as deities, the name meaning the “pourers forth”; a valley was named after them. There seems to be a connection between these, as types of Fertile Nature, and the many-bosomed Isis and Diana of Ephesus. In Psalm 106:37, the word is translated as “devils,” and we are told that the Canaanites shed the blood of their sons and daughters to them. Their title seems to come from the same root ShD, from which the god named El Shaddai is derived. <note>W.W.W.</note>
The Arabic Shedim means “Nature Spirits,” Elementals; they are the afrits of modern Egypt and djins of Persia, India, etc.

**Sidereal.** Anything relating to the stars, but also, in Occultism, to various influences emanating from such regions, such as “sidereal force,” as taught by Paracelsus, and the sidereal (luminous), ethereal body, etc.

**Si-dzang** (*Chin*.). The Chinese name for Tibet; mentioned in the Imperial Library of the capital of Fo Kein, as the “great seat of Occult learning,” 2207 years B.C. (*Secret Doctrine*, I., p. 271.)

**Sige** (*Gr*.). “Silence”; a name adopted by the Gnostics to signify the root from which the Aeons of the second series proceed.

**Sighra** or *Sighraga* (*Sk*.). The father of Moru, “who is still living through the power of Yoga, and will manifest himself at the beginning of the *Krita* age in order to re-establish the *Kshatriyas* in the nineteenth *Yuga*,” according to the Puranic prophecies. “Moru” stands here for “Morya,” the dynasty of the Buddhist sovereigns of Pataliputra which began with the great King Chandragupta, the grandfather of King Ashoka. It is the first Buddhist Dynasty. (*Secret Doctrine*, I., 378.)

**Sigurd** (*Scand*.). The hero who slew Fafnir, the “Dragon,” roasted his heart and ate it, after which he became the wisest of men. This is an allegory referring to Occult study and initiation.

**Simeon-ben-Jochai.** An Adept-Rabbi who was the author of the *Zohar* (which see).
